en.title: Mudeungsan National Park (Gwangju)
en.overview: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢ and is located in the northern and eastern districts of Gwangju, as well as in Damyang-gun and Hwasun-gun. The park is primarily composed of various types of rocks including Hwasun andesite, Mudeungsan tuff (quartz andesite tuff, Mudeungsan basalt, quartz andesite), Dogok volcanic rock, Mimu granite, biotite granite, quartz porphyry, and dike rocks.
en.pull_quote: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢...
paragraphs: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢ and is located in the northern and eastern districts of Gwangju, as well as in Damyang-gun and Hwasun-gun. The park is primarily composed of various types of rocks including Hwasun andesite, Mudeungsan tuff (quartz andesite tuff, Mudeungsan basalt, quartz andesite), Dogok volcanic rock, Mimu granite, biotite granite, quartz porphyry, and dike rocks.

The most notable feature of Mudeungsan is its columnar jointing. Columnar joints are formed when high-temperature lava cools on the surface, resulting in polygonal columns. These columnar joints can be well observed in the Mudeungsan columnar joint area (Seoseokdae, Ipsukdae, Gwangseokdae), Gyubong Rock, and Jungbong. Particularly, the highest peak of Mudeungsan, Cheonwangbong, at an elevation of 1,187m, features vertical jointed rocks that rise dramatically, resembling a stone wall. The rock formation known as Saeinbong, named for its resemblance to a jade seal, is located on the western ridge of Jangbuljae and consists of a curtain-like rock cliff.

paragraphs: 無等山は1972年5月22日に道立公園に指定され、2013年3月4日に国立公園第21号に指定されました。無等山国立公園は全体面積75.425㎢で、全南光州統合特別市の北区と東区、潭陽郡と華順郡に位置しています。無等山国立公園は主に華順安山岩、無等山凝灰岩（石英安山岩質凝灰岩、無等山溶岩、石英安山岩）、ドゴク火山岩、ミムンサン花崗岩、黒雲母花崗岩、石英斑岩、岩脈などで構成されています。

無等山の最も大きな特徴は柱状節理です。柱状節理は高温の溶岩が噴出した後、地表で冷却される過程で収縮して多角形の石柱が割れて形成される多角形の角がある柱を指します。このような柱状節理は無等山柱状節理帯（西石台、立石台、光石台）、規峰岩、中峰などでよく観察できます。特に海抜1,187mの無等山最高峰である天王峰周辺は西石台・立石台・規峰などの垂直節理の岩石が石垣のようにそびえ立ち、壮観を成しています。まるで玉璽のようだと名付けられたサイイン峰は、ジャンブルジェから西の稜線に屏風のような岩壁で構成されています。

paragraphs: 无等山于1972年5月22日被指定为省立公园，并于2013年3月4日被指定为第21号国家公园。无等山国家公园的总面积为75.425平方公里，位于全南光州统合特别市的北区和东区，以及潭阳郡和华顺郡。无等山国家公园主要由华顺安山岩、无等山凝灰岩（石英安山岩质凝灰岩、无等山火山岩、石英安山岩）、多谷火山岩、米门花岗岩、黑云母花岗岩、石英斑岩和岩脉等组成。
无等山的最大特点是柱状节理。柱状节理是高温熔岩喷发后，在地表冷却过程中收缩而形成的多角形石柱。这种柱状节理在无等山柱状节理带（西石台、立石台、光石台）、规峰岩和中峰等地可以很好地观察到。特别是海拔1,187米的无等山最高峰天王峰周围，垂直节理的岩石如石墙般高耸，形成壮观的景象。被称为玉璽的赛因峰位于长佛斋的西侧山脊，由屏风状的岩壁构成。

en.title: Chungjangno
en.overview: If Myeongdong exists in Seoul, Chungjangno exists in Gwangju, Jeonnam. As the city expands, many new bustling streets have emerged, but the center of Gwangju will always be Chungjangno. Chungjangno was the main north-south road connecting the South and North Gates during the city wall era and was referred to as the city center. The commercial area on Chungjangno began to form shortly after the Japanese colonial period in 1911 when a Japanese national opened a general store called 'Yeomok' across from the current Industrial Bank.
en.pull_quote: If Myeongdong exists in Seoul, Chungjangno exists in Gwangju, Jeonnam. As the city expands, many new bustling streets have emerged, but the center of Gwangju will always be Chungjangno.
paragraphs: If Myeongdong exists in Seoul, Chungjangno exists in Gwangju, Jeonnam. As the city expands, many new bustling streets have emerged, but the center of Gwangju will always be Chungjangno. Chungjangno was the main north-south road connecting the South and North Gates during the city wall era and was referred to as the city center.

The commercial area on Chungjangno began to form shortly after the Japanese colonial period in 1911 when a Japanese national opened a general store called 'Yeomok' across from the current Industrial Bank. After that, shops owned by Japanese nationals began to appear around Chungjangno 1-ga, and the reason they could dominate the commercial area was due to the presence of the Japanese Governor-General's office at the former provincial government site. The name 'Chungjangno' is derived from the posthumous title of Kim Deok-ryeong, a general during the Imjin War. The first streetlights on Chungjangno were oil lamps. Historically, it has been a hub for clothing, suits, and food services, attracting many young people and becoming known as a street of trends and youth.

en.title: 3.8 Democracy Movement Memorial Hall
en.overview: The 3.8 Democracy Movement Memorial Hall is an exhibition and educational facility established to commemorate and inherit the history and spirit of the 3.8 Democracy Movement, which was initiated by high school students in Daejeon on March 8, 1960. This movement, a spontaneous democratization effort against the dictatorship and corruption of the Liberal Party regime, is recognized for its historical value as a national memorial day. The hall features permanent and special exhibitions showcasing historical materials, records, photos, and videos from that time.

en.title: Daejeon Expo Science Park
en.overview: Established to commemorate the 1993 Daejeon World Expo, which was the first international expo recognized by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE) in Korea, this science park utilizes the facilities and grounds for public science education. The park features the Hanbit Tower, symbolizing a beam of light connecting the past, present, and future based on wise history. The 93-meter tall tower serves as an observatory inspired by science and space, offering views of the park and Daejeon city.
en.pull_quote: Established to commemorate the 1993 Daejeon World Expo, this science park utilizes the facilities and grounds for public science education.
paragraphs: Established to commemorate the 1993 Daejeon World Expo, which was the first international expo recognized by the Bureau International des Expositions (BIE) in Korea, this science park utilizes the facilities and grounds for public science education. The park features the Hanbit Tower, symbolizing a beam of light connecting the past, present, and future based on wise history. The 93-meter tall tower serves as an observatory inspired by science and space, offering views of the park and Daejeon city.

In front of the Hanbit Tower, there is a musical fountain in the Water Light Square that connects to the Expo Bridge, providing exciting songs and fountain shows for visitors. During the night operation period, a splendid media facade unfolds against the backdrop of the Hanbit Tower, allowing visitors to enjoy colorful video displays using special night lighting.

en.title: National Daejeon Cemetery Honor Trail
en.overview: The Honor Trail within the National Daejeon Cemetery is designed for veterans and visitors to walk comfortably while reflecting on the meaning of love for the country. This trail, created along the cemetery, consists of seven courses in red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet, and is also known as the 'Rainbow Trail'. It is designed as a forest path, allowing visitors to experience nature, and is gentle enough for the elderly and children to walk without difficulty.
en.pull_quote: The Honor Trail within the National Daejeon Cemetery is designed for veterans and visitors to walk comfortably while reflecting on the meaning of love for the country.
paragraphs: The Honor Trail within the National Daejeon Cemetery is designed for veterans and visitors to walk comfortably while reflecting on the meaning of love for the country. This trail, created along the cemetery, consists of seven courses in red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet, and is also known as the 'Rainbow Trail'. It is designed as a forest path, allowing visitors to experience nature, and is gentle enough for the elderly and children to walk without difficulty.

Thanks to the shade of the trees, it can be used comfortably even in summer. Along the trail, visitors can encounter various attractions such as the Memorial Hall for the National Railway, Pine Forest, Bamboo Grove, and Observation Deck.

en.title: Root Park
en.overview: Root Park is a theme park opened on November 1, 1997, featuring sculptures symbolizing surnames and the Korean Genealogy Museum, along with various facilities. It is an educational park that fosters the values of filial piety and ownership spirit, and it is a family-friendly park that hosts various events, showcasing its unique characteristics as an urban nature park set against beautiful natural scenery.
en.pull_quote: Root Park is a theme park opened on November 1, 1997, featuring sculptures symbolizing surnames and the Korean Genealogy Museum.
paragraphs: Root Park is a theme park opened on November 1, 1997, featuring sculptures symbolizing surnames and the Korean Genealogy Museum, along with various facilities. It is an educational park that fosters the values of filial piety and ownership spirit, and it is a family-friendly park that hosts various events, showcasing its unique characteristics as an urban nature park set against beautiful natural scenery.

The park features surname sculptures that allow visitors to reconnect with their roots, a deep spring representing the four seasons, a waterfront stage for various events, a grassy square at the center of the park, and an observation deck that offers a panoramic view of the park, as well as various facilities such as a forest bathing area, a filial culture garden, and a healing rest area.

en.title: Boramae Mountain Happiness Forest Trail
en.overview: The Boramae Mountain Happiness Forest Trail is a trail created around Boramae Mountain. Boramae Mountain (457.6m) was once called 'Treasure Mountain' because it was believed that treasures were buried there, and it is a beloved mountain in Daejeon. The trail circles around Boramae Mountain, returning to the starting point, and is approximately 13 km long. Visitors can walk comfortably in the shade of the dense trees, and in autumn, the foliage is impressive.
en.pull_quote: The Boramae Mountain Happiness Forest Trail is a trail created around Boramae Mountain.
paragraphs: The Boramae Mountain Happiness Forest Trail is a trail created around Boramae Mountain. Boramae Mountain (457.6m) was once called 'Treasure Mountain' because it was believed that treasures were buried there, and it is a beloved mountain in Daejeon.

The trail circles around Boramae Mountain, returning to the starting point, and is approximately 13 km long. Visitors can walk comfortably in the shade of the dense trees, and in autumn, the foliage is impressive. Additionally, visitors can enjoy Boramae Mountain Fortress, observation decks, and Gochoksa Temple. Nearby attractions include Hanwha Eagles Park, Chungmu Gymnasium, and Daejeon Aquarium.

zh.overview: 博罗梅山幸福森林步道是围绕博罗梅山修建的步道。博罗梅山（457.6米）曾因埋藏宝物而被称为“宝物山”，如今是大田市民喜爱的代表性山脉。该步道环绕博罗梅山一周，回到起点，长度约为13公里。游客可以在郁郁葱葱的树荫下舒适地行走，秋天的红叶尤为迷人。

paragraphs: The Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District in Nam-gu, Ulsan, is the only theme park in Korea with whale tourism infrastructure. It features the Whale Museum and the country's first dolphin aquarium, allowing visitors to experience the ecology and culture of whales. The 'Whale Sea Tour Ship' began operations in July 2009, and in April 2013, it was replaced with a cruise-class vessel, marking the beginning of a new era in whale tourism.

In May of the same year, a spectacular sight was captured as thousands of minke whales appeared, starting with one. Riding the Whale Sea Tour Ship offers a unique experience to enjoy coastal scenery and search for actual whales. The ship is equipped with various facilities such as a grand hall, performance stage, VIP room, meeting room, café, and convenience store, enhancing the convenience of tourism.

en.title: Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District
en.overview: The Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District is a cultural center for whales established in the Jangsaengpo area of Nam-gu, Ulsan. It is a historical area where whales have inhabited since prehistoric times, and it is the only tourist district in Korea where visitors can comprehensively experience the history and culture related to whales. The district is home to various exhibition and experience facilities focused on whale ecology and whaling culture. The main facility, the Jangsaengpo Whale Museum, displays various artifacts such as whale skeletons and whaling tools, while the Whale Ecology Experience Center is the first dolphin aquarium in Korea.
en.pull_quote: The Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District is a cultural center for whales established in the Jangsaengpo area of Nam-gu, Ulsan. It is a historical area where whales have inhabited since prehistoric times, and it is the only tourist district in Korea where visitors can comprehensively experience the history and culture related to whales.
paragraphs: The Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District is a cultural center for whales established in the Jangsaengpo area of Nam-gu, Ulsan. It is a historical area where whales have inhabited since prehistoric times, and it is the only tourist district in Korea where visitors can comprehensively experience the history and culture related to whales. The district is home to various exhibition and experience facilities focused on whale ecology and whaling culture.

The main facility, the Jangsaengpo Whale Museum, displays various artifacts such as whale skeletons and whaling tools, while the Whale Ecology Experience Center is the first dolphin aquarium in Korea, allowing visitors to observe dolphins' daily lives. Additionally, to promote whale cultural tourism, the Whale Sea Tour Ship operates the only whale exploration cruise in Korea, allowing exploration of whales in the East Sea off Ulsan. The Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District highlights the relationship between whales and humans, establishing itself as a marine cultural space that integrates ecology, education, and tourism.

ja.title: 長生浦クジラ文化特区
ja.addr: 蔚山広域市 南区 長生浦クジラ路 244 (マエム洞)
ja.overview: 長生浦クジラ文化特区は、蔚山広域市 南区 長生浦一帯に整備されたクジラ文化の中心地です。先史時代からクジラが生息していた海域で、韓国で唯一クジラに関連する歴史と文化を総合的に体験できる観光特区です。特区内には、クジラの生態や捕鯨文化をテーマにした展示・体験施設が密集しています。代表施設である長生浦クジラ博物館では、クジラの骨格や捕鯨道具など様々な遺物が展示されており、クジラ生態体験館は国内初のイルカ水族館です。

en.title: Sinbulsan Waterfall Natural Recreation Forest
en.overview: Sinbulsan Waterfall Natural Recreation Forest is located at the foot of Sinbulsan Mountain (1,159m), the second highest peak of the Yeongnam Alps, boasting beautiful mountain scenery over 1,000 meters above sea level. The surrounding valleys are filled with bizarre rock formations and diverse tree species, preserving the mysteries of ancient times. The clear and clean valleys provide abundant water, allowing visitors to experience both mental and physical healing. Unlike other recreation forests in the country, it is divided into upper and lower recreation areas, with the upper area known for its slow-paced environment.
en.pull_quote: Sinbulsan Waterfall Natural Recreation Forest is located at the foot of Sinbulsan Mountain (1,159m), the second highest peak of the Yeongnam Alps, boasting beautiful mountain scenery over 1,000 meters above sea level.

The surrounding valleys are filled with bizarre rock formations and diverse tree species, preserving the mysteries of ancient times. The clear and clean valleys provide abundant water, allowing visitors to experience both mental and physical healing. Unlike other recreation forests in the country, it is divided into upper and lower recreation areas, with the upper area known for its slow-paced environment.

The upper recreation area features five log cabins and 16 guest rooms, serving as a base camp for easy exploration of the famous Eulalia grass fields at Ganjeolgot and Sinbulsan. It is also quieter and more comfortable due to the absence of passing vehicles. The lower recreation area has two guest houses with 18 rooms and two annexes, making it a popular summer retreat. A 30-minute walk leads to Pareuso Waterfall, known for its beautiful scenery.

en.title: Ilsan Beach (Ulsan)
en.overview: Adjacent to Daewangam Park, Ilsan Beach is an urban beach where you can enjoy stunning sea views during the day and beautiful nightscapes in the evening. Covering an area of 40,290㎡, with a length of 850m and a width of 42-61m, the beach has shallow waters and gentle slopes, making it perfect for family outings. The beach's Milky Way Plaza offers a resting area with soft lighting and a view of the sea, attracting many visitors year-round.
en.pull_quote: Adjacent to Daewangam Park, Ilsan Beach is an urban beach where you can enjoy stunning sea views during the day and beautiful nightscapes in the evening.
paragraphs: Adjacent to Daewangam Park, Ilsan Beach is an urban beach where you can enjoy stunning sea views during the day and beautiful nightscapes in the evening. Covering an area of 40,290㎡, with a length of 850m and a width of 42-61m, the beach has shallow waters and gentle slopes, making it perfect for family outings. The beach's Milky Way Plaza offers a resting area with soft lighting and a view of the sea, attracting many visitors year-round.

Every summer, various events such as the July Marine Festival and performances on a permanent stage in July and August provide diverse attractions and entertainment. Eopungdae, located in front of Ilsan Beach, was a place where kings of the Unified Silla period enjoyed leisure. From Eopungdae, you can overlook Daewangam Park, Minsum Island, and Ilsan Beach, feeling the ambiance of the kings.

en.title: Jinha Beach
en.overview: Located in Jinha-ri, Seosaeng-myeon, Ulju-gun, in southern Ulsan, Jinha Beach is the best beach in Ulsan. As you drive north along National Route 31, you will see the Ganjeolgot Lighthouse jutting out towards the sea, and beyond it lies Jinha Beach. Thanks to its slightly sheltered location facing north, Jinha Beach allows large waves to relax and calm down. The fine sandy beach stretches about 2km, with suitable water temperatures, making it a perfect summer retreat for visitors from all over the country.
en.pull_quote: Located in Jinha-ri, Seosaeng-myeon, Ulju-gun, in southern Ulsan, Jinha Beach is the best beach in Ulsan.
paragraphs: Located in Jinha-ri, Seosaeng-myeon, Ulju-gun, in southern Ulsan, Jinha Beach is the best beach in Ulsan. As you drive north along National Route 31, you will see the Ganjeolgot Lighthouse jutting out towards the sea, and beyond it lies Jinha Beach. Thanks to its slightly sheltered location facing north, Jinha Beach allows large waves to relax and calm down.

The fine sandy beach stretches about 2km, with suitable water temperatures, making it a perfect summer retreat for visitors from all over the country. Behind the sandy beach, a pine forest provides a dense shade, making it an excellent resting place to catch your breath after swimming. The beautiful islands of Ideokdo and Myeongseondo, with their pine forests and shallow waters, are ideal for family outings. ◎ Travel Information to Experience the Charm of Hallyu - This is the beach where the characters Seo-ha and Do-yoon, Ji-eum and Cho-won walked together in the drama.

en.title: Seongnamsa Temple (Ulsan)
en.overview: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The name Seongnamsa is derived from the fact that it is located south of Gajisan, which is also known as Seokmyeonsan. It is said that the monk Doi, who introduced Zen Buddhism to Korea during the reign of King Heondeok (the 41st king of Silla, 809-826 AD), discovered the site of Gajisan while searching for a sacred place.
en.pull_quote: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism.
paragraphs: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The name Seongnamsa is derived from the fact that it is located south of Gajisan, which is also known as Seokmyeonsan.

The monk Doi, who introduced Zen Buddhism to Korea during the reign of King Heondeok (the 41st king of Silla, 809-826 AD), discovered the site of Gajisan while searching for a sacred place and established the temple to pray for the protection of Silla. After several reconstructions, the temple was destroyed during the Imjin War but was rebuilt in 1674 (the 15th year of King Hyeonjong) with the support of the local governor. Over the years, the temple fell into disrepair but was restored again in 1912 by Monk Uun, only to be devastated during the Korean War.

en.pull_quote: Local recommended partner · Course linking nearby restaurants and safe accommodations
paragraphs: Yeongpyeongsa Temple is a traditional Buddhist temple located in Janggun-myeon, Sejong City, under the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. It features traditional buildings and three caves. The founder, Monk Hwanseong, aimed to create a place for the happiness of all beings and world peace.

Yeongpyeongsa is also famous for its double cherry blossoms and in autumn, the temple and surrounding areas are covered in white chrysanthemums. The Janggun Mountain Chrysanthemum Festival held every October has become a national festival, and the temple offers temple stay programs.

en.overview: Located within the Gokbok Reservoir Municipal Park in Yeonseomyeon, Sejong Special Self-Governing City, this park was established to commemorate the Yeongi Great Victory. A 10m high monument was erected in 1997, and the surrounding area has been developed into a park.

en.overview: Located near Jagcheonjeong and Amethyst Cave Country in Ulju-gun, Ulsan, this restaurant is famous for its pot lid chicken stew. The restaurant has dedicated parking for convenience.

en.title: Dongbu Bunsik
en.overview: Dongbu Bunsik is a famous kalguksu (knife-cut noodle) restaurant located in Unyang, Ulju-gun. It has a simple, rustic atmosphere like a countryside snack bar, run by local grandmothers in a cooperative format. Popular menu items include kalguksu, mulguksu (cold noodles), bibim guksu (spicy mixed noodles), and Unyang Hanwoo beef bulgogi kimbap. The kimbap is unique with the addition of minari (water parsley), giving it a fragrant twist. Nearby, Jinha Beach and Ganwolsan Mountain are great for a visit.

en.title: Samtaeyukgyeong Hwae Town
en.overview: Samtaeyukgyeong Hwae Town is named to express the intention of serving guests like the three ministers of the Joseon Dynasty. The sashimi fish is mainly sourced from Jeju Island, accompanied by various side dishes. In addition to the main dish of sashimi, grilled fish, steamed eggs, pancakes, shrimp tempura, gakkuk (noodle soup), tonkatsu, rice with fish roe, and spicy soup are also served. The restaurant is very spacious with well-arranged private rooms, allowing for a cozy dining experience. There is dedicated parking available in front of the restaurant and a little walk away in the alley. Nearby attractions include the Jangsaengpo Whale Museum and Seonam Lake Park, making it a great place to visit.

en.title: Yuldong Park
en.overview: Yuldong Park in Seongnam is a natural lake park designed to preserve nature as much as possible, featuring beautiful scenery with lawns, hills, and a lake. It was named Yuldong Park due to the abundance of chestnut trees since the Baekje period. The park includes the Cheongju Han Clan Munjeong Tombstone (Gyeonggi Cultural Heritage) and the 3.1 Movement Memorial Tower. Additionally, it offers a large open lawn for citizens and a 1.8 km lakeside walking path to enjoy the beauty of nature.
en.pull_quote: Yuldong Park in Seongnam is a natural lake park designed to preserve nature as much as possible, featuring beautiful scenery with lawns, hills, and a lake.
paragraphs: Yuldong Park in Seongnam is a natural lake park designed to preserve nature as much as possible, featuring beautiful scenery with lawns, hills, and a lake. It was named Yuldong Park due to the abundance of chestnut trees since the Baekje period.

The park includes the Cheongju Han Clan Munjeong Tombstone (Gyeonggi Cultural Heritage) and the 3.1 Movement Memorial Tower. Additionally, it offers a large open lawn for citizens and a 1.8 km lakeside walking path to enjoy the beauty of nature, a book-themed park encouraging voluntary reading, a children's playground, and a dog park, providing various relaxation spaces and tourist attractions.

en.title: Mangyeongam
en.overview: Mangyeongam, a traditional temple (No. 74), is located on the slopes of Yeongjangsan, offering the best view of Seoul from Seongnam. It is known as a place where kings visited from the late Goryeo to early Joseon periods to pray for the prosperity of the nation and the well-being of the people. At Mangyeongam, you can see the Mangyeongam Stone Buddha, designated as a Gyeonggi Cultural Heritage.

en.title: Hwahongmun (華虹門)
en.overview: At Hwaseong, the Suwoncheon River flows north and south, and floodgates were installed at the connecting parts of the fortress, with the northern floodgate called Buksumun and the southern floodgate called Namsumun. Hwahongmun is the northern floodgate of Hwaseong, featuring seven rainbow-shaped gates. Notably, the sizes of the seven gates differ, with the central gate being wider and larger than the side gates, effectively controlling rainfall. On the eastern hill of Hwahongmun, there is the beautifully constructed Banghwa Suiryujeong.

en.title: Gwanggyosan
en.overview: Gwanggyosan (582m above sea level) stretches about 2 km north and south between the Gyeongbu Expressway and the road connecting Seoul and Suwon, located in Sang Gwanggyo-dong, Suwon. The ridge of the mountain is very tranquil and gentle, surrounded by lush trees, making it a great place for forest bathing or a cozy day hike. Gwanggyosan protects Suwon from the cold winds coming from the north and is known as the main mountain of Suwon, originally named Gwangaksan, but was renamed Gwanggyosan by King Taejo of Goryeo.
en.pull_quote: Gwanggyosan (582m above sea level) stretches about 2 km north and south between the Gyeongbu Expressway and the road connecting Seoul and Suwon.
paragraphs: Gwanggyosan (582m above sea level) stretches about 2 km north and south between the Gyeongbu Expressway and the road connecting Seoul and Suwon, located in Sang Gwanggyo-dong, Suwon. The ridge of the mountain is very tranquil and gentle, surrounded by lush trees, making it a great place for forest bathing or a cozy day hike.

Gwanggyosan protects Suwon from the cold winds coming from the north and is known as the main mountain of Suwon, originally named Gwangaksan, but was renamed Gwanggyosan by King Taejo of Goryeo. Historically, Gwanggyosan has been considered one of the eight scenic spots of Suwon, with its beautiful scenery of snow-covered trees being the most celebrated among them. Until 1994, access was completely restricted during autumn (1 month) and spring (3 months) due to fire concerns, but since autumn 1995, it has been open year-round to provide a resting space for residents and expand leisure opportunities.

en.title: National Sejong Arboretum
en.overview: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city. Opened in October 2020, it is the second national arboretum following the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum, aimed at preserving and utilizing tree genetic resources by climate and vegetation types. The arboretum consists of three main areas: the Garden Exhibition Area, Plant Education Experience Area, and Community Participation Activity Area.
en.pull_quote: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city.
paragraphs: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city. Opened in October 2020, it is the second national arboretum following the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum, aimed at preserving and utilizing tree genetic resources by climate and vegetation types. The arboretum consists of three main areas: the Garden Exhibition Area, Plant Education Experience Area, and Community Participation Activity Area.

The Garden Exhibition Area consists of nine gardens, including a traditional Korean garden that embodies the beauty of Korean tradition, a bonsai garden, a wildflower garden, a maple garden, an amphibian observation area, an ecological forest, a clear stream garden, an iris garden, and a wall garden. The Plant Education Experience Area has 11 spaces designed for understanding and experiencing plants, including a folk plant garden, a four-season exhibition garden, a rare and specialty plant garden, a forest garden, a garden plant measuring area, a forest restoration garden, a healing garden, a hibiscus garden, a children's forest experience area, a pollinator garden, and a commemorative garden for the IFLA World Landscape Architects Congress.
The Community Participation Activity Area is designed for citizen participation and leisure activities.

ja.title: 国立セジョン樹木園
ja.addr: セジョン特別自治市 樹木園路136 (セジョン洞)
ja.overview: 国立セジョン樹木園は、韓国初の都市型国立樹木園です。政府セジョン庁舎に隣接しており、都市の中で自然を体験できる空間として整備されています。気候や植生タイプ別の樹木遺伝資源の保存と資源化を目的とした国家樹木園の拡充計画に基づき、国立白頭大干樹木園に続いて2020年10月に2番目にオープンしました。国立セジョン樹木園は、主に庭園展示観覧地区、植物教育体験地区、コミュニティ参加活動地区で構成されています。

庭園展示観覧地区は、韓国伝統庭園を含む9つの庭園で構成されています。盆栽園、野生花園、紅葉庭園、両生類観察園、生態林、清流庭園、アヤメ園、壁庭園が含まれています。植物教育体験地区は、植物に対する理解と体験を目的とした11のスペースで構成されています。民俗植物園、四季展示園、希少・特産植物園、森林庭園、庭園植物測定所、森林緑化園、癒しの庭、ムクゲ園、幼児森林体験園、ポリネーターガーデン、IFLA世界造園家大会記念庭園が含まれています。

en.title: Geumgang Pedestrian Bridge (Iung Bridge)
en.overview: The Geumgang Pedestrian Bridge (Iung Bridge) is a representative landmark of Sejong City, built as the first double-deck single-sided steel truss bridge in South Korea. Its unique design greatly enhances the urban landscape. The bridge embodies the concept of a 'fantastic time travel,' reflecting the imaginative urban structure of Sejong. The upper part of the bridge features rest and convenience facilities for pedestrians, along with various event and play experience areas, while the lower part includes a pleasant dedicated bicycle path ensuring safety for pedestrians and convenience for cyclists.

en.title: Geolpo Central Park
en.overview: Geolpo Central Park, located in Geolpo-dong, Gimpo City, is a representative relaxation park of Gimpo, established in 2006 with the theme of a cultural park that embodies Gimpo's history and future. Covering over 150,000㎡, it is home to 70,000 trees including pine and jujube trees, with walking paths and flower gardens themed as Flower Light Place, Water Light Place, and Star Light Place along the straight central path. In summer, the central water fountain square operates as a splash pad, and the Galaxy Forest waterfall serves as a water play area, loved by family visitors.
en.pull_quote: Local Recommended Partners · Nearby Restaurants · Safe Accommodation Link Course
paragraphs: Geolpo Central Park, located in Geolpo-dong, Gimpo City, is a representative relaxation park of Gimpo, established in 2006 with the theme of a cultural park that embodies Gimpo's history and future. Covering over 150,000㎡, it is home to 70,000 trees including pine and jujube trees, with walking paths and flower gardens themed as Flower Light Place, Water Light Place, and Star Light Place along the straight central path. en.pull_quote: Local Recommended Partners · Nearby Restaurants · Safe Accommodation Link Course
paragraphs: Hyoja Gang Yeong-cheon, a member of the Jinju Gang clan, lost his father at the age of three and lived with his widowed mother, Yeon-il Jeong. At the age of seven, his mother fell ill and became bedridden. Despite his young age, Yeong-cheon showed great filial piety. While caring for his sick mother, when her condition worsened and she lost consciousness, he broke his finger on the threshold to draw blood and let it flow into her mouth, collapsing.

His mother woke up to find her son bleeding and collapsed, and after careful nursing, he was able to wake up. The plaque hanging in front of the main gate reads, 'Hyoja Eobmugang Yeong-cheon Ji Mun-gak Gang Hee 39th Year Kyungjin March 15th Entry', indicating that this Hyoja Gate was built in the 26th year of King Sukjong (March 15, 1700). The original building was lost over nearly 290 years, and it was restored in 1987.

en.pull_quote: Gueunsa Temple, located in Sagok 2-ri, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon-gun, is a shrine dedicated to the nine scholars who...
paragraphs: Gueunsa Temple, located in Sagok 2-ri, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon-gun, is a shrine dedicated to the nine scholars who, in 1455 during the reign of King Danjong, retreated to the mountains due to their resentment over the usurpation of the throne by Suyang Daegun. These scholars (Kim Si-seup, Jo Sang-chi, Park Do, Park Jae, Park Gyu-son, Park Hyo-son, Park Cheon-son, Park In-son, Park Gye-son) dedicated their lives to the principles of integrity and loyalty.

The nine scholars lived in huts in the mountainous valleys of Geunnam-myeon, such as Yukdan-ri, Jamgok-ri, and Sagok-ri, focusing on agriculture while gathering to play Go and discuss worldly matters. However, as the times changed, they dispersed to various places. In the 9th year of King Injo's reign (1631), several scholars, including Lee Ji-yeon, gathered their intentions to build a shrine and held memorial ceremonies every spring and autumn. In 1865, during the Daewon-gun's order to abolish Confucian academies, the shrine faced destruction, but it was rebuilt in 1921 and restored again in 1977 with the help of local benefactors after being devastated during the Korean War.

en.title: Yongam-ri Prehistoric Site
en.addr: 1121 Yongam-ri, Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province
en.overview: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun. This site is formed on the alluvial plain of the upper reaches of the Bukhan River, winding around the areas of Wirari and Yongam-ri. Excavations conducted by the Gangwon Historical and Cultural Research Institute from 2001 to 2003 revealed over 230 remains, including 176 house sites, 32 burial pits, 14 pillar-supported buildings, and 11 earthen tombs, showcasing the highest density of Bronze Age remains in the country.
en.pull_quote: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun.
paragraphs: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun. This site is formed on the alluvial plain of the upper reaches of the Bukhan River, winding around the areas of Wirari and Yongam-ri. Excavations conducted by the Gangwon Historical and Cultural Research Institute from 2001 to 2003 revealed over 230 remains, including 176 house sites, 32 burial pits, 14 pillar-supported buildings, and 11 earthen tombs, showcasing the highest density of Bronze Age remains in the country.

The Bronze Age settlement formed in the Yongam-ri area is evaluated as a very important site that can shed light on the lifestyle and residential development of the Bronze Age in the Bukhan River basin, as well as the diffusion routes of Bronze Age culture, dating back to at least the 10th century BC to the 6th century BC. The site is also considered to have great preservation value as it is a rare village site in East Asia. A large quantity of stone tools, including chipped stone tools made from flakes, as well as various forms of stone axes and arrowheads, have been excavated. These stone tools exhibit complete or partially completed forms typical of Bronze Age remains.

paragraphs: ファチョンのヨンアム里先史遺跡は、江原特別自治道ファチョン郡ハナム面にある青銅器時代の大規模な村の遺跡です。この遺跡は、ウィラリとヨンアム里の周辺を流れる北漢江の上流の沖積平野に形成されており、2001年から2003年にかけて江原歴史文化研究所の発掘により、176の住居跡、32の埋葬穴、14の柱建物、11の土葬墓など230以上の遺構が発見され、国内最高の密度を示す青銅器時代の遺跡です。

ヨンアム里周辺に形成された青銅器時代の集落は、少なくとも紀元前10世紀から紀元前6世紀まで形成された集落であり、青銅器時代の北漢江流域の生活文化や居住発展の研究、青銅器文化の伝播経路を明らかにする非常に重要な遺跡と評価されており、東アジアでも稀な村の遺跡という点で保存価値が高いです。出土した遺物には、剥片の一部を加工した石器（剥片石器）が大量に出土し、さまざまな形の石斧や石矢じりなども出土しました。これらの石器は青銅器時代の遺跡に見られる完全な形や半分完成した形を示しています。

paragraphs: 华川的龙岩里史前遗址是位于江原特別自治道华川郡哈南面的青铜器时代大规模村落遗址。该遗址位于北汉江上游的冲积平原上，环绕着威拉里和龙岩里。2001年至2003年间，江原历史文化研究所的发掘结果显示，发现了176个房屋遗址、32个埋葬坑、14个柱子建筑和11个土葬墓等230多个遗迹，展示了国内青铜器时代遗迹的最高密度。
龙岩里地区形成的青铜器时代聚落被评估为非常重要的遗址，可以揭示北汉江流域青铜器时代的生活文化和居住发展历史，以及青铜器文化的传播路径，至少可以追溯到公元前10世纪到公元前6世纪。该遗址在东亚也是罕见的村落遗址，具有很高的保护价值。出土的文物中，大量的石器（剥片石器）和各种形状的石斧和石箭头也被发现。这些石器展示了青铜器时代遗址中出现的完整形态或部分完成的形态。

en.title: Baeknyeon Hanwoo
en.overview: Located in a narrow alley in Yangsan-dong, Gwangju, Baeknyeon Hanwoo is a premium Korean beef restaurant. It features a simple and stylish exterior, welcoming guests into a beautifully decorated Hanok-style interior with various seating options, including private rooms and spaces for group gatherings. They use only the highest quality Hanwoo beef, and their rib meat is layered with muscle and fat, providing exceptional taste and texture. The 'Flower Meat' (Salchisal) is known for its rich flavor, and they also offer various dishes like raw beef, octopus, and bibimbap.

paragraphs: Daejeon Solomon Law Park is a legal education theme park operated by the Ministry of Justice. It serves as a learning center for law and justice, where children, teenagers, and the general public can learn and experience the law in a fun and engaging way. The park offers various free legal experience and training programs for children, teenagers, and local citizens, allowing them to learn about the rule of law while having fun.

Just as King Solomon wisely realized justice through trials, Solomon Law Park allows citizens to experience and feel the freedom, wisdom, and justice of a law-governed society, helping them build the qualities and knowledge necessary for democratic citizenship. The legal experience center offers a broad understanding of the history of law worldwide and Korea's legal system, with facilities for legislative experiences, scientific investigations, mock trials, and prison experiences. There is also a 'Law Village' for preschool children, and various legal experience and training programs are provided to the public centered around the legal experience center and legal training center.

en.title: Uam Historical Park
en.overview: Uam Historical Park is an urban neighborhood park located in Dong-gu, Daejeon, where the great Confucian scholar Uam Song Si-yeol studied during the late Joseon Dynasty. From 1991 to 1997, buildings such as Jangpan-gak, a museum, and a Confucian academy were recreated, and it was reborn as a historical park on April 17, 1998. This park was established to honor and preserve the legacy of Uam Song Si-yeol, who flourished Confucian thought in this land during the late Joseon Dynasty. It contains historically significant cultural heritage, including Namganjeongsa, where Song Si-yeol taught his disciples in his later years, and Gikukjeong, known for its architectural beauty.

paragraphs: Located near Gyodong Intersection in Sokcho, New York Bakery Sokcho Branch is the oldest bakery in the area. It's so famous that no local resident is unaware of it. The somewhat shabby yet tidy exterior reflects the passion and dedication of the owner, who has been focused on baking for over 50 years. Upon entering the bakery, the enticing aroma of freshly baked bread stimulates your appetite.

If you're unsure about what to buy among the neatly arranged breads, the squid rice bread is highly recommended. The squid rice bread is the signature menu item of New York Bakery, which won a silver medal at the 2018 'Our Rice Bread Competition'. The dough is made by mixing flour and rice flour, filled with local specialties like squid, dried radish greens, and cheese, baked to perfection with a unique flavor. Above all, its nutty and chewy texture is exceptional, with a hint of spiciness that enhances its taste.

整然と並べられた数多くのパンの中で、何を買うべきか迷ったら、イカ米パンをお勧めします。イカ米パンは2018年の「私たちの米パン機能競技大会」で銀賞を受賞したニューヨークベーカリーの代表メニューです。小麦粉と米粉を混ぜた生地に、速川の特産品であるイカや干し大根、チーズなどを入れて焼き上げ、独特の風味を持っています。何よりも香ばしくてもちもちした食感が絶品で、ほんのりとした辛さが旨味を引き立てます。

en.title: Woljeongsa Temple Stay
en.overview: Woljeongsa is a thousand-year-old temple located on Odaesan Mountain, founded in 643 AD by the monk Jajangyulsa during the Silla Dynasty. The temple houses numerous national treasures, including an octagonal stone pagoda and a stone statue of a bodhisattva, and is famous for its beautiful path lined with over 1,700 towering fir trees. Woljeongsa offers year-round temple stays, providing an opportunity to experience the daily life of monks and learn about Korean Buddhist culture in a serene mountain setting. The temple stay program is divided into experiential and relaxation types.

The temple stay program is divided into experiential and relaxation types, with options available in English, Chinese, and Japanese.

The relaxation temple stay focuses on rest for two days and one night at the temple. Aside from meals, guests can enjoy free time walking along the fir tree path or meditating. The experiential temple stay involves participating in various programs over the weekend, focusing on rejuvenating the body and mind. Activities include meals at the temple, ceremonial prayers, making prayer beads, silent meditation, and tea time with monks. The prayer bead-making activity involves creating beads for each bow made during prayers.

en.title: Hoengseong Catholic Church
en.overview: This church showcases the modern church history of the Hoengseong area and the characteristics of post-war stone architecture. Originally, there was a chapel of Pungsuwon Catholic Church here, which was elevated to a parish in 1930, and a tiled wooden structure was built. After the original building was destroyed during the Korean War, the current stone church was constructed. The building features a Latin cross-shaped floor plan, and the interior mass space is designed as an auditorium without columns or walls.
en.pull_quote: This church showcases the modern church history of the Hoengseong area and the characteristics of post-war stone architecture.
paragraphs: This church showcases the modern church history of the Hoengseong area and the characteristics of post-war stone architecture. Originally, there was a chapel of Pungsuwon Catholic Church here, which was elevated to a parish in 1930, and a tiled wooden structure was built. After the original building was destroyed during the Korean War, the current stone church was constructed. The building features a Latin cross-shaped floor plan, and the interior mass space is designed as an auditorium without columns or walls.

The wooden truss above the main ceiling retains its original form from the time of construction. At the center of the front is an octagonal bell tower topped with a dome, housing a bell imported from France at the time of construction. Although the auxiliary buildings have changed several times, the exterior of the parish has mostly been preserved, showcasing the architectural style of the time. As a religious space where mass is still held, visitors should be mindful not to disturb the ceremonies and prayers of the congregation.

en.title: Donghae Marine Resource Center
en.overview: The Donghae Marine Resource Center, under the Korea Fisheries Resources Agency, works to preserve salmon, a key returning species along the East Coast, through breeding, nurturing, releasing, and creating natural spawning grounds. Over 70% of Korean salmon are born in the Namdaecheon River in Yangyang, where they grow for 3-4 years in the North Pacific before returning to spawn. However, due to river destruction, the number of returning salmon has decreased, prompting the center to perform artificial fertilization and hatch young salmon, which are then nurtured for about five months before being released into the Namdaecheon River.
en.pull_quote: The Donghae Marine Resource Center, under the Korea Fisheries Resources Agency, works to preserve salmon, a key returning species along the East Coast.
paragraphs: The Donghae Marine Resource Center, under the Korea Fisheries Resources Agency, works to preserve salmon, a key returning species along the East Coast, through breeding, nurturing, releasing, and creating natural spawning grounds. Over 70% of Korean salmon are born in the Namdaecheon River in Yangyang, where they grow for 3-4 years in the North Pacific before returning to spawn. However, due to river destruction, the number of returning salmon has decreased, prompting the center to perform artificial fertilization and hatch young salmon, which are then nurtured for about five months before being released into the Namdaecheon River.

The salmon ecology experience center within the facility provides detailed information about the hatching and growth process of salmon, as well as their returning routes. Visitors can observe young salmon that have hatched through artificial fertilization feeding and growing in the breeding facility. The center operates ecological experience programs, welcoming adult salmon in October-November and sending young salmon in February-March. Visitors have the opportunity to touch the returning salmon or release young salmon from a container into the river, allowing for close observation of their ecology.

paragraphs: 东海生物资源中心隶属于韩国水产资源公团，致力于保护东海岸的主要回归鱼种——鲑鱼，通过种苗培育、养殖、放流及自然产卵场的建设等项目。超过70%的韩国鲑鱼在位于杨阳的南大川出生，经过3-4年在北太平洋生长后返回南大川产卵。然而，由于河流破坏，回归的鲑鱼数量减少，因此中心进行人工授精，孵化的幼鱼在南大川放流前会养殖约五个月。
中心内设有鲑鱼生态体验馆，详细介绍鲑鱼的孵化和生长过程、回归路线等相关信息。游客可以观察通过人工授精孵化的幼鱼在养殖场中进食和生长的情况。中心在10月至11月迎接母鲑鱼，并在2月至3月进行幼鱼放流的生态体验项目。游客有机会触摸回归的鲑鱼，或将装在水桶里的幼鱼放入河中，近距离观察鲑鱼的生态。

en.title: Matdrin
en.overview: Matdrin is a restaurant specializing in soft tofu stew and potato dishes, located near Ojukheon in Gangneung City, Gangwon Province. The main menu includes Matdrin Potato Soup, Soft Tofu Potato Soup, and Soft Tofu Bone Noodle Soup. Other popular dishes include beef small intestine hot pot and octopus small intestine hot pot. The broth, simmered with bones, is great for hangovers when served with plenty of bean sprouts. The pickled radish served as a side dish is delicious, and the crunchy napa cabbage salad is a special treat. All side dishes, including soft tofu, are available at a self-serve bar for convenience.

en.title: Myeongseongok
en.overview: Myeongseongok is an old restaurant specializing in seolleongtang (ox bone soup) and oxtail soup located in Noam-dong, Gangneung City. It is a great place to visit when craving something warm, housed in a remodeled traditional Korean house. The exterior retains the style of an old improved hanok, while the interior has been transformed into a spacious dining area. The rich broth is filled with generous portions of meat, making it a delicacy when served with rice and pickled radish. Side dishes include napa cabbage kimchi, pickled radish, and soy sauce pickled radish, which pair well with seolleongtang or oxtail soup. The noodles served with seolleongtang are presented separately, allowing for personal preference.

en.title: Chungju Sangdae Village
en.overview: Located in the heart of the Korean Peninsula, Sangdae Village in Jidang-ri, Angseong-myeon, Chungju, is a historically rich area. Once known as Jijang-ri, this mountain basin village has a deep history, having been part of the Mahan territory during the Three Han period and a battleground during the Three Kingdoms era. The only existing Goguryeo stele, the Jungwon Goguryeo Stele, is located east of the village.
en.pull_quote: Located in the heart of the Korean Peninsula, Sangdae Village in Jidang-ri, Angseong-myeon, Chungju, is a historically rich area.
paragraphs: Located in the heart of the Korean Peninsula, Sangdae Village in Jidang-ri, Angseong-myeon, Chungju, is a historically rich area. Once known as Jijang-ri, this mountain basin village has a deep history, having been part of the Mahan territory during the Three Han period and a battleground during the Three Kingdoms era. The only existing Goguryeo stele, the Jungwon Goguryeo Stele, is located east of the village.

Sangdae Village is famous for its production of Cheongdo peaches and is home to many skilled artisans. Here, traditional crafts such as straw weaving, willow crafts, and wood crafts are preserved, along with traditional songs and liquors. Seasonal festivals like the Peach Blossom Festival in spring, the Starry Night Film Festival in summer, and the Mountain Music Concert in winter bring vitality to the village.

zh.overview: 忠州相对村位于朝鲜半岛的中心，历史悠久。这个山间村庄曾被称为地藏里，三韩时期是马韩的领土，三国时期则是激烈的领土争夺战的地方。村东有唯一现存的高句丽碑——中原高句丽碑。
zh.pull_quote: 忠州相对村位于朝鲜半岛的中心，历史悠久。

相对村以其清道桃的生产而闻名，村里有许多手艺人。这里保留了传统工艺品、农歌和传统酒，并可以进行体验。此外，春天会举行桃花节，夏天有星空电影节，冬天则有山间音乐会，给村庄带来了生机。

en.title: Bonghwanggyeong (Neungamri Island)
en.overview: Bonghwanggyeong is the 7th scenic spot of the Han River and is a great place for nature learning and walking trails. It is home to various migratory birds, including mandarin ducks and swans. The area features beautiful reed beds and is a popular spot for photographers. Visitors can enjoy the wild bird sanctuary via the waterfront walking path and admire the views from the observation deck.
en.pull_quote: Bonghwanggyeong is the 7th scenic spot of the Han River and is a great place for nature learning and walking trails.
paragraphs: Bonghwanggyeong is the 7th scenic spot of the Han River and is a great place for nature learning and walking trails. It is home to various migratory birds, including mandarin ducks and swans.

The area features beautiful reed beds and is a popular spot for photographers. Visitors can enjoy the wild bird sanctuary via the waterfront walking path and admire the views from the observation deck. The area includes a grassy plaza, bike paths, levee roads, and a youth camping site, along with a recreation area and observation deck.

ja.title: 鳳凰景（ヌンアムリ島）
ja.region_label: 忠北 忠州市 中央塔面
ja.addr: 忠北 忠州市 中央塔面 カフン里 720
ja.overview: 鳳凰景は漢江の八景の一つで、自然学習場と散策路に適した場所です。様々な種類の渡り鳥が生息しており、マンダリンダックやコハクチョウも見ることができます。さらに、渡り鳥と共に水草や葦の群生が美しい景観を作り、多くの写真家が訪れるスポットです。水辺の散策路を通じて野生鳥類観察ができ、展望台からは葦の森や松林、渡り鳥の飛翔を楽しむことができます。

zh.addr: 忠北 忠州市 中央塔面 加兴里 720
zh.overview: 凤凰景是汉江八景之一，是一个适合自然学习和散步的小径。这里栖息着多种候鸟，包括鸳鸯和大天鹅。与候鸟一起，水草和芦苇丛形成了美丽的景观，吸引了许多摄影师。游客可以通过水边步道观察野生鸟类，并从观景台欣赏芦苇林、松树林和候鸟的飞翔。

en.title: Jecheon Siraekguk
en.overview: Jecheon Siraekguk is located in Hwasan-dong, Jecheon City, Chungcheongbuk-do. It was featured on the TV Chosun program 'Food Traveler Heo Young-man's White Rice Journey'. The restaurant has a nostalgic atmosphere with a well-preserved exterior. The signature dishes include Siraekguk (dried radish soup) and Siraekbap (dried radish rice). The restaurant is also popular for its egg rolls and baked eggs.
en.pull_quote: Signature Dish: Siraekbap
paragraphs: Jecheon Siraekguk is located in Hwasan-dong, Jecheon City, Chungcheongbuk-do. It was featured on the TV Chosun program 'Food Traveler Heo Young-man's White Rice Journey'. The restaurant has a nostalgic atmosphere with a well-preserved exterior. The signature dishes include Siraekguk (dried radish soup) and Siraekbap (dried radish rice).

The Siraekguk served with rice is also very popular. Other favorites include egg rolls and baked eggs. They also offer takeout and delivery for their Siraek, pickled vegetables, and natural vinegar. The restaurant is conveniently located near Jecheon IC, with attractions like Uirimji and Gyodong Folk Village nearby.

en.overview: Geumgang Restaurant, located in Yeongchun-myeon, Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, has been serving customers since 1979. The menu includes Deodeok Baekban (deodeok set meal), Sanchae Bibimjaengban Naengmyeon (mixed mountain vegetable cold noodles), Sanchae Bibimbap, and Acorn Jelly Rice. en.title: Deoklim Mountain Vegetable Restaurant
en.overview: Located next to a small parking lot at the entrance of Sokrisan, this restaurant features a tiled roof and offers dishes made from wild vegetables and mushrooms harvested directly from Sokrisan. The menu includes Sanchae Jeongsik (mountain vegetable set meal), Deodeok Gui Jeongsik (grilled deodeok set meal), Mushroom Stew Jeongsik, Sanchae Bulbaek Jeongsik, Bibimbap, and Seafood Pancakes, available for orders of two or more. The main entrance is easily accessible, and outdoor tables allow diners to enjoy the fresh mountain air. Nearby attractions include Sokrisan Sculpture Park, Oligil, and Beopjusa Temple.

en.title: Palbongsan Mountain (Seosan)
en.overview: Palbongsan Mountain is located on the western side of the Taean Peninsula. Although it is not very high, it appears to rise prominently due to its location in the lowlands of the west coast. The mountain's shape resembles a folding screen and rises regularly, embracing the village. The name 'Palbongsan' comes from the eight peaks that line up, and there is a legend that the smallest peak cried out for not being included every December.

ja.title: パルボンサン（西山）

en.title: Seosan Haemi Eupseong Zelkova Tree
en.overview: In front of the southern Jin-nam gate of Haemi Eupseong, there is a large zelkova tree estimated to be around 300 years old. Locally, it is also called 'Hoya Tree'. In the late Joseon period, there was a prison behind the tree where persecuted Catholic believers were held, and between 1790 and 1880, those imprisoned were tortured by being hung from branches extending to the east of this tree. Recognized for its historical significance, it was designated as a cultural asset of Chungcheongnam-do in 2008.
en.pull_quote: Local Recommended Partner · Nearby Restaurants and Safe Accommodation Courses
paragraphs: In front of the southern Jin-nam gate of Haemi Eupseong, there is a large zelkova tree estimated to be around 300 years old. Locally, it is also called 'Hoya Tree'.

In the late Joseon period, there was a prison behind the tree where persecuted Catholic believers were held, and between 1790 and 1880, those imprisoned were tortured by being hung from branches extending to the east of this tree. Recognized for its historical significance, it was designated as a cultural asset of Chungcheongnam-do in 2008.

Meanwhile, the eastern branch was broken by a storm in the 1940s, and the middle trunk was broken on June 26, 1969, but it has been protected and managed through several surgeries and soil improvement. Haemi Eupseong also preserves various old buildings such as the inner house, eastern government office, and guesthouse. Nearby, there are also Haemi Martyrdom Site (Yeosutgol), Haemi Confucian School, Haemi Eupseong Historical Camping Site, and Haemi Market. Additionally, the Seosan Aramegil and Haemi International Sacred Site paths pass through, making it a good idea to combine these for sightseeing.

en.title: Poamsan Mountain (Chungju)
en.overview: Poamsan, recognized as one of the 'Five Great Mountains of Joryeong' along with nearby Wolaksan, Juhulsan, and Joryeongsan, is located within Wolaksan National Park, marking the boundary between Chungju's Sangmo-myeon and Mungyeong in Gyeongsangbuk-do. It lies on the main ridge of the Baekdudaegan mountain range and connects to Wulhang Sam Bong via Haneuljae. Historically known as Hanheollyeong, Haneuljae served as a vital transportation route connecting the north and south of the Korean Peninsula until the Joryeong Gate was opened during the Joseon Dynasty.
en.pull_quote: Local recommended partner · Course linked with nearby restaurants and safe accommodations
paragraphs: Poamsan, recognized as one of the 'Five Great Mountains of Joryeong' along with nearby Wolaksan, Juhulsan, and Joryeongsan, is located within Wolaksan National Park, marking the boundary between Chungju's Sangmo-myeon and Mungyeong in Gyeongsangbuk-do. It lies on the main ridge of the Baekdudaegan mountain range and connects to Wulhang Sam Bong via Haneuljae. Historically known as Hanheollyeong, Haneuljae served as a vital transportation route connecting the north and south of the Korean Peninsula until the Joryeong Gate was opened during the Joseon Dynasty. Additionally, Mireuksaji, located below Haneuljae, is a significant temple site established during the early Goryeo period, flanked by Sinseonbong and Poamsan, with Wolaksan as the main mountain.

Poamsan features a unique combination of valley and ridge hiking. Most trails start from the Mireuksaji parking lot, passing through Haneuljae to the summit of Poamsan, leading to Mansubong and Yongambong. In Mansugol Valley, visitors can dip their feet in the stream, providing a refreshing break. The rocky paths are well-maintained, with wooden steps in some areas, though it can be crowded with hikers.

ja.title: ポアム山（忠州）
ja.region_label: 忠清北道 忠州市 水安堡面
ja.addr: 忠清北道 忠州市 水安堡面 ミルクサジギル
ja.overview: ポアム山は、近くの月岳山、周瑚山、鳥嶺山と共に「鳥嶺五岳」として知られ、月岳山国立公園内に位置し、忠州市の上毛面と慶尚北道の聞慶市の境界を形成しています。また、白頭大幹の主脊上にあり、ハヌルジェを境に月航三峰と接続しています。この地のハヌルジェは元々ハンファンリョンと呼ばれ、朝鮮時代に鳥嶺の関門が開かれるまで、朝鮮半島の南北を結ぶ重要な交通路としての役割を果たしていました。

en.pull_quote: Local recommended partner · Course linked with nearby restaurants and safe accommodations
paragraphs: A small path lies to the left just past the three-story stone pagoda in Mireuk-ri, Wolaksan. This path opens up to a refreshing breeze under the clear sky, surrounded by picturesque scenery of yellow pines, oak trees, and sea pines. Known as 'Haneuljae', the path leads down to a ditch that sometimes dries up due to drought, but is adorned with beautiful wildflowers like pink water lilies, deep purple swamp flowers, and yellow straw flowers. Although named Haneuljae (525m above sea level) as if it touches the sky, it is not particularly high.

Haneuljae serves as a boundary connecting Mireuk-ri in Chungju and Gwanum-ri in Mungyeong, taking about 30-40 minutes (2km) to walk from Mireuk-ri to Gwanum-ri. The rugged unpaved road leads to a smooth asphalt road at the top of Haneuljae, where the western peak of Daemisan (1,115m above sea level) comes into view. Additionally, the old temple site of Jungwon Mireuk-ri, believed to have been established during the late Silla to early Goryeo period, is located below Haneuljae.

The mountain and valley create a beautiful scenery that changes with the seasons, making it a perfect spot for a peaceful hike. At the summit, there is Boryeonsan Fortress, also known as Bonghwangseong or Cheonryongseong, built with earth and stones along the ridge.

At the summit, there is Boryeonsan Fortress, also known as Bonghwangseong or Cheonryongseong, built with earth and stones along the ridge. The gentle sloping paths are covered with thick fallen leaves, creating a soft carpet-like feel, while some steep sections can be challenging to climb.

In spring, the summit is adorned with a vast field of azaleas. The steep slopes on both sides of the main ridge from the summit to Hanamchi and Dongmak Pass are home to clusters of Quercus acutissima and Quercus variabilis, along with various tree species such as cherry trees, ash trees, camellias, ginger trees, yellow jujube trees, azaleas, and poison ivy, each showcasing their unique beauty. en.title: Angseong Hot Spring Area
en.overview: The Angseong Hot Spring Area is a large carbonated hot spring town located in the vicinity of Donsan-ri and Neungam-ri in Angseong-myeon, Chungju. The hot spring water, sourced from over 700m underground, has a relatively low temperature of 25-38 degrees Celsius, necessitating additional hot baths. Along the roadside, there are 7-8 hot spring baths, and every year, the 'Yangseong Carbonated Hot Spring Resort Festival' is held to promote the excellence of the carbonated hot spring water. Additionally, Chungju City has developed parks and facilities to enhance the development of the Angseong Hot Spring Area.

en.title: Mokgye Solbat (Chungju)
en.overview: Located below the village of Zhoune in Jangcheon-ri, Gagum-myeon, Chungju, Mokgye Solbat is an area of pine trees, historically known as Mokgye Naru. This area features 100-200 year-old pine trees and serves as a resting spot for vacationers during the summer. It is a 3,800-pyeong forest composed solely of pine trees, designated as a protected area by Chungju City. Mokgye Naru has a legend associated with it, one of which states that it became a significant inland waterway during the Joseon Dynasty.
en.pull_quote: Located below the village of Zhoune in Jangcheon-ri, Gagum-myeon, Chungju, Mokgye Solbat is an area of pine trees, historically known as Mokgye Naru. This area features 100-200 year-old pine trees and serves as a resting spot for vacationers during the summer...
paragraphs: Located below the village of Zhoune in Jangcheon-ri, Gagum-myeon, Chungju, Mokgye Solbat is an area of pine trees, historically known as Mokgye Naru. This area features 100-200 year-old pine trees and serves as a resting spot for vacationers during the summer. It is a 3,800-pyeong forest composed solely of pine trees, designated as a protected area by Chungju City. Mokgye Naru has a legend associated with it, one of which states that it became a significant inland waterway during the Joseon Dynasty.

However, Mokgye Naru suffered from major fires every year, causing significant damage. In search of a solution to these fires, a geomancer visited the area and suggested a method to redirect the waterway. The villagers transported soil from the river's center to create a mound, successfully redirecting the river towards Mokgye after more than six months, and planted many pine trees on that mound. This is how the Mokgye Solbat came to be.

しかし、モッキョナリは毎年大火災が発生し、甚大な被害を受けました。これらの火災を克服するために、風水師がこの地を訪れ、水の流れを変える方法を教えてくれました。村人たちは川の真ん中から土を運び、山を作りました。半年以上かけて川の水をモッキョの方に向けることに成功し、その山には多くの松の木を植えました。これが今日のモッキョソルバットの由来です。

然而，木溪渡口每年都会发生大火，造成严重损失。为了克服这些火灾，一位风水师来到这里，告诉村民们改变水流的方法。村民们将河中心的土运来堆成山，经过半年多的努力，成功将河水引向木溪，并在那座山上种植了许多松树。这就是今天的木溪松林的由来。

en.title: Samgilpo Port
en.overview: Located at the northern tip of the Taean Peninsula, Samgilpo Port is the largest harbor among several along the Daehwa Embankment. It attracts many tourists from surrounding areas and the capital region. While the taste of sashimi prepared on the spot from fishing boats may be unmatched, the flavor of sashimi made from freshly caught fish offers a unique delight only found at the western sea ports. This area is particularly known for its abundance of black sea bream, which thrive in the brackish waters where seawater and freshwater meet.

It attracts many tourists from surrounding areas and the capital region. While the taste of sashimi prepared on the spot from fishing boats may be unmatched, the flavor of sashimi made from freshly caught fish offers a unique delight only found at the western sea ports. This area is particularly known for its abundance of black sea bream, which thrive in the brackish waters where seawater and freshwater meet.

Along the coastal road connected to the harbor, there are various sashimi restaurants where you can enjoy meals while taking in the scenery. Additionally, the Daehwa Embankment is known as a paradise for winter migratory birds, attracting numerous birds during the winter, creating a spectacular sight. This location is also the starting point of the Seosan Arame-gil Samgil Naru-gil (hiking trail, cherry blossom road), making it a great option for combined tourism. Furthermore, across the Daehwa Embankment, you can find Dobido Port, and the western sea features the Nanjido Island.

en.title: Buyeo Garim Fortress
en.overview: Garim Fortress is a mountain fortress built on Seongheung Mountain (260.1m) in the southern part of Buyeo-gun. It is strategically located between Buyeo's Sabiseong Fortress and the mouth of the Geumgang River, believed to have been constructed by King Dongseong of Baekje to protect Sabiseong. The parking lot below the fortress is only about 200m from the South Gate, making it relatively easy to enjoy the fortress's scenic views. There is also a memorial hall dedicated to those who participated in the Baekje Restoration Movement.

en.title: Birthplace of Lee Sang-jae
en.overview: This is the site of the birthplace of Lee Sang-jae (1850-1927), a social activist during the late Joseon Dynasty. Lee Sang-jae joined Christianity early on and worked to awaken the national spirit through faith movements. In the 18th year of Gojong's reign (1881), he visited Japan as a member of the Shin Sa Yu Ramdan and returned to serve as the secretary to the U.S. envoy Park Jeong-yang in the 25th year of Gojong's reign (1888). After returning from the U.S., he felt a strong need for new civilization and organized the Independence Association with Seo Jae-pil in the 2nd year of Gwangmu (1898) to lead the enlightenment of the people.
en.pull_quote: This is the site of the birthplace of Lee Sang-jae (1850-1927), a social activist during the late Joseon Dynasty. Lee Sang-jae joined Christianity early on and worked to awaken the national spirit through faith movements.
paragraphs: This is the site of the birthplace of Lee Sang-jae (1850-1927), a social activist during the late Joseon Dynasty. Lee Sang-jae joined Christianity early on and worked to awaken the national spirit through faith movements. In the 18th year of Gojong's reign (1881), he visited Japan as a member of the Shin Sa Yu Ramdan and returned to serve as the secretary to the U.S. envoy Park Jeong-yang in the 25th year of Gojong's reign (1888). After returning from the U.S., he felt a strong need for new civilization and organized the Independence Association with Seo Jae-pil in the 2nd year of Gwangmu (1898) to lead the enlightenment of the people.

In 1927, when the nationalist and socialist factions formed a united front to organize the New Korean Association with the goal of fighting against Japan, he was elected as the founding president. His works include the essay collections 'Young People' and 'The Foundation of the Nation for Young People'. The teacher's birthplace is a thatched house with an anchae (main house) and sarangchae (guest house), consisting of four rooms in the front and two on the side, with a gate featuring a raised design. The main house was built around 1800, and the guest house was constructed around 1926, but the original building was destroyed in 1955, and the current structure was restored in 1972 and 1980.

en.title: Shinseongni Reed Field
en.overview: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea. It has been used as a filming location for various movies and dramas, including 'Joint Security Area (JSA)' and 'Kingdom', due to its beautiful scenery. The sunlight shimmering on the waves of the Geumgang River creates a mystical harmony, and in winter, it serves as a habitat for migratory birds such as swans and teal, making it a popular spot for nature study and photography.
en.pull_quote: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea.
paragraphs: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea. It has been used as a filming location for various movies and dramas, including 'Joint Security Area (JSA)' and 'Kingdom', due to its beautiful scenery. The sunlight shimmering on the waves of the Geumgang River creates a mystical harmony, and in winter, it serves as a habitat for migratory birds such as swans and teal, making it a popular spot for nature study and photography.

In particular, since the completion of the Geumgang River embankment in 1990, a large freshwater lake has been created nearby, attracting even more winter migratory birds. The reed field also showcases different colors and charms in each season, and it's delightful to experience the subtly different sounds of the reeds in the wind throughout the year. Observing the reed crab, which lives in the reed field, adds another layer of enjoyment. At the entrance, there is a reed experience center where you can learn more about reeds and the history and uses of the reed fields that were once much larger before agricultural land development.

en.title: Jangchun Dakgaejang
en.overview: Jangchun Dakgaejang is a specialty restaurant for dakgaejang (spicy chicken soup) located in Wondang-dong, Dangjin City, Chungcheongnam-do. Known for its single menu item, the dakgaejang is made with chicken, green onions, and bracken, resulting in a rich and spicy broth. Side dishes include baek-kimchi (white kimchi) and radish salad, served in a way that allows you to help yourself. They also offer refills for the broth if needed. Opening early in the morning, it attracts both locals and travelers looking for breakfast.

en.title: Hanwoo Ga Joheun Nal
en.overview: Hanwoo Ga Joheun Nal is located in Deokji-ri, Eumbong-myeon, Asan City, Chungcheongnam-do. Built in a traditional hanok style, it features a charming and vintage interior. The restaurant has group seating available, making it suitable for gatherings. Their signature dishes include various grilled Hanwoo beef cuts such as rib, sirloin, and eye of round. Hanwoo marinated grilled beef and raw beef sashimi are also very popular. Meal options include galbitang (beef rib soup), bibimbap with raw beef, beef soup, Hamheung cold noodles, and soybean paste stew.

en.title: Deoksune Garibi No. 1
en.overview: Deoksune Garibi No. 1 is a clam specialty restaurant located in Dokgo-ri, Daesan-eup, Seosan City, Chungcheongnam-do. The exterior shows signs of age, and the interior resembles a traditional street food stall. Their signature dishes include steamed clams and grilled clams, with seasoned grilled giant clams being a popular choice. The fun of grilling fresh ingredients on the grill is a highlight. They also serve eel, conch, sashimi, and seasoned flatfish. Noodle dishes include seafood ramen and seafood kalguksu (knife-cut noodles).

The exterior shows signs of age, and the interior resembles a traditional street food stall. Their signature dishes include steamed clams and grilled clams, with seasoned grilled giant clams being a popular choice.

The fun of grilling fresh ingredients on the grill is a highlight. They also serve eel, conch, sashimi, and seasoned flatfish. Noodle dishes include seafood ramen and seafood kalguksu (knife-cut noodles). Conveniently located near Seosan IC, it is close to Hwanggeumsan and Beolcheonpo Beach.

en.title: Nunggil Village, Jinan
en.overview: Nunggil Village is located in Nunggeum-ri, Donghyang-myeon, Jinan-gun. Originally part of Yongdam-gun's Idong-myeon, it was incorporated into Donghyang-myeon after the administrative merger in 1914. The village is named Nunggil, meaning 'prosperous village.' In 2002, it was designated as a green rural experience village, leading to the development of various facilities.

en.title: Deogyusan National Park (Main Office, Jeoksang Branch)
en.overview: Deogyusan was designated as the 10th national park in South Korea in 1975, alongside Odaesan. It is a prominent mountain formed in the center of the Sobaek Mountains, which branch off from the Taebaek Mountains. Deogyusan spans across Jeollabuk-do Muju and Jangsu, as well as Gyeongsangnam-do Geochang and Hamyang, with its highest peak, Hyangjeokbong, reaching 1,614 meters.

paragraphs: Deogyusan was designated as the 10th national park in South Korea in 1975, alongside Odaesan. It is a prominent mountain formed in the center of the Sobaek Mountains, which branch off from the Taebaek Mountains. Deogyusan spans across Jeollabuk-do Muju and Jangsu, as well as Gyeongsangnam-do Geochang and Hamyang, with its highest peak, Hyangjeokbong, reaching 1,614 meters.

The Gucheondong Valley, known for its 13 platforms, over 10 ponds, and 20 waterfalls, represents the beauty of Deogyusan, which has been celebrated since ancient times. The main peak, Hyangjeokbong, is surrounded by majestic ridges stretching over 30 kilometers to the southwest.

en.title: Maisan Provincial Park
en.overview: Maisan is a mountain formed from sedimentary layers that were lithified due to geological activity during the Late Cretaceous period. It is located at the boundary of Danyang-ri in Jinan-eup and Dongchon-ri in Mayang-myeon, about 32 km east of Jeonju, and serves as the center of the Geumgang and Seomjin River watersheds.

It is located at the boundary of Danyang-ri in Jinan-eup and Dongchon-ri in Mayang-myeon, about 32 km east of Jeonju, and serves as the center of the Geumgang and Seomjin River watersheds.
The mountain consists of two peaks, Ammaisan (687.4m) and Sumaesan (681.1m), along with over ten smaller peaks. Depending on the season, the mountain is referred to by four different names.

ja.title: クムダンサ（ジナン）
ja.region_label: 全北 ジナン郡 マリョン面

en.overview: Hyoja Imok Mountain Jeongnyeogak features a gabled roof with one room on both the front and sides. Inside, there is an inscribed stone tablet and five plaques related to its restoration. To the west of this structure is a stone tablet erected in 1990.

en.title: Yongamsa (Jangsu)
en.overview: Yongamsa, located in Chunsong-ri, Cheoncheon-myeon, Jangsu-gun, is a shrine dedicated to five Confucian scholars from the early Joseon period, including Anseong. It was established in 1818 and, like other Confucian academies, was demolished in 1871 but was rebuilt in 1946.

en.title: Buan Hyanggyo
en.addr: 25 Hyanggyo-gil, Buan-eup, Buan-gun, Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province
en.overview: Hyanggyo is a national educational institution established during the Joseon Dynasty to honor the spirits of great Confucian scholars and to educate and enlighten local residents. en.title: Jinan Eunsusa Cheongsil Pear Tree
en.addr: Dongchon-ri, Maryeong-myeon, Jinan-gun, Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province
en.overview: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains. The leaves are oval-shaped with serrated edges, and both sides are hairless and firm. The fruit is brown or green and ripens to yellow in the fall. The Cheongsil pear tree growing in the Eunsusa Temple in Jinan is estimated to be over 640 years old. The tree has a unique appearance, with a large trunk splitting into four branches at the top, supporting the upper part.
en.pull_quote: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains.
paragraphs: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains. The leaves are oval-shaped with serrated edges, and both sides are hairless and firm. The fruit is brown or green and ripens to yellow in the fall. The Cheongsil pear tree growing in the Eunsusa Temple in Jinan is estimated to be over 640 years old.

The tree has a unique appearance, with a large trunk splitting into four branches at the top, supporting the upper part. This area is influenced by the terrain, and when the wind blows, the firm leaves of the Cheongsil pear tree shake and create an indescribable sound. Additionally, in winter, if water is placed next to the base of the Cheongsil pear tree, icicles can form upside down towards the tips of the branches. The Cheongsil pear tree is a native Korean species, and there are not many left today, making large trees especially rare and designated as a natural monument. The Eunsusa Cheongsil pear tree is currently surrounded by a fence, with an information sign installed nearby.

While you can enjoy various cuts of pork like brisket and fresh pork belly, the pork bulgogi set with generous portions of meat and vegetables is particularly famous among locals. When you order, you'll be served a variety of side dishes including spicy octopus sauce, steamed eggs, fresh kimchi, and perilla leaves.
en.pull_quote: Signature Dishes: Brisket, Fresh Pork Belly, Pork Bulgogi, Thinly Sliced Pork Belly, and Nurungji.
paragraphs: Located near the Gunsan Arts Center in Jikok-dong, Gunsan, Tosilbaegi is a traditional restaurant that exudes the charm of a long-standing eatery. While you can enjoy various cuts of pork like brisket and fresh pork belly, the pork bulgogi set with generous portions of meat and vegetables is particularly famous among locals.

When you order, you'll be served a variety of side dishes including spicy octopus sauce, steamed eggs, fresh kimchi, and perilla leaves. The rich soybean paste stew is a highlight, and during weekdays, the restaurant can get quite busy with office workers. There is no dedicated parking, so it's best to use nearby alleys. en.title: Sarangori

paragraphs: Sarangori, located at the entrance of the National Jeonju Museum in Hyojadong, Jeonju, specializes in duck dishes using eco-friendly domestic ducks. Parking is available in front of the restaurant.

en.title: Seosu Haejangguk
en.overview: Seosu Haejangguk is a restaurant in Seosu-myeon, Gunsan, known for its beef head soup and yukhoe (raw beef sashimi). Located in a quiet rural area, it offers convenient parking. Although it is set up in a container, the restaurant has both table and floor seating, and the interior is clean. True to its reputation as a Gunsan eatery, it serves only two confident menu items: beef head soup with a clear and clean broth filled with meat, and hanwoo yukhoe.
en.pull_quote: Signature Dishes: Beef Head Soup, Yukhoe, Rice, etc.
paragraphs: Seosu Haejangguk is a restaurant in Seosu-myeon, Gunsan, known for its beef head soup and yukhoe (raw beef sashimi). Located in a quiet rural area, it offers convenient parking. Although it is set up in a container, the restaurant has both table and floor seating, and the interior is clean. True to its reputation as a Gunsan eatery, it serves only two confident menu items: beef head soup with a clear and clean broth filled with meat, and hanwoo yukhoe.

The beef head soup is tender and the yukhoe is fresh. Compared to other restaurants, it opens early and closes early. It may close earlier if the prepared ingredients run out, and since the yukhoe is limited in quantity, it's best to visit early in the morning. It has been featured in educational programs.

en.title: Gu Jeomangjoon House
en.overview: Gu Jeomangjoon House is a seafood and fish restaurant located in Docheong-ri, Byeonsan-myeon, Buan, famous for its clams. The signature dish is clam porridge, which has a delightful texture and a subtle aroma, making it a delicacy. You can also enjoy clam soup and clam kalguksu (noodle soup). The side dishes, including napa cabbage kimchi, onion kimchi, and mustard leaf kimchi, are exceptional. en.title: Gocheonamho (Migratory Bird Habitat)
en.addr: Gocheonam-ro, Hwangsan-myeon, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
en.overview: Gocheonamho is the largest reed habitat in South Korea. The Gocheonam reed fields host rare birds such as the black stork and eagles, as well as 90% of the world's migratory swans that perform spectacular dances during winter. A total of 54 bird species (excluding unidentified species) have been observed, making it the largest migratory bird habitat in the country, with 33 species of waterfowl, 5 species of raptors, and 16 other bird species.
