en.title: Royal Family's Stroll
en.overview: The 'Royal Family's Stroll', a traditional cultural event you can experience before departure at Incheon International Airport, recreates Joseon Dynasty royal court life. At Terminal 1, the king and queen are reenacted strolling through the palace. At Terminal 2, a royal procession of the king and military officers is reenacted at the late Joseon martial arts exhibition hall. After the event, visitors can take commemorative photos with performers wearing royal court costumes and regalia for a unique experience. Watching Joseon-era life directly before your eyes
en.pull_quote: Incheon Yeongjong-gu Seasonal Recommended Festival · Incheon International Airport (2026.01.05 ~ 2026.12.31)
paragraphs: The 'Royal Family's Stroll', a traditional cultural event you can experience before departure at Incheon International Airport, recreates Joseon Dynasty royal court life. At Terminal 1, the king and queen are reenacted strolling through the palace. At Terminal 2, a royal procession of the king and military officers is reenacted at the late Joseon martial arts exhibition hall.

After the event, visitors can take commemorative photos with performers wearing royal court costumes and regalia for a unique experience. Watching Joseon-era life directly before your eyes offers special entertainment and provides sights for airport visitors. It is also a great event to watch with family.

ja.title: 王家の散歩
ja.addr: 仁川広域市永宗区空港路 272 (雲西洞)
ja.overview: 仁川国際空港で出国前に出会える伝統文化行事「王家の散歩」は、朝鮮時代の宮中生活を再現するイベントです。第1旅客ターミナルでは、王と王妃が宮殿を散歩する姿が再現されます。第2旅客ターミナルでは、朝鮮後期の武科（武官の試験）展示場に王の行幸と武官の行列が再現されます。イベント終了後、宮中服飾や儀仗物を着用した出演者と一緒に記念写真を撮ることができ、一風変わった経験ができます。朝鮮時代の生活を目の前で
ja.pull_quote: 仁川永宗区 季節のおすすめ祭り・仁川国際空港 (2026.01.05 ~ 2026.12.31)
paragraphs: 仁川国際空港で出国前に出会える伝統文化行事「王家の散歩」は、朝鮮時代の宮中生活を再現するイベントです。第1旅客ターミナルでは、王と王妃が宮殿を散歩する姿が再現されます。第2旅客ターミナルでは、朝鮮後期の武科（武官の試験）展示場に王の行幸と武官の行列が再現されます。
イベント終了後、宮中服飾や儀仗物を着用した出演者と一緒に記念写真を撮ることができ、一風変わった経験ができます。朝鮮時代の生活を目の前で直接観覧することができ、特別な楽しさをプレゼントし、空港で行われる行事として空港を訪れる訪問客に見どころを提供します。ご家族と一緒に観覧するのにもぴったりの行事です。

zh.overview: 「王室出巡」是可以在仁川國際空港（機場）出境前體驗的傳統文化活動，重現了朝鮮時代的宮中生活。在第一航廈會重現國王與王妃在宮闕內散步的景象；在第二航廈則會在朝鮮後期的武科展示場重現國王出巡與武官的儀仗隊伍。活動結束後，可以與身穿宮中服飾及儀仗道具的演出人員合影留念，帶來別具一格的體驗。親眼欣賞朝鮮時代的生活

zh.overview: 安城男寺黨巴ウ덕이風物團常設表演是自2003年起舉辦的安城市代表文化內容。代表安城市立男寺黨巴ウ덕이風物團的2026年常設表演「Gombaeng-i Tteotda」是以「市集的興致，震撼景福宮！」為副標題，將男寺黨遊戲的精髓——6個馬場（Act）以現代感重新詮釋並呈獻的表演。表演於每週六、日效下午2點在安城男寺黨表演場進行約90分鐘。
zh.pull_quote: 京畿安城市寶蓋面 季節推薦慶典 · 安城男寺黨表演場 (2026.04.04 ~ 2026.11.29)
paragraphs: 安城男寺黨巴ウ덕이風物團常設表演是自2003年起舉辦的安城市代表文化內容。代表安城市立男寺黨巴ウ덕이風物團的2026年常設表演「Gombaeng-i Tteotda」是以「市集的興致，震撼景福宮！」為副標題，將男寺黨遊戲的精髓——6個馬場（Act）以現代感重新詮釋並呈獻的表演。
表演於每週六、日效下午2點在安城男寺黨表演場進行約90分鐘。現場充滿了嗩吶與小銅鑼交織而成的充滿活力的風物表演、在3公尺高空上展現驚險技藝與風趣談話的走繩（Eoreum）、旋轉盤子（Beona）、展現翻滾特技的Salpan等豐富多彩的看點。

en.title: Culture Lounge Gyeonggi, Jang (Field/Market)
en.overview: Gyeonggi Culture Lounge 'Gyeonggi, Jang' is a complex cultural space that introduces Gyeonggi-do's local contents in one place. This space is structured around hands-on experiences so that visitors can directly experience regionally-based contents. 'Local Radar' is a customized experience program that allows individuals to design their Gyeonggi travel according to personal tastes. 'Gyeonggi Ceramic Shop' is a space that simultaneously offers relaxation and experience through ceramic craft experiences and tea tastings. Overall, it is in the form of a complex cultural platform combining exhibition, experience, and performance functions, characterized by operating based on visitor participation.

en.title: Han River History Exploration
en.overview: The 'Han River History Exploration' program provides attractive tourist commentaries and education to appreciate and share Han River landscapes and historical/cultural assets, allowing citizens and tourists to experience and enjoy the riverside. In addition, it aims to revitalize Han River history and culture enjoyed in daily life by developing various contents that allow citizens to actively participate and experience firsthand, such as experiential activities.
en.pull_quote: Seoul Yeongdeungpo-gu Season Recommended Festival · Hangang Park and Nearby Cultural Heritage (2026.04.20 ~ 2026.11.15)
paragraphs: The 'Han River History Exploration' program provides attractive tourist commentaries and education to appreciate and share Han River landscapes and historical/cultural assets, allowing citizens and tourists to experience and enjoy the riverside. In addition, it aims to revitalize Han River history and culture enjoyed in daily life by developing various contents that allow citizens to actively participate and experience firsthand, such as experiential activities.

Explorers walk along designated courses covering the Han River basin and nearby cultural heritage while listening to the commentary of a Han River docent. The Han River History Exploration operates on a total of 16 courses, where visitors can walk and explore the history of the Han River related to each course.

ja.title: 漢江歴史探訪
ja.addr: ソウル特別市 永登浦区 汝矣島路 330 (汝矣島洞)
ja.overview: 「漢江歴史探訪」プログラムは、漢江の景観および歴史・文化資源を鑑賞・共有する魅力的な観光解説と教育を提供し、市民や観光客に漢江沿いを体験・鑑賞させます。また、体験活動など市民が能動的に参加して直接経験できる多様なコンテンツを開発し、日常の中で楽しむ漢江の歴史文化を活性化させようとしています。探訪客は定められたコースに沿って漢江流域および近隣の文化遺産を歩きながら、漢江解説士の解説を聞きます。

zh.title: 漢江歷史探訪
zh.addr: 首爾特別市永登浦區汝矣島路330（汝矣島洞）
zh.overview: 「漢江歷史探訪」計畫提供欣賞與分享漢江景觀及歷史文化資源的迷人觀光解說與教育，讓市民與旅客體驗並欣賞漢江河畔。此外，亦開發讓市民能主動參與並親身體驗的各種內容（如體驗活動等），藉此活化在日常生活中享受的漢江歷史文化。參訪旅客沿著既定路線漫步於漢江流域及鄰近文化遺產，並聆聽漢江解說員的解說。

en.title: 2026 5th Jeju Biennale: Iyahong Modakchigok Iyahong : The Art of Transformation
en.overview: Civilization that blossomed on Jeju, a volcanic island of the Eurasian Plate, flowed not only from the sea but also arrived from northern land civilizations. Various elements scattered, gathered into Jeju, mixed, and transformed, shaping the ecology, geography, and lifestyle known as today's Jeju. Entering its 10th year, the 5th Jeju Biennale focuses on Jeju's dynamic process of scattering ('heok-gi-da'), gathering ('mo-dak-chi-da'), and transforming ('iyahong') upon meeting northern civilizations.
en.pull_quote: Jeju-si, Jeju Seasonal Recommended Festival · Jeju Museum of Art (2026.08.25 ~ 2026.11.15)
paragraphs: Civilization that blossomed on Jeju, a volcanic island of the Eurasian Plate, flowed not only from the sea but also arrived from northern land civilizations. Various elements scattered, gathered into Jeju, mixed, and transformed, shaping the ecology, geography, and lifestyle known as today's Jeju.

Entering its 10th year, the 5th Jeju Biennale focuses on Jeju's dynamic process of scattering ('heok-gi-da'), gathering ('mo-dak-chi-da'), and transforming ('iyahong') upon meeting northern civilizations. To this end, the biennale adopts 'Iyahong', the refrain of the 'Iyahong Taryeong' folk song that flowed from the mainland and became another indigenous folk song of Jeju, as its theme and core concept. Through Jeju, where principles of climate and diet are imbued, the Jeju Biennale aims to present the survival methods and aesthetics woven together by objects, nature, human life, and divinity.

en.title: 20th Century Photography Masters Exhibition - Light, Stopping Time
en.overview: In an era where hundreds of millions of images are easily born on liquid crystal screens and vanish lightly with a single tap of a finger. Amidst the flood of digital technology and artificial intelligence, anyone can easily capture and duplicate moments. Within the maze of light pixels, the heavy resonance and lingering imagery conveyed by analog photography are gradually fading. Amidst the repetition of easy production and consumption, we are losing the 'authenticity of gazing' at subjects deeply for a long time.
en.pull_quote: Seoul Jung-gu Recommended Seasonal Festival · Art Chosun Space (2026.11.20 ~ 2027.03.28)
paragraphs: In an era where hundreds of millions of images are easily born on liquid crystal screens and vanish lightly with a single tap of a finger. Amidst the flood of digital technology and artificial intelligence, anyone can easily capture and duplicate moments. Within the maze of light pixels, the heavy resonance and lingering imagery conveyed by analog photography are gradually fading. Amidst the repetition of easy production and consumption, we are losing the 'authenticity of gazing' at subjects deeply for a long time.

Since its inception, photography has been a physical exploration mediated by light and an art of time that captures and leaves behind a single cross-section of flowing time. The masterpieces born from the fingertips of 20th-century masters were not mere reproductions of phenomena through cold machines. They were the artists' unique philosophies that stared squarely at and interpreted the world. As a concept contrasting with digital images, analog-printed photographic works are called 'physical prints'. These are photographs completed as silver salt (photosensitive components combining silver and halogen elements) and platinum textures permeate the printing paper under the red light of a darkroom.

ja.title: 20世紀の写真巨匠展 - 光、時間を止める
ja.addr: ソウル特別市中区世宗大路21ギル30 (太平路1街)
ja.overview: 一日に何億枚もの画像が液晶画面の上で簡単に生まれ、指一本で軽く消滅する時代。デジタル技術と人工知能の氾濫の中で、誰もが簡単に瞬間を捉えて複製できるようになった。軽いピクセルの迷宮の中で、アナログ写真が伝える重厚な響きと残像は徐々に薄れている。簡単な生産と繰り返しが繰り返される中、私たちは対象を長く深く凝視する「見つめることの真正性」を失いつつある。
ja.pull_quote: ソウル中区 季節のおすすめ祭り · アート朝鮮スペース (2026.11.20 ~ 2027.03.28)
paragraphs: 一日に何億枚もの画像が液晶画面の上で簡単に生まれ、指一本で軽く消滅する時代。デジタル技術と人工知能の氾濫の中で、誰もが簡単に瞬間を捉えて複製できるようになった。軽いピクセルの迷宮の中で、アナログ写真が伝える重厚な響きと残像は徐々に薄れている。簡単な生産と繰り返しが繰り返される中、私たちは対象を長く深く凝視する「見つめることの真正性」を失いつつある。

写真は誕生の瞬間から光を媒体とした物理的探求であり、流れる時間の一断面を捉えて残す時間の芸術であった。20世紀の巨匠の指先から生まれた名作たちは、冷たい機械を通じた単なる現象の複製ではなかった。世の中を正面から凝視し、解釈した作家固有の哲学であった。デジタル画像と対比される概念として、アナログ方式で焼き付け・出力した写真作品を「フィジカルプリント(physical print)」と呼ぶ。暗室の赤い灯りの下で銀塩（銀とハロゲン元素が結びついた感光成分）の粒子と白金のキメが印画紙に染み込みながら完成した写真たちである。

zh.title: 20世紀攝影巨匠展 - 光，凝結時間
zh.addr: 首爾特別市中區世宗大路21街30（太平路1街）
zh.overview: 在這個每天都有數億張影像在螢幕上輕鬆誕生、又隨著手指輕輕一揮而消逝的時代。在數位技術與人工智慧氾濫的洪流中，每個人都能輕易捕捉並複製瞬間。在輕盈的像素迷宮中，類比攝影所傳遞的厚重迴響與餘韻正逐漸淡去。在輕易的生產與消費不斷重複的同時，我們正逐漸失去對主體進行長久、深邃凝視的「凝視的真實性」。
zh.pull_quote: 首爾中區季節推薦慶典 · Art Chosun Space（2026.11.20 ~ 2027.03.28）
paragraphs: 在這個每天都有數億張影像在螢幕上輕鬆誕生、又隨著手指輕輕一揮而消逝的時代。在數位技術與人工智慧氾濫的洪流中，每個人都能輕易捕捉並複製瞬間。在輕盈的像素迷宮中，類比攝影所傳遞的厚重迴響與餘韻正逐漸淡去。在輕易的生產與消費不斷重複的同時，我們正逐漸失去對主體進行長久、深邃凝視的「凝視的真實性」。

攝影自誕生之日起，便是以光為媒介的物理探索，是捕捉並留下流逝時間其中一個切面的時間藝術。誕生於20世紀巨匠指尖的名作，絕非透過冰冷機器對現象的單純複製，而是作者直視世界並進行詮釋的獨特哲學。作為與數位影像相對應的概念，以類比方式沖洗、輸出的攝影作品被稱為「實體照片（physical print）」。這些照片是在暗室的紅燈下，由銀鹽（銀與鹵素元素結合的感光成分）粒子與鉑金的紋理滲入相紙中完美完成的結晶。

Janchi Madang features a traditional play zone, Busan Intangible Heritage Art Fair, Hanbok Culture Week-linked traditional and craft markets, stamp tour, wish-writing, Hanbok rental, and traditional accessory experiences. This festival is designed to let visitors experience Busan's intangible heritage and traditional culture through performances and participatory activities.

Walking together through downtown Daejeon in autumn, participants can directly experience the value of energy and environment, and think about a sustainable future for all citizens. paragraphs: The 'All-Citizen Energy Walking Festival' is an eco-friendly energy participation program prepared to commemorate the 2026 Daejeon World Conference on Photovoltaic Energy (WCPEC-9). Walking together through downtown Daejeon in autumn, participants can directly experience the value of energy and environment, and think about a sustainable future for all citizens. This event is a walking program that anyone can joyfully participate in without ranking competition, starting from Daejeon Expo Citizens' Square and covering the Hanbat Arboretum area to complete mobile stamp missions.

By completing a total of 4 missions through smartphone QR verification, participants can receive completion rewards and a mobile completion certificate. Along with the walking program, various programs are operated to make learning about energy easy and fun. It is a citizen-participatory energy festival where individual steps gather to create a greener tomorrow.

en.title: Yeongju Apple Festival
en.overview: The 2026 Yeongju Apple Festival is an autumn festival to experience with all five senses the highest quality Yeongju apples grown in Yeongju's clear nature. This year, the festival delivers the taste and charm of Yeongju apples simultaneously from the production origin and the downtown area. It will be held around the Buseok-myeon Maze Park from October 30 to November 1, and events will also take place at Seoul Cheonggye Plaza from November 13 to November 15. Yeongju apples are characterized by high sugar content and crisp texture due to the large temperature range and abundant sunlight.

It will be held around the Buseok-myeon Maze Park from October 30 to November 1, and events will also take place at Seoul Cheonggye Plaza from November 13 to November 15. Yeongju apples are characterized by high sugar content and crisp texture due to the large temperature range and abundant sunlight. At the festival site, various experience programs, diverse variety displays, and apple markets will be held.

Colorful tasting events and cultural performances are also prepared. Visitors can fully enjoy the autumn scenery along with Buseoksa Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Blending the freshness of direct-from-farm produce with exciting performances and events, it is a fruitful venue providing pleasant memories for all ages. It is a golden opportunity to experience the superb autumn scenery of Yeongju as well as the highest quality Yeongju apples and abundant entertainment right in the heart of downtown Seoul.

en.overview: Located in Yeongwol, A-Ple is a health- and eco-conscious vegan bakery cafe. They bake gluten-free and vegan goods fresh in-store daily, avoiding animal products, white flour, and white sugar. Instead of sugar syrup, they use unrefined raw sugar syrup, and offer soy milk and milk options for their beverages. Even their takeout packaging uses biodegradable, eco-friendly disposables.
en.pull_quote: Signature Menu: Apple Milk Tea, Ham & Cheese Egg Sandwich, Fluffy Egg Sandwich, Americano, Cafe Latte, etc.

They avoid animal products as well as white flour and white sugar. The cafe also uses unrefined raw sugar syrup instead of sugar syrup, with options for both soy milk and regular milk. Takeout packaging for both bakery and drinks features eco-friendly, biodegradable disposables.

en.title: Jungbunaeryuk
en.addr: Yeongwol Mansion Apartment, 89 Hassongan-gil, Yeongwol-gun, Gangwon-do
en.overview: Jungbunaeryuk is a cafe located in Yeongwol Seobu Market. Instead of a formal signboard, it simply features the word 'Coffee' written on a disposable coffee cup hanging outside. The interior matches this simple, rustic vibe. The menu is hand-written by the owner rather than professionally designed. Above all, this place is famous for its exceptional coffee, and the interior reflects the owner's pride in drip coffee. There is an item called 'Korean Crunch Chocolate' on the menu, which is actually made of nurungji (scorched rice) rather than chocolate.
en.pull_quote: Signature Menu: Yeongwol Misutgaru, Americano, Latte, Iced Milk Tea, etc.

en.title: Ogeurani Red Bean Bread
en.overview: Located in Palkoi-ri at the entrance of Mount Taehwasan in Yeongwol, this bakery cafe specializes in red bean bread. You can enjoy a wide variety of red bean buns, including handmade red bean bread, glutinous rice, soboro (streusel), fresh cream, custard, and black sesame red bean bread. Ogeurani uses 100% domestic red beans prepared in-house, along with organic ingredients like organic flour, natural starter, refined sea salt, and unrefined sugar for healthy treats. In addition to coffee, they offer unique specialty drinks such as black sesame milk, red bean milk, and floral lemonade.
en.pull_quote: Signature Menu: Handmade Red Bean Bread, Injeolmi Cream Red Bean Bread, Fresh Cream Red Bean Bread, etc.

en.title: Donggangui Achim
en.overview: Donggangui Achim (Morning of Donggang) is a natural dining restaurant located in Yeongwol-gun, Gangwon-do. Situated along the Donggang River facing Mount Bongraesan, it is a favorite among golfers visiting nearby Donggang Cista CC, travelers on Donggang rafting trips, and locals alike. A popular set menu features gondre-bap (thistle rice) served alongside smoked or fresh duck meat. The meat is pre-grilled over firewood and finished right at your table.
en.pull_quote: Signature Menu: Gondre Set Meal, Smoked Duck / Fresh Meat Plate, Donggang Set Meal, etc.
paragraphs: Donggangui Achim is a natural dining restaurant located in Yeongwol-gun, Gangwon-do. Situated along the Donggang River facing Mount Bongraesan, it is a favorite among golfers visiting nearby Donggang Cista CC, travelers on Donggang rafting trips, and locals alike. A popular set menu features gondre-bap (thistle rice) served alongside smoked or fresh duck meat. The meat is pre-grilled over firewood and finished right at your table.

A variety of side dishes made with Gangwon-do wild mountain greens and dried herbs stimulate the appetite. Their soybean paste stew made with homemade doenjang is also exceptionally noteworthy. Mixing the soft, chewy pressure-cooked gondre-bap with seasoned soy sauce makes it even more delicious. The restaurant features a stylish wooden structure exterior that is hard to find nowadays. Guests can dine indoors or out on the terrace. A spacious private parking lot outside makes parking very convenient.

en.title: National Cheongtaesan Natural Recreation Forest
en.overview: Centered around the 1,200m-high main peak of Mount Cheongtaesan, this national forest management model complex features lush, well-balanced artificial and natural forests. Home to a wide array of wild flora and fauna, it feels like visiting a natural museum. en.title: Taegisan Mountain
en.overview: Mount Taegisan forms the boundary between Dunnae-myeon in Hoengseong-gun and Bongpyeong-myeon in Pyeongchang-gun. According to legend, King Taegi, the last king of Jinhan, was chased by Silla forces, built Taegisan Fortress (1.8km), and made his last stand—remnants of which still remain. The deep mountain valley, home to abundant primitive plant life and scenic spots like Mulhangari Waterfall and Chotdaebawi (Candlestick Rock), is breathtaking. At the foot of the mountain in Shindae-ri, Cheongil-myeon, stands Bongboksa Temple, founded by Master Jajang Yulsa in the 16th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla, while a refreshing spring—the source of the Seomgang River—gushes from the mid-slopes.

en.title: Byeongjibang Valley
en.overview: Byeongjibang Valley in Hoengseong is a stunning valley located in Gapcheon-myeon, Hoengseong-gun, Gangwon-do, also known as Byeongjibangri Valley or Sandi Valley. Surrounded by lofty peaks such as Eodapsan, Taeuisan, and Balgyosan, the scenery is magnificent, and the crystal-clear, icy stream water flows from the source of the Seomgang River, a tributary of the Namhangang River. The name 'Byeongjibang' originates from a folktale stating that the soldiers of King Taegi, the last king of Jinhan who fled from King Park Hyeokgeose, once stayed here.
en.pull_quote: Byeongjibang Valley in Hoengseong is a stunning valley located in Gapcheon-myeon, Hoengseong-gun, Gangwon-do. Also known as Byeongjibangri Valley or Sandi Valley, it is surrounded by lofty peaks...
paragraphs: Byeongjibang Valley in Hoengseong is a stunning valley located in Gapcheon-myeon, Hoengseong-gun, Gangwon-do. Also known as Byeongjibangri Valley or Sandi Valley. Surrounded by lofty peaks such as Eodapsan, Taeuisan, and Balgyosan, the scenery is magnificent, and the crystal-clear, icy stream water flows from the source of the Seomgang River, a tributary of the Namhangang River. The name 'Byeongjibang' originates from a folktale stating that the soldiers of King Taegi, the last king of Jinhan who fled from King Park Hyeokgeose, once stayed here.

A paved road stretches approximately 10km along the valley, with large free parking lots set up roadside. As one of the most remote valleys in Hoengseong-gun, the area boasts lush foliage, and the Seonnyetang (Fairies' Pond) area features various strange rock formations and wildflowers. Smaller tributaries like Garakgol, Godeonggol, Semgol, and Jujutgol flow nearby. With abundant water, it is a popular summer retreat. The general campsite near Byeongjibang Valley is equipped with auto-camping sites, parking, drinking fountains, and sports facilities, making it ideal for family camping. Visitors can camp freely or use the paid campsites.

渓谷に沿って舗装道路が約10kmほど伸びており、渓谷の道路沿いには大型無料駐車場が整備されています。横城郡で最も奥地に属するこの渓谷一帯は樹木が生い茂り、仙女湯一帯には様々な奇岩怪奇や野草が見られます。周囲にはカラクコル、ゴドングコル、セムコル、チュチュッコルなどの小さな支流が流れ、水量が豊富で夏場の避暑客に人気があります。周辺の総合キャンプ場にはオートキャンプ場、駐車場、炊事場、運動施設などが整っており、家族でのキャンプに最適です。野営をすることも、有料キャンプ場を利用することもできます。

zh.title: 炳芝坊溪谷
zh.addr: 江原特別自治道橫城郡甲川面炳芝坊里
zh.overview: 橫城炳芝坊溪谷是位於江原道橫城郡甲川面的一處美麗溪谷，又被稱為炳芝坊里溪谷或山地溪谷。四周被御踏山、太義山、發橋山等高山峻嶺環繞，景致秀麗。溪谷之水流自南漢江支流蟾江的發源地，極其清澈冰涼。「炳芝坊」這個名稱據說源自一則傳說：古代遭到朴赫居世追擊的辰韓末代國王太基王，其麾下的士兵曾在此停留駐紮。

沿著溪谷鋪設了約 10 公里的道路，道路旁設有大型免費停車場。此處屬於橫城郡最偏遠的地帶，區內樹木鬱鬱蔥蔥，仙女湯一帶則有各式奇岩怪石與野花點綴。周圍流淌著加樂谷、古登谷、泉谷、柱礎谷等小型支流，因水量豐沛而成為夏季熱門的避暑勝地。炳芝坊溪谷周邊的綜合露營區配備了汽車露營區、停車場、飲水台、運動設施等，非常適合家庭一同前來露營。旅客可以選擇自備帳篷露營，或是使用付費露營場。

en.title: Pungsuwon Catholic Church
en.overview: Pungsuwon Catholic Church in Hoengseong traces its origins to the early 1800s, when around 40 believers led by Shin Tae-bo (Peter) settled here to escape religious persecution from Yongin, Gyeonggi-do. The Pungsuwon parish once oversaw 29 branch churches across 12 counties, including Chuncheon, Wonju, Hwacheon, Yanggu, Hongcheon, Hoengseong, Pyeongchang, and Yangpyeong. Separation of the Wonju parish began in 1896, followed by Chuncheon in 1920 and Hongcheon in 1948.
en.pull_quote: Pungsuwon Catholic Church in Hoengseong traces its origins to the early 1800s, when around 40 believers led by Shin Tae-bo (Peter) settled here to escape persecution...
paragraphs: Pungsuwon Catholic Church in Hoengseong traces its origins to the early 1800s, when around 40 believers led by Shin Tae-bo (Peter) settled here to escape persecution from Yongin, Gyeonggi-do. The Pungsuwon parish once oversaw 29 branch churches across 12 counties, including Chuncheon, Wonju, Hwacheon, Yanggu, Hongcheon, Hoengseong, Pyeongchang, and Yangpyeong. Separation of the Wonju parish began in 1896, followed by Chuncheon in 1920 and Hongcheon in 1948.

Located in Yuhyeon-ri, Seowon-myeon, Hoengseong-gun, Gangwon-do, Pungsuwon Catholic Church was designated as a Gangwon-do Tangible Cultural Heritage in 1982. Facing southwest on a low hill, the church building features a three-aisled plan where the nave and aisles are divided by colonnaded arcades and ceiling structures. The composition of the protruding main entrance at the front center, the second-floor circular window, and the bell tower with third-floor twin arched windows and louvered vents emphasizes verticality with upward-narrowing buttresses, leaving a striking impression on the central facade.

en.title: Holocene Eco School
en.overview: The Holocene refers to the geological epoch following the Pleistocene of the Quaternary period, spanning from about 10,000 years ago to the present, also known as the Alluvial or Recent epoch. This period is also when humans began agriculture and pastoral activities, systematically threatening all ecosystems. Most species went extinct due to human activity during this era, known as the Holocene extinction—the sixth extinction caused by destructive humans, raising major ecological concerns.
en.pull_quote: The Holocene refers to the geological epoch following the Pleistocene of the Quaternary period, spanning from about 10,000 years ago to the present... It marks a time when humanity began...
paragraphs: The Holocene refers to the geological epoch following the Pleistocene of the Quaternary period, spanning from about 10,000 years ago to the present, also known as the Alluvial or Recent epoch. This period is also when humans began agriculture and pastoral activities, systematically threatening all ecosystems.

Most species went extinct due to human activity during this era, known as the Holocene extinction—the sixth extinction caused by destructive humans, raising major ecological concerns. Accordingly, to raise awareness of the current ecological crisis and provide an opportunity to deeply reflect on nature and life, the school goes beyond breeding and restoring endangered species. It serves as a practical model for environmental conservation through maintaining biodiversity via basic research such as insect species preservation, classification of insect resources, and ecology.

en.title: Cheonmunin Maeul (Astronomers' Village)
en.overview: Located at an altitude of 650 meters at the edge of Chiaksan Mountain in Hoengseong, Gangwon-do, Cheonmunin Maeul is a place where the universe meets pure nature amidst high skies and clean air, allowing visitors to see countless stars flowing across a night sky free of light pollution. It is used as an observation site by many amateur astronomers both domestically and abroad, and serves as a regular spot for observations and research by amateur astronomy clubs, astrophotography clubs, and school teachers.
en.pull_quote: Located at an altitude of 650m at the edge of Chiaksan Mountain in Hoengseong, Gangwon-do, Cheonmunin Maeul is a place where the universe meets pure nature under a night sky...
paragraphs: Located at an altitude of 650 meters at the edge of Chiaksan Mountain in Hoengseong, Gangwon-do, Cheonmunin Maeul is a place where the universe meets pure nature amidst high skies and clean air, allowing visitors to see countless stars flowing across a night sky free of light pollution. It is used as an observation site by many amateur astronomers both domestically and abroad, and serves as a regular spot for observations and research by amateur astronomy clubs, astrophotography clubs, and school teachers.

To help visitors understand stars and the universe, the village is equipped with related videos, slide photos, and books, allowing guests to see and hear seasonal constellations and the beautiful stories woven into them. Visitors can observe the night sky through a large 14-inch astronomical telescope and appreciate various astrophotographs. Cheonmunin Maeul will remain a long-cherished hometown of the heart for anyone who loves stars, serving as an optimal observation spot for amateur astronomers and a memorable place for the general public to keep a beautiful night sky in their hearts.

en.title: Deulkkotpineun Eondeok (Wildflower Hill)
en.overview: Deulkkotpineun Eondeok is a Korean cuisine specialty restaurant located near Dunnae Station in Hoengseong-gun, Gangwon-do. Having operated for a long time, it is highly recommended by locals. Their signature menu is the ssambap set (wrapped rice meal), which generously offers a variety of wrappers, side dishes, and meat, leaving a deep impression with its neat and warm food. Other menu items include spicy braised chicken (dakbokkeumtang) and traditional herbal chicken soup (hanbang baeksuk). It is a great place to spend quality time with family and friends, and many ski resort visitors stop by due to nearby resort facilities.

en.title: Geumgangsan Sutbulgui
en.overview: Hoengseong Hanwoo (Korean beef) is renowned for its exceptional quality and taste, as evidenced by the large number of tourists attending the annual Hanwoo Festival. Geumgangsan Sutbulgui uses only grade 1 or higher beef certified by the Hoengseong Livestock Cooperative, and grills it exclusively over Gangwon pine charcoal to showcase the clean and savory flavor of charcoal-grilled Hanwoo. Using only vegetables grown directly on their farm, it is a place where you can trust and truly enjoy the authentic taste of Hanwoo.

en.title: Gwangam Makguksu
en.overview: Located in front of the Hoengseong Hanul Art Museum, Gwangam Makguksu is famous for its makguksu (buckwheat noodles), made by kneading 100% buckwheat flour, pressing the noodles directly through a noodle press, and serving them in a rich beef bone broth. The bibim makguksu (spicy mixed noodles) offers a choice between pollack and soy sauce flavors, with the soy sauce flavor being great for young children. The suyuk (boiled pork slices) served alongside the noodles uses pork shoulder boiled with various medicinal herbs such as cinnamon and ginger, making it tender and free of any gamey odor.

en.overview: Cottage Saengun is an emotional cafe located in Hoengseong, Gangwon-do, with drip coffee and Americano as its most popular menus. en.title: Wirari Seven-Story Stone Pagoda
en.overview: The Wirari Seven-Story Stone Pagoda is a Goryeo-dynasty stone pagoda located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do. At the time of excavation, the base and up to the third story retained their original form, but from the fourth story onward, the main bodies (oksin) were missing, leaving only the roof stones (okgaeseok). The scattered pieces of the base, pagoda body, and roof stones were collected and re-erected. The roof stones and the body stones of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd stories are original, while those of the 4th story and above were supplemented during restoration in 1975.
en.pull_quote: The Wirari Seven-Story Stone Pagoda is a Goryeo-dynasty stone pagoda located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do. At the time of excavation, the base and up to the third story...
paragraphs: The Wirari Seven-Story Stone Pagoda is a Goryeo-dynasty stone pagoda located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do. At the time of excavation, the base and up to the third story retained their original form, but from the 4th story onward, the main bodies were lost, leaving only the roof stones. The scattered base members, pagoda body stones, and roof stones were collected and re-erected. The roof stones and body stones of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd stories are original, while the body stones above the 4th story were added during the 1975 restoration. The shape of the pagoda features a 7-story pagoda body placed on a large foundation stone.

The body stones of the pagoda have pillar shapes carved on each corner, and the 2nd story decreases significantly in height compared to the 1st story, after which it decreases very gradually. The roof stones have 3-tier supports on the underside, and the eaves are horizontal, lifting slightly upward at the four corners. The top finial ornaments are entirely gone, leaving only a single round stone. Although small in scale, the carving of pillars on the body stones and the 3-tier roof stone supports show a style and technique very similar to the Namgyewon Seven-Story Stone Pagoda, suggesting that the two pagodas were built around the same period.

en.title: Yonghasan Mountain (Gangwon Peace Region National Geopark)
en.overview: Granite is a plutonic rock formed when magma solidifies deep underground. Rocks formed under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions deep underground experience 'weathering', where they easily break down as temperature and pressure decrease when they rise near the earth's surface. In particular, weathering occurs actively when rocks come into contact with moisture underground.
en.pull_quote: Granite is a plutonic rock formed when magma solidifies deep underground. Rocks formed under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions deep underground near...
paragraphs: Granite is a plutonic rock formed when magma solidifies deep underground. Rocks formed under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions deep underground experience 'weathering', where they easily break down as temperature and pressure decrease when they rise near the earth's surface. In particular, weathering occurs actively when rocks come into contact with moisture underground.

This is a type of chemical weathering (a phenomenon where the bonds of minerals constituting rocks break down and crumble) that occurs underground, hence called deep weathering (or chemical deep weathering). When such deep weathering processes accelerate, even hard rocks become weak enough to be easily crushed by human hand power, and the material generated is called saprolite. However, when granite that has undergone little or no weathering is exposed above the ground, it has a short contact time with moisture and does not undergo further deep weathering, thus forming large-scale rock quarries. In other words, Yonghasan Mountain formed its fracture structures after the weathered and weakened material (saprolite) was washed away following deep weathering.

en.pull_quote: According to the historical records of Muwisa Temple, it was first established in 875 (the 1st year of King Heongang) by National Master Doseon as Galoksa Temple. Shortly after, around 905 (the 9th year of King Hyogong) and onward...
paragraphs: According to the historical records of Muwisa Temple, it was first established in 875 (the 1st year of King Heongang) by National Master Doseon as Galoksa Temple. Shortly after, around 905 (the 9th year of King Hyogong) and onward, National Master Seongak Hyeongmi (864–917) of the Gajisanmun Seon (Zen) school stayed at Muwigapsa Temple at the request of King Taejo Wang Geon of Goryeo. He restored the temple and widely propagated Buddhist teachings, gaining massive public support. Thus, it is known that Muwisa was founded as Muwigapsa Temple before the early 10th century when Monk Hyeongmi resided there.

However, according to the temple's historical records, Hyeongmi renamed it Maoksa Temple during his third reconstruction in 946 (the 1st year of King Jeongjong) of the Goryeo Dynasty. Yet, 946 was already 30 years after Hyeongmi passed away, and it was the year the 'Stupa Monument of National Master Seongak of Muwigapsa Temple in Goryeo', written by Choi Eon-wi, was erected, making this date hard to believe. This is likely a misunderstanding by later generations regarding the fact that Hyeongmi extensively restored Muwigapsa with the support of Wang Geon and propagated his teachings. Muwisa was founded before the early 10th century and was reconstructed by Hyeongmi.

paragraphs: Dasanchodang is a representative historic site where the late Joseon Silhak (Practical Learning) scholar Jeong Yak-yong stayed and continued his academic activities during his exile in Gangjin. Exiled following the Sinyu Persecution in 1801, he moved through several places before settling here in 1808. He dedicated about 10 years until his release to teaching disciples, researching, and writing.

During this period, he completed massive, representative works of Joseon Silhak such as 'Mokmin Simseo' and 'Gyeongse Yupyo', and is evaluated as the place where Silhak thought was synthesized. Dasanchodang was not merely a residence, but a space where academic achievements were intensively made, playing a crucial role in Jeong Yak-yong establishing a practical and reality-centered academic system. Today, Dongam and Seoram, the spaces where disciples stayed, have been restored, along with various preserved historical remains such as 'Jeongseok' (engraved characters said to have been carved by Jeong Yak-yong himself), Yakcheon (medicinal spring), Dajo (tea stove), Yeonjiseokgasan (rockery pond), and Cheonilgak Pavilion, offering a glimpse into his life and philosophy.

この時期に『牧民心書』、『経世遺表』など朝鮮の実学を代表する膨大な著作を完成させ、実学思想を大成した場所と評価される。茶山草堂は単なる住まいではなく、学的成果が集中的に生み出された空間であり、丁若鏞が実用的かつ現実中心的な学問体系を確立する上で重要な役割を果たした。現在は東庵と西庵、弟子たちが滞在した空間が復元されており、丁若鏞が自ら文字を彫ったと伝えられる「丁石」、お茶を沸かした薬泉、茶竈、蓮池石假山、天一閣など様々な遺跡が一緒に保存されており、彼の生活と思想を垣間見ることができる。

en.pull_quote: Poet Yeongrang Kim Yun-sik was born here on January 16, 1903, as the eldest son of Kim Jong-ho's two sons and three daughters. Called Chaejun in his childhood, he later changed his name to Yun-sik...
paragraphs: Poet Yeongrang Kim Yun-sik was born here on January 16, 1903, as the eldest son of Kim Jong-ho's two sons and three daughters. Called Chaejun in his childhood, he later changed his name to Yun-sik. Yeongrang is his pen name, which he predominantly used during his literary activities.

Until his passing on September 29, 1950, Poet Yeongrang published around 80 gem-like poems, about 60 of which were written during the period he lived here, refusing the Japanese colonial policy of forced name changes and Shinto shrine worship before liberation. Yeongrang's birthplace was traded a few times after Yeongrang moved to Seoul in 1948, but it was purchased and managed by Gangjin-gun in 1985. The main building, which had been partially altered, was restored to its original form in 1992, and the gate quarters, which had been demolished, were restored in 1993 based on historical research by Yeongrang's family. The birthplace still preserves the well, camellia tree, jar platform, and persimmon tree that served as subjects for his poems, and is widely planted with peonies.

paragraphs: Baengnyeonsa Temple is said to have been founded during the reign of King Munseong of Silla by National Master Muyeom (801–888) under the name Manduksa Temple, named after the mountain. After falling into decline, National Master Wonmyo Yose reconstructed it on the old site in the 7th year of King Huijong of Goryeo, and it became widely renowned through the Baengnyeon Association, leading to its current name, Baengnyeonsa. It is also well-known as a space where Dasan Jeong Yak-yong, who was exiled to Gangjin during the Joseon Dynasty, communicated and interacted with Master Aam Hyejang, transcending religion and age.

Mandaksan Mountain, where Baengnyeonsa and Dasanchodang are located, has an abundance of wild tea plants and has been called Dasan (Tea Mountain) since ancient times. Jeong Yak-yong adopted the pen name 'Dasan' in reference to his exile and stay here, which became his representative moniker. Flowers starting to bloom from late November reach full bloom around late March, and in April, they fall to the ground, dyeing the forest red once again. Baengnyeonsa operates various temple stay programs such as relaxation-type, group experiential-type, and tea ceremony experience programs, and Dasanchodang and Dasan Museum are located around the temple.

paragraphs: Gangjin has an exceptionally large number of traditional Korean set meal (hanjeongsik) restaurants. Deciding which one to visit is a pleasant dilemma of traveling to Gangjin. If you ask locals in Gangjin which Korean restaurant they visit most often, they will undoubtedly recommend Myeongdong Sikdang without hesitation.

Once you receive your table spread, the natural characteristics of Gangjin—blending mountains, fields, and the sea—are vividly revealed before you. Seafood delicacies like sliced raw fish, raw abalone, giant clam soup, and grilled eel, alongside tteok-galbi (grilled short rib patties), yukhoe (beef tartare), and Gangjin's specialty fried shiitake mushrooms, form a true feast of rare delicacies. Their homemade fermented salted small octopus (toha-jeot) and soy-sauce marinated crab are so popular that guests often ask to pack up the leftovers, while the samhap (fermented skate, boiled pork slices, and aged kimchi) is also counted among regulars' favorite menu items.

paragraphs: Bogildo Yun Seondo Worim is a scenic cultural heritage site in South Korea where Gosan Yun Seondo (1587–1671), a civil servant, poet, and scholar of the Joseon Dynasty, spent his later years. Upon hearing the news of the Second Manchu Invasion of Korea while in Haenam, he headed to Ganghwado, but King Injo had already surrendered to the enemy in Namhanseong Fortress. Abandoning worldly affairs, Gosan reportedly stopped in Bogildo, captivated by its scenery on his way to Jeju Island. Naming the beautiful spots across the island, Gosan composed masterpiece classical Chinese poems such as 『Eobusasisa』 (The Fisherman's Seasons). Bogildo Yun Seondo Worim is one of Korea's top three traditional gardens showcasing typical Joseon-era garden styles.

Yun Seondo reportedly said of this place, 'I named it Buyong because the terrain looks like a lotus bud bursting into bloom.' Buyongdong Garden is both a living and recreational space personally created by Gosan, representing a quintessential Joseon-era villa garden (byeolsseo). paragraphs: 甫吉島尹善道園林被指定為大韓民國的名勝文化遺產，是朝鮮時代的文臣、詩人兼學者孤山尹善道（1587~1671）度過晚年之處。孤山尹善道身處海南時聽聞丙子胡亂的消息並抵達江華島，但仁祖已在南漢山城向敵人投降。因此，孤山拋棄世俗前往濟州島的途中，被甫吉島的景色所迷倒而決定留在此地。孤山為甫吉島內風景秀麗的景致命名，並在各地往返間創作了《漁父四時詞》等如珠寶般珍貴的漢詩。甫吉島尹善道園林展現了朝鮮時代代表性的庭園樣式，是韓國三大傳統庭園之一。

en.pull_quote: Cheongsando is the southernmost island of the Dadohae archipelago, 19.2 km from Wando and 50 minutes by boat from Wando Port. Known for its extraordinary natural beauty...
paragraphs: Cheongsando is the southernmost island of the Dadohae archipelago, located 19.2 km away from Wando and a 50-minute boat ride from Wando Port. Blessed with exceptionally stunning natural scenery, it has long been called 'Cheongsan-yeosu' (Blue Mountains and Clear Waters) or 'Seonsan' and 'Seonwon' (Mountain and Source of Taoist Hermits), as it is beautiful enough for immortals to roam.

Designated as Dadohae Haesang National Park on December 23, 1981, it was selected as Asia's first Cittaslow on December 1, 2007. Cheongsando's Slow Road consists of 11 courses, 17 paths, and a total length of 42.195 km, allowing visitors to experience unique themes on each course. Featuring photo zones, blue seas, green mountains, gudeuljangnong (traditional terraced stone paddy fields), and stone-walled paths, it is a one-of-a-kind walking island in the country.

en.title: Sinduji Garden
en.addr: 548 Sinji-ro, Sinji-myeon, Wando-gun, Gwangju-Jeonnam Special Metropolitan City
en.overview: Located on a hill, Sinduji Garden features a somewhat unique terraced exterior. It is a two-story Western-style red brick house with the restaurant on the lower floor. The interior is kept clean and tidy like any typical restaurant, and the ornamental stones placed here and there catch the eye. Signature menus include eogeotang (spicy eel soup) and saengseon maeuntang (spicy fish stew). Particularly, the spicy fish stew offers a fresh taste and generous southern hospitality, as Wando easily provides fresh seafood, delighting diners. The spread of over 10 basic side dishes is enough to fill you up.

ja.region_label: 全羅南道 莞島郡 新智面
ja.addr: 光州全南特別市 莞島郡 新智面 新지로 548
ja.overview: 新斗池ガーデンは丘の上に位置しており、階段状のやや変わった外観を持っている。赤いレンガで建てられた2階建ての洋風住宅で、下層階に食堂がある。内装は一般的な食堂のように清潔で綺麗に管理されており、食堂内のあちこちに置かれた水石（鑑賞用の石）が目を引く。代表メニューはウナギのスープ（チャンオタン）と魚の辛口メウンタンである。特に魚のメウンタンは、新鮮な海産物を手軽に入手できる莞島ならではの新鮮な味わいと南道の豊富な人情が食べる人を喜ばせてくれる。10種類以上を超える基本おかずだけでもお腹がいっぱいになる場所だ。

zh.overview: 新斗池花園餐廳位於山丘上，擁有階梯狀的獨特外觀。這是一棟紅磚建造的兩層樓洋房，一樓為餐廳。內部如同一般餐廳般乾淨整潔，餐廳各處擺放的水石（觀賞石）格外引人注目。招牌菜色為鰻魚湯與鮮魚辣湯。特別是鮮魚辣湯，因為莞島盛產新鮮海鮮，其鮮美滋味與南道濃厚的人情味讓人大飽口福。光是超過10種以上的豐富小菜就足以讓人大快朵頤。

ja.region_label: 全羅南道 莞島郡 莞島邑

en.title: Mirak Sikdang
en.addr: 15 Gunnae 11-gil, Wando-gun, Gwangju-Jeonnam Special Metropolitan City
en.overview: Located in Wando, Mirak Sikdang is a monkfish specialty restaurant loved by locals. Their signature dish, agui-jjim (braised spicy monkfish), is widely adored for its tender texture, chewy taste, and spicy, zesty seasoning, with fried rice enjoyed after the meal being another crowd favorite. In addition, they offer various menus such as braised pufferfish (bok-jjim), clear pufferfish soup (bok-jiri), spicy pufferfish soup (bok-maeuntang), monkfish soup (agui-tang), and duck soup (ori-tang). With a spacious, clean interior and an open kitchen, it is great for family dinners and group gatherings.

paragraphs: From Goheung-eup, take Provincial Road No. 851 northwest, turn left at the Haknim Village bamboo grove three-way intersection, drive 4 km to reach the Goheungman Embankment, and turn right for another 1 km to arrive at Pungryu Beach.

With a sandy beach about 500m long and 50m wide, the sand is wide and clean, the waves are calm, and the water is shallow—making it ideal for children to play. The gentle slope of the beach allows visitors to experience clam-digging in the tidal flats during low tide. Though cozy in size, the beach is densely lined with pine trees and evergreen trees providing cool shade from the heat, and flat wooden platforms (pyeongsang) make it a top spot for car-camping and wild camping. It is one of the few beaches where cooking/grilling is permitted.

en.overview: Sorokdo Island is located less than 1 km from Nokdong Port at the tip of the Goheung Peninsula in Gwangju-Jeonnam Special Metropolitan City. It is called Sorokdo because the island's shape resembles a young deer (sorok). Though the island is not large, its pristine natural environment, coastal scenery, and historical monuments have made it a rising tourist attraction in Goheung-gun.

Opened in 2009, Sorokdae Bridge allows visitors to reach the island via National Route 27, increasing tourism and making it much easier for residents to travel back and forth.

en.title: Gwangdeokgyegok Valley
en.overview: Located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do, Gwangdeokgyegok Valley is a pristine valley situated in the upper reaches of Sanaecheon Stream, originating from Mt. Gwangdeoksan, passing through Mt. Baegunsan, and flowing into the Bukhangang River. Nestled between Mt. Baegunsan and Mt. Gwangdeoksan, it boasts beautiful natural scenery and unpolluted crystal-clear waters featuring small waterfalls and pools. In autumn, the surrounding mountains like Baegunsan, Gwangdeoksan, Muhakbong, Beonamsan, Gamtubong, and Sanghaebong offer breathtaking foliage views. In summer, its cool waters and breeze make it an optimal summer retreat for families.

paragraphs: Located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do, Gwangdeokgyegok Valley is a pristine valley situated in the upper reaches of Sanaecheon Stream, originating from Mt. Gwangdeoksan, passing through Mt. Baegunsan, and flowing into the Bukhangang River. Nestled between Mt. Baegunsan and Mt. Gwangdeoksan, it boasts beautiful natural scenery and unpolluted crystal-clear waters featuring small waterfalls and pools.

In autumn, the surrounding mountains like Baegunsan, Gwangdeoksan, Muhakbong, Beonamsan, Gamtubong, and Sanghaebong offer breathtaking foliage views. In summer, its cool waters and breeze make it an optimal summer retreat for families. The valley is uncrowded and shallow, making it great for children to play in the water, while well-equipped restrooms and parking lots add convenience. Nearby guesthouses and lodging facilities allow for relaxing after water play, and attractions like Tomato Sculpture Park, Hwaimdong Jeongsa Historic Site, and Bokjusan Natural Recreation Forest offer pleasant walks and forest bathing.

en.title: Bimok Park
en.overview: Located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do, Bimok Park is a place honoring the sorrow and sacrifice of the Korean War. It is also the birthplace of the beloved Korean national song, 'Bimok' (Wooden Cross). The song originated in the mid-1960s when a young officer in the Baegamsan valley, north of Peace Dam, discovered an overgrown stone grave of an unknown soldier and wrote lyrics commemorating his youthful soul.

paragraphs: Located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do, Bimok Park is a place honoring the sorrow and sacrifice of the Korean War. It is also the birthplace of the beloved Korean national song, 'Bimok' (Wooden Cross). The song originated in the mid-1960s when a young officer in the Baegamsan valley, north of Peace Dam, discovered an overgrown stone grave of an unknown soldier and wrote lyrics commemorating his youthful soul.

The park features the Bimok Tower, an unknown soldier's stone grave monument, a mountain magnolia sculpture, and a song monument. The song monument is erected at the entrance of the Bimok Park parking lot, inscribed with the lyrics of 'Bimok'. The Bimok Tower was built with the devotion of Hwacheon residents to commemorate the patriots who died for their country during the Korean War.

en.title: Bisugumi Village
en.overview: Hidden by Lake Paroho, Bisugumi Village is a secret destination where you can immerse yourself in untouched natural beauty rather than crowded tourist spots. Formed right after the Korean War when evacuees settled down to cultivate slash-and-burn fields, the village became known as an 'island within the land' after overland routes were blocked by the construction of Hwacheon Dam. While it once housed 100 households, only 3 families have guarded this place since the 1970s.

Formed right after the Korean War when evacuees settled down to cultivate slash-and-burn fields, the village became known as an 'island within the land' after overland routes were blocked by the construction of Hwacheon Dam. While it once housed 100 households, only 3 families have guarded this place since the 1970s.

Preserved so naturally that vehicles cannot pass through, the village scenery looks like a picture. Frequently featured on various TV programs such as 'Running Man' and 'Battle Trip', it is one of Hwacheon's hidden tourist gems. Walking through the forest along the valley gives you a special feeling as if nature and you have become one.

en.title: Yongdamgyegok Valley
en.overview: Yongdamgyegok Valley is located on the right side when heading from Sachang-ri, Hwacheon-gun toward Chuncheon Jichon via Route 56. Boasting splendid scenery, the powerful streams gushing along the winding valley evoke a sense of refreshment. The valley houses the dragon pool (Yongso), also known as Gameoso, as well as Baegundam (Gokunyeongdang) and Gaeddongsoi. Among them, Yongso is the symbol of Yongdamgyegok Valley. Located at the entrance of the valley, this 10-meter-deep basin flows with a swirling motion resembling a dragon's movement.

溪谷內坐落著俗稱釜潭（Gameoso）的龍沼，以及白雲潭（谷雲影堂）、狗糞沼等景點。其中，龍沼可說是龍潭溪谷的象徵。位於溪谷入口處，是一個深達10米的深潭，湍急迴旋的水流模樣宛如巨龍飛舞。相傳過去住在這裡的龍升天時，才造就了現在這樣的地形。

en.title: Gangbyeon Hoetjip
en.overview: Located in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do, Gangbyeon Hoetjip is a restaurant specializing in freshwater fish dishes. You can enjoy seasonal freshwater fish sashimi, such as trout, grass carp, and mandarin fish, while admiring the wonderful view of Lake Paroho. Maeuntang (spicy fish stew) featuring chewy hand-pulled dough (sujebi) and a deep broth is a popular menu item. Operating hours may change, so it is recommended to check in advance before visiting.

en.title: Gwangdeok Byeorarae
en.overview: Like a hidden gem, this cafe is located at the entrance of Hwacheon's Cho Gyeong-cheol Observatory. You can enjoy a variety of cakes and coffee in a cute and quiet atmosphere. The interior, remodeled from a traditional Korean Hanok building, has limited seating but creates a sentimental vibe with its interior design, and outdoor tables are also available in the courtyard. Well-maintained in every corner, it is great for taking photos. Dalgona cake is a popular signature menu item. It is a great place to enjoy bread and drinks before heading to the observatory, or to take a break while playing in Baegun Valley or driving.

ja.overview: 華川の曹景哲（チョ・ギョンチョル）天文台の入口に位置する隠された宝石のようなカフェである。こぢんまりとしながらも静かな雰囲気の中で、様々なケーキとコーヒーを楽しむことができる。韓屋の建物をリモデリングした店内は席数は多くないが、感性的なインテリアで雰囲気を醸し出しており、庭にはテラス席も用意されている。隅々まで手入れされており、写真撮影にぴったりである。ダルゴナケーキがシグネチャーメニューとして大人気である。天文台に行く前にパンやドリンクを楽しむのに良く、白雲渓谷で水遊びをしたりドライブ途中に立ち寄るのにも良い。

zh.addr: 江原特別自治道華川郡天文台길 8
zh.overview: 這是一間宛如隱藏寶石般的咖啡廳，位於華川曹景哲天文台入口處。在精緻而寧靜的氛圍中，您可以品嚐到各式蛋糕與咖啡。由傳統韓屋改建而成的內部空間雖不大，但充滿情感的室內裝潢營造出獨特氛圍，庭院也備有戶外座位。每個角落都打理得十分用心，非常適合拍照留念。焦糖餅蛋糕是店內的人氣招牌餐點。前往天文台前很適合來這裡享用麵包與飲品，或是在白雲溪谷戲水、開車兜風途中順道小憩。

en.title: Haetgol Makguksu
en.overview: Located in Sanae-myeon, Hwacheon-gun, this makguksu (buckwheat noodles) restaurant has only 4 tables. Though small, it boasts a 50-year tradition and is run by an elderly couple. Upon ordering, you can watch the elderly owner press the noodles directly from the noodle press. The restaurant's makguksu features easily breakable noodles and a mild style reminiscent of Pyongyang naengmyeon. It can be enjoyed with either water or mixed style by pouring broth to your liking. Side dishes like suyuk (boiled pork slices), acorn jelly, and handmade tofu pair wonderfully together.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialty: Makguksu · Suyuk, Handmade Tofu, Acorn Jelly

en.title: Hwacheon Eojuktang
en.overview: A renowned restaurant specializing in Hwacheon's local delicacy, eojuktang (spicy fish porridge soup), whose taste has been certified in various culinary competitions. The eojuk, simmered in a broth infused with various herbal medicines such as astragalus root, Solomon's seal, cinnamon, kudzu, wild mountain ginseng, and licorice, is superb. It draws many visitors seeking a summer health tonic, and its uniquely thick potato pancakes are also a favorite. From the nature-surrounded restaurant entrance to the courtyard and interior, musical instruments and vintage props collected by the owner over a long time highlight the restaurant's unique character.

zh.title: 華川雜魚粥湯

en.title: Neung-gasa Temple
en.addr: 21, Palbong-gil, Jeomam-myeon, Goheung-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City
en.overview: Neung-gasa Temple, a branch temple of Songgwangsa Temple (the head temple of the 21st Parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism), is one of the four major temples in the Honam region, boasting a large scale on flat terrain. Originally founded in 417 by Buddhist Monk Ado and named Bohyeonsa, it was completely burned down during the Japanese Invasions of Korea, then reconstructed in 1644 (the 22nd year of King Injo's reign of the Joseon Dynasty) by Master Byeokcheon Jeonghyeon, who renamed it Neung-gasa. Master Byeokcheon was originally practicing asceticism at Jirisan Mountain at the age of 90 when a Buddha appeared in his dream and gave him a revelation to build a temple to save all sentient beings.

paragraphs: Neung-gasa Temple, a branch temple of Songgwangsa Temple (the head temple of the 21st Parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism), is one of the four major temples in the Honam region, boasting a large scale on flat terrain. Originally founded in 417 by Buddhist Monk Ado and named Bohyeonsa, it was completely burned down during the Japanese Invasions of Korea, then reconstructed in 1644 (the 22nd year of King Injo's reign of the Joseon Dynasty) by Master Byeokcheon Jeonghyeon, who renamed it Neung-gasa. Master Byeokcheon was originally practicing asceticism at Jirisan Mountain at the age of 90 when a Buddha appeared in his dream and gave him a revelation to build a temple to save all sentient beings, leading him to newly construct Neung-gasa here.

Existing temple buildings include Daeungjeon Hall (Treasures No. 1307), which features a 5-bay front, 3-bay side, and a hip-and-gable roof, as well as Eungjingak Hall, the bell pavilion, Cheonwangmun Gate, and monks' quarters. Neung-gasa runs a Temple Stay program for southern sea meditation travel. Situated at the foot of Palyeongsan Mountain, it allows visitors to explore the mountain, and right past the temple is the adjacent Palyeongsan Auto Camping Ground.

en.title: Heungyang eupseong Fortress Site & Okhari Honggyo Bridge in Goheung
en.addr: Okhari, Goheung-eup, Goheung-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City
en.overview: The Heungyang eupseong Fortress Site is where the Heungyang-hyeon district office was located from its establishment in 1441 until its administrative name was changed to Goheung-gun in 1914, leaving traces of the fortress built during the Heungyang-hyeon period throughout Goheung-eup. Walking up the sloped village road behind the Goheung Jonsimdang History and Culture Park, you can see remnants of the fortress walls on the upper ridge. The site preserves fortress gates, walls, defensive bastions (chiseong), and wells, playing a crucial role in understanding the history and culture of Goheung-gun.

paragraphs: The Heungyang eupseong Fortress Site is where the Heungyang-hyeon district office was located from its establishment in 1441 until its administrative name was changed to Goheung-gun in 1914, leaving traces of the fortress built during the Heungyang-hyeon period throughout Goheung-eup. Walking up the sloped village road behind the Goheung Jonsimdang History and Culture Park, you can see remnants of the fortress walls on the upper ridge. The site preserves fortress gates, walls, defensive bastions (chiseong), and wells, playing a crucial role in understanding the history and culture of Goheung-gun. The Okhari Honggyo Bridge in Goheung is a rainbow-shaped stone bridge constructed during the late Joseon Dynasty. Designated as a Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City Tangible Cultural Heritage, there are two rainbow bridges flowing through Okhari. The upper bridge is relatively large, featuring a dragon head carved on the front of the rainbow shape and a dragon tail on the reverse side.

The lower bridge is larger in scale than the upper one. While similar in shape, it differs from the front bridge in that a dragon head is attached to the center of the underside ceiling. Both bridges were built during the late Joseon Dynasty and are grand in scale. Currently, the tops of both bridges are much higher than the ground level, which is due to changes in the topography over later generations.

下の紅교は上の橋より規模が大きい。形は上のものと似ているが、龍の頭が橋の下側の天井の中央に取り付けられている点が前の紅교とは異なる。どちらの橋も朝鮮時代後기에作られたもので、規模が大きく雄大である。現在、両橋の頂上が地面よりもはるかに高いが、これは後代に下るにつれて地形が変わったためである。

en.title: Deokheung Beach
en.addr: Deokheung-ri, Dongil-myeon, Goheung-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City
en.overview: Deokheung Beach is located on Naenarodo Island in the southeastern part of the Goheung Peninsula. Centuries-old old pine trees growing on rock banks along the coastline provide cool shade, and the wide beach is covered with fine sand. With its gentle slope, it is gaining spotlight as a family summer resort. Because it is relatively lesser-known, it is a great spot for those seeking a quiet getaway, and is also called Deokheung Haebyeon.

en.overview: Located on Geogeumdo Island, Jeokdaebong Peak (592m above sea level) is the second highest peak in Goheung-gun after Palyeongsan Mountain. Unlike its broad and gentle mountain shape, it boasts exceptionally stunning views. Standing at the summit, the seas and islands around Wando to the west, Geomundo to the south, and Yeosu to the east come into view at a glance. On a clear day, the view is so clear that even Jeju Island can be seen in the distance. Due to these geographical characteristics, a large beacon mound measuring 34 meters in circumference and 7 meters in diameter sits at the summit, which was used during the Joseon Dynasty to transmit emergency signals such as invasions by Japanese raiders.
en.pull_quote: Located on Geogeumdo Island, Jeokdaebong Peak (592m above sea level) is the second highest peak in Goheung-gun after Palyeongsan Mountain, boasting exceptionally stunning views...
paragraphs: Located on Geogeumdo Island, Jeokdaebong Peak (592m above sea level) is the second highest peak in Goheung-gun after Palyeongsan Mountain. Unlike its broad and gentle mountain shape, it boasts exceptionally stunning views. Standing at the summit, the seas and islands around Wando to the west, Geomundo to the south, and Yeosu to the east come into view at a glance. On a clear day, the view is so clear that even Jeju Island can be seen in the distance. Due to these geographical characteristics, a large beacon mound measuring 34 meters in circumference and 7 meters in diameter sits at the summit, which was used during the Joseon Dynasty to transmit emergency signals such as invasions by Japanese raiders.

The foothills of Jeokdaebong are also known to be the site of a Mokjangseong (Joseon-era ranch fortress). It is recorded as a tax ranch where a 30-ri long fortress was built around Jeokdaebong to raise 116 horses. Traces of the ranch fortress still remain in various places along the forest road connecting Seokjeong-ri and Eojeon-ri, crossing Geogeumdo from north to south. Nearby tourist attractions around Jeokdaebong include Ikgeum Beach in the southern part of Geogeumdo, where the water is so clear that seafood can be seen 2 to 3 meters deep, and Geogeum Ecological Forest on the southeastern foothills of Jeokdaebong.

paragraphs: 巨金島に位置し、高興郡では八影山に次いで高い赤大峰（標高592m）は、どっしりとした山容とは異なり、展望が非常に優れた山である。山頂に立つと、西側に莞島、南側に巨文島、東側に麗水一帯の海や島が一望できるだけでなく、天気が良ければ遠く済州島が見えるほど展望が良い。このような地形的特徴のため、赤大峰の山頂には朝鮮時代に倭寇の侵入などの非常事態を伝達していた周囲34メートル、直径7メートルの大きな烽火台が山頂にある。
赤大峰のふもとはまた、朝鮮時代の牧場城があった場所として知られている。赤大峰を中心に30里の長さの城を築き、馬116頭を育てた税納の牧場として伝えられている。巨金島の南北を縦断して石井里と漁田里を結ぶ林道のあちこちに牧場城の痕跡が今も残っている。赤大峰周辺の観光地としては、巨金島の南側に水深2〜3mの底の海産物が見えるほど水が綺麗な益金海水浴場があり、赤大峰の東南側のふもとに巨金生態の森がある。

paragraphs: 位於巨金島上的赤大峰（海拔592公尺）是高興郡內僅次於八영山的高峰，與平緩的山勢不同，是一座視野極佳的山峰。站在山頂上，西側的莞島、南側的巨文島、東側麗水一帶的海景與島嶼盡收眼底，天氣好的話甚至能遠眺濟州島，視野堪稱一流。由於這種獨特的地理特徵，赤大峰山頂上建有周長34公尺、直徑7公尺的大型烽火臺，在朝鮮時代用於傳遞倭寇入侵等緊急狀況。

paragraphs: Dongbang Gisikdang is located in Gwayeok-myeon, Goheung-gun. This place exclusively serves thinly sliced pork belly (daepae samgyeopsal) set meals. With its excellent value for money, even solo travelers can enjoy a hearty meal without burden. Dongbang Gisikdang's bulgogi set meal provides a separate grill so you can cook it yourself. Alongside the thinly sliced pork belly, twelve delicious side dishes are served.

While pork belly is delicious wrapped in ssam vegetables with ssamjang, it tastes even better when accompanied by the side dishes served alongside. The side dishes mainly consist of pickled vegetables (jangajji) and kimchi. In particular, the onion kimchi available exclusively at Dongbang Gisikdang is as refreshing and flavorful as water kimchi, offering a clean finish when eaten with the meat. Additionally, the blue crab stew (kkotge-jjigae) is a unique specialty only tasted here. The broth, flavored with doenjang (soybean paste) and a hint of red pepper powder, contains a large piece of blue crab and tofu. Because green onions and onions provide the foundational broth flavor, it is spicy yet refreshing and clean.

paragraphs: 高興郡過駅面に位置する東方気士食堂。ここはテペサムギョプサル（極薄切り豚バラ肉）の定食のみを販売している。コスパが素晴らしく、一人旅の旅行者でも気軽に食べることができる。東方気士食堂のプルコギ定食は、自分で焼いて食べられるように鉄板が別に出される。テペサムギョプサルの脇には、12種類の美味しいパンチャン（おかず）が並ぶ。

サムギョプサルはサンチュなどの包み野菜に包んでサムジャンをつけて食べるのも美味しいが、もっと美味しく食べたいなら一緒に提供されるパンチャンを添えて食べるのが良い。パンチャンは主にチャンアッチ（醤油漬け）類とキムチが中心であり、特に東方気士食堂でしか味わえないタマネギキムチは水キムチのように爽やかで旨味があり、肉と一緒に食べるとすっきりとした後味を感じることができる。また、ワタリガニのチゲも東方気士食堂でのみ味わえる名物だ。テンジャンと少量の唐辛子粉などで出汁をとったチゲの中には、大きめのワタリガニのぶつ切りと豆腐が入っている。ネギやタマネギなどが基本のスープの味を出しているため、ピリ辛でありながらも爽やかですっきりとしている。

paragraphs: 位於高興郡過역면的東方騎士食堂，這裡只販售薄切五花肉定食。性價比極高，即使是獨旅遊客也能毫無負擔地享用。東方騎士食堂的烤肉定食會另外提供烤盤讓客人自己動手烤。薄切五花肉旁擺滿了十二種美味的小菜。

en.overview: If you are curious about the taste of Goheung, we recommend visiting Jungang Sikdang in Dohwa-myeon, which has maintained a consistent flavor for 38 years. Jungang Sikdang specializes in seafood set meals featuring various seafood, along with refreshing and clean blue crab soup (kkotge-tang), and spicy bulnak (octopus and bulgogi). Here, you can also taste conger eel (baemjangteo) shabu-shabu, raw fish, seasoned raw fish salad, and savory, mild wild freshwater eel all at once.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialty: Special Set Meal · Blue Crab Soup / Bulnak / Wild Freshwater Eel, etc.
paragraphs: If you are curious about the taste of Goheung, we recommend visiting Jungang Sikdang in Dohwa-myeon, which has maintained a consistent flavor for 38 years. Jungang Sikdang specializes in seafood set meals featuring various seafood, along with refreshing and clean blue crab soup (kkotge-tang), and spicy bulnak (octopus and bulgogi). Here, you can also taste conger eel (baemjangteo) shabu-shabu, raw fish, seasoned raw fish salad, and savory, mild wild freshwater eel all at once. The signature seafood set meal is divided into special, medium, and regular set meals. Customers mostly order the medium set meal, which includes conger eel sashimi, gizzard shad sashimi, parboiled octopus, steamed croaker, fermented skate samhap, and king prawns, accompanied by various types of kimchi such as aged kimchi (mgeunji) and salted seafood (jeotgal) which pair wonderfully with the raw fish.

Even the side dishes served go exceptionally well with the raw fish. Jungang Sikdang hides a special flavor you cannot experience anywhere else: dipping conger eel sashimi in citron (yuja) ade/syrup and dried conger eel steamed dish made exclusively with conger eels that cannot be served fresh to customers. The refreshing citron syrup and savory seafood decorate your mouth with a fresh yet mild harmony.

paragraphs: Gwayeok Gisiknim Sikdang serves a hearty set meal at a reasonable price, consisting of everyone's favorite pork belly, well-cooked savory rice, and thirteen side dishes. It features a single menu item: pork belly set meal. So many side dishes and pork belly are served that the table legs practically shake. The pork belly, which looks fresh even to the naked eye, is generously topped with chives and carrots.

The reason the meat is grilled with chives is that the unique aroma of chives neutralizes the gamey odor of the pork belly. While it is delicious to wrap well-grilled meat in fresh ssam vegetables with ssamjang, it is also great when paired with the side dishes. The side dishes served immediately upon ordering include blue crab soy-sauce jangajji, seasoned spicy crab, perilla leaf kimchi, slightly aged kimchi, and stuffed cucumber kimchi. These are not just filler side dishes, but every single one of them is delicious. It has been featured on SBS and MBC programs.

ja.pull_quote: 代表的な名物：サムギョプサル定食
paragraphs: 過駅気士様食堂は、誰もが好きなサムギョプサルと上手に炊き上げた味わい深いご飯、13種類のパンチャンで構成されたボリューム満点の定食を手頃な価格で提供している。サムギョプサル定食の単品メニューのみである。テーブルの足が揺れるほど数多くのおかずとサムギョプサルが出てくる。見た目にも新鮮に見えるサムギョプサルにニラとニンジンがたっぷりと乗せられている。

肉をニラと一緒に焼く理由は、ニラが持つ特有の香りがサムギョプサルの獣臭さを消してくれるからだ。よく焼けた肉を新鮮な包み野菜にサムジャンをつけて包んで食べるのも良いが、パンチャンと一緒に添えて食べても美味しい。肉と一緒に注文と同時に提供されるおかずは、ワタリガニの醤油漬け、ヤンニョムケジャン、エゴマの葉のキムチ、少し熟したキムチ、オイソバギ（きゅうりのキムチ）などであるが、数だけを揃えたパンチャンではなく、一つ一つがすべて美味しい。SBSやMBCの番組で紹介されたことがある。

en.title: Korean Traditional Food Culture Experience Center (Jeonggangwon)
en.overview: Founded by Korean food researcher Cho Jung-gang, the Korean Traditional Food Culture Experience Center was established to promote and offer hands-on experiences with traditional Korean food culture. Located in Yongpyong-myeon, Pyeongchang-gun, it showcases traditional hanok stays, cooking classes, and formal Korean table d'hôte (hanjeongsik) to spread the taste and style of Korea. Nestled in an auspicious site surrounded by Mt. Geumgangsan's foothills and the flowing Geumgang Valley, the accommodation is divided into traditional hanok and modern rooms. The tiled hanok features traditional ondol flooring and views of Mt. Geumgangsan.

Located in Yongpyong-myeon, Pyeongchang-gun, it showcases traditional hanok stays, cooking classes, and formal Korean table d'hôte (hanjeongsik) to spread the taste and style of Korea. Nestled in an auspicious site surrounded by Mt. Geumgangsan's foothills and the flowing Geumgang Valley, the accommodation is divided into traditional hanok and modern rooms. The tiled hanok features traditional ondol flooring and refreshing views of Mt. Geumgangsan.

The new building, overlooking the Geumgang Valley, offers condo-style rooms. Traditional cooking classes are popular among both Koreans and international visitors. Participants can handcraft and taste traditional Korean dishes such as bibimbap, gochujang (chili paste), kimchi, and mackerel ssamjang. The food is made with ingredients carefully sourced and grown by Jeonggangwon, including fermented sauces from over 500 jars in the yard and vegetables harvested from the garden. Visitors can also check out the hanok experience hall to dress up and take photos in hanok, and the food museum showcasing vintage farm implements and kitchen utensils.

en.title: Odaesan National Park
en.overview: Designated as the country's 11th national park in 1975, Odaesan National Park spans an area of 327.904 ㎢. With Birobong Peak (1,563m above sea level) as its main peak, five grand peaks including Dongdaesan (1,434m), Durobong (1,422m), Sangwangbong (1,491m), and Holyeongbong (1,561m) stand like a folding screen. Below Noinbong Peak (1,338m), which breaks off to the east, lies the breathtaking Sogeumgangsan Scenic Area. To the west sits Mt. Gyebangsan (1,577m), renowned for its stunning snowscapes.

Below Noinbong Peak (1,338m), which breaks off to the east, lies the breathtaking Sogeumgangsan Scenic Area.

en.title: Mt. Cheongoksan (Pyeongchang)
en.overview: Named after the abundant wild cheongok greens growing natively in the area, Mt. Cheongoksan stands 1,256m above sea level and features a relatively flat ridge boasting the famous 'Yukbaekmajigi' plateau at its peak. The hike takes about 5 hours, and a headquarters for Samshin (Three Spirits) belief is located near the summit. Next to the Yukbaekmajigi Cheongoksan Observatory, a hiking trail leads to the summit, divided into a walking path and a barrier-free wooden deck sharing trail.

Cheongoksan stands 1,256m above sea level and features a relatively flat ridge boasting the famous 'Yukbaekmajigi' plateau at its peak. The hike takes about 5 hours, and a headquarters for Samshin (Three Spirits) belief is located near the summit. Next to the Yukbaekmajigi Cheongoksan Observatory, a hiking trail leads to the summit, divided into a walking path and a barrier-free wooden deck sharing trail.

The barrier-free sharing trail spans a total of 760m, allowing wheelchair and stroller users to ascend to the summit of Mt. Cheongoksan. It takes about 20 minutes on foot from the observatory to reach the top. The highland plains of Cheongoksan cultivate highland vegetables such as radishes and cabbages; in particular, mid-season radishes are famous for their pear-like sweetness. Nearby attractions include Cheongoksan Dokkaebi (Goblin) Road, Saneomi Ranch, and Suha Valley.

en.title: Naeunggyegok Valley
en.overview: Located in Naeung-ri, Pyeongchang-eup, Naeunggyegok Valley is a wide valley featuring abundant water as the Pyeongchanggang River meanders in an S-shape. Steep cliffs interspersed with the river create exceptionally stunning scenery. Sandy patches and pebbles spread throughout make it an ideal spot for water play and camping. With its wide river and crystal-clear waters teeming with native freshwater fish like mandarin fish, torrent catfish, and catfish, as well as freshwater snails, it is a wonderful place for fishing and enjoying nature. Nearby guesthouses offer rural experience programs such as picking chili peppers and digging potatoes.

en.title: Sangwonssa Temple (Odaesan)
en.overview: Sangwonssa Temple is a millennium-old temple located near Woljeongsa Temple, serving as a branch temple of Woljeongsa, the head temple of the 4th District of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. Known to have been founded by Monk Jajang during the reign of Queen Seondeok of Silla, it was actually reconstructed by King Seongdeok in 705 and named Jinyeowon. It is the only temple in the country housing a statue of Munsu Bodhisattva (Manjusri) and is famous for the anecdote where King Sejo visited to cure his skin disease and was healed. The current temple was rebuilt following a fire in 1946, leaving no ancient buildings except for Yeongsanjeon Hall. It preserves precious cultural heritage including a National Treasure bronze bell, a Munsu Child Bodhisattva statue, a Munsu Bodhisattva statue, and King Sejo's handwritten restoration appeal, and is ideal to visit along the 9km Sunjae-gil trail starting from Woljeongsa.

ja.addr: 江原特別自治道平昌郡珍部面五台山路1211-50
ja.overview: 上願寺は、大韓仏教曹渓宗第4教区の本寺である月精寺の末寺であり、月精寺の近隣に位置する千年の古刹です。新羅の善徳女王の時代に慈蔵律師によって建てられたと伝えられていますが、実際には聖徳王が705年に寺を重創し、真如院と呼びました。国内で唯一、文殊菩薩像を祀る寺院であり、世祖が皮膚病を治すために訪れて病気が治ったというエピソードでも有名です。現在の寺院は1946年の火災以降に再建されたもので、霊山殿を除けば古い建物は残っていません。国宝の銅鐘、文殊童子像、文殊菩薩像、世祖の直筆による重創勧善文など貴重な文化遺産を所蔵しており、月精寺から始まる9kmの善財路に沿って訪れるのに適しています。

zh.addr: 江原特別自治道平昌郡珍部面五台山路 1211-50

en.title: Woljeongsa Temple & Fir Tree Forest
en.overview: Woljeongsa Temple was founded in 643 (the 12th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla) by Monk Jajang on Mt. Odaesan, an entire mountain designated as a Buddhist sanctuary. As the head temple of the 4th District of the Jogye Order, it oversees some 60 temples and 8 hermitages, holding countless cultural treasures including the National Treasure Octagonal Nine-Story Stone Pagoda, and Treasures such as the Seated Stone Bodhisattva and Seated Wooden Munsu Child Bodhisattva of Woljeongsa. A roughly 1km stretch from Woljeongsa's Iljumun Gate to Geumganggyo Bridge unfolds into a magnificent fir tree forest housing about 1,700 fir trees.

paragraphs: Woljeongsa Temple was founded in 643 (the 12th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla) by Monk Jajang on Mt. Odaesan, an entire mountain designated as a Buddhist sanctuary. As the head temple of the 4th District of the Jogye Order, it oversees some 60 temples and 8 hermitages, holding countless cultural treasures including the National Treasure Octagonal Nine-Story Stone Pagoda, and Treasures such as the Seated Stone Bodhisattva and Seated Wooden Munsu Child Bodhisattva of Woljeongsa. A roughly 1km stretch from Woljeongsa's Iljumun Gate to Geumganggyo Bridge unfolds into a magnificent fir tree forest housing about 1,700 fir trees.

The fir tree forest is a representative tourist attraction of the millennium-old temple Woljeongsa, loved by visitors across all four seasons, making it a must-visit spot when coming to Woljeongsa. Woljeongsa operates Templestay programs divided into rest-oriented and experience-oriented types, allowing visitors to leave the secular world behind and recharge their weary bodies and minds deep in the mountains. Alongside Templestay, there is the Woljeongsa Chulga School for ordinary people to experience the life of a novice monk. Additionally, the Odaesan Meditation Village (OMV), spanning approximately 99,170㎡—about 14 times the size of a soccer field—features accommodations, cultural experience facilities, restaurants, gardens, and forest trails to help escape daily life.

en.title: Moon Garden
en.addr: 64 Oryugol-gil, Gyegok-myeon, Haenam-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City
en.overview: Located in Seongjin-ri, Gyegok-myeon, Haenam-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City, Moon Garden is embraced by Oryuje Reservoir and overlooked by Mt. Heukseoksan. About 50 years ago, barren land where earth and stone were excavated for a reservoir embankment was cultivated into fields and orchards, which were later cleared for a home site and planted with various saplings to create the current garden. Planted with around 200 species of trees and flowers, it is a naturalistic garden where visitors can beautifully experience changing seasons.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delicacies: Strawberry Latte · Berry Matcha Latte / Peach Berry Iced Tea / Hwangchil Extract Handmade Tea / Americano, etc.

Planted with around 200 species of trees and flowers, it is a naturalistic garden where visitors can beautifully experience changing seasons, offering views of Mt. zh.title: Moon Garden 月亮花園
zh.addr: 全羅南道光州統合市海南郡 계곡면 誤謬골길 64
zh.overview: 位於全羅南道光州統合市海南郡溪谷面星津里的「Moon Garden」，被誤謬貯水池環抱，並由黑石山所俯瞰。大約50年前，這裡曾因水庫堤壩工程挖取土石而成為荒地，後來被開墾為農田與果園，並在打地基、種植各種樹苗後打造成現今的花園。園內種植了約200種樹木與花卉，是一座能深刻感受四季變化的自然主義花園。周邊風光極其優美，夏天雨天時可欣賞變成黑石、冬天雪天時可欣賞變成白石的陸地盡頭海南名山——黑石山。

Dadohaehaesang National Park is divided into 8 districts depending on the region (Heuksan/Hongdo, Bigeum/Dochodo, Jodo, Soan/Cheongsando, Geomun/Baekdo, Narodo, Geumodo, and Palyeongsan districts).

The park and its surroundings consist of various rock formations formed by Paleozoic schist and gneiss, Mesozoic Gyeongsang Basin sedimentary layers, and volcanic activity such as tuff and granite. Geological landmarks where these features can be observed include Mulneomimok in Geomundo Island and Heuksando Island. It is also an excellent place to observe sea cliffs, a typical coastal landform of the Korean Peninsula. (Source: Korea National Park Service)

paragraphs: Myodangdo is an island attached to Gogeumdo Island, located about 20ri (approx. 8km) away. On February 17, 1598 (the 31st year of King Seonjo's reign), the last year of the Jeongyu War, Admiral Yi Sun-sin led a naval force of about 8,000 troops from Gohado Island (now Chungmu-dong, Mokpo-si) to establish a camp here. On July 16 of that year, General Chen Lin arrived in Gogeumdo with 5,000 naval troops as reinforcement from Ming China, built Gwanwangmyo Shrine to pray for victory, and formed an allied front to repel Japanese invaders.

In particular, this location served as a naval stronghold. After Admiral Yi moved his camp to Gogeumdo, Japanese forces—which had been slaughtering and pillaging in Jangheung and Goheung—fled toward Suncheon, resulting in fewer battles. The Admiral focused more time and effort on building the main headquarters and taking care of refugees. Yu Seong-ryong wrote in 'Jingbirok' (The Book of Corrections): 'When the Admiral arrived in Gogeumdo, not only was the military might majestic, but civilians on the island numbered tens of thousands of households, ten times that of the Hansando era.' en.pull_quote: Representative Specialty: Haetae Jeongsik
paragraphs: Located in Gangjin, a region renowned for Namdo-style Korean set meals, Haetae Sikdang is a representative local restaurant that serves healthy meals prepared with ingredients nurtured by pristine nature. Featured in Yu Hong-jun's travelogue 'My Cultural Heritage Tour', this traditional Namdo restaurant offers the Haetae Jeongsik (set meal) for 1 to 4 people. The dishes changes depending on the season, weather, and market availability, allowing visitors to enjoy fresh seasonal flavors.

Spring brings Gangjin's specialty giant surf clams; summer features freshwater eel; gizzard shad and raw spot prawns take center stage in autumn; and maseengi (hair seaweed) soup warms up the winter. To preserve the freshness and natural flavors of the ingredients, dishes are prepared with minimal seasoning. The signature soybean paste stew and bulgogi, which have remained consistently delicious over the years, offer flavors unique to Haetae Sikdang. Located adjacent to the Gangjin Intercity Bus Terminal, it is also about a 5-minute walk from the birthplace of poet Yeongrang.

en.pull_quote: Duryunsan is a scenic tourist destination rich in temples and historical sites, standing 700 meters tall at the southern tip of the Korean Peninsula. Its forests of subtropical evergreen and temperate deciduous trees...
paragraphs: Rising 700 meters high at the southern tip of the Korean Peninsula, Duryunsan is a scenic tourist destination rich in temples and historical sites. It holds significant botanical value as a forest of subtropical evergreen broad-leaved trees and temperate deciduous broad-leaved trees. It is also a provincial park in Jeonnam Gwangju Metropolitan City that embraces Daeheungsa Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Formed by eight rocky peaks, Duryunsan features a lotus-shaped mountain topography. Its ridge is formed by eight peaks, including Garyunbong, Duryunbong, Gokgebong, and Noseungbong.

These eight peaks form a rounded circle, resembling a giant holding up their right hand toward the South Sea. Duryunsan was also historically called Daedunsan; this name is interpreted as deriving from 'Handeum' (combining 'deum' meaning mountain and the modifier 'han' meaning big), which evolved into Daedeum and then Daedun. The ridge connecting Daedun Mountain to the main peak and the Changchungdong Valley leading into Daeheungsa Temple form the center of the provincial park. Covered in lush silver grass, the summits of the eight large and small peaks offer panoramic views of the West and South Seas dotted with islands. paragraphs: Located in front of Sagu Village along the coastal road from Ttangkkeun Galdu to Namchang, Sagumi Beach preserves the pristine freshness of an untouched ocean. Untouched by heavy development, it is a great spot for families to enjoy a quiet and relaxing getaway.

In the distance, the setting sun to the left of Ttangkkeun Sajabong Peak paints the small islands of the Dadohae archipelago in brilliant shades of red.
