en.pull_quote: Situated on the western side of Dalmasan Mountain (489m), often called the Geumgangsan Mountain of the southern region, Mihwangsa is the southernmost mainland temple in Korea, founded in 749...
paragraphs: Situated on the western side of Dalmasan Mountain (489m), often called the Geumgangsan Mountain of the southern region, Mihwangsa is the southernmost mainland Buddhist temple in Korea, founded in the 8th year of King Gyeongdeok's reign (749) during the Silla Dynasty. Once prosperous enough to oversee 12 hermitages, it gradually declined after monks who set out to restore the temple 100 years ago suffered a disaster at sea. Left vacant for a long time, the temple began to breathe again in 1989 when monks Jiun, Hyeongong, and Geumgang arrived. Following a decade of restoration projects, buildings such as Myeongbujeon Hall, Daeungbojeon Hall (a Treasure), and Eungjingak Hall (a Treasure) now stand orderly, renewing its status as one of Korea's most beautiful temples.

Mihwangsa always offers a fantastic landscape blending the sunset over the West Sea with the bizarre rocks of Dalmasan Mountain. Notably, the foundation stones of Daeungbojeon Hall feature rare carvings of marine creatures like turtles and crabs, adding to the intrigue. At the Budo (stupa) field, reached by a 10-minute walk along the forest path, you can also encounter simple carvings of child monks and goblin faces. The mountain peak is about a 1-hour walk away, offering panoramic views of the Dadohae archipelago...

paragraphs: Located on Duryunsan Mountain, Daeheungsa is a temple reportedly founded by Monk Ado during the 22nd year of King Seongwang of Baekje. In 2018, it was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site under the name 'Sansa, Buddhist Mountain Monasteries in Korea'. Daeheungsa is a temple where the spirit of patriotic Buddhism lives on; during the Imjin War, it served as the general headquarters for the monk-soldier army led by Grand Master Seosan. Furthermore, Monk Cho-ui, believing that the truth of Buddhism and the joy of meditation are dissolved within tea,

entered the valley of Daeheungsa, built Iljiam Hermitage, and devoted himself solely to ascetic practice for over 40 years. This established Daeheungsa as the sacred site of Korea's tea culture. Daeheungsa houses national treasures such as the Seated Stone Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva at Bukmireukam Hermitage, while the Grand Master Seosan Relics Museum preserves items bestowed by King Seonjo, including jade rice bowls, jade bowls, Seosan's own calligraphy, a palanquin, shoes, and Buddhist scriptures written in gold and silver.

en.pull_quote: Meaning 'End of the Land' where the sea and sky meet, Ttangkkeun is where the Baekdudaegan mountain range runs southward and makes its final surge before stopping—the start and end of Baekdudaegan...
paragraphs: Meaning 'End of the Land' where the sea and sky meet, Ttangkkeun is where the Baekdudaegan mountain range runs southward and makes its final surge before stopping—marking both the beginning and the end of the Baekdudaegan. It is also the place where the energy (gi) of the Korean Peninsula is most densely gathered. Ancient sages and artists considered it a sacred place to open the gates of heaven with that energy and offer sacred rituals.

Therefore, stories have been passed down in Ttangkkeun Village that if you make a wish toward the sky and sea, your wish will come true and hope will blossom. Because of this symbolism, many tourists from all over the country visit Ttangkkeun. It serves as the starting point for national pilgrimages and an important strategic hub and transit route for marine culture.

en.title: Mahan Cultural Park
en.overview: Mahan Cultural Park was created to offer a glimpse into the unique ancient history of the Yeongsan River basin by helping visitors understand the ancient jar coffins scattered throughout the region. The Tomb Exploration Museum is themed around the myth of birth from an egg, featuring restored models of the jar coffin excavation process and burial styles. When illuminated at night, it creates a fantastic spaceship-like atmosphere. The exterior of the exhibition hall is shaped like a jar coffin, and the inside houses a video hall showing various films and an administrative office. The Namhae Watchtower serves as an observatory offering panoramic views of the Sampo River streams, Wolchulsan Mountain, Mongdan in Muan, and Donggang in Naju. Inside the Mongjeon of the Tomb Exploration Museum, the excavation site of the Naedong-ri Chobung-gol Ancient Tomb Cluster is recreated, along with a fun artifact-hunting play space for children. The Mahan confederacy consisted of 54 states distributed across the central-southern region of the Korean Peninsula from the 3rd–2nd centuries BCE to the late 5th–early 6th centuries CE, until the remaining forces in the Yeongsan River basin were absorbed by Baekje in the mid-6th century.

ja.overview: 馬韓文化公園は、栄山江（ヨンサンガン）流域に点在する古代の甕棺墓（かめかんぼ）を理解し、栄山江流域ならではの独自性に満ちた古代史を展望するために作られました。古墳探査館は卵生神話をモチーフにしており、内部には甕棺墓の発掘過程や遺体の埋葬形態が模型で復元されています。夜間にライトアップされると、宇宙船のような幻想的な雰囲気を醸し出します。展示館の外観は甕棺の形状をイメージしており、内部には各種映像を上映する映像ホールと管理事務所があります。南海櫓は、三浦江（サンポガン）の水流、月出山（ウォルチュルサン）、務安（ムアン）のモンダン、羅州（ナジュ）の東江（トングァン）を一望できる展望台です。古墳探査館のモンジョン内部には、内洞里（ネドンリ）草墳谷（チョブンゴル）古墳群の出土当時の様子が再現されており、子どもたちのための遺物探し体験スペースがあります。馬韓は、紀元前3〜2世紀から紀元後5世紀末〜6世紀初めにかけて我が国の中南部地域に54か国が点在し、6世紀半ばに栄山江流域に残っていた残存勢力まで百済に吸収された古代国家です。

en.title: Yeongam Hyanggyo (Confucian School)
en.overview: Yeongam Hyanggyo was first established in 1420 (the 2nd year of King Sejong's reign in the Joseon Dynasty). After being burned down during the Japanese Invasions of Korea and a fire in 1918, it was rebuilt, only to suffer the hardship of being completely destroyed once again during the Korean War. The current buildings include the Daeseongjeon Shrine reconstructed in 1951, the Dongjae and Seojae student dormitories in 1963, and the Myeongnyundang Lecture Hall in 1969, with the remaining structures built sequentially afterward. The layout uniquely features the educational and ritual spaces arranged side by side on the east and west.

paragraphs: Yeongam Hyanggyo was first established in 1420 (the 2nd year of King Sejong's reign in the Joseon Dynasty). After being burned down during the Japanese Invasions of Korea and a fire in 1918, it was rebuilt, only to suffer the hardship of being completely destroyed once again during the Korean War. The current buildings include the Daeseongjeon Shrine reconstructed in 1951, the Dongjae and Seojae student dormitories in 1963, and the Myeongnyundang Lecture Hall in 1969, with the remaining structures built sequentially afterward.

The layout uniquely features the educational and ritual spaces arranged side by side on the east and west. Myeongnyundang, the lecture hall where students gathered to study, was built with a scale of 4 bays in the front and 2 bays on the sides. Daeseongjeon, which enshrines the ancestral tablets of Confucius and other sages of China and Korea, is decorated with modest elegance. In addition, there is a Naesammun Gate separating the two spaces and a neat, square pond.

en.title: Dogapsa Temple
en.overview: Nestled on a wide mountain slope facing Jujibong Peak with Dogapbong Peak on the southern side of Wolchulsan Mountain—often called the 'Mount Geumgang of the Southern Province'—Dogapsa Temple is a historic Buddhist sanctuary originated when National Master Doseon, one of the four great eminent monks of Silla, grandly rebuilt the original Munsuasa Temple. In 1456 (the 2nd year of King Sejo's reign in Joseon), Royal Preceptor Sumi built an enormous complex consisting of 966 halls, pavilions, and 12 hermitages by royal command. Generations of eminent monks and masters, including Master Yeondam, Master Heoju, and Master Cho-ui, resided here to spread the true principles of enlightenment, establishing Dogapsa as a vibrant sanctuary where spiritual practice and teachings never cease.

paragraphs: Nestled on a wide mountain slope facing Jujibong Peak with Dogapbong Peak on the southern side of Wolchulsan Mountain—often called the 'Mount Geumgang of the Southern Province'—Dogapsa Temple is a historic Buddhist sanctuary originated when National Master Doseon, one of the four great eminent monks of Silla, grandly rebuilt the original Munsuasa Temple. In 1456 (the 2nd year of King Sejo's reign in Joseon), Royal Preceptor Sumi built an enormous complex consisting of 966 halls, pavilions, and 12 hermitages by royal command. Generations of eminent monks and masters, including Master Yeondam, Master Heoju, and Master Cho-ui, resided here to spread the true principles of enlightenment, establishing Dogapsa as a vibrant sanctuary where spiritual practice and teachings never cease.

Dogapsa is also a treasured repository of sacred cultural heritage that has preserved the essence of Buddhist art and culture for centuries. It houses numerous cultural heritages such as the Haetalmun Gate (National Treasure), Seated Stone Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva (National Treasure), Seated Stone Buddha (Treasure), Manjusri, Samantabhadra, and Elephant Statues (Treasure), along with the monument steles of Doseon and Sumi. en.title: Dr. Wangin Historic Site & Seonggidong National Tourist Area
en.overview: Dr. Wangin traveled to Japan during the reign of King Geunchogo of Baekje to spread Baekje's advanced culture, and he is revered in Japan as the cultural patriarch who introduced civilization. Located on the foothills of Munpilbong Peak east of Gurim Village, the Dr. Wangin Historic Site restores his legacy as his historical significance has been newly illuminated. It consists of Dr. Wangin's Tomb, the inner and outer gates, Munsanjae, Yangsajae, an exhibition hall, a statue of Dr. Wangin, and a study cave. Among them, Dr. Wangin's Tomb enshrines his portrait and ancestral tablet, where memorial rites are held annually. Munsanjae and Yangsajae are where Dr. Wangin studied and nurtured future generations; they have been restored after only their foundations remained on the middle slopes of the western side of Wolchulsan Mountain.

The study cave is a rock grotto used by Dr. Wangin when he trained in his studies. The exhibition hall features paintings depicting his birth, studies, journey to Japan, and transmission of learning. In addition, there is Seongcheon Spring, said to be water Dr. Wangin drank, and a historical monument erected next to his birthplace. Doljeonggopass, located west of Seonggidong, is said to have earned its name because the scholar looked back with lingering attachment at his beloved hometown while parting with colleagues and disciples before leaving for Japan. en.title: Yeongamho Lake (Migratory Bird Habitat)
en.overview: Yeongamho Lake is a large-scale lake created following the completion of the Yeongam-Geumho seawalls. The Yeongam and Geumho seawalls connect Samho-eup in Yeongam-gun with Hawon-myeon and San-i-myeon in Haenam-gun, with construction beginning in 1985 and completed in 1996. Thanks to its nutrient-rich mudflats, expansive water surface, and warm climate, Yeongamho Lake serves as a migratory route and intermediate stopover for migratory birds. Among the winter migratory birds visiting the habitat, ducks and geese finish breeding in Siberia, travel down through areas like Cheonsuman Bay on the west coast and the Geumgang Estuary starting in October to reach the reclaimed lands of the southwestern coast, and head north again in March.

The Yeongam and Geumho seawalls connect Samho-eup in Yeongam-gun with Hawon-myeon and San-i-myeon in Haenam-gun, with construction beginning in 1985 and completed in 1996. Thanks to its nutrient-rich mudflats, expansive water surface, and warm climate, Yeongamho Lake serves as a migratory route and intermediate stopover for migratory birds.

Among the winter migratory birds visiting the Yeongamho Migratory Bird Habitat, ducks and geese finish breeding in Siberia, travel down through areas like Cheonsuman Bay on the west coast and the Geumgang Estuary starting in October to reach the reclaimed lands of the southwestern coast, and head north again in March. Summer migratory birds, such as egrets, spend the winter in Southeast Asia, move to Korea in April to breed, and migrate southward again around September. Ecological surveys conducted by the Ministry of Environment since October 1996 have reported it as a migratory bird habitat inhabited by 34 species of winter birds, transforming this area into a new tourism landmark. Nearby attractions include Wolchulsan National Park, Dogapsa Temple, the Dr. Wangin Historic Site, and the Jeollanam-do Agricultural Museum.

在造訪靈岩湖候鳥過冬地的候鳥中，屬於冬候鳥的鴨類與大雁在西伯利亞完成繁殖後，從10月起經由我國西海岸的淺水灣、錦江河口等地南下至西南海岸填海區，到了3月又再次北返。夏候鳥白鷺類則在東南亞過冬，4月時移動至我國繁殖，9月左右再度南遷。環境部自1996年10月起實施的生態調查中，將其報導為棲息著34種冬候鳥的候鳥過冬地，使該地區蛻變成為全新的觀光名勝。周邊有月出山國立公園、道岬寺、王仁博士遺跡地、全羅南道農業博物館等許多觀光景點。

en.title: Wolchulsan National Park
en.overview: Designated as Korea's 20th national park in 1988, Wolchulsan Mountain was formed when massive granite rock masses of the Honam Jeongmaek mountain range clashed with the Southern Sea and rose up over countless years of weathering. Although Wolchulsan has a relatively small area of 56.22 ㎢, it is home to a diverse distribution of flora and fauna, and boasts high-caliber cultural heritage including national treasures. The peak of Wolchulsan is Cheonhwangbong (809m), known as a sacred place where ancestral rites to the heavens have been held since the Silla Dynasty. Centered around Cheonhwangbong Peak, the northern and eastern sides feature magnificent scenery created by huge boulders perched atop bold ridge lines, while the southern and western areas showcase formations where large and small rocks resemble stacked pagodas.

en.title: Dosolgokgyo Valley (Seonunsan Mountain)
en.overview: Along with Naejangsan Mountain, Gochang is renowned as one of the best spots for autumn foliage in the Honam region. In particular, Dosolgokgyo Valley around Seonunsan Mountain in Gochang is said to bloom with red flowers three times a year. In spring, the Natural Monument camellia forest flaunts its vibrant red hues, followed by red spider lilies in early autumn, and finally, brilliant autumn foliage once the lilies fade. Walking from Seonunsa Temple to Dosolam Hermitage along the Dosolcheon Stream, visitors can enjoy gorgeous autumn leaves and picturesque snowy winter landscapes. Designated as a Scenic Site in 2009, the Dosolgokgyo Valley area is beautiful in all four seasons.

In particular, Dosolgokgyo Valley around Seonunsan Mountain in Gochang is said to bloom with red flowers three times a year. In spring, the Natural Monument camellia forest flaunts its vibrant red hues, followed by red spider lilies in early autumn, and finally, brilliant autumn foliage once the lilies fade. Walking from Seonunsa Temple to Dosolam Hermitage along the Dosolcheon Stream, visitors can enjoy gorgeous autumn leaves and picturesque snowy winter landscapes. Designated as a Scenic Site in 2009, the Dosolgokgyo Valley area is beautiful in all four seasons.

Often called the 'Geumgang Mountain of Honam,' Seonunsan Mountain is also known as Dosolsan Mountain. Embracing the historic Seonunsa Temple, the mountain features dense forests, bizarre rock formations, and scenic wonders scattered throughout the valley, such as Jinheunggul Cave, Yongmungul Cave, Nakjodae Pavilion, and Cheonmabong Peak. In front of the Seonunsa tourist parking lot, you can find a Natural Monument ivy vine, and as you walk from Seonunsa toward Dosolam Hermitage, a giant Natural Monument pine tree stands next to Jinheunggul Cave. The camellia forest behind Daeungjeon Hall of Seonunsa Temple is also designated as a Natural Monument.

湖南の小金剛と呼ばれる禅雲山は、別名「道率山」とも呼ばれる。名刹である禅雲寺を懐に抱く禅雲山は、森林が生い茂り奇岩怪石が多く、渓谷に沿って振興窟、竜門窟、落照台、天馬峰などの絶景が至る所に点在している。禅雲寺観光地の駐車場の前にある渓谷には天然記念物のテイカカズラがあり、禅雲寺から道率庵へと登っていく途中、振興窟の隣には天然記念物の長沙松がそびえ立っている。禅雲寺大雄殿の後ろのツバキ林は天然記念物に指定されている。

en.title: Dongho Beach
en.overview: Dongho Beach is famous for its long, expansive sandy shore. Stretching over 4 km with fine sand and a gentle slope, it attracts numerous vacationers during the summer. With a shallow water depth of 0.5 to 1.5 meters, it is ideal for children to play in the water, and a magnificent centuries-old pine forest stands just behind the beach. The shade provided by the pine trees offers a refreshing breeze even in mid-summer, making it a great resting spot. The sunset over the West Sea viewed from here is particularly breathtaking.

en.title: Gusipo Beach
en.overview: Gusipo Beach is the largest beach in Gochang-gun, featuring a long, wide sandy shore and a dense pine forest. With its gentle slope, it is the perfect summer getaway for families. To the south of the beach lies a natural cave where dozens of residents and hundreds of rock doves reportedly took refuge for half a year during the Jeongyu War, and bizarre rock formations are scattered along the coastline. Beautiful islands, including Gamakdo Island, float gracefully in the open sea, and at dusk, you can witness a stunning sunset that paints the West Sea's Chilsan Sea in brilliant shades of red. It is also a popular spot for auto-camping enthusiasts, with various convenience facilities well-equipped nearby.

en.title: Munsubsa Temple (Gochang)
en.overview: Munsubsa Temple is nestled on the mid-slope of Munsubsan Mountain (621m), which forms the border between Gochang and Jangseong in Jeollanam-do. Passing the Gosu Pottery Site from Gosu-myeon township and heading upward leads to Josan Reservoir; following the left valley for about 6 km brings you to Munsubsa Temple. It is said to have been founded by Master Jajang. Legend has it that while returning from practicing at Mount Qingliang in Tang China, Jajang passed by Mount Munsu in Baekje territory, felt it resembled Mount Qingliang, and offered prayers in a stone cave. There, he discovered a stone statue of the Bodhisattva of Wisdom underground and built the temple.

paragraphs: Munsubsa Temple is nestled on the mid-slope of Munsubsan Mountain (621m), which forms the border between Gochang and Jangseong in Jeollanam-do. Passing the Gosu Pottery Site from Gosu-myeon township and heading upward leads to Josan Reservoir; following the left valley for about 6 km brings you to Munsubsa Temple. It is said to have been founded by Master Jajang. Legend has it that while returning from practicing at Mount Qingliang in Tang China, Jajang passed by Mount Munsu in Baekje territory, felt it resembled Mount Qingliang, and offered prayers in a stone cave. There, he discovered a stone statue of the Bodhisattva of Wisdom underground and built the temple.

Treasures housed here include the Daeungjeon Hall of Munsubsa, the Wooden Seated Shakyamuni Triad Buddha, the Wooden Seated Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and Ten Kings Statues of Munsubsa, alongside Jeollabuk-do Tangible Cultural Heritages such as Munsubu Pavilion and Munsubsa Stupas, as well as Myeongbujeon Hall and Hansanjeon Hall. The Natural Monument baby maple tree forest at Munsubsa is planted along an 80-meter section from the Iljumun Gate to the temple entrance. Around 500 baby maple trees, aged between 100 and 400 years old, grow naturally here. In autumn, the colorful foliage harmonizes with the gently rolling mountain scenery around the millennium-old temple.

en.title: Woojin Eel
en.overview: Located in Gochang, Woojin Tidal Flat Eel specializes in pungcheon eel. The term 'pungcheon' does not refer to a local region, but rather to the point where freshwater and saltwater meet in rivers connected to the West or South Sea, where tidal variations are large. Raised in tidal flats where the sea and river meet without artificial feed, these eels are uniquely chewy in texture compared to others. You can savor the plump and savory tidal flat pungcheon eel dipped in a sweet and salty soy sauce.

en.title: Jeongjanamu Hoejip
en.overview: Jeongjanamu Hoejip is a restaurant specializing in seafood. Located near Gusipo Beach in Gochang-gun, Jeollabuk-do, it is a great dining spot to enjoy after exploring the beach. Foodies line up not only for sea bass and flounder sashimi, but also for their signature webfoot octopus dishes. Visiting in spring or autumn is recommended to taste seasonal webfoot octopus. Parking is available in the vacant lot in front of the restaurant for a more relaxing dining experience.

en.title: Sindeok Sikdang
en.overview: Located at the three-way intersection at the entrance of Seonunsa Temple, this famous pungcheon eel restaurant has been passed down through two generations since the late 1960s. Eel is a stamina food, long symbolizing blood and vitality replenishment, making it great as a snack for the elderly and children as well as for women's skin beauty. The eel sauce is made from a base broth boiled down from eel bones, mixed with gochujang (chili paste) and various seasonings, then simmered for hours, holding over 30 years of culinary secrets. After being pre-grilled and allowed to absorb the flavors, the eel is grilled a second time before serving, melting softly in your mouth.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialties: Grilled Eel with Bamboo Salt · Grilled Seasoned Eel, etc.

ja.overview: 禅雲寺の入り口の三差路に位置し、1960年代末から2代にわたって続いている風川うなぎの有名店。うなぎはスタミナ料理であり、古くから補血・強壮を象徴する強精食品として、お年寄りや子どものおやつはもちろん、女性の美容にも非常に良い食品である。うなぎのタレもうなぎを煮出して抽出した基本だしにコチュジャンと各種薬味を加え、数時間じっくり煮込んでおり、30余年の味の秘訣が込められている。一度軽く焼いて下味を染み込ませた後、本焼きして提供されるうなぎの蒲焼きは、口に入れると柔らかくとろける。食事を兼ねる場合は、ご飯と一緒に香ばしいテンジャンチゲや熟成された塩辛が出てくる。

zh.overview: 位於禪雲寺入口三叉路口，是一家自60年代末起傳承兩代的知名風川鰻魚老店。鰻魚是補充體力的料理，自古以來便象徵著補血、滋補的強身食品，不僅適合作為老人與兒童的點心，對女性的皮膚美容也非常有益。鰻魚醬汁是以熬煮鰻魚骨萃取出的高湯為基底，加入辣椒醬與各種調味料慢火熬煮數小時而成，凝聚了30多年的美味秘訣。烤鰻魚經過初烤入味後，再進行複烤出爐，入口即化、口感軟嫩。若搭配正餐，則會附上白飯、濃郁的大醬湯以及風味醇厚的醃製海鮮。

en.title: Incheon Garden
en.overview: Located in Gochang-gun, Incheon Garden strives to provide trustworthy food and is situated near Seonunsa Temple from the Asan-myeon three-way intersection. A renowned eatery that has maintained its dedication for over 30 years, its specialty is clean and savory freshwater shrimp spicy soup (maeuntang), made with freshwater shrimp caught in the clear waters of Ungokho Lake and various home-grown organic vegetables. In addition, spicy and tangy catfish maeuntang and flavorful minnow maeuntang are also signature dishes of this place. They serve thoughtfully prepared food without chemical seasonings, making their various sauces and salted seafood in-house.

ja.title: 仁川ガーデン
ja.addr: 全羅北道高敞郡牙山面元平길 9
ja.overview: 高敞郡に位置する仁川ガーデンは、安心して食べられる料理を提供するために努めている場所で、牙山面の三差路から禅雲寺の近くに位置している。30年という長い歳月の間、変わらぬ心で料理を作り続けてきたグルメ店であり、雲谷湖の澄んだ水で獲れた川エビと、自家栽培の各種有機野菜を入れて作ったさっぱりかつコクのある川エビのメウン탕（辛い鍋）がこの店の自慢の味である。また、ピリ辛でほろ苦いナマズのメウン탕や、旨味のあるドジョウのメウン탕もこの店ならではの絶品。化学調味料を使用せず、各種味噌や塩辛は手作りするなど、真心が込められた料理を提供している。

en.title: Gamami Beach
en.addr: 355, Gamami-ro, Hongnong-eup, Yeonggwang-gun, Jeollanam-do (Jeollanam-do Gwangju Special Metropolitan City)
en.overview: Opened in 1925, this beach is located 24 km west of Yeonggwang-eup. It features a 1 km long, 200 m wide crescent-shaped sandy beach, backed by a lush pine forest of over 2,000 trees that creates a cozy atmosphere. With clear water and a shallow depth of 1-2 meters, it is celebrated as one of the three major beaches in the Honam region. The name 'Gamami' originates from Geumjeongsan Mountain behind it, whose ridge is said to resemble the tail of a harnessed horse (駕馬尾). Natural monuments like yellow-billed egrets and black-tailed gulls inhabit the area.
en.pull_quote: A beach located 24 km west of Yeonggwang-eup, opened in 1925. Featuring a 1 km long, 200 m wide crescent-shaped sandy beach and a lush pine forest of over 2,000...

The name 'Gamami' originates from Geumjeongsan Mountain behind it, whose ridge is said to resemble the tail of a harnessed horse (駕馬尾). Natural monuments like yellow-billed egrets and black-tailed gulls inhabit the area.

Countless islands dot the sea in front of the beach, and fishing boats sailing leisurely across the water create an overwhelmingly peaceful scene. Furthermore, the sunset over the West Sea, which dyes the Chilsan Sea in shades of red, offers a unique charm quite different from the sunrise of the East Sea. en.pull_quote: Nestled on the slopes of Bulgapsan Mountain in Yeonggwang-gun, Bulgapsa Temple is well-known as a premier spot for fully bloomed red spider lilies. As a branch temple...
paragraphs: Nestled on the slopes of Bulgapsan Mountain in Yeonggwang-gun, Bulgapsa Temple is well-known as a premier spot for fully bloomed red spider lilies. As a branch temple of Baekyangsa, the head temple of the 18th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, it was named 'Bulgapsa (佛甲寺)' carrying the significance of being the first Buddhist doctrinal center established by Marananta when Buddhism was introduced during the reign of King Chimnyu of Baekje (384 AD).

The temple preserves structures showcasing styles from the mid-Joseon dynasty and onwards, such as the Daeungjeon Hall and Cheonwangmun Gate. In the dense forest, visitors can spot the endangered wild plant, the yellow surprise lily (Lycoris chinensis), and in autumn, it is loved as a premier seasonal travel destination where red cluster amaryllis flowers form massive colonies.

en.pull_quote: A Confucian academy established to commemorate Gang Hang (1567–1618), a civil official of the mid-Joseon dynasty. While serving as a junior official, the Jeongyu War broke out...
paragraphs: This Confucian academy was established to commemorate Gang Hang (1567–1618), a civil official of the mid-Joseon dynasty. While serving as a junior official in the Ministry of Taxation and Ministry of Justice, the Jeongyu War broke out, prompting him to gather a militia to fight before being captured as a prisoner of war by Japanese troops and escorted to Japan. While in Japan, he gathered information on the country's history and geography to send back to his homeland while introducing Neo-Confucianism to Japan. After returning to his homeland in the 33rd year of King Seonjo's reign (1600), he declined official posts and dedicated himself solely to reading and nurturing future generations. The academy was bestowed the name 'Yonggyesa' by the royal court in the 13th year of King Injo's reign (1635) and was rebuilt in the 28th year of King Sukjong's reign (1702).

It was rebuilt again during the Japanese colonial period and has undergone several renovations since then to reach the present day. It follows a traditional layout with an educational space at the front and a sacrificial ritual space at the rear (Jeon-hak-hu-myo). The lecture hall, serving as the educational space, features a wooden floor in the center with heated ondol rooms on both sides. Passing through the inner three-gate in the back leads to a small shrine housing Gang Hang's spirit tablet. On the left foothill lies Gang Hang's tomb. (Source: Korea Heritage Service)

paragraphs: 朝鮮中期の文臣である姜抗（1567〜1618）を追慕するために建てられた書院である。姜抗は工曹佐郎や刑曹佐郎を務めていた最中に丁酉再乱が起こると、義兵を集めて活動した末に倭敵の捕虜となり日本へ連行された。日本に滞在中、その国の歴史や地理などを調べて故国へ送りつつ、日本には性理学を伝えた。宣祖33年（1600）に帰国した後、官職を辞退して読書と後進の育成にのみ専念した。この書院は仁祖13年（1635）に朝廷から「龍渓寺」という名前を下賜され、粛宗28年（1702）に改築された。
日帝強占期にも改築され、その後も数回の補修を経て現在に至っている。前方に教育空間を設け、後方に祭祀空間を設けた「前学後廟」の配置となっている。教育空間である講堂は中央に板の間を置き、両脇にオンドル部屋を配置している。後ろにある内三門を通り過ぎると、姜抗の位牌を祀った小規模な祠堂がある。左側の山すそには姜抗の墓所がある。（出所：国家遺産庁）

paragraphs: Hanmaum Park was established in 2002 to secure eco-friendly green and resting spaces, improve the image of the nuclear power plant and surrounding areas, and foster a place of harmony with the local community. Located near the Yeonggwang Nuclear Power Headquarters, Hanmaum Park spans approximately 327 square meters, making it the largest of its kind in the Honam region. The park is equipped with various sports facilities, cultural facilities, and a traditional park, serving as a venue for relaxation and physical training.

Additionally, it features a wild flower garden planted with numerous domestic wildflowers, utilized as a natural ecological experience center, along with a traditional pavilion offering exceptional scenery where visitors can enjoy the sunset over the West Coast. As Hanmaum Park is created for relaxation and physical conditioning, visitors are encouraged to take pride and care in cherishing and protecting all facilities and the environment.

Near Seoldo Port in Yeomsan-myeon, Yeomsan Church features a martyr's monument, a joint burial site for martyrs, and an exhibition hall, while Yawol Church in Yawol-ri houses a martyr's memorial hall to honor the noble sacrifices and faith of the martyrs. en.pull_quote: The Christian Martyrs Site is a historic location commemorating 194 martyrs who sacrificed their lives while protecting their faith during the Korean War, recognized as a representative...
paragraphs: The Christian Martyrs Site is a historic location commemorating 194 martyrs who sacrificed their lives while protecting their faith during the Korean War, recognized as a representative martyrdom site recorded even in global church history. Near Seoldo Port in Yeomsan-myeon, Yeomsan Church features a martyr's monument, a joint burial site for martyrs, and an exhibition hall, while Yawol Church in Yawol-ri houses a martyr's memorial hall to honor the noble sacrifices and faith of the martyrs.

Yawol Church was the first church in the Yeomsan region established by missionary Eugene Bell in 1908, and later with the establishment of Yeomsan Church in 1939, it established itself as the center of local Christian culture. However, during the Korean War in 1950, a tragic event occurred where clergy and church members sacrificed their lives defending their faith, totaling 194 martyrs centered around Yeomsan Church and Yawol Church. Today, this place is visited by many pilgrims seeking to reflect on the meaning of Korean Christian martyrdom history and revisit the values of peace and harmony.

野月教会は1908年に宣教師ユージン・ベルが建てた塩山地域初の教会であり、その後1939年に塩山教会が設立されて地域キリスト教文化の中心地として定着した。しかし、1950年の朝鮮戦争当時、教役者と教徒たちが信仰を守り犠牲となる悲劇に見舞われ、塩山教会と野月教会を中心に計194名の殉教者が発生した。今日、ここは韓国キリスト教の殉教歴史の意味を振り返り、平和と和合の価値を再認識する巡礼地として多くの訪問者が訪れている。

paragraphs: 基督教徒殉教地是為緬懷在韓戰期間堅守信仰而犧牲的194名殉教者之歷史現場，被譽為世界教會史上亦有記載的代表性殉教地。位於鹽山面雪島港附近的鹽山教會建有殉教紀念碑、殉教者合葬墓與展示室，野月里的野月教會則設有殉教紀念館，紀念殉教者們崇高的犧牲與信仰。
野月教會是1908年由傳教士尤金·貝爾建立的鹽山地區第一座教會，隨後於1939年設立鹽山教會，奠定了當地基督教文化的中心地位。然而在1950年韓戰期間，發生了教職人員與信徒堅守信仰而犧牲的悲劇，以鹽山教會與野月教會為中心共產生了194名殉教者。如今，這裡吸引許多訪客前來，細細省思韓國基督教殉教歷史的意義，並重溫和平與和諧的價值。

en.overview: Yeonggwang Galmaegi Sikdang is a Korean restaurant near Beopseong Port where you can enjoy a hearty spread of barley-cured dried yellow corvina (bori-gulbi), a specialty of Yeonggwang. The spicy grilled octopus skewers (nakji-horong) and soy sauce marinated crab (ganjang-gejang) are especially famous. en.title: Dokcheon Sikdang
en.addr: 162-1 Dokcheon-ro, Haksan-myeon, Yeongam-gun, Jeollanam-Gwangju Integrated City, Jeollanam-do
en.overview: Located on the Dokcheon Octopus Food Street, where visitors can taste traditional foods of the West Coast tidal flats such as horong nakji (wrapped webfoot octopus) and galnaktang (beef and octopus soup), Dokcheon Sikdang is considered the original home of galnaktang and nakji yeonpotang (octopus hot pot). Operating since 1970, it has been featured in various media outlets and received the Local Food Award in January 1995. Furthermore, it was selected as a 'Great Restaurant' by Sports Seoul's 'Matjib & Meotjib' and the Korea Traditional Food Preservation Association, and received the Traditional Culture Master Award in October 1996.

Furthermore, it was selected as a 'Great Restaurant' by Sports Seoul's 'Matjib & Meotjib' and the Korea Traditional Food Preservation Association, and received the Traditional Culture Master Award in October 1996. Eating the pork belly wrapped in ssam vegetables with salted fermented shrimp and perilla seed powder is a unique specialty of this place.

en.title: Jeamsan Mountain
en.addr: San 1-1 Geumsan-ri, Jangheung-eup, Jangheung-gun, Jeollanam-Gwangju Integrated City, Jeollanam-do
en.overview: Standing at 807 meters, Jeamsan Mountain is located at the end of the Sobaeksan Mountains, forming the border with Boseong-gun northeast of Jangheung-eup. With numerous large valleys and springs, it is called the 'King's Rock (Jeam) Mountain' because the surrounding rocks appear to bow toward the peak's rock. It is a famous mountain in Honam featuring gentle strange rocks and stones, hiking trails overlooking the South Sea, and native pine trees, royal azaleas, and various wild herbs. The soaring peak truly matches the name King's Rock.
en.pull_quote: Standing at 807 meters, Jeamsan Mountain is located at the end of the Sobaeksan Mountains, forming the border with Boseong-gun northeast of Jangheung-eup. With numerous large valleys and springs...
paragraphs: Standing at 807 meters, Jeamsan Mountain is located at the end of the Sobaeksan Mountains, forming the border with Boseong-gun northeast of Jangheung-eup. With numerous large valleys and springs, it is called the 'King's Rock (Jeam) Mountain' because the surrounding rocks appear to bow toward the peak's rock. It is a famous mountain in Honam featuring gentle strange rocks and stones, hiking trails overlooking the South Sea, and native pine trees, royal azaleas, and various wild herbs. The soaring peak truly matches the name King's Rock, and the ridges on both sides stretch out vigorously.

In addition, deep in the mountain are the 'Brother Rocks,' named after a sad legend of poor brothers who fell to their deaths while picking wild herbs and turned into rocks. About 50 meters below the Brother Rocks are the Uisangam and Wonhyo hermitages. At the summit sits Jeamdan altar where rain-praying rituals were held, offering views of Mudeungsan, Wolchulsan, Cheonwansan, Jonjesan mountains, and the South Sea in the distance. In spring, the ridge stretching from Gomjaesan to Sajasand is so brilliantly covered with royal azaleas that its reddish glow reaches toward the Dadohae (Archipelago). Azaleas begin to bloom in late April after azaleas fade, reaching full bloom in mid-May under the warm sea breeze of the South Sea.

また、山中には貧しい兄弟が山菜を採りに行って転落死し岩になったという「兄弟岩」があり、兄弟岩から50メートル下った左右には義相庵と元暁庵という寺院があります。頂上には雨乞いを行ったジェアムダンがあり、遠くには無등山・月出山・天冠山・尊帝山や南海が見渡せます。春にはコムジェサン（熊財山）を経由してサジャサン（獅子山）に至る稜線が、遠くから見ても赤い気配が多島海に向かって広がるほどヤマツツジの花で美しく輝きます。ヤマツツジは、ツツジが色あせる4月下旬から咲き始め、5月中旬になると南海の温かい風を受けて華やかに満開を迎えます。

此外，山中還有傳說中貧窮兄弟上山採野菜時失足墜落化為岩石的「兄弟岩」，在兄弟岩下方50公尺左右的左右兩側分別有義相庵和元曉庵。山頂上建有用於舉行祈雨祭的帝岩壇，從這裡可以遠眺無等山、月出山、天冠山、尊帝山以及南海。每到春天，從熊財山通往獅子山的陵線，即使從遠處望去，鐵樹花也紅得耀眼，彷彿一片紅色的氣勢正朝著多島海延伸。鐵樹花在杜鵑花褪色的4月下旬開始綻放，到了5月中旬便會迎著南海溫暖的海風絢麗盛開。

en.title: National Cheonwansan Natural Recreation Forest
en.addr: 842-1150 Chilgwan-ro, Gwansan-eup, Jangheung-gun, Jeollanam-Gwangju Integrated City, Jeollanam-do
en.overview: Cheonwansan Mountain, one of the five major mountains in Honam, is a 723-meter-high mountain on the border of Gwansan-eup and Daedeok-eup. The entire mountain is composed of rocks, with peaks piercing the sky. It offers spectacular scenery with red camellias in spring and silver grass in autumn. Particularly, jagged rocks protrude near the summit, earning the mountain the name Cheonwansan because they resemble a heavenly emperor's crown decorated with jewels. The encounter between the sea breeze crossing the mountain range and the majestic Cheonwansan creates a natural power beyond human capability.
en.pull_quote: Cheonwansan Mountain, one of the five major mountains in Honam, is a 723-meter-high mountain on the border of Gwansan-eup and Daedeok-eup. The entire mountain is composed of rocks, with peaks piercing the sky...
paragraphs: Cheonwansan Mountain, one of the five major mountains in Honam, is a 723-meter-high mountain on the border of Gwansan-eup and Daedeok-eup. The entire mountain is composed of rocks, with peaks piercing the sky. It offers spectacular scenery with red camellias in spring and silver grass in autumn. Particularly, jagged rocks protrude near the summit, earning the mountain the name Cheonwansan because they resemble a heavenly emperor's crown decorated with jewels. The encounter between the sea breeze crossing the mountain range and the majestic Cheonwansan creates a natural power beyond human capability.

Climbing the mountain unfolds the southern Dadohae archipelago like an oriental painting, while to the north, Wolchulsan in Yeongam, Jeamsan in Jangheung, and Mudeungsan in Jeollanam-Gwangju Integrated City come into view at a glance. On clear days, Hallasan Mountain on Jeju Island mysteriously appears across the sea. Along the ridges, bizarre rocks stand like an exhibition of natural sculptures, and a vast silver grass field of over 50,000 pyeong near the summit creates a magnificent spectacle. Furthermore, Cheonwansa Temple is located within 500 meters, connecting with Cheonwansan's hiking trails to play a major role in cultural heritage exploration and hiking.

山に登ると南海岸の多島海が一幅の東洋画のように広がり、北には霊岩の月出山、長興の帝岩山、全羅南道光州統合特別市の無等山が一望でき、天気が良ければ海側に済州島の漢拏山が神秘的に姿を現します。稜線の上には奇岩怪石が自然の彫刻展示場のように並び、頂上付近には5万余坪ものススキ畑が広がり圧巻の光景を作り出します。また、すぐ近くにはチョングァンサ（天冠寺）があり、天冠山の登山道と繋がっているため、文化財の探訪と登山を同時に楽しむことができます。

登上山頂，南海的多島海風光如同一幅東洋畫般展開，向北望去，靈岩的月出山、長興的帝岩山、全羅南道光州統合特別市的無等山盡收眼底，天氣晴朗時甚至能隱約望見大海方向的濟州島漢拏山。山脊上奇岩怪石林立，宛如自然雕塑的展覽館，山頂附近則有約五萬坪的紫芒草群落，蔚為壯觀。此外，距離天冠寺不到500公尺，並與天冠山的登山步道相連，對文化遺址考察與登山具有極大價值。

en.title: Yuchi Natural Recreation Forest
en.addr: 154 Hyuyangrim-gil, Yuchi-myeon, Jangheung-gun, Jeollanam-Gwangju Integrated City, Jeollanam-do
en.overview: Located in the upper stream area of Jangheung Dam, Yuchi Natural Recreation Forest allows visitors to appreciate outstanding natural scenery, including Rainbow Waterfall and Ongnyeo Waterfall flowing down from Ongnyeobong Peak, and magnificent bizarre rocks such as the legendary Byeon Gang-soe and Ongnyeo Rocks. The forests surrounding the recreation forest are rich in phytoncides emitted from about 400 species of warm-temperate trees, including konara oak, maple, walnut, torreya, paper mulberry, oaks, cornus fruit, painted maple, mountain cherry, and maple trees.
en.pull_quote: Located in the upper stream area of Jangheung Dam, Yuchi Natural Recreation Forest allows visitors to appreciate outstanding natural scenery, including Rainbow Waterfall and Ongnyeo Waterfall...
paragraphs: Located in the upper stream area of Jangheung Dam, Yuchi Natural Recreation Forest allows visitors to appreciate outstanding natural scenery, including Rainbow Waterfall and Ongnyeo Waterfall flowing down from Ongnyeobong Peak, and magnificent bizarre rocks such as the legendary Byeon Gang-soe and Ongnyeo Rocks. The forests surrounding the recreation forest are rich in phytoncides emitted from about 400 species of warm-temperate trees, including konara oak, maple, walnut, torreya, paper mulberry, oaks, cornus fruit, painted maple, mountain cherry, and maple trees. In autumn, the foliage is stunning, allowing visitors to enjoy forest bathing and relaxation unlike anywhere else in the country.

Equipped with 17 forest cabins, a water playground, a playground, a campsite, sports facilities, a parking lot, and a suspension bridge, it is an optimal place for family and group relaxation as well as various events. In addition, hiking trails, walking paths, mountain bike courses, and driving courses around Jangheung Dam are gaining popularity. Near the recreation forest is Borimsa Temple, which holds high Buddhist historical value. Visitors can enjoy forest bathing utilizing Borimsa Forest Bathing Area, which features a torreya forest over 300 years old around the temple and a large-scale green tea plantation growing naturally.

paragraphs: Along with Jirisan, Naejangsan, Wolchulsan, and Byeonsan, Cheonwansan is one of the five major mountains in Honam. Located on the border of Gwansan-eup and Daedeok-eup, it stands 723 meters high, with the entire mountain formed of rocks and peaks piercing the sky like needles. Famous rocks such as Gi Rock, Lion Rock, and Buddha Rock boast their unique appearances. Particularly, jagged rocks protruding near the summit earned the mountain the name Cheonwansan as they resemble a heavenly emperor's crown decorated with jewels. Climbing the mountain reveals the southern Dadohae archipelago like an oriental painting, while to the north, Wolchulsan in Yeongam, Jeamsan in Jangheung, and Mudeungsan in Jeollanam-Gwangju Integrated City can be seen at a glance. On clear days, you can even view Hallasan Mountain on Jeju Island.

Along the ridges, bizarre rock formations resemble an exhibition of natural sculptures, and a silver grass colony spanning over 50,000 pyeong near the summit creates a spectacular view. Every autumn, the Cheonwansan Silver Grass Festival is held at Yeondaebong Peak on the summit of Cheonwansan. On the mid-slope of the mountain sits Cheonwansa Temple, which preserves cultural assets such as a three-story stone pagoda, stone lantern, and five-story stone pagoda. Cheonwansan also features forest cabins, a campsite, a natural observation center, a children's playground, and water play areas.

en.pull_quote: Bakdaljae Natural Recreation Forest is a natural recreation area located in Pyeongdong-ri, Baegun-myeon, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do, featuring lush forests of 150-year-old pine trees and other species harmonizing with unique rock formations. Bakdaljae Natural...
paragraphs: Bakdaljae Natural Recreation Forest is a natural recreation area located in Pyeongdong-ri, Baegun-myeon, Jecheon-si, Chungcheongbuk-do, featuring lush forests where roughly 150-year-old pine trees and mixed trees coexist in harmony with bizarre rocks. Situated between Mt. Juronsan and Mt. Sirangsan, it was established as a pristine natural recreation space for public health, emotional cultivation, and regional development through multi-purpose forest management. Spanning a total area of 1.7㎢, its accommodations consist of log cabins and loess rooms, with group lodging also available.

Two campsites are provided, and the parking lot covers an area of 6,300㎡ with a capacity of about 200 vehicles. Additional amenities include a foot volleyball court, volleyball court, hiking trails, a water play area, and an ecological pond. The hiking trails within the recreation forest are free for everyone to use. The animal enclosure houses 116 animals across 12 species, including fallow deer, blue peacocks, white peacocks, golden pheasants, silver pheasants, and Lady Amherst's pheasants. The natural observation garden features 224 plants of 12 species such as Japanese red pines, while the flower garden contains 2,424 plants of 7 species including oak-leaf hydrangeas. At the Bakdaljae pass summit, there is an octagonal pavilion and a spring.

paragraphs: 朴達才自然休養林位於忠清北道堤川市白雲面平洞里，是一處150年左右的松樹與雜木共存的茂密森林與奇岩怪石相得益彰的自然休養林。朴達才自然休養林作為主論山與侍郎山之間得天獨厚的自然休養空間，其創建目的不僅是為了國民的健康休養與情操陶冶，更透過森林的多功能經營來增進公益功能並促進地方開發。總面積達1.7平方公里，住宿設施由木屋與黃土房區組成，並備有團體宿舍。
設有2處露營場，停車場面積達6300平方公尺，約可停放200輛車。此外，還配備了足排球場、排球場、登山步道、戲水池、生態蓮花池等設施，休養林內的登山步道供所有人免費使用。動物飼養場飼養著梅花鹿、藍孔雀、白孔雀、金雞、銀雞、白腹錦雞等12種116隻動物；自然觀察園內有黑松等12種224株植物；花卉園則分佈著木繡球等7種2424株植物。在朴達才山埡口設有八角亭與清泉。

en.title: Woraksan National Park
en.overview: Mt. Woraksan is located in the middle section where the Baekdudaegan mountain range connects Mt. Sobaeksan to Mt. Sokrisan. With rugged mountain terrain and soaring rock cliffs resembling fierce tigers, it boasts breathtaking scenery harmonized with deep mountain valleys, waterfalls, and pools. Woraksan National Park was designated as the 17th national park on December 31, 1984. Spanning across Jecheon-si, Chungju-si, Danyang-gun, and Mungyeong-si, it is surrounded to the north by Chungju Lake and Cheongpung Lake, and to the east by the 8 Scenic Views of Danyang...
en.pull_quote: Mt. Woraksan sits centrally along the Baekdudaegan between Mt. Sobaeksan and Mt. Sokrisan, boasting rugged terrain, towering cliffs like fierce tigers, and stunning scenery with deep valleys, waterfalls, and pools...
paragraphs: Mt. Woraksan is centrally located where the Baekdudaegan connects Mt. Sobaeksan to Mt. Sokrisan. Its rugged terrain and towering rock cliffs, rising like fierce tigers, blend with deep valleys, waterfalls, and pools to boast magnificent scenery. Woraksan National Park was designated as the 17th national park on December 31, 1984. Spanning the administrative districts of Jecheon-si, Chungju-si, Danyang-gun, and Mungyeong-si, it is embraced by Chungju Lake and Cheongpung Lake to the north, and surrounded by scenic natural landscapes such as the 8 Scenic Views of Danyang and Sobaeksan National Park to the east, and Mungyeong Saejae and Sokrisan National Park to the south.

The main peak of Mt. Woraksan, Yeongbong, is also called Guksabong and has been revered as a sacred mountain since ancient times. Centered around Mt. Woraksan, there are numerous picturesque peaks including Haseulsan, where snow reportedly lingers even in summer, Munsubong, and Mansubong. Upon reaching the summit (Yeongbong), resilient pine trees that have weathered countless storms remain evergreen across all four seasons, and open skies stretch out refreshingly in all directions. In addition, the stunning views of Chungju Lake and Cheongpung Lake can be seen at a glance. In summer, the abundant valley water offers a refreshing escape from the sweltering heat.

ja.title: 月岳山（ウォラクサン）国立公園
ja.region_label: 忠北 堤川市 寒水面
ja.addr: 忠清北道 堤川市 寒水面 弥勒松渓路 1647
ja.overview: 月岳山は小白山から俗里山へと繋がる白頭大幹の中間に位置し、険しい山容と猛虎のようにそそり立つ奇岩断崖が深い渓谷や滝、淵などと調和し、この上なく美しい景観を誇っている。月岳山国立公園は1984年12月31日に17番目の国立公園に指定された。行政区域上では堤川市、忠州市、丹陽郡、聞慶市にまたがり、北は忠州湖畔と清風湖畔が月岳山を巻き込み、東は丹陽八景と小白山国立公園、南は聞慶鳥嶺や俗里山国立公園のような美しい自然景観に囲まれている。
ja.pull_quote: 月岳山は白頭大幹が小白山と俗里山を結ぶ中間に位置し、険しい山容、猛虎のようにそそり立つ奇岩断崖が深い渓谷や滝、淵と調和し美しい景観を誇る。月岳山国立…
paragraphs: 月岳山は白頭大幹が小白山から俗里山へと繋がる中央に位置しており、険しい山容、猛虎のようにそそり立つ奇岩断崖が深い渓谷や滝、淵と調和して最高の美しさを誇っている。月岳山国立公園は1984年12月31日に17番目の国立公園に指定された。行政区域としては堤川市、忠州市、丹陽郡、聞慶市にまたがり、北には忠州湖畔と清風湖畔が月岳山を包み込み、東には丹陽八景と小白山国立公園、南には聞慶鳥嶺や俗里山国立公園などの美しい自然景観に囲まれている。

月岳山の霊峰は国師峰とも呼ばれ、古くから神聖な山として「霊峰」と呼ばれている。月岳山を中心に夏でも雪が解けないという下雪山をはじめ、文殊峰、万寿峰などの秀麗な峰々が連なり、山頂（霊峰）に登ると幾多の風雪に耐え抜いて育ったチョウセンゴヨウマツが四季を通じて青々と茂り、東西南北が開けた空が爽やかに広がる。また、忠州湖と清風湖の美しい姿が一望できる。夏場には豊かな水量の渓谷の水が猛暑を忘れさせてくれる。

zh.pull_quote: 月岳山位於白頭大幹連接小白山與俗里山的中間地帶，山勢險峻，奇岩峭壁如猛虎般聳立，與深谷幽壑、瀑布深潭交相輝映，展現極致美景。月岳山國立…
paragraphs: 月岳山位於白頭大幹連接小白山與俗里山的中間位置，山勢險峻，奇岩斷崖如猛虎般高聳，與深山幽谷、瀑布與深潭相融合，展現出極具魅力的美景。月岳山國立公園於1984年12月31日被指定為第17座國立公園。行政區域涵蓋堤川市、忠州市、丹陽郡與聞慶市，北有忠州湖畔與清風湖畔環繞月岳山，東鄰丹陽八景與小白山國立公園，南接聞慶鳥嶺與俗里山國立公園等優美的自然景觀。
月岳山靈峰又稱國師봉，自古被視為神聖之山而稱為「靈峰」。以月岳山為中心，周圍羅列著夏天也不融雪的下雪山、文殊峰、萬壽峰等秀麗的山峰。登上山頂（靈峰）時，歷經萬古風霜生長而成的松樹四季常青，東西南北豁然開朗的天空令人心曠神怡。此外，忠州湖與清風湖的美景盡收眼底。夏季時，水量豐沛的溪谷流水讓人忘卻酷暑。

en.title: Deokdong Valley
en.overview: Deokdong Valley is a 5km-long stream originating from Mt. Baegunsan (1,087m) and Mt. Sipsabong (984.8m) flowing down to Wondeokdong. Though less well-known than nearby Yongha Gugok or Songgye Valley, its beautiful rock formations, lush forests, and crystal-clear water are second to none. The valley is shallow and clear, making it ideal for water play, and its dense foliage makes it a supreme summer retreat secretly cherished and frequently visited by locals from Jecheon during the summer months. Fishing and gathering activities are prohibited by local residents to preserve the valley. Portable restrooms and deck paths are placed here and there for the convenience of visitors.
en.pull_quote: Deokdong Valley originates from Mt. Baegunsan (1,087m) and Mt. Sipsabong (984.8m) and flows 5km to Wondeokdong. Though less famous than Yongha Gugok or Songgye Valley...
paragraphs: Deokdong Valley is a 5km-long valley originating from Mt. Baegunsan (1,087m) and Mt. Sipsabong (984.8m) down to Wondeokdong. Compared to nearby Yongha Gugok or Songgye Valley, it is relatively unknown, but its beautiful bizarre rocks, dense forests, and pristine water are second to none.

The valley is not deep and its water is crystal clear, making it perfect for water play. With its lush woods, it is an unbeatable summer retreat that Jecheon locals keep closely guarded and frequently visit in the summer. All fishing and gathering activities in the valley are prohibited by the residents. Portable restrooms and wooden deck paths are installed throughout to ensure the convenience of summer vacationers.

en.title: Songgye Valley
en.overview: Songgye Valley is a representative valley tourist destination in Jecheon, located within Woraksan National Park. Surrounded like a folding screen by the foothills of Mt. Woraksan (1,094m), it effectively helps visitors forget the summer heat. In particular, the clear water flowing through the valley is ice-cold, drawing numerous vacationers looking to cool off during the summer. Popular among those seeking refuge from the heat in lush forests and deep valleys in summer, it also shines as a vibrant autumn foliage destination connected with Chungju Lake.
en.pull_quote: Songgye Valley is located within Woraksan National Park and stands out as Jecheon's premier valley destination. Encircled like a screen by Mt. Woraksan (1,094m)...
paragraphs: Songgye Valley is located inside Woraksan National Park and is considered Jecheon's representative valley tourist spot. The foothills of Mt. Woraksan (1,094m) surround it like a folding screen, making it a wonderful place to forget the summer heat. In particular, the clear water flowing through the valley is ice-cold, attracting many summer vacationers seeking relief from the warmth. It is popular in summer for its dense woods and deep gorges, and in autumn, it gains acclaim as a foliage-viewing spot linked with Chungju Lake.

The Mt. Woraksan area was designated as a national park on December 31, 1984. It is dotted with tourist attractions such as the natural monument Manggaenamu tree, Deokjusa Temple, and Mireukri Temple Site, which capture the attention of hikers. The scenic spots around the valley, including Wolgwang Waterfall, Haksodae, Jayeondae, Cheongbyeokdae, Waryongdae, Palrangso, Mangpokdae, and Sukyeongdae, are collectively known as the 8 Scenic Views of Songgye. Jayeondae, located at the entrance of Songgye Valley, impresses visitors with its clear valley water, wide bedrock, and deep pool. Wolgwang Waterfall is a 3--tier waterfall about 30 meters high, and Sukyeongdae is a historical site where the Woraksan Shrine was established and rituals were held since the Silla Dynasty.

ja.overview: 松渓渓谷は月岳山国立公園内に位置する渓谷で、堤川を代表する渓谷観光地と言える。松渓渓谷は月岳山（1,094m）の麓が屏風のように囲んでおり、夏の暑さを忘れさせてくれる。特に渓谷を流れる澄んだ水は氷のように冷たく、夏季には暑さを冷まそうと多くの避暑客が訪れる。夏には鬱蒼とした森林と深い渓谷の中で暑さを逃れる人々でにぎわい、秋には忠州湖と連動した紅葉の名所として注目を集めている。
ja.pull_quote: 松渓渓谷は月岳公園内に位置する渓谷で、堤川を代表する渓谷観光地。月岳山（1,094m）の麓が屏風のように囲み、夏の暑さをしっかりと忘れさせてくれる。特…
paragraphs: 松渓渓谷は月岳山国立公園内に位置する渓谷で、堤川を代表する渓谷観光地である。松渓渓谷は月岳山（1,094m）の麓が屏風のように囲んでおり、夏の暑さを十分に忘れさせてくれる。特に渓谷を流れる澄んだ水は氷のように冷たく、夏季には暑さを和らげようと多くの避暑客が訪れる。夏には生い茂った森と深い渓谷で暑さを避ける人々に人気があり、秋には忠州湖と連動した紅葉観光地として脚光を浴びている。

月岳山一帯は1984年12月31日に国立公園に指定された。また、天然記念物のマンゲナム（イヌツゲの一種）、徳周寺、弥勒里寺址などの観光名所が点在し、登山客の足を止めさせる。渓谷周辺にある月光瀑布、鶴巣台、自然台、清壁台、臥竜台、八郎沼、望瀑台、水鏡台などは松渓八景として名を知られている。自然台は松渓渓谷の最初の入口に位置する場所で、澄んだ渓谷の水と広い岩盤、深い淵が印象的である。月光瀑布は30メートルほどの3段の滝であり、水鏡台は新らしき時代から月岳神祠を設けて祭祀を行っていた場所である。

zh.title: 松溪溪谷
zh.addr: 忠청北道堤川市寒水面松溪里
zh.overview: 松溪溪谷位於月岳山國立公園內，可說是堤川最具代表性的溪谷旅遊景點。松溪溪谷四周被月岳山（1,094公尺）的山麓如屏風般環繞，讓人完全忘卻夏日的暑氣。特別是流經溪谷的清澈溪水冰涼刺骨，夏季時吸引大量避暑客前來消暑。夏天時，茂密的林木與深邃的溪谷深受躲避酷暑的人們喜愛；秋天則與忠州湖相連，成為備受矚目的賞楓勝地。
zh.pull_quote: 松溪溪谷位於月岳山國立公園內，是堤川的代表性溪谷景點。松溪溪谷周圍有月岳山（1,094公尺）群山環繞如屏風，足以讓人忘卻夏日暑氣。特…
paragraphs: 松溪溪谷位於月岳山國立公園內，堪稱堤川的代表性溪谷觀光勝地。松溪溪谷被月岳山（1,094公尺）的群山如屏風般環繞，足以讓人忘卻夏日的炎熱。特別是流淌在溪谷中的清水冰涼如冰，夏天吸引了眾多避暑客前來消暑。夏季時，茂密的森林與深邃的溪谷吸引了避暑人群；秋季時則作為與忠州湖相連的賞楓景點而備受矚目。
月岳山一帶於1984年12月31日被指定為國立公園。此外，天然紀念物椴樹、德周寺、彌勒里寺址等觀光名勝散落其間，讓登山客駐足停留。溪谷周邊的月光瀑布、鶴巢台、自然台、清壁台、臥龍台、八郎沼、望瀑台、水鏡台等被合稱為「松溪八景」。自然台位於松溪溪谷的第一入口處，清澈的溪水、寬廣的岩盤與深邃的深潭令人印象深刻。月光瀑布是高約30公尺的三段瀑布，水鏡台則是自新羅時代起設置月岳神祠並進行祭祀的地方。

en.title: Jeongbangsa Temple
en.overview: A thousand-year-old temple located on the ridge of Sinseonbong peak in the Geumsusan mountain range at an elevation of 1,016m, Jeongbangsa Temple is a subsidiary temple of Beopjusa Temple on Mt. Sokrisan of the Jogye Order, reportedly founded by Master Uisang during the Silla Dynasty. Reaching the temple offers panoramic views of Cheongpung Lake and surrounding mountains that resemble a wonderland, instilling a sense of natural wonder. A rock cliff covers one-third of the main hall's roof, and its grand and peculiar appearance evokes the greatness of nature. The temple grounds house the main hall, monk quarters, and Hyeonhyemun Gate.
en.pull_quote: Jeongbangsa Temple is a millennium-old temple on the Sinseonbong ridge of Geumsusan (1,016m), a branch temple of Beopjusa, reportedly founded by Master Uisang of Silla...
paragraphs: Jeongbangsa Temple is a thousand-year-old temple situated on the Sinseonbong ridge of the Geumsusan range at an elevation of 1,016m. A branch of Beopjusa Temple on Mt. Sokrisan under the Jogye Order, it was reportedly founded by Master Uisang during the Silla period. Upon climbing to the temple, visitors can overlook Cheongpung Lake and surrounding mountains, which resemble an ethereal fairyland and evoke a deep sense of natural wonder. An imposing rock cliff covers one-third of the main hall's roof, and its grand, unique shape inspires awe at the greatness of nature. The temple precinct includes the main hall, monk quarters, and Hyeonhyemun Gate.

Built in 1825, the main hall is a 12-kan wooden tiled building, and the monk quarters consist of a 5-kan structure. Hyeonhyemun is the main gate of the temple, also known as Iljumun (One-Pillar Gate), constructed as a 1-kan wooden gate. Inside the main hall sits the presiding Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva statue, 60cm in height and 30cm in shoulder width, with a post-Buddha painting behind it. The Seated Wooden Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva and Votive Relics of Jeongbangsa Temple in Jecheon refer to the wooden Avalokitesvara statue enshrined in the main hall and the relics discovered within it. This seated statue is enshrined as the main Buddha and clearly exhibits the typical characteristics of mid-Joseon Dynasty bodhisattva sculptures.

paragraphs: 曹渓宗俗里山法住寺の末寺である浄方寺は、標高1,016mの錦繍山の麓、神仙峰の稜線にある千年の古刹であり、新羅時代の義湘大師が創建したと伝えられている。寺に登ると、神仙の世界を彷彿とさせる清風湖と周辺の山々を一望でき、自然の神秘を感じさせてくれる場所である。法堂の屋根の3分の1を覆う岩壁があり、その雄大で奇抜な姿は自然の偉大さを実感させる。浄方寺の境内には法堂、寮舎、現慧門などがある。

1825年に建てられた法堂は12間、寮舎は5間の規模の木造瓦葺き家屋である。現慧門は寺の正門であり、一柱門とも呼ばれる1間規模の木造門である。法堂の中には主尊仏である高さ60cm、肩幅30cmの観音菩薩像があり、仏像の後ろに後仏タンク（仏画）が描かれている。堤川浄方寺木造観音菩薩坐像及び腹蔵遺物は、堤川の浄方寺法堂に祀られている木製の観音菩薩坐像とその中から出てきた遺物である。この木造観音菩薩坐像は浄方寺の法堂に主仏として祀られており、典型的な朝鮮中期の菩薩像の特徴をよく示している。

paragraphs: 淨方寺為曹溪宗俗里山法住寺的末寺，位於海拔1,016公尺的錦繡山脈神仙峰稜線上，是座千年古剎，傳說由新羅時代的義湘大師所創建。登上寺廟，宛如仙境般的清風湖與周邊山巒盡收眼底，是個能感受大自然奧妙的地方。法堂屋頂的三分之一覆蓋著岩壁，雄偉奇特的樣貌令人讚嘆大自然的偉大。淨方寺境內有法堂、寮舍、現慧門等。

en.title: Muamsa Temple
en.overview: Climbing up the valley heading east from Seongnae-ri village in Jecheon, Kachiseongsan Mountain stretches its ridge on the left and Donsan Mountain on the right, nestled deep within which lies Muamsa Temple. Although said to have been founded during the Silla Dynasty, the exact founding year is unknown, though it is estimated to have existed since before the early Joseon Dynasty. However, the current main hall, Geuknakjeon, has been confirmed to have been reconstructed in the 16th year of King Yeongjo's reign (1740), and the seated wooden Tathagata statue here is estimated to have been crafted around the same time. Alongside the Buddha statue, Muamsa preserves relics such as a bronze bodhisattva head and Jeonpae.
en.pull_quote: Ascending the eastern valley from Seongnae-ri village in Jecheon, between Kachiseongsan and Donsan mountains, lies the deeply embraced Muamsa Temple...
paragraphs: Climbing the valley running east from Seongnae-ri village in Jecheon, Kachiseongsan stands on the left and Donsan on the right with long ridges, and deep in their embrace sits Muamsa Temple. While said to be built in the Silla period, the precise founding date is unknown, though it is presumed to predate the early Joseon Dynasty. The current main hall, Geuknakjeon, was verified to have been rebuilt in 1740 (the 16th year of King Yeongjo), and the wooden seated Tathagata statue inside is believed to have been created concurrently. Muamsa also preserves relics such as a bronze bodhisattva head and wooden tablets (jeonpae).

A rocky peak sits southwest of the temple resembling an old monk, so it is called Nojangam (Old Monk Rock). Legend says this rock only appears when fog rolls in, which inspired the temple's name, Muamsa (Mist Rock Temple). Existing structures include Geuknakjeon, Chilseonggak, Sansingak, monk quarters, guest rooms, and guardian rooms. Geuknakjeon preserves a seated wooden Amitabha Buddha, a post-Buddha painting, and a Jijang (Ksitigarbha) painting. en.title: Gowon Galbi
en.overview: Gowon Galbi is a barbecue restaurant located in the city center along Uibyeongdae-ro in Jecheon-si. Jecheon Myeongdong Gorigul is an alley brand developed by Jecheon City featuring various meat restaurants, among which Gowon Galbi showcases Hanwoo charcoal-grilled beef. Housed in a remodeled traditional Korean house (hanok), it exudes a serene ambiance with private rooms, making it ideal for treating guests and enjoying a private dining experience. Operating since 2002, its antique interior gives off a cozy feel reminiscent of visiting a hometown home.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialties: Gogwandaejak · Seasoned King Ribs / Handmade Seasoned Pork Ribs / Gowon Haejangguk, etc.
paragraphs: Gowon Galbi is a barbecue restaurant situated in the city center along Uibyeongdae-ro, Jecheon-si. Jecheon Myeongdong Gorigul is a local alley brand developed by Jecheon City featuring diverse meat eateries, with Gowon Galbi specializing in charcoal-grilled Hanwoo beef.

The restaurant, created by remodeling a traditional hanok, offers a tranquil atmosphere with private rooms available, making it wonderful for hosting guests and enjoying private dining. In operation since 2002, its antique interior provides the warm sensation of visiting a hometown home. Main specialties here include Gogwandaejak, seasoned king ribs, Hanwoo yukhoe (beef tartare), and pork ribs, while dining options feature cold noodles (myeon) and hangover soup (haejangguk).

en.title: Worak Sanjang
en.overview: Worak Sanjang is a Korean cuisine specialty restaurant located in Jecheon-si, Chungbuk. Situated near a valley, it allows guests to dine coolly on traditional flat wooden pyeongsang benches during the summer. Visitors can enjoy a wide array of local comfort foods such as homemade tofu kimchi, potato pancakes, acorn jelly (dotorimuk), and seasoned deodeok root, as well as meals like bibimbap and cheonggukjang (fermented soybean paste) set menus, nourishing stamina dishes made with country chicken and duck, and freshwater spicy fish stew. Making reservations in advance ensures a more convenient visit.

en.title: Boriam Hermitage (Namhae)
en.overview: In 683, Master Wonhyo built a small thatched hermitage here to practice asceticism, and after seeing Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, he named the mountain Bogwangsan and the hermitage Bogwangsa. Later, Yi Seong-gye offered 100 days of prayers here before founding the Joseon Dynasty. In gratitude, King Hyeonjong designated this temple as a royal shrine in 1660 and renamed the mountain Geumsan and the temple Boriam. Perched on the peak of Geumsan Mountain, Boriam offers a panoramic view of Geumsan's unique rock formations and the azure Namhae sea.
en.pull_quote: In 683, Master Wonhyo built a small thatched hermitage here to practice asceticism, and after seeing Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, he named the mountain Bogwangsan... Later, Yi Seong-gye offered 100 days of prayers here and opened the Joseon...
paragraphs: In 683, Master Wonhyo built a small thatched hermitage here to practice asceticism, and after seeing Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, he named the mountain Bogwangsan and the hermitage Bogwangsa. Later, Yi Seong-gye offered 100 days of prayers here before founding the Joseon Dynasty. In gratitude, King Hyeonjong designated this temple as a royal shrine in 1660 and renamed the mountain Geumsan and the temple Boriam. Perched on the peak of Geumsan Mountain, Boriam is a beautiful temple where you can take in the bizarre rock formations of Geumsan and the blue scenery of Namhae at a glance.

Inside the temple grounds, the 'Jwaseondae' rock where Master Wonhyo is said to have practiced seated meditation catches the eye, and the nearby rock cave called 'Ssanghongmun' is known as the best among the 38 scenic views of Geumsan. Along with Hongyeonam Hermitage at Naksansa Temple in Yangyang, Gangwon-do, and Bomunsa Temple on Ganghwado Island, Incheon, it is one of the three major prayer sites in Korea, visited by endless streams of devotees. Geumsan is called a 'rock zoo' due to its outstanding scenery, the 'Geumgang Mountain of Namhae,' and numerous animal-shaped rocks. Founded by Master Wonhyo at the summit of Geumsan, where you can look down upon the harmony of the indigo sea and green fields to fully enjoy the beauty of Hallyeohaesang National Park, it is one of the nation's top three prayer sites.

paragraphs: 683年に元暁大師がここで草庵を建てて修行し、観世音菩薩にまみえた後、山の名前を菩光山、草庵を菩光寺と名付けた。のちに李成桂がここで百日祈願をして朝鮮王朝を開いたといわれ、その感謝の意味を込めて1660年に孝宗がこの寺を王室の原堂とし、山の名前を錦山、寺の名前を菩提庵に変更した。錦山の山頂に位置する菩提庵は、錦山の奇岩怪石と青々とした南海の景色を一望できる美しい寺である。

境内には元暁大師が座禅したという座禅台の岩が目を引き、付近の双虹門という岩の洞窟は錦山38景の筆頭として知られている。江原道襄陽郡の洛山寺紅蓮庵、京畿道強化島の菩門寺とともに、国内三大祈願処の一つとして信徒たちが連日列をなして訪れている。優れた景色と南海の金剛山、動物の形をした岩が多いことから「岩の動物園」と呼ばれる錦山。紺碧の海と緑豊かな田園の調和を見下ろすことができ、閑麗海上国立公園の美しさを満喫できる錦山の山頂に元暁大師が創建した韓国三大祈願処の一つ。

paragraphs: 西元683年，元曉大師在此地搭建草堂修行，親睹觀世音菩薩後，將山名改為菩光山，草堂名為菩光寺。後來李成桂曾在此進行百日祈禱並開創朝鮮王朝，為表感謝之意，朝鮮顯宗於1660年將此寺定為王室的祈福道場，並將山名改為錦山，寺名改為菩提庵。坐落於錦山山頂的菩提庵是一座美麗的寺廟，可將錦山的奇岩怪石與蔚藍的南海風光盡收眼底。
寺內有相傳為元曉大師打坐的「座禪臺」岩石，引人注目；附近的「雙虹門」岩洞則被譽為錦山38景之首。這裡與江原道襄陽郡洛山寺紅蓮庵、京畿道江華島菩門寺並稱為韓國三大祈願處，信徒們絡繹不絕。錦山因景色秀麗、被譽為「南海的金剛山」，且擁有許多動物造型的岩石而被稱為「岩石動物園」。由元曉大師創建於錦山山頂，俯瞰著靛藍海水與翠綠田野交織的美景，盡情享受閑麗海上公園的風光，是韓國三大祈願處之一。

en.title: Dogok Wolpo Beach
en.overview: Dogok Wolpo Beach is located south of Namhae-eup. Unlike beaches with plain sandy shores, it features a blend of smooth pebble stones and sand, flanked by pine forests planted as windbreaks. With spots for rocky shore fishing, it is a cozy beach where families can spend a quiet time. The scenery of Koktubang Beach on the left side of the beach is superb, and a coastal tourist road nearby allows visitors to fully enjoy the coastal splendors. The beach shore features a moderate mix of gravel and sand.

en.title: Hogusan County Park
en.overview: Designated as a Namhae County Park, Hogusan County Park stands at 650 meters above sea level. Yongmunsa Temple, nestled on Hogusan Mountain, is the largest and oldest temple in Namhae. Hogusan, shaped like a lying tiger, features various trees shimmering in the sunlight, with clear valley streams flowing down to Yongso Pond, where a dragon is said to have ascended to heaven. The mountain embraces Yongmunsa Temple; observing the mountain terrain from inside the temple reveals a cozy and warm atmosphere in all directions, contrasting with the fierce tiger and dragon names.

When you enter the temple and observe the mountain terrain, despite the tiger and dragon names inspired by the mountain and temple, the surroundings are cozy and warm on all sides. It is said to have been built as the successor to Bogwangsa—which was established when Master Wonhyo of the Silla Dynasty visited Geumsan and its temple fortune flourished—alongside many other temples built nearby. It was also designated as a royal prayer temple (Sguksa) during the reign of King Sukjong of the Joseon Dynasty.

虎九山は龍門寺を抱いており、寺の中に足を踏み入れて山の気勢を眺めると、虎と龍から取った山と寺の名前に反して四方が穏やかで温かい。新羅時代の元暁大師が錦山を訪れて建てた菩光寺の寺運が隆盛するにつれ、近隣に建てられた多くのお寺と共に建てられたもので、菩光寺の後身であると伝えられており、朝鮮時代の粛宗の時に守国寺に指定され、王室の保護を受けた寺院でもある。

en.title: Seolheulsan Mountain
en.overview: Seolheulsan Mountain is adjacent to Mangsan Mountain in Honghyeon-ri, Nam-myeon, Namhae-gun, and is renowned for its spectacular sunrise views. Looking down from the summit, the deep inlet of Anggangman Bay comes into full view, and you can also overlook Nodo Island (where Seo Po Kim Man-jung was exiled) and the charming little islands of Hallyeohaesang National Park. A beacon mound has been restored at the summit of Seolheulsan. Historically, beacon mounds were placed in locations with wide panoramic views, allowing visitors to overlook the Hallyeo Waterway, Anggangman Bay, and the endless open sea.

en.title: Oryukdo Raw Fish Center
en.overview: Located at a scenic viewpoint where the beautiful panorama of Mijo Port unfolds like a folding screen, Oryukdo Raw Fish Center is a great place to enjoy delicious and fresh sliced raw fish (hwed). In addition, various dining options such as grilled fish, spicy raw fish stew (maeuntang), special mulhoe (cold raw fish soup), and mulhoe naengmyeon are available. Private room facilities are also provided.

en.title: Jisan Restaurant
en.overview: A special dish you can uniquely taste in Namhae, famed for its pristine waters, is jolbok (little pufferfish) cuisine. Jolbok belongs to the pufferfish family and is also called milbok, or norangbok in Yeosu. Pufferfish is rich in collagen, making it great for women's skin care, and high in protein, making it popular for curing hangovers. Featuring jolbok as its main dish, Jisan Restaurant is located right in front of Mijo Port—the largest port in Namhae-gun—and is renowned for its clean and refreshing flavors. The main specialties here are jolbok-guk (clear pufferfish soup) and jolbok튀김 (fried pufferfish).

en.title: Haebinjeong
en.overview: Located within Namhae Geumsan National Park, Haebinjeong meticulously selects and uses only fresh fish freshly caught from Samcheonpo, offering meat with a savory texture and exceptional taste. You can dine while enjoying breathtaking views of the open sea. Meals are served as full course table settings (hansang-charim). The representative menu is the Sotbap Hansang, which includes stone-pot rice with grilled fish, marinated spicy crabs (yangnyeom gejang), duburuchim (stir-fried pork), and various side dishes. Other options include the Yangnyeom Gejang Hansang and seasonal cold noodles (naengmyeon).

en.title: Sangju Bada Raw Fish Restaurant
en.overview: Sangju Beach is located inside Hallyeohaesang National Park. Being a seaside area, there are an abundance of raw fish restaurants around. Among them, Sangju Bada Raw Fish Restaurant stands out with its off-white granite exterior finish and large sign on the roof. The long rectangular interior is neatly arranged and surprisingly spacious. True to its seaside location, portions are generous, and the spicy, hearty maeuntang (fish stew) made with fresh ingredients offers a truly special taste.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delicacy: Natural Assorted Raw Fish · Braised Hairtail / Anchovy Ssambap / Mulhoe, etc.

Yi Gok was a late Goryeo dynasty scholar and the father of Yi Saek. He passed the Yuan dynasty civil service examination, gaining recognition for his talent and spreading his literary fame. paragraphs: Mallyang-ri Camellia Forest in Seo-myeon, one of the Eight Scenic Views of Seocheon, is designated as a Natural Monument. Here, 85 camellia trees, approximately 500 years old, form a dense forest across 8,265㎡. Visiting the camellia forest from late March to early May allows visitors to fully enjoy shy red camellia flowers blooming amidst green leaves. Climbing up to Dongbaekjeong Pavilion at the summit offers a panoramic view of the blue West Sea and beautiful sunsets.

In particular, the scenery of the sea harmonizing with the landscape of Oryeokdo Island right in front gives the joy of appreciating a piece of oriental painting. Due to strong winds on the western side of the Mallyang-ri Camellia Forest, only a few trees remain, while about 70 trees are distributed on the eastern side. Camellia trees, belonging to the Theaceae family, are subtropical evergreen broad-leaved trees that grow up to 7m tall, but the camellia trees here are about 2m tall and spread sideways due to strong winds. According to legend, about 500 years ago, the naval commander of Mallyang received a revelation in a dream that if he extensively propagated flower clusters by the seaside, laughter and prosperity would always bloom in the village. When he went to the seaside, flowers were indeed there...

特に、目の前にある島・オリョクド（五力島）の風景と調和した海の姿は、まるで一幅の東洋画を見ているかのような喜びを与えてくれる。馬梁里の椿の森の西側は風が強く数本しか残っておらず、東側には70余株が分布している。ツバキ科に属する椿は高さ7mまで育つ暖帯性の常緑広葉樹であるが、ここの椿は強風のために高さが2m前後であり、横に広がっている。伝説によると、約500年前、馬梁の水軍僉使（スグンチョムサ）が夢の中で海辺にある花の塊をたくさん増やせば村にいつも笑い花が咲き繁栄するだろうというお告げを受け、海辺に行ってみると本当に花があったため増殖させた...

en.overview: This is a scenic raw fish restaurant located at Chunjangdae Beach in Seocheon, Chungnam. While famous for its autumn gizzard shad (jeon-eo) dishes, the secret to its popularity lies in 100% fresh natural raw fish caught in the West Sea every dawn, accompanied by eco-friendly side dishes made with rice and vegetables farmed directly by the owner. en.title: Seosan Hoegwan
en.overview: Contrary to its name, Seosan Hoegwan is located in Seocheon, not Seosan, and specializes in Seocheon's famous webfoot octopus (juggumi). Located right in front of the tidal flat at Mallyangpogu Port in Seocheon, it is famous for serving fresh and delicious webfoot octopus caught live using conch shells in this region. The restaurant serves webfoot octopus cooked in iron-griddle stir-fry (cheolpan-bokkeum) and shabu-shabu styles, with peak season lasting from around February to early May. In addition, it offers various seafood menus such as rockfish soup and blue crab soup, with the webfoot octopus iron-griddle stir-fry being the main signature dish. Nearby tourist attractions such as Dongbaekjeong Pavilion above Mallyangpogu Port, Seocheon Marine Glamping, and Chunjangdae Beach are clustered around, making it a great place to combine for sightseeing.

en.title: Sujeong Naengmyeon
en.overview: Sujeong Naengmyeon is located on the left side of Pangyo Station, a 10-minute drive from Seocheon Interchange toward Buyeo. Featuring three private rooms, it is great for holding various gatherings in a cozy atmosphere, and Sujeong Naengmyeon is famous enough to have a considerable number of regular customers. Unlike the rapidly changing flavors of modern times, Sujeong Naengmyeon's cold noodles have remained unchanged and consistent for 25 years.

Located 21 km south of Namhae-eup, it attracts numerous vacationers every summer due to the pleasant feel of the sand against bare feet.

en.title: Songjeong Solbaram Beach (Pine Wind Beach)
en.overview: Songjeong Solbaram Beach is the second-largest bathing resort in Namhae following Sangju Eunmorae Beach. Featuring pine trees over 100 years old, the beach connects two villages, Songjeong Village and Songnam Village. The name originated from the late Joseon dynasty when a pavilion acting as a surveillance post under the Tongyeong Forest Surveillance Control Department to protect forests like Geumsan and Daegoksan was called Songjeong (松停). Consequently, Songjeong Village became situated above the roadside frequented by visitors searching for Geumsan, Namhae's famous mountain along National Route 19, and the pristine beaches of Sangju and Songjeong.

The name originated from the late Joseon dynasty when a pavilion acting as a surveillance post under the Tongyeong Forest Surveillance Control Department to protect forests like Geumsan and Daegoksan was called Songjeong (松停). Consequently, Songjeong Village became situated above the roadside frequented by visitors searching for Geumsan, Namhae's famous mountain along National Route 19, and the pristine beaches of Sangju and Songjeong.

In January 2020, Songjeong Beach created the 'Songjeong Solbaram Campsite' utilizing crushed stone, Asian pines, and hackberry trees to make it comfortable for campers to stay, gaining popularity as a southern emotional travel destination. The surroundings of the beach feature rocky coastline lines and long-standing sea pine trees over a century old. Furthermore, stepping slightly outside the beach reveals coastal scenery of steep cliffs mixed with pebble stones and bizarre rocks.

en.title: Jirisan National Park (Hadong)
en.overview: Jirisan is a sacred mountain located at the southern end of the Sobaek Mountain Range, boasting mysterious mountain terrain with large and small peaks and rich tourism resources that attract visitors throughout all four seasons. Spanning three provinces and five cities/counties—including Hadong-gun, Hamyang-gun, and Sancheong-gun in Gyeongsangnam-do, Namwon-si in Jeollabuk-do, and Gurye-gun in Jeollanam-do—it is one of the three major sacred mountains (Samsinsan) along with Geumgangsan and Hallasan. Regarded as Korea's premier natural realm once called Duryusan or Bangjangsan, Jirisan is where the Baekdudaegan mountain range heads south and stands tall, blocked by the Seomjinjin River.
en.pull_quote: Jirisan is a sacred mountain located at the southern end of the Sobaek Mountain Range, boasting mysterious mountain terrain with large and small peaks and rich tourism resources that attract visitors throughout all four seasons. Gyeongsangnam-do...

Regarded as Korea's premier natural realm once called Duryusan or Bangjangsan, Jirisan is formed where the Baekdudaegan mountain range heads south only to stand tall against the barrier of the Seomjin River. In the Hadong area, tourist resources are abundant, including temples like Ssanggyesa and Chilbulsa, as well as Bunil Waterfall, Hwagae Valley, Cheonghakdong, and Doinchon.

en.title: Bulil Waterfall
en.overview: Bulil Waterfall is one of the eight scenic views of Jirisan, located 3 km away from Ssanggyesa Temple. Along the hiking trail from Ssanggyesa, there is a small hermitage called Guksaam. Right beside Bulilam Hermitage, Bulil Waterfall cascades down a cliff like a stream of water pouring from the sky. Standing 60 meters high and 3 meters wide, this naturally formed two-tier waterfall never dries up year-round, although the volume of water varies by season. Below the waterfall are Yongchu Pool and Hak Pool, adding a deep sense of natural mystery.

en.title: Chilbulsa Temple (Hadong)
en.overview: Perched at an altitude of approximately 800 meters on Banyabong Peak of Jirisan, Chilbulsa Temple is said to have been founded after the seven sons of King Suro—the founder of Geumgwan Gaya in the Nakdong River basin around the Gimhae area in the early Three Kingdoms period—came here to practice asceticism and all attained enlightenment. Growing into a central temple of Gaya Buddhism, Chilbulsa became even more famous for building 'Ajabang' (a hypogeum room where a single fire could keep the room warm for 100 days) during the reign of King Hyegong of Silla about 1,100 years ago. The original structures were destroyed by war and later rebuilt in 1978 by Venerable Jewoldang Tonggwang.

en.title: Hadong Goseong Fortress
en.overview: This is a stone fortress built during the Silla Dynasty, featuring a nearly pentagonal shape along the mountain ridge. The 'Hadong-gun Eupji' (Gazetteer of Hadong-gun County) is the sole historical source regarding the fortress's history. Based on records, location, and scale, it is believed to have been constructed by Silla for military purposes. However, recent opinions suggest it may be a fortress of Goguryeo origin, built when Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo marched south through Silla to subdue Japanese forces in the early 5th century.
en.pull_quote: This is a stone fortress built during the Silla Dynasty, featuring a nearly pentagonal shape along the mountain ridge. The 'Hadong-gun Eupji' is the sole historical source...
paragraphs: This is a stone fortress built during the Silla Dynasty, featuring a nearly pentagonal shape along the mountain ridge. The 'Hadong-gun Eupji' is the sole historical source regarding the fortress's history. Based on records, location, and scale, it is believed to have been constructed by Silla for military purposes, though recent opinions suggest it may be a Goguryeo-style fortress built when King Gwanggaeto the Great moved south in the early 5th century.

The walls were solidly built using squared stones and natural rocks. While the fortress walls remain mostly intact, the section overlooking the Seomjin River to the southwest has collapsed, leaving only piles of stone. Located on a high ridge halfway up the mountain chain stretching from Jirisan, the fortress has a ladder-like cross-section, solidly built with processed rectangular stones and featuring two gates on the north and south.

en.title: Hadong Songnim Park (Pine Tree Forest)
en.overview: Created in 1745 (the 21st year of King Yeongjo's reign in the Joseon Dynasty) by Dohobusa Jeon Cheon-sang, this pine forest was planted to protect Hadong-eup (then Cheongha-eup) by blocking the sea breeze from Gwangyang Bay and the sandy winds of the Seomjin River. About 1,500 pine trees were planted at its creation, and today around 900 trees, including successor saplings, carry on its legacy. The 260-year-old aged pines, clear Seomjin River, and expansive white sandy beach combine to resemble a landscape painting, drawing poets and scholars since ancient times.
en.pull_quote: Created in 1745 by Dohobusa Jeon Cheon-sang to protect Hadong-eup from sea breezes and sandy winds, this pine forest features ancient trees and a wide sandy beach...
paragraphs: Created in 1745 (the 21st year of King Yeongjo's reign in the Joseon Dynasty) by Dohobusa Jeon Cheon-sang, this pine forest was planted to protect Hadong-eup (then Cheongha-eup) by blocking the sea breeze from Gwangyang Bay and the sandy winds of the Seomjin River. About 1,500 pine trees were planted at its creation, and today around 900 trees, including successor saplings, carry on its legacy. The 260-year-old aged pines, clear Seomjin River, and expansive white sandy beach combine to resemble a landscape painting, drawing poets and scholars since ancient times.

Because of this, Hadong is called the home of 'Baeksacheongsong' (white sand and green pines) and 'Baeksacheongjuk' (white sand and green bamboos). Historically, Hadong Songnim was a venue where women held spring flower-viewing picnics, and the sandy beach in front of the forest served as an inland beach when seawater flowed in and out. Today, it is loved as a space offering natural education and relaxation to both locals and tourists. In particular, on the first full moon of the lunar year (Jeongwol Daeboreum), a 'Daljip Taeugi' (moonhouse burning) event is held on the sandy beach to harbor the wishes of Hadong residents, fostering harmony with neighbors from the Jeolla region.

paragraphs: 朝鮮英祖21年（1745年），都護府使田天祥為了阻擋光陽灣的海風與蟾津江的沙塵暴、保護河東邑（當時的清河邑）而營造了這片松林。建林之初種植了約1,500棵松樹，如今包含後繼樹在內，約有900多棵松樹延續著其脈絡。歷經260多年歲月的古松與清澈的蟾津江、寬廣的白沙灘相互輝映，宛如一幅風景畫，自古以來便吸引無數詩人墨客駐足。
因此，河東被稱為「白沙青松」、「白沙青竹」之鄉。河東松林自古是婦女們舉辦春遊踏青的場所，松林前的白沙灘曾因海水漲退而發揮內陸海水浴場的作用。如今，這裡成為深受當地居民與遊客喜愛的自然教育與休憩空間。特別是在正月大滿月時，白沙灘上會舉辦寄託河東郡民願望的「燒月屋」活動，與鄰近的全羅道居民一同營造和諧交流的盛會。
