en.title: Samsingung Palace
en.overview: Located in Muggye-ri, Cheongam-myeon, Samsingung sits at an elevation of 850 meters after winding through the mountain path of Cheonghakdong deep within Jirisan, the sacred mountain of the Korean people. The official name of Samsingung is Baedal Seongjeon Samsingung. Established in 1983 by local native Kang Min-ju (Venerable Hanpul), it restores the 'Sodo' (sacred ritual area) of the Gojoseon era. As a sacred shrine of the Baedal people enshrining Hwanin, Hwanung, and Dangun—the founding ancestors of the nation—it has established itself as a national sanctuary preserving Korea's orthodox Taoist lineage and practicing Seon (immortal) arts.
en.pull_quote: Located at an elevation of 850m deep within Jirisan, Samsingung is a sacred sanctuary established to restore the ancient Sodo and enshrine the nation's founding ancestors...
paragraphs: Located in Muggye-ri, Cheongam-myeon, Samsingung sits at an elevation of 850 meters after winding through the mountain path of Cheonghakdong deep within Jirisan, the sacred mountain of the Korean people. The official name of Samsingung is Baedal Seongjeon Samsingung. Established in 1983 by local native Kang Min-ju (Venerable Hanpul), it restores the 'Sodo' (sacred ritual area) of the Gojoseon era. As a sacred shrine of the Baedal people enshrining Hwanin, Hwanung, and Dangun—the founding ancestors of the nation—it has established itself as a national sanctuary preserving Korea's orthodox Taoist lineage and practicing Seon (immortal) arts. Over 1,500 stone towers, piled up by Venerable Hanpul—who inherited the ancient Seon traditions—and his disciples through training, harmonize with the surrounding forest to exude an exotic ambiance.

These stone towers are called 'Wonryeok Sostae' here. In the Samhan period, 'Sodo'—sacred grounds where sacrifices were offered to heavenly deities—were marked with 'Sostae' (tall wooden poles topped with wild goose carvings) to prevent ordinary people from approaching. Just as prayers are embedded in a village shrine, wishes are made while stacking Sostae with stones from the foot of Jirisan to restore the ancient Sodo. By building 3,333 Sostae to form a sanctuary, it aims to revive our nation's unique spiritual culture and realize the ideal of 'Hongik Ingan' (broadly benefiting humanity).

ja.title: 三星宮（サムシングン）
ja.region_label: 慶南 河東郡 青岩面
ja.addr: 慶尚南道 河東郡 青岩面 三星宮길 13
ja.overview: 青岩面黙渓里に位置し、韓民族の霊山である智異山の懐深く、青岩面青鶴洞の山道を曲がりくねって1.5㎞ほど歩くと標高850mに三星宮が佇んでいる。三星宮の正確な名称は「倍達聖殿三星宮」で、この地出身の姜民珠（ハンプル仙師）が1983年に古朝鮮時代の蘇都を復元し、民族の聖祖である桓因、桓雄、檀君を祀る倍達民族聖殿として、民族の正統な道脈である仙道を守り、神仙道を修行する民族の道場として定着しつつある。昔から伝わってきた仙道を受け継いだハンプル仙師が修業者たちと共に石を積み上げて作り上げた1,500余りの石塔が、周辺の森と調和して異国的な情緒を醸し出している。
ja.pull_quote: 智異山の懐深く、標高850mに位置する三星宮は、古朝鮮時代の蘇都を復元し、民族の聖祖を祀るために建てられた聖地である…
paragraphs: 青岩面黙渓里に位置し、韓民族の霊山である智異山の懐深く、青岩面青鶴洞の山道を曲がりくねって1.5㎞ほど歩くと標高850mに三星宮が佇んでいる。三星宮の正確な名称は倍達聖殿三星宮で、この地出身の姜民珠（ハンプル仙師）が1983年に古朝鮮時代の蘇都を復元し、民族の聖祖である桓因、桓雄、檀君を祀る倍達民族聖殿として、民族の正統道脈である仙道を守り、神仙道を修行する民族の道場として定着しつつある。昔から伝わってきた仙道を受け継いだハンプル仙師が修業者たちと共に修行しながら積み上げた1,500余りの石塔が周辺の森と調和し、異国的な情緒を醸し出している。
これらの石塔はここでは「元力ソスタ（솟대）」と呼ばれる。三韓時代に天神に祭祀を捧げた聖地「蘇都」には、一般人の接近を禁じるため高い木の上にガチョウの彫刻を載せたソスタを目印にした。ソウォンダン（城隍堂）に祈りを込めるように、願いを込めて智異山の麓の石でソスタを積み上げ、昔の蘇都を復元している。3,333個のソスタを積み上げて聖殿をなし、我が民族固有の精神文化を取り戻して「弘益人間」の世界を…

zh.overview: 位於青岩面墨溪里，深入韓民族靈山智異山的懷抱中，沿著青岩面青鶴洞的山路蜿蜒步行約1.5公里，便能在海拔850米處見到三星宮。三星宮的正稱是「倍達聖殿三星宮」，由當地出身的姜民柱（韓菩仙師）於1983年復原古朝鮮時代的蘇都而成。作為供奉民族聖祖桓因、桓雄、檀君的倍達民族聖殿，它正逐漸確立為守護民族正統道脈、修行神仙道的民族道場。由繼承自古流傳仙道的韓菩仙師與修行者們一同疊石堆砌而成的1,500多個石塔，與周圍的森林相融，散發著異國風情。
zh.pull_quote: 位於海拔850米智異山深處的三星宮，是為了復原古朝鮮蘇都、供奉民族聖祖而建的聖殿……
paragraphs: 位於青岩面墨溪里，深入韓民族靈山智異山的懷抱中，沿著青岩面青鶴洞的山路蜿蜒步行約1.5公里，便能在海拔850米處見到三星宮。三星宮的正稱是倍達聖殿三星宮，由當地出身的姜民柱（韓菩仙師）於1983年復原古朝鮮時代的蘇都而成。作為供奉民族聖祖桓因、桓雄、檀君的倍達民族聖殿，它正逐漸確立為守護民族正統道脈、修行神仙道的民族道場。由繼承自古流傳仙道的韓菩仙師與修行者們一同修行並疊石堆砌而成的1,500多個石塔，與周圍的森林相融，散發著異國風情。
這些石塔在這裡被稱為「元力솟대（長竿）」。在三韓時代，祭祀天神的聖地「蘇都」通常會立上頂端雕有大雁木雕的長竿，以禁止一般人接近。就像在城隍堂中寄託祈願一樣，人們利用智異山腳下的石塊堆砌長竿來復原古代的蘇都。透過堆疊3,333個長竿建立聖殿，找回我民族固有的精神文化，實現「弘益人間」的世界……

en.title: Dongheung Sikdang
en.overview: Located in Hadong-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do, Dongheung Sikdang is a specialty restaurant specializing in freshwater clam (jaecheop) dishes. Jaecheop is widely known as a hangover cure because it activates liver function, relieves fatigue, and restores vitality. The owner personally cooks dishes using only wild jaecheop harvested from the Seomjin River, offering exceptional flavor. Jaecheopguk (clam soup), seasoned with wild water dropwort from the foothills of Jirisan, is fragrant and deep, while jaecheophoe (raw clam salad), made by mixing freshly picked clams withチョogochujang (sweet and spicy chili paste) and assorted vegetables, boasts a sweet, sour, and delightfully chewy texture.

en.title: Chatnip Masul (Tea Leaf Magic)
en.overview: Located in Hadong, Chatnip Masul is a tranquil space where visitors can savor the deep taste and aroma of tea in a serene atmosphere, taking time to focus entirely on themselves. You can enjoy a tea seed tea-ceremony course while listening to stories about tea food and various tea varieties. Tea selections include roasted tea (deok-eum-cha), black tea, yellow tea, oolong tea, and aged white tea (nobaek-cha), allowing you to choose according to your preference. Hadong is visited by many travelers throughout the seasons due to its abundant attractions, and stopping by Chatnip Masul provides healthy food and a comfortable sanctuary as a healing city.

en.title: Sumvawi (Shumbawi Rock)
en.overview: Located about 2.5 hours from Seoul, Sumvawi sits at the foot of Gyebangsan Mountain, South Korea's 5th highest peak known for its pristine nature at the 'Happy 700' highland (where human biological rhythms are said to be most active). Gyebangsan is currently popular for winter trekking due to its snow-covered landscapes and yew tree clusters, and an auto-camping site right below the hiking trail makes it great for family leisure. Nearby attractions include the Lee Seung-bok Memorial Hall, Bangadari Mineral Spring, Woljeongsa Temple in Odaesan, Bongpyeong Buckwheat Flower Village, Yongpyong Ski Resort, and Phoenix Park. Visitors can enjoy seasonal sports like skiing in winter and rafting or mountain ATVs in summer.
en.pull_quote: Representative Specialties: Trout Sashimi · Fried Trout / Grilled Trout, etc.
paragraphs: Located about 2.5 hours from Seoul, Sumvawi sits at the foot of Gyebangsan Mountain, South Korea's 5th highest peak known for its pristine nature at the 'Happy 700' highland. Nearby attractions include the Lee Seung-bok Memorial Hall, Bangadari Mineral Spring, Woljeongsa Temple in Odaesan, Bongpyeong Buckwheat Flower Village, Yongpyong Ski Resort, and Phoenix Park. Visitors can enjoy seasonal sports like skiing in winter and rafting or mountain ATVs in summer.

Sumvawi's trout sashimi is served mixed with vegetable, soybean powder, and perilla powder, making it a well-being dish suited for modern healthy lifestyles. All vegetables and wild greens here are freshly sourced from the surrounding unpolluted nature. In particular, rice is freshly cooked to order in a traditional stone pot, offering a piping-hot meal accompanied by savory Nurungji (scorched rice water). Designated as an exemplary restaurant by Pyeongchang-gun.

ja.title: シムバウィ
ja.addr: 江原特別自治道平昌郡龍坪面雲頭嶺路651
ja.overview: ソウルから約2時間30分ほど要するシムバウィは、人間の生体リズムが最も活発になる「happy700高地」に位置し、空気が綺麗で景色が良い韓国で5番目に高い山・鶏芳山（ケバンサン）の麓にある。特に鶏芳山は雪に覆われた雪景色やチョウセンゴヨウ（注目）の群生地として最近注目を集める冬山であり、登山道のすぐ下にオートキャンプ場があるため家族連れのレジャーにぴったりだ。周辺の有名な観光地としては、李承福記念館、芳台里（パンダリ）薬水、五台山月精寺、平昌面メ밀（そば）꽃村、龍坪スキー場、フェニックスパークが隣接しており、冬はスキー、夏はラフティングやバギーなどスポーツと連動した様々な観光を楽しむことができる。
ja.pull_quote: 代表的な絶品グルメ：マス刺身・マスの唐揚げ / マスの塩焼きなど

シムバウィのマス刺身は、きな粉やエゴマ粉を野菜と一緒に和えて食べるスタイルで、近年のウェルビーイング（健康志向）に関心のある人々に適した料理である。ここですべての野菜やナムルは、周囲の自然から得た無公害の食材として提供されており、特に石釜で食べる分だけのご飯をその都度炊き上げるため、熱々のご飯と香ばしいおこげスープ（スンニュン）の味わいが絶品の店である。平昌郡指定の模範飲食店。

zh.title: 沈岩（쉼바위）
zh.addr: 江原特別自治道平昌郡龍坪面雲頭嶺路651
zh.overview: 從首爾出發約需2小時30分鐘的沈岩，坐落於韓國第五高山——雞芳山的山腳下。這裡位於「Happy 700高地」（人體生物節律最活躍的高地），空氣清新、風景秀麗。特別是雞芳山以覆滿白雪的雪景和紅豆杉群落成為近期備受矚目的冬日名山，登山步道下方設有汽車露營場，非常適合全家大小一同休閒度假。周邊著名景點有李承福紀念館、芳臺里藥水、五台山月精寺、蓬坪蕎麥花村、龍坪滑雪場及鳳凰公園等。冬天可以滑雪，夏天可以體驗漂流和山地越野車，讓您盡情享受豐富多樣的運動休閒旅遊。
zh.pull_quote: 代表美食：鱒魚生魚片 · 炸鱒魚 / 烤鱒魚等

en.title: Memilkkotpilmuryeop (When Buckwheat Flowers Bloom)
en.overview: Memilkkotpilmuryeop is a restaurant located inside the former home of author Gasan Lee Hyo-seok, where he was born in 1907 and lived until age 14. Offering authentic Gangwon-do local flavors, the restaurant serves healthy food prepared with self-farmed buckwheat and organic vegetables. Featured in various media outlets, it can accommodate large groups of up to 130 people. Signature dishes include soy sauce herb buckwheat noodles and homemade buckwheat jelly, alongside other buckwheat-based treats like homemade buckwheat jelly rice soup and buckwheat potato pancakes.
en.pull_quote: Representative Specialties: Soy Sauce Herb Buckwheat Noodles (Bibim) · Cold Buckwheat Noodles / Spicy Buckwheat Noodles / Homemade Buckwheat Jelly, etc.

en.title: Naeri Valley
en.overview: Yeongwol Naeri Valley is a scenic valley located in Gimsatgat-myeon, Yeongwol-gun, about 30 km past Gossi Cave from Yeongwol-eup toward Sangdong. Only about 3 km of the valley entrance is accessible to visitors, while the rest is surrounded by virgin forests, creating breathtaking hidden scenery. It is one of Yeongwol's representative valley destinations, formed by the convergence of waters flowing down from Guryongsan Mountain in Gyeongsangbuk-do and springs from the fir forests of Sendalsan Mountain in Gangwon-do. Surrounded by mountains, it features crystal-clear waters and aquatic life such as local fish species.

paragraphs: Yeongwol Naeri Valley is a scenic valley located in Gimsatgat-myeon, Yeongwol-gun, about 30 km past Gossi Cave from Yeongwol-eup toward Sangdong. Only about 3 km of the valley entrance is accessible to visitors, while the rest is surrounded by virgin forests, creating breathtaking hidden scenery. It is one of Yeongwol's representative valley destinations, formed by the convergence of waters flowing down from Guryongsan Mountain in Gyeongsangbuk-do and springs from the fir forests of Sendalsan Mountain in Gangwon-do. Surrounded by mountains, it features crystal-clear waters and aquatic life such as local fish species.

With its majestic mountain topography and clear flowing waters, the valley attracts many summer vacationers looking to enjoy family water play and fishing with children. Nearby sits Chilyong Waterfall, and bizarre rock cliffs harmonize with the lush forest to create magnificent views. In spring, bright red azaleas blooming among the rocks around the valley are a stunning sight. Nearby attractions include the historic walking trail of Cheongnyeongpo, Seonam Village's Peninsula Terrain, and Byeolmaro Observatory. Cheongnyeongpo is located 5 km from Yeongwol-eup where the poet Kim Sat-gat lived, featuring his former home, literature museum, and engraved poems.

ja.title: 内里渓谷（ネリゲゴク）
ja.addr: 江原特別自治道寧越郡金삿갓面内里渓谷路
ja.overview: 寧越（ヨンウォル）の内里渓谷は、寧越郡金삿갓面にある美しい渓谷で、寧越邑から高氏洞窟を過ぎて上東方面へ30kmの地点にある。渓谷の入り口から約3kmほどだけが人の足跡が届き、残りの区域は原生林に囲まれて秘境を演出している。慶尚北道の九龍山から流れ下る水と、江原道の仙達山のモミの森から湧き出る水が合流して渓谷を形成する、寧越を代表する渓谷観光地である。山々に囲まれ、澄んだ綺麗な水とカダクメギなどの魚類や多様な水生動物が生息している。

zh.overview: 寧越內里溪谷是位於寧越郡金삿갓面的一處美麗溪谷，距離寧越邑穿過高氏洞窟往上東方向約30公里處。溪谷入口僅約3公里左右有人跡罕至，其餘區域皆被原始森林包圍，呈現出絕美的秘境景致。這裡匯集了慶北九龍山流下的水與江原道仙達山冷杉林湧出的清泉，是寧越最具代表性的溪谷旅遊勝地。周圍群山環繞，擁有清澈見底的溪水，並棲息著山女魚等魚類及各種水生動物。

en.title: Yeongwol Orayeon (Gangwon Paleozoic National Geopark)
en.overview: Orayeon, part of the Donggang River section, is a pristine scenic area where fluvial landforms are intensively developed, serving as a representative site for entrenched meandering rivers. It features a continuous distribution of various micro-fluvial landforms such as river cliffs (vertical cliffs around Orayeon), canyon topography (Orayeon Valley) formed by river erosion, abandoned channels (Sangseonam, Jungseonam, Haseonam) showing traces of past river flows, and pools, riffles, and runs.

paragraphs: Orayeon, part of the Donggang River section, is a pristine scenic area where fluvial landforms are intensively developed, serving as a representative site for entrenched meandering rivers. It features a continuous distribution of various micro-fluvial landforms such as river cliffs (vertical cliffs around Orayeon), canyon topography (Orayeon Valley) formed by river erosion, abandoned channels (Sangseonam, Jungseonam, Haseonam) showing traces of past river flows, and pools, riffles, and runs. These fluvial elements harmonize with the vegetation landscape blending rivers, exposed rock outcrops, and forest zones, demonstrating the representative scenic perfection of the Donggang River basin.

In particular, the spatial contrast created by river flows and rock terrain highlights Orayeon as one of the most scenic areas in the upper Donggang River. Orayeon is a geological site based on the Mesozoic Jurassic Bansong Formation distributed around Geoun-ri, Yeongwol-eup, Yeongwol-gun, Gangwon-do, primarily consisting of clastic sedimentary rocks such as sandstone and shale.

ja.title: 寧越魚ラ淵（江原古生代国家地質公園）

ja.overview: 東江の一部区間にあたる魚ラ淵（オラヨン）一帯は、河川地形が集約的に発達した自然の景観地域であり、穿入蛇行河川が典型的に見られる代表的な区間である。ここでは河川の外側斜面に発達した河食崖（魚ラ淵一帯の垂直絶壁）、河川の侵食作用により形成された峡谷地形（魚ラ淵渓谷）、過去の河川の流路の痕跡を示す旧河道（上・中・下仙岩）、そして淵（プール）、瀬、急流など多様な河川微地形が連続的に分布している。

特に河川の流れと岩盤地形が作り出す空間的対比は、魚ラ淵を東江上流区間の中でも景観的代表性が際立つ地域に際立たせている。魚ラ淵は、江原特別自治道寧越郡寧越邑巨雲里一帯に分布する中生代ジュラ紀の盤松層を基盤岩とする地質名所で、主に砂岩と頁岩（シェール）からなる砕屑性堆積岩が分布している。

特別是河川流向與岩盤地形所產生的空間對比，使魚羅淵在東江上游區段中成為景觀代表性極為突出的地區。魚羅淵是以分佈於江原特別自治道寧越郡寧越邑巨雲里一帶的中生代侏羅紀半松層為基盤岩的地質名勝，主要分佈有砂岩和頁岩等碎屑沉積岩。

en.title: Gossigul Cave (Gangwon Paleozoic National Geopark)
en.overview: Offering a glimpse into 400 million years of mystery, Gossi Cave is one of South Korea's representative caves. It was named after the Go family, who took refuge here during the Japanese invasions of Korea (Imjin War), and is also said to have been used as a ascetic training ground. In the past, visitors crossed the 130m-wide Namhangang River by ferry to reach the entrance, but a bridge now connects directly to the cave. Designated as a Natural Monument on June 4, 1969, Gossi Cave is nationally protected for its exceptional academic and natural heritage value, opening to the public on May 15, 1974.

paragraphs: Offering a glimpse into 400 million years of mystery, Gossi Cave is one of South Korea's representative caves. It was named after the Go family, who took refuge here during the Japanese invasions of Korea (Imjin War), and is also said to have been used as a ascetic training ground. In the past, visitors crossed the 130m-wide Namhangang River by ferry to reach the entrance, but a bridge now connects directly to the cave. Designated as a Natural Monument on June 4, 1969, Gossi Cave is nationally protected for its exceptional academic and natural heritage value, opening to the public on May 15, 1974.

Gossi Cave is a classic limestone cave featuring a multi-layered structure. The lower layer takes the form of a horizontal cave where groundwater flows like a small stream, and passages extend southwest from the entrance. The total main tunnel length is about 950m and branch tunnels measure about 2,438m, bringing Gossi Cave's total length to 3,388m, of which only a 500m section is developed and open to the public. Most of the main tunnel has developed along joint planes within the limestone.

en.title: Beopheungsa Temple (Yeongwol)
en.overview: Nestled in the foothills of Sajasang Mountain in Yeongwol, Gangwon-do, Beopheungsa Temple was founded in 643 (the 12th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla) by Master Jajang Yulsa to pray for national prosperity and the well-being of the people. Initially started as Heungnyeongsa Temple housing Buddha's true sarira (relics), it later became a central temple of the Sajasang Mountain school—one of the Nine Mountain Schools of Seon—when Jinghyo Jeoljung, a disciple of Silla Seon master Doyun, opened a Seon gate. Rebuilt in 1163 during the reign of King Uijong of Goryeo, it has preserved its Buddhist lineage through numerous destructions and reconstructions up to the Joseon Dynasty.
en.pull_quote: Nestled in the foothills of Sajasang Mountain in Yeongwol, Gangwon-do, Beopheungsa Temple was founded in 643 (the 12th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla) by Master Jajang Yulsa to pray for national…
paragraphs: Nestled in the foothills of Sajasang Mountain in Yeongwol, Gangwon-do, Beopheungsa Temple was founded in 643 (the 12th year of Queen Seondeok of Silla) by Master Jajang Yulsa to pray for national prosperity and the well-being of the people. Initially started as Heungnyeongsa Temple housing Buddha's true sarira (relics), it later became a central temple of the Sajasang Mountain school—one of the Nine Mountain Schools of Seon—when Jinghyo Jeoljung, a disciple of Silla Seon master Doyun, opened a Seon gate. Rebuilt in 1163 during the reign of King Uijong of Goryeo, it has preserved its Buddhist lineage through numerous destructions and reconstructions up to the Joseon Dynasty.

Surrounded by dense pine forests, Beopheungsa is one of South Korea's five Jeokmyeolbogung (sanctuaries housing Buddha's relics), offering a deep sense of Buddhist culture in a tranquil atmosphere. Within the temple grounds remain three stone pagodas, a seated guardian stone Buddha, a grotto where Master Jajang practiced asceticism, and the Jeokmyeolbogung shrine. Various cultural heritage items, such as the Saritap stupa, the Monument for Master Jinghyo of Heungnyeongsa, the Stupa of Master Jinghyo, and the Heungnyeongseonwonji site, showcase the temple's profound history and tradition.

ja.title: 法興寺（ポンフンサ・寧越）
ja.addr: 江原特別自治道寧越郡水주面武陵法興路1352
ja.overview: 江原道寧越の獅子山（サジャサン）の麓に位置する法興寺は、643年（新羅の善徳女王12年）に慈蔵律師が国家の繁栄と民の安寧を祈願して創建した寺院である。当時、仏の真身舎利を奉安し興寧寺として始まったここは、のちに新羅の禅僧・道允の弟子である澄効切中が禅門を開き、九山禅門の一つである獅子山門の中心寺院となった。高麗の毅宗代の1163年に再建されて以降も、朝鮮時代に至るまで数度の焼失と再建を繰り返しながら法脈を受け継ぎ、長い年月の中でもその歴史的意味を守ってきた場所である。

鬱蒼とした松林に囲まれた法興寺は、韓国の5大寂滅宝宮（仏の舎利を祀る聖地）の一つであり、閑静な雰囲気の中で深い仏教文化を感じることができる。境内には旧・興寧禅院の威勢を偲ばせる3基の石塔と守護石仏座像、慈蔵律師が修行した土窟、寂滅宝宮などが残っている。また、舎利塔、興寧寺澄効大師宝印塔、澄効大師浮屠、興寧禅院址など多様な文化遺産を通じて、寺院の深い歴史と伝統をあわせて見ることができる。

zh.title: 法興寺（寧越）

zh.overview: 坐落於江原道寧越獅子山麓的法興寺，是643年（新羅善德女王12年）由慈藏律師為祈求國家繁榮與百姓安寧而創建的寺院。當時奉安了佛陀真身舍利並以興寧寺為起點，此後隨著新羅禪僧道允的弟子澄効切中開創禪門，這裡成為九山禪門之一的獅子山門中心寺院。高麗毅宗時期（1163年）重修後，經歷朝鮮時代多次燒毀與重建，薪火相傳至今，在漫長歲月中守護著其歷史意義。

被蒼鬱松林環繞的法興寺是韓國五大滅寶宮（供奉佛舍利之聖地）之一，能在寧靜的氛圍中感受深厚的佛教文化。境內保留了讓人聯想起昔日興寧禪院威勢的三座石塔、守護石佛坐像、慈藏律師曾在此修行的土窟以及滅寶宮等。此外，透過舍利塔、興寧寺澄効大師寶印塔、澄効大師浮屠、興寧禪院址等多樣文化遺產，可以一窺寺院悠久的歷史與傳統。

en.title: Yeongwol Hyanggyo (Confucian School)
en.overview: Yeongwol Hyanggyo is a local educational institution founded in 1398 (the 7th year of King Taejo) during the Joseon Dynasty. During Joseon, it functioned as a national educational institution responsible for educating and enlightening local citizens. Although all buildings except the Daeseongjeon Shrine were destroyed during the Korean War in 1950, it maintains its current appearance through multiple renovations and repairs. Yeongwol Hyanggyo is arranged in a 'jeonhak humyo' layout, with the Myeongnyundang lecture hall in the front and the Daeseongjeon ritual hall in the rear. Myeongnyundang, where Confucian students studied, is a gable-roofed building measuring 3 bays wide and 2 bays deep.

Daeseongjeon, which enshrines Confucian sages, is a double-eaved hip-and-gable roofed building measuring 5 bays wide and 3 bays deep. It houses the spirit tablets of China's five sages (Confucius, Yan Hui, Zengzi, Zisi, Mencius), the Ten Wise Disciples, the Six Sages of the Song Dynasty, and Korea's Eighteen Sages. During the Joseon Dynasty, the state provided land, books, and slaves, allowing one instructor to teach a quota of 30 students. en.pull_quote: This is a Three Kingdoms period mountain fortress located on Jeongyangsan Mountain in Yeongwol-eup. Built with stones by cleverly utilizing the natural terrain of Jeongyangsan protruding toward…
paragraphs: This is a Three Kingdoms period mountain fortress located on Jeongyangsan Mountain in Yeongwol-eup. Built with stones by cleverly utilizing the natural terrain of Jeongyangsan protruding toward the Namhangang River, it is estimated to have been first constructed in the late 5th to early 6th century when the Three Kingdoms vied for the Han River basin. It remained in continuous use until the early Joseon Dynasty. Along with the Jungwon Goguryeo Stele in Chungju and Ondalsanseong Fortress in Danyang, it is one of Goguryeo's cultural heritage sites located in the central region.

Situated on a steep mountain peak at an elevation of 550m at the end of the Bonghwangsan Mountain ridge, it boasts excellent locational conditions as a fortress. The overall flat layout forms a wide trapezoid facing northwest. The fortress is largely divided into an inner wall (1,060m in circumference) and an outer wall (570m in circumference), with a total wall length reaching 1,630m. It is comparable in scale to Samnyeonsanseong Fortress in Boeun, which is considered one of the largest among ancient Korean mountain fortresses based on wall size alone. The outer wall was constructed after the Goryeo Dynasty to increase the inner wall's capacity, utilizing natural cliffs for many sections and building artificial walls where necessary during emergency situations.

en.title: Dangoljib
en.overview: Located in Naeil-dong, Miryang-si, Dangoljib is a specialty pork soup restaurant (dwaeji-gukbap) situated inside the Miryang Traditional Market. They serve a variety of menus including dwaeji-gukbap, sundae-gukbap (blood sausage soup), and naejang-gukbap (offal soup). The dwaeji-gukbap is served in the traditional toryeom style (scalding rice in hot broth), and their mixed soup blends meat and offal harmoniously for a deep, rich flavor. It is widely known as a famous restaurant in Miryang, having been featured in various media outlets. The seating area offers a mix of Western-style tables and traditional low tables. Be sure to use the restaurant's exclusive parking lot to avoid parking fees.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delicacy: Dwaeji-gukbap · Naejang-gukbap / Mixed Soup / Sundae-gukbap, etc.
paragraphs: Located in Naeil-dong, Miryang-si, Dangoljib is a specialty pork soup restaurant situated inside the Miryang Traditional Market. They serve a variety of menus including dwaeji-gukbap, sundae-gukbap, and naejang-gukbap. The dwaeji-gukbap is served in the traditional toryeom style, and the mixed soup boasts a deep flavor where meat and offal harmonize wonderfully.

It is so well-known that it has been featured in various media as a must-visit eatery in Miryang. The dining area features a mix of table and floor seating. You must use the restaurant's dedicated parking lot to avoid parking charges, so be sure to check in advance.

en.title: Miryangro (RO)
en.overview: Nestled along the foothills of Gucheonsan Mountain in Miryang, Miryangro (RO) is a cafe boasting architectural beauty that won the Miryang Architectural Landscape Award. en.title: Gayasan National Park (Hapcheon)
en.addr: 1200, Gayasan-ro, Gayasan National Park Office, Hapcheon-gun, Gyeongsangnam-do
en.overview: Gayasan National Park was designated as a national park on October 13, 1972. Covering a total area of 76.256㎢ across the border of Gyeongsangnam-do and Gyeongsangbuk-do, its soaring Sangwangbong Peak, also known as Udusan Mountain, proudly displays its majestic presence. Since ancient times, this place has been renowned as one of the top 10 scenic spots in Haedong (Korea) or one of the eight scenic views of Joseon. It is also home to Haeinsa Temple, the fundamental temple of Korea's Hwaeom sect and the guardian of the Tripitaka Koreana (Palman Daejanggyeong).

en.title: Hongryudong Valley
en.overview: Hongryudong Valley is a 4km valley stretching from Gayasan National Park to the entrance of Haeinsa Temple. It is called Hongryudong because the autumn foliage is so intensely red that it casts a crimson reflection on the flowing water. The sound of water flowing through the surrounding pine forests and crashing against strange rock formations is said to have made the great scholar Choi Chi-won deaf, and legend has it that he disappeared, becoming a Taoist immortal, leaving behind only his hat and shoes. There is Nongsanjeong Pavilion and a large rock inscribed with poetical verses by Choi Chi-won.

The valley features major cultural heritage sites such as Nongsanjeong Pavilion, Nakhwadam Pool, and Bunok Waterfall. Notably, opposite Nongsanjeong, you can see the autograph of scholar Choi Chi-won carved into the rock, making it even more famous.

en.title: Hapcheonho Lake
en.overview: Hapcheonho Lake is an artificial lake created in 1988 by damming the Hwanggang River, a tributary of the Nakdonggang River, to build the Hapcheon Dam. While completing the dam brought the pain of submerging several villages, Hapcheon-gun gained the magnificent scenery of Hapcheonho, which embraces the reflections of surrounding famous mountains in a single embrace. The surrounding area is famous for local specialties such as braised crucian carp (bungeo-jjim), icefish, and catfish stew (megi-tang), and visitors can enjoy fishing and water leisure sports. Additionally, cherry trees line the Hapcheonho Dulle-gil trail, offering dazzling cherry blossoms in spring, cool shade in summer, and brilliant autumn foliage in fall. The atmospheric scenery in the early morning where mountain mist and water vapor mingle is the highlight of the Hapcheonho Dulle-gil.

ja.overview: 陜川湖は1988年、洛東江の支流である黄岡の水をせき止めて陜川ダムを建設した際にできた人工湖。陜川郡は陜川ダムの竣工により複数の村が水没するという悲しみがあったが、その代わりに周辺の名山の影をひとまとめにした陜川湖の素晴らしい景観を手に入れた。周辺ではフナの蒸し物、ワカサギ、ナマズのスープといった特産グルメが有名で、釣りやウォータースポーツを楽しむことができる。また、陜川湖の둘레길（周辺遊歩道）には桜の木が長く並んでおり、春には華やかな桜、夏には涼しい木陰、秋には色鮮やかな紅葉が楽しめる。早朝、山の霧と水煙が入り交じる趣ある風景は、陜川湖둘레길のハイライトである。

en.title: Haeinsa Temple (Hapcheon)
en.overview: Haeinsa Temple is one of Korea's three major temples, founded in the 3rd year of King Aejang of Silla by two monks, Sun-ung and I-jeong. Its name originates from the 'Haein Samadhi' in the Avatamsaka Sutra (Hwaeomgyeong), and it was built as one of the ten Hwaeom temples to widely propagate Hwaeom philosophy. King Taejo of Goryeo designated this place as a state temple and bestowed 500 gyeol of farmland in return for Master Hirangdaesa's help. Meanwhile, Haeinsa is called the Temple of the Dharma (Beopbojongchal) among the Three Jewels Temples because it enshrines the Tripitaka Koreana woodblocks, a UNESCO Memory of the World, in the Daejanggyeong Panjeon (Depository). The temple grounds also feature various halls such as Daejanggyeong Panjeon, Daejeokgwangjeon, and Myeongbujeon. Subordinate hermitages include Wondangam, Hongjeam, Yongtapsinwon, Gounam, Ganworam, and Cheongnyangsa.

en.title: Odosan Natural Recreation Forest
en.overview: Nestled on the slopes of Mt. Odosan, Odosan Natural Recreation Forest spans across Gajo-myeon in Geochang-gun, and Myosan-myeon and Bongsan-myeon in Hapcheon-gun. To the northeast, it forms the tail end of the Gayasan Mountain Range alongside Mt. Dumusan. To the north, the recreation forest is close to Haeinsa Temple (a renowned Dharma-treasure temple), Mt. Gayasan, and Mt. Maewasan, while connecting to Lake Hapcheon to the south, offering abundant nearby attractions and stunning natural scenery.

Along the valley within the recreation forest, visitors will find convenient amenities such as a visitor center, forest cabins, cooking areas, camping decks, and campsites. In particular, the hiking trail ascending behind the forest cabins connects to Suseongsan, a smaller peak on Mt. Odosan's ridge, offering sweeping views of Lake Hapcheon far below. Odosan Healing Forest within the recreation site runs forest healing programs, making it a wonderful spot to enjoy with family. The forest boasts dense natural stands of pine and oak trees, alongside a diverse understory of mountain cherry, wild grapes, and hardy kiwifruit vines, making it a great natural study area for youths and students.

梧桐山自然休養林内の渓谷沿いには、ビジターセンター、森の中の家、炊事場、キャンプデッキ、キャンプ場など、休養客のための便宜施設があります。特に、森の中の家を背にして登る登山コースは、梧桐山麓の小さな峰である成熟山とつながっており、付近の陜川湖が足元に見下ろせる眺望が素晴らしいです。休養林内の梧桐山癒やしの森では森林治癒プログラムを実施しており、家族と一緒に楽しむのに最適です。梧桐山自然休養林の林相は天然林のマツやコナラ類の豊かな森が造成されており、ヤマザクラ、ヤマブドウ、マタタビや草本類などの多様な植生が分布しており、青少年の自然学習にも良い場所です。

休養林內的溪流沿線設有遊客服務中心、林間小屋、炊事場、露營木棧道與露營場等便利設施供休養旅客使用。特別是從林間小屋後方出發的登山步道，連接至梧桐山支脈的小山峰成熟山，登高遠眺可將附近的陜川湖美景盡收眼底。休養林內的梧桐山療癒之林定期舉辦森林療癒課程，非常適合與家人一同前往體驗。休養林內的植被主要由松樹和櫟樹組成的茂密天然林構成，並混生有野櫻桃樹、山葡萄藤、獼猴桃藤及各種草本植物，是青少數與學生進行自然學習的絕佳場所。

en.title: Monument for State Preceptor Wongyeong, Bonyasa Temple Site, Hapcheon
en.overview: Erected to honor State Preceptor Wongyeong, this stele was originally located at the old site of Bonyasa Temple before being moved in 1961 to its current location inside the grounds of Haeinsa Temple. Built in 1125 (the 3rd year of King Injong's reign during the Goryeo Dynasty), the monument well exhibits the sculptural techniques and simple roof stone designs characteristic of the mid-Goryeo period. Standing 2.3 meters tall and 1.2 meters wide, it is made of granite and features a tortoise pedestal, stele body, and roof stone, with the thinness of each component being a distinct characteristic.
en.pull_quote: Erected to honor State Preceptor Wongyeong, this stele was originally located at the old site of Bonyasa Temple before being moved in 1961 to its current location inside the grounds of Haeinsa Temple...
paragraphs: Erected to honor State Preceptor Wongyeong, this stele was originally located at the old site of Bonyasa Temple before being moved in 1961 to its current location inside the grounds of Haeinsa Temple. Built in 1125 (the 3rd year of King Injong's reign during the Goryeo Dynasty), the monument well exhibits the sculptural techniques and simple roof stone designs characteristic of the mid-Goryeo period. Standing 2.3 meters tall and 1.2 meters wide, it is made of granite and features a tortoise pedestal, stele body, and roof stone, with the thinness of each component being a distinct characteristic.

According to the inscription, State Preceptor Wongyeong traveled to Song Dynasty China alongside State Preceptor Daegak, returned home, and became a prelate (Seungtong) in 1104 (the 9th year of King Sukjong's reign). He also served as a teacher to King Yejong. After residing at Guwibasa Temple, he passed away, and the king bestowed upon him the posthumous title 'Wongyeong.' The inscription was composed by Kim Bu-il and written in calligraphy by Lee Won-bu.

en.title: Geumwonsan Natural Recreation Forest
en.overview: Geumwonsan Forest Resources Management Office preserves a pristine natural environment alongside historical and cultural value, operating both Geumwonsan Eco-Arboretum and Geumwonsan Natural Recreation Forest. Located at the highest altitude in Korea, Geumwonsan Eco-Arboretum was established to collect, preserve, research, and exhibit around 1,500 rare and endemic plant species. It features diverse theme gardens such as a rhododendron garden, rock garden, Korean fir conservation garden, and hydrangea garden, alongside a forest experience education center, visitor center, and wooden deck trails.

en.title: Deogyusan National Park (Namdeogyu Branch)
en.overview: Located in the heart of the Baekdudaegan mountain range, Mt. Deogyusan was designated as the 10th national park in 1975. Spanning across four counties bridging the Yeongnam and Honam regions—Muju-gun and Jangsu-gun in Jeollabuk-do, and Geochang-gun and Hamyang-gun in Gyeongsangnam-do—a total area of 229.43㎢ is designated as parkland. Deogyusan National Park is surrounded by Mt. Gayasan to the east, Mt. Naejangsan to the west, Mt. Jirisan to the south, and Mt. Gyeryongsan and Mt. Soknisaksan to the north. Mt. Deogyusan is the fourth-highest mountain in South Korea (Hyangjeokbong Peak at 1,614m) with high ecological preservation value, and serves as a water source for the Geumgang River flowing north and the Nakdonggang River flowing east.
en.pull_quote: Located in the heart of the Baekdudaegan mountain range, Mt. Deogyusan was designated as the 10th national park in 1975...
paragraphs: Located in the heart of the Baekdudaegan mountain range, Mt. Deogyusan was designated as the 10th national park in 1975. Spanning across four counties bridging the Yeongnam and Honam regions—Muju-gun and Jangsu-gun in Jeollabuk-do, and Geochang-gun and Hamyang-gun in Gyeongsangnam-do—a total area of 229.43㎢ is designated as parkland. Deogyusan National Park is surrounded by Mt. Gayasan to the east, Mt. Naejangsan to the west, Mt. Jirisan to the south, and Mt. Gyeryongsan and Mt. Soknisaksan to the north. Mt. Deogyusan is the fourth-highest mountain in South Korea (Hyangjeokbong Peak at 1,614m) with high ecological preservation value, and serves as a water source for the Geumgang River flowing north and the Nakdonggang River flowing east.

Deogyusan Gucheondong Valley features winding odd-shaped cliffs and rapids with 13 large rocky plateaus, about 10 ponds, and 20 waterfalls, forming a picturesque valley that ancient sages dubbed the 33 scenic views. In the Geochang area, Wolseong Valley is located, renowned as a deep, clear, and beautiful valley that attracts many tourists. Centered around its main peak, Hyangjeokbong (1,614m), Mt. Deogyusan boasts majestic ridges around 1,300 meters high stretching southwestward for about 30 kilometers.

en.title: Songgyesa Temple (Geochang)
en.overview: Surrounded by clear valleys and dense forests at the foot of Bukdeogyusan Mountain, Songgyesa Temple is a branch temple of Haeinsa Temple, the head temple of the 12th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. Originally founded in 652 (the 6th year of Queen Jindeok's reign) by the monks Wonhyo and 의상 as Songgyeram after establishing Yeongchwisa Temple and five subordinate hermitages, the temple has produced many eminent monks over the centuries. After being completely burned down along with the five hermitages during the Japanese Invasion of Korea, it lay in ruins until Jinmyeong reconstructed Songgyeram during the reign of King Sukjong.
en.pull_quote: Surrounded by clear valleys and dense forests at the foot of Bukdeogyusan Mountain, Songgyesa Temple is a branch temple of Haeinsa Temple, the head temple of the 12th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. It was founded in 652...
paragraphs: Surrounded by clear valleys and dense forests at the foot of Bukdeogyusan Mountain, Songgyesa Temple is a branch temple of Haeinsa Temple, the head temple of the 12th parish of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. Originally founded in 652 (the 6th year of Queen Jindeok's reign) by the monks Wonhyo and Uisang as Songgyeram after establishing Yeongchwisa Temple and five subordinate hermitages, the temple has produced many eminent monks over the centuries. After being completely burned down along with the five hermitages during the Japanese Invasion of Korea, it lay in ruins until Jinmyeong reconstructed Songgyeram during the reign of King Sukjong.

It was burned down again during the Korean War and restored by Monk Seungmin in 1969. In 1995, Wonjeong dismantled the leaning Yeongchuiru Pavilion (built during the 1969 restoration) to rebuild it and renamed it Mungak. Existing buildings include Geuknakbojeon Hall, Daeungjeon Hall, Mungak (Bell Pavilion), and Yosachae (monks' quarters), while cultural artifacts include a Seated Amitabha Buddha, a small bronze bell, and three Buddhist paintings. From the Daeungjeon Hall of Songgyesa, visitors can enjoy a direct view of Surideom on Bukdeogyusan Mountain, and the winter snowscape of Songgyesa creates yet another magnificent scenery crafted by the mountain.

朝鮮戦争の時に再び全焼したが、1969年に僧民（スンミン）スニム（僧侶）が再建した。1995年に元情（ウォンジョン）が1969年の再建時に建立した霊鷲楼が傾いたため解体して再建し、「文角」と改名した。現存する建物としては極楽宝殿を中心に大殿、文角（鐘閣）、寮舎などがあり、遺物としては阿弥陀如来坐像、小鐘、仏画3点などがある。松渓寺の大雄殿からは北徳裕山のスリドムが正面に見え、冬の松渓寺の雪景色は北徳裕山が織りなすもう一つの絶景を演出する。

朝鲜战争时再次被完全烧毁，于1969年由僧民法师重建。1995年，元井因1969年重建时建造的灵鹫楼倾斜而将其拆除重建，并更名为文阁。现存建筑以极乐宝殿为中心，包括大雄殿、文阁（钟阁）、寮舍等，文物则有阿弥陀如来坐像、小钟、佛教绘画3幅等。从松溪寺的大雄殿可以正面欣赏北德裕山秀丽峰（Surideom）的景色，而冬季松溪寺的雪景更是展现了北德裕山造就的又一壮丽景观。

en.title: Wolseong Valley
en.overview: Wolseong Valley is formed along Wolseongcheon Stream on the eastern foothills of Namdeogyusan Mountain. Although the valley is not very wide, the surrounding mountain terrain is so majestic that it boasts abundant water flow. Scattered rocks provide great resting spots alongside water play areas, and the crystal-clear stream weaves between boulders to create small waterfalls and rapids as it flows down toward Wicheon Valley and Suseungdae Valley in Galgye-ri.
en.pull_quote: Wolseong Valley is formed along Wolseongcheon Stream on the eastern foothills of Namdeogyusan Mountain. Although the valley is not very wide, the surrounding mountain terrain is so majestic that it boasts abundant water flow...
paragraphs: Wolseong Valley is formed along Wolseongcheon Stream on the eastern foothills of Namdeogyusan Mountain. Although the valley is not very wide, the surrounding mountain terrain is so majestic that it boasts abundant water flow. Scattered rocks provide great resting spots alongside water play areas, and the crystal-clear stream weaves between boulders to create small waterfalls and rapids as it flows down toward Wicheon Valley and Suseungdae Valley in Galgye-ri.

Heading upstream, visitors will find spots like Janggunbawi Shelter and numerous great locations for water play all the way up to Wolseong Bridge 1. If you turn right onto the narrow road from the entrance of Sansu Village and head up along Mahakdong Valley, you can enjoy a scenic walking course that overlooks the breathtaking views of Sansu-ri Hill reaching up to the sky before descending into Byeonggok-ri. Wolseong Valley ends at Hwangjeom Ticket Office, the starting point for hiking Namdeogyusan Mountain. Following the paved road past the ticket office leads over Namnyeongjae Pass to Yeonggaksa Temple in Seosang-myeon, Hamyang-gun, the starting point for the Deogyusan Mountain ridge traverse, making it a wonderful driving course due to its stunning mountain scenery.

paragraphs: 月城渓谷は南徳裕山の東側の麓を流れる月城川沿いに形成された渓谷。渓谷の幅は広くないが、周辺の山勢が非常に雄大で水量が豊か。渓谷での水遊びとともに一息つける岩が至る所に転がっており、渓谷の水は岩の間を縫うように小さな滝や瀬を作りながら、葛渓里の渭川渓谷と洙勝台渓谷へと流れ下っていく。

en.title: Geumwonsan Mountain
en.overview: The original name of Geumwonsan Mountain is said to have been 'Geomeun San' (Black Mountain) because it looked dark, located to the west of the old Gohyeon area. Another legend suggests it originates from a tale where a golden monkey living on this mountain was captured and trapped in a rock called Wonam. Geumwonsan sits on the Baekdudaegan mountain ridge extending from the Namdeogyusan Mountain branch, and following the ridge stretching southeast leads to Gibaeksan Mountain.
en.pull_quote: The original name of Geumwonsan Mountain is said to have been 'Geomeun San' (Black Mountain) because it looked dark, located to the west of the old Gohyeon area, or from a legend about a golden monkey...
paragraphs: The original name of Geumwonsan Mountain is said to have been 'Geomeun San' (Black Mountain) because it looked dark, located to the west of the old Gohyeon area. Another legend suggests it originates from a tale where a golden monkey living on this mountain was captured and trapped in a rock called Wonam. Geumwonsan sits on the Baekdudaegan mountain ridge extending from the Namdeogyusan Mountain branch, and following the ridge stretching southeast leads to Gibaeksan Mountain.

Geumwonsan features many large and small ponds and pools, including Yuancheong Falls, Jaun Falls, and Hansudong Valley, alongside cultural heritage sites such as rock-carved Buddha images. Geumwonsan Natural Recreation Forest is established near Yuancheong Falls, and with its gentle hiking trails and non-strenuous courses, it is a great mountain for beginner hikers and families.

paragraphs: 金源山の本来の名前は、かつて古県（コヒョン）の西側に位置し山が黒く見えることから「黒い山」と呼ばれたという伝承や、この山に住んでいた黄金色のサルを「元岩」という岩に閉じ込めたという伝説に由来するという説がある。金源山は南徳裕山の裾野から続く白頭大幹の稜線に位置しており、南東へ延びる稜線を進むと箕白山に出会う。
金源山には、ユアンチョン（劉安青）瀑布、紫雲瀑布、漢水洞渓谷をはじめとする大小の淵や滝壺が多く、磨崖仏などの文化遺跡も豊富。劉安青瀑布の近隣には金源山自然休養林が造成されており、登山コースが険しくなく道が緩やかなため、登山初心者やファミリー層の登山地としてもおすすめの山である。

en.title: Geoyeolsanseong County Park
en.overview: Geochang-gun is an inland mountainous region in the northwestern part of Gyeongsangnam-do, bordering Gyeongsangbuk-do and Jeollabuk-do across Deogyusan National Park. To the north rise Deogyusan, Wolbongsan, and Sudosan mountains; to the west, Gibaeksan and Geumwonsan mountains; and to the east, Uisangbong and Bigyasan mountains. The south is surrounded by relatively low Boroksan and Cheolmasan mountains, forming an intermountain basin. Geoyeolsanseong County Park is located about 3 km west of Geochang-eup and centers around Geoyeolseong Fortress, built by Baekje loyal martyrs and volunteer armies to rebuild the nation.
en.pull_quote: Geochang-gun is an inland mountainous region in the northwestern part of Gyeongsangnam-do, bordering Gyeongsangbuk-do and Jeollabuk-do across Deogyusan National Park...
paragraphs: Geochang-gun is an inland mountainous region in the northwestern part of Gyeongsangnam-do, bordering Gyeongsangbuk-do and Jeollabuk-do across Deogyusan National Park. To the north rise Deogyusan, Wolbongsan, and Sudosan mountains; to the west, Gibaeksan and Geumwonsan mountains; and to the east, Uisangbong and Bigyasan mountains. The south is surrounded by relatively low Boroksan and Cheolmasan mountains, forming an intermountain basin. Geoyeolsanseong County Park is located about 3 km west of Geochang-eup and centers around Geoyeolseong Fortress, built by Baekje loyal martyrs and volunteer armies to rebuild the nation.

Geoyeolseong Fortress is a historic open-air educational site where a fierce battle took place: after resisting for three years following the fall of Baekje, it fell in the 3rd year of King Munmu of Silla (663) to Silla generals Kim Heum-sun and Cheonjon, resulting in the decapitation of some 700 Baekje revival soldiers. Existing ruins include a 2.1 km-long, 7 m-wide fortress wall that partially retains its original form, along with 7 watchtower sites and 2 wells. In addition, Geochang Sculpture Park is located along the bicycle-only road, allowing visitors to appreciate the beauty of great nature.

居烈城は百済敗亡後3年間抗戦したが、新羅の文武王3年（663）に新羅の将軍・金欽純、天存らに陥落され、百済の復興軍約700名が斬首された熾烈な戦闘が繰り広げられた歴史の生きた教育の場でもある。現存する遺跡として長さ2.1km、幅7mの山性が部分的に原形をとどめており、物見台（楼）の跡が7か所、井戸が2か所ある。また、自転車専用道路沿いに位置する居昌彫刻公園が形成されており、大自然の美しさを鑑賞することができる。

en.title: Suseungdae Imjungeun Garden
en.overview: Suseungdae Imjungeun Garden is a specialty restaurant specializing in Hanwoo (Korean beef) and Samgyeopsal (pork belly), located just a 5-minute drive from Suseungdae Tourist District. It is frequently visited by out-of-towners looking to taste high-quality Geochang beef. The signature menu is the Iron-pan Pork Bulgogi Ssambap Set, and a variety of other dishes are available—such as the Mountain-heap Beef Bulgogi Table and Cauldron Spicy Chicken Stew—allowing guests to choose according to their taste.

en.title: Happles Farm Ciderry
en.overview: Happles Farm Ciderry is a place where apples are directly cultivated, harvested, juiced, and fermented to make apple cider. Cider refers to a type of carbonated fruit wine made by fermenting apples, and a ciderry is a cidery that produces apple cider—much like how a winery is a place that produces wine. As South Korea's first farm ciderry, the cafe is situated on a hill beneath Ahopsan Mountain, offering a panoramic view of Geochang-eup at a glance.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialties: Apple Cider · Custard Apple Pie / Soft Cider / Apple Hamburger Steak, etc.

Cider refers to a type of carbonated fruit wine made by fermenting apples, and a ciderry is a cidery that produces apple cider—much like how a winery is a place that produces wine.

As South Korea's first farm ciderry, the cafe is situated on a hill beneath Ahopsan Mountain, offering a panoramic view of Geochang-eup at a glance. Visitors can taste a variety of foods made with apples harvested directly from the apple orchard, including drinks, desserts, and even meals.

en.title: Oeyanggan Gusi
en.overview: Oeyanggan Gusi, a Hanwoo specialty restaurant, is famous for its soybean paste stew (doenjang-jjigae) boiled on the grill plate right after grilling meat. Using only high-quality Hanwoo beef and domestic kimchi, they boil the stew using specially homemade soybean paste and vegetables grown in Geochang. With multiple private rooms available, it is great for small gatherings.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialties: Hanwoo Yukhoe (Beef Tartare) · Hanwoo Gui (Grilled Beef) / Hanwoo Beef / Yukhoe Bibimbap / Hanwoo Mungtaengi (Raw Beef Slices), etc.

en.overview: Opened in August 2004, Dami Hoejip spans about 150 pyeong across two floors, featuring two spacious halls and four private rooms. The building also houses accommodations and a karaoke facility for added convenience, backed by a parking lot of about 100 pyeong. en.title: Iwon Sikdang
en.overview: Iwon Sikdang is a renowned 50-year traditional eatery and the original birthplace of Bak-sok Mil-guk Nakji-tang (octopus soup with gourd and wheat noodles). Selected as an exemplary restaurant designated by Chungnam, it is a representative dining spot for Taean tourism. Primarily using tidal-flat octopus caught in Iwon-myeon, Taean-gun, this local food restaurant uses agricultural produce from the Chungnam region. You can enjoy the local specialty of Wonbuk and Iwon-myeon—Bak-sok Nakji-tang, made by slicing the inside of a bottle gourd, adding vegetables and tidal-flat octopus for a clear, refreshing broth, served here with kalguksu (knife-cut noodles) and sujebi (hand-torn dough soup).

en.title: Jeonggane Bak-sok Nakji-tang
en.overview: Jeonggane Haemul Son-kalguksu has been specializing in bak-sok nakji-tang and seafood knife-cut noodles since opening in 1998. Bak-sok nakji-tang is a traditional Taean dish born from the old days when locals boiled tender tidal-flat octopus—commonly found along the Taean coast—with gourd instead of expensive meat to create a refreshing soup. Using only fresh mud-flat octopus from the Taean region, the meat remains tender rather than tough, and kalguksu noodles can be added to the broth. Made exclusively with domestic Korean wheat, the noodles ensure both great taste and health.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialties: Bak-sok Nakji-tang · Korean Wheat Seafood Hand-cut Noodles

ja.title: チョンガネ パクソクナクチタン
ja.addr: 忠清南道泰安郡泰安邑수등길 6
ja.overview: チョンガネ海鮮手打ちカルグクスは、泰安にあるパクソクナクチタンと海鮮カルグクスの専門店として1998年にオープンしました。パクソクナクチタンは泰安の伝統料理で、遠い昔、貴重で高価な肉の代わりに泰安の海辺でよく獲れる干潟のタコとヒョウタンを一緒に煮込んでさっぱりとしたスープ料理として食べていたものを、食堂で売り始めたものです。泰安地域で採れる新鮮な泥タコのみを使用しているため、茹でても硬くならず柔らかく、スープにカルグクスの麺を追加することができます。麺は国産の韓国産小麦のみを使用しており、味と健康の両方を追求しています。

zh.overview: 「鄭家네海鮮手工刀削麵」專營葫蘆章魚湯與海鮮刀削麵，於1998年開業。葫蘆章魚湯是泰安的傳統美食，古時候人們捨棄昂貴的肉類，將泰安海邊常見的灘塗章魚與葫蘆瓜一起熬煮，作為清爽解渴的湯品享用，後來才開始在餐廳販售。店內僅使用泰安地區產的新鮮泥灘章魚，即使煮久了也不會韌，口感軟嫩，湯頭還能額外添加刀削麵。麵條堅持使用韓國產本土小麥，兼顧美味與健康。

en.title: Anmyeon-do Anheung Ggot-gejang
en.overview: Located right in front of Anmyeon-do Recreational Forest, this is a specialty restaurant for soy sauce-marinated raw crabs (ganjang gejang). Anheung Ggot-gejang highlights the savory and light flavor of blue crab without being overly salty. It is complemented by about 13 neat and clean side dishes, including snail soybean paste stew, squid, and bulgogi. Another culinary secret of this house is its soy sauce-marinated jumbo prawns (ganjang daeha-jang). Prepared just like ganjang gejang, the sweet and savory soy flavor soaks deeply into the tender shrimp meat, making it a perfect side dish.

en.title: Seondori Ssangdo Coast, Biin
en.overview: Seondori in Biin-myeon got its name because it was historically a bustling route for boats. Though times have changed and boats are no longer seen, the beach, waves, and islands remain to preserve its scenic beauty. Off the coast of Seondori lie two small uninhabited islands called Ssangdo (Twin Islands). Legend has it that a widower with twin sons went out to sea, encountered a storm, and perished; when the twin sons waited anxiously for their father and died, they turned into rocks. The beach features the Seondori Tidal Flat Experience Center, allowing visitors to walk across to Ssangdo about 300 meters from the shore during low tide. Grilled clams and knife-cut noodles around Biin Beach, along with the gorgeous West Sea sunset, are unmissable highlights.

ja.overview: 庇仁面（ピインミョン）の仙道里（ソンドリ）は、昔、船が多く行き交う通り道だったことから名付けられた場所ですが、時代が変わった今では船はなくなり、海水浴場や波、島などが残り美しい風景を守っています。仙道里の沖合には「桑島（サンド）」と呼ばれる2つの小さな無人島があります。ここには、双子の子供を持つやもめが海に出て高波に遭って亡くなり、双子の息子たちが父親を待ちわびて死んで岩になったという伝説があります。この海岸は仙道里干潟体験場のある干潟で形成されており、干潮時には海岸から約300メートル離れた桑島まで歩いて渡ることができます。庇仁海水浴場周辺の貝焼きやカルグクス、そして西海の美しい夕日も見逃せません。

en.title: Yi Ha-bok's Old House in Seocheon
en.overview: Preserved in its original form as a modest, traditional folk farmhouse typical of Korea's central region, Yi Ha-bok's Old House in Seocheon was designated as a National Folk Cultural Heritage in 1984 in recognition of its historical value. Built in the late 19th century by a descendant of the scholar Mogeun Yi Saek—who constructed the 3-room main quarters—the house was expanded in the early 20th century with the addition of the sarangchae (men's quarters), lower wing, and upper wing, alongside a major expansion of the main quarters. Considered an auspicious site in geomancy, the property's sense of enclosure is further enhanced by neatly planted juniper, Chinese parasol, and evergreen trees.

paragraphs: Preserved in its original form as a modest, traditional folk farmhouse typical of Korea.s central region, Yi Ha-bok's Old House in Seocheon was designated as a National Folk Cultural Heritage in 1984 in recognition of its historical value. This house was built in the late 19th century by a descendant of Mogeun Yi Saek, who constructed a 3-room main wing. Later, in the early 20th century, the sarangchae (men's quarters), lower wing, and upper wing were newly built, and the main wing was substantially expanded to take its current form. Geomantically, this location is considered an auspicious site, and rows of juniper, Chinese parasol, and evergreen trees further define its secluded ambiance.

Today, it is managed by the Cheongam Cultural Foundation, which carries on the legacy of Cheongam Yi Ha-bok—an educator and rural enlightenment activist from Seocheon. An exhibition hall displaying folk artifacts and books has been built right next door for visitors to explore alongside the old house. Programs such as 1-night 2-day stays, farming experiences, and photography tours are also operated here. Nearby attractions include Seocheon Yi Saek Experience Village, Seocheon Botanical Art Museum, Munheonseowon Confucian Academy, Hansan Hyanggyo, Hansan Ramie Fabric Cultural Center, Hansan Fortress, Geonjisanseong Fortress, and the Hansan 5-Day Market.

en.title: Seocheon Botanical Art Museum
en.overview: Seocheon Botanical Art Museum is located inside Yi Saek Experience Village, a rural tourism village honoring the loyalty and scholarship of Yi Saek, a loyal subject of the late Goryeo Dynasty. The museum features a lotus garden, maze garden, sotdae (pole) garden,onggi (traditional earthenware) exhibition hall, bonsai exhibition hall, open-air café, and an experiential learning center. Opened by a retired elementary school principal in 2003, the gardens showcase bonsai, trees, and oonggi jars collected and nurtured over 40 years.

en.title: Five-Story Stone Pagoda in Seongbuk-ri, Seocheon
en.overview: Standing at 6.2 meters tall, the Five-Story Stone Pagoda in Seongbuk-ri was built during the Goryeo Dynasty. However, reflecting the characteristics of the Seocheon region—which was formerly Baekje territory—it adopts the Baekje architectural style, resembling the Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Jeongnimsa Temple Site in Buyeo. This pagoda faithfully follows the Baekje stone pagoda style, featuring a single-layer foundation and a five-story body. In particular, each side tapers narrower at the top and wider at the bottom, forming a trapezoidal shape that clearly marks it as a Baekje pagoda.

However, reflecting the characteristics of the Seocheon region—which was formerly Baekje territory—it adopts the Baekje architectural style, resembling the Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Jeongnimsa Temple Site in Buyeo. In particular, each side tapers narrower at the top and wider at the bottom, forming a trapezoidal shape that clearly marks it as a Baekje pagoda.

Thus, it holds significant historical value for tracing the transmission routes and distribution of Baekje-style stone pagodas, earning its designation as a National Treasure in 1963. Nearby attractions include Biin Eupseong Fortress, Biin Hyanggyo, Biin Beach, and Wolmyeongsan Mountain, making it great to visit in combination.

en.title: Sumun Beach
en.overview: Sumun Beach is located southeast of Jangheung-eup. Lined with fantastic palm trees on both sides of the road leading to the beach, it offers an exotic, southern atmosphere. The sandy beach faces the wide, clean waters of Deuknyang Bay in the South Sea, and is surrounded by dense pine forests, making it a quiet retreat that helps summer vacationers beat the heat. Since 2005, a camping tent village has been set up and operated around the beach so that family travelers can enjoy a unique summer getaway. Okseom Water Park is also located near the beach, making accommodation convenient.

en.title: Borimsa Temple (Jangheung)
en.overview: Borimsa Temple is an ancient temple located in Bongdeok Valley on Gajisan Mountain. As one of the three major Borim temples in the East (India, China, and Korea), it is also the place where Seon (Zen) Buddhism first entered and settled in Korea. When Wonpyo Daedeok laid its foundation in 759, it seems to have remained in the form of a modest thatched hermitage, and its founding legend adds interest for visitors. Place names related to the tale remain scattered throughout the area.
en.pull_quote: Borimsa Temple is an ancient temple located in Bongdeok Valley on Gajisan Mountain. As one of the three major Borim temples in the East (India, China, and Korea), it is also the place where Seon Buddhism first entered...
paragraphs: Borimsa Temple is an ancient temple located in Bongdeok Valley on Gajisan Mountain. As one of the three major Borim temples in the East (India, China, and Korea), it is also the place where Seon (Zen) Buddhism first entered and settled in Korea. When Wonpyo Daedeok laid its foundation in 759, it seems to have remained in the form of a modest thatched hermitage, and its founding legend adds interest for visitors. Place names related to the tale remain scattered throughout the area.

In the past, Borimsa Temple was grand and magnificent. Although it declined due to the Joseon Dynasty's Confucian-supremacist and anti-Buddhist policies and suffered war damage during the Korean War, it has since been restored. The North and South Three-Story Stone Pagodas of Borimsa enshrine the true sarira (relics) of the Buddha, and the stone lantern between them signifies that the light of the Buddha shines in all directions. The Stele for State Preceptor Bojo's Changseong Pagoda records the state preceptor's achievements, the Seon state of mind, and the founding legend. In the middle of the courtyard is a mineral spring that never dries up even during severe droughts, and the nutmeg tree forest surrounding the temple offers fresh and divine energy.

paragraphs: 寶林寺是位於迦智山鳳德溪谷的古剎。它是東洋三大寶林（印度、中國、韓國）之一，也是韓國禪宗最早傳入並扎根的地方。759年元表大德在此開基時，似乎還只是草庵的形式，其淵源傳說讓造訪者感到津津樂道，各地至今仍留存著與其相關的地名。
過去的寶林寺規模宏大、景色秀麗，雖在朝鮮時代的崇儒抑佛政策下沒落，並在韓戰中遭受戰火破壞，但後來已修復重建。寶林寺南北三層石塔供奉著佛陀的真身舍利，其間的石燈寓意著佛陀的光芒照亮四方。普照禪師創成塔碑是為了將事蹟流傳後世而刻在木、石或鐵器上的碑文，記載著禪的境界、普照國師的行誼以及創建淵源傳說等。寶林寺庭院中央有一處即使在嚴重乾旱也不乾涸的藥泉，寺廟周圍的榧樹林則散發著清新與神聖的氣息。

en.title: Bada House
en.overview: A local culinary hotspot situated right in front of the breakwater between Sumun Beach and Sumun Port in Jangheung. Although it gained widespread fame after being featured on SBS's 'Mat-dae-mat' (Taste vs. Taste), it has long been renowned locally for its seasoned ark shell (cockle/manila clam) sashimi. Clam meat is tossed with water dropwort (minari) and onions in gochujang and vinegar, offering a unique sweet taste that follows a non-irritating tartness. Refreshing clam soup is also served in between to soothe the palate.
en.pull_quote: Representative Delicacy: Samhap (Beef, Pen Shell, Shiitake Mushrooms) / Seasoned Clam Sashimi Set / Gizzard Shad Course / Spicy Rockfish Stew, etc.
paragraphs: A local culinary hotspot situated right in front of the breakwater between Sumun Beach and Sumun Port in Jangheung. Although it gained widespread fame after being featured on SBS's 'Mat-dae-mat' (Taste vs. Taste), it has long been renowned locally for its seasoned ark shell sashimi. Clam meat is tossed with water dropwort and onions in gochujang and vinegar, offering a unique sweet taste that follows a non-irritating tartness. Refreshing clam soup is also served in between to soothe the palate.

The secret to the famous seasoned clam sashimi lies in the vinegar used exclusively by this restaurant. Kept secretly in a large Cheongju (refined rice wine) bottle in a corner of the kitchen, the vinegar is reportedly made by fermenting makgeolli (rice wine). Homemade makgeolli is aged once more to extract the vinegar. The gochujang is also homemade, blended with the makgeolli vinegar to create the chojang (chili paste sauce). While Bada House specializes in pen shells and clams, it also serves seasonal raw fish like gizzard shad, sea bass, and conger eel depending on the time of year.

paragraphs: 長興の水文海水浴場と水文港の間にある防波堤の前に位置する郷土のグルメ店。SBSの『味対味』で紹介されて有名になり始めたが、地元では昔からアサリの刺身の和え物で評判が高かった店。貝の身にセリとタマネギを加え、コチュジャンと酢で and ざく切りにして和えたもので、刺激的ではない爽やかな酸味の後にほのかな甘みが広がるのが独特。合間に口の中をさっぱりさせてくれるすっきりとしたアサリ汁も一緒に提供される。

評判のアサリの刺身和えの秘訣はこの店だけで使っている酢にある。清酒の瓶に入れられ、厨房の一角に秘密裏に隠しておいた酢は、マッコリを発酵させて作ったものだという。手造りのマッコリをもう一度熟成させて酢を得る。コチュジャンも手造りで、マッコリ酢を加えてチョジャン（酢コチュジャン）を作る。バダハウスはタイラギやアサリを専門に扱っているが、季節によりコノシロ、スズキ、ハモ（スズキ目ハモ科の魚）なども刺身で提供している。

paragraphs: 這是一間位於長興水文海水浴場與水文港之間防波堤前的在地美食名店。自從在SBS節目《味對味》中亮相後開始聲名大噪，但在當地，這裡長久以來就以涼拌花蛤生魚片聞名。將貝肉加入水芹菜和洋蔥，用辣椒醬和醋涼拌，在溫和的酸味之後帶有獨特的清甜。店家還會穿插提供清爽的蛤蜊湯來療癒味蕾。

en.title: Jangheung Gaetmaeul
en.overview: Gaetmaeul Hojip is a raw fish specialty restaurant located at Sumun Port in Anyang-myeon, Jangheung-eup, where you can savor seasonal delicacies. In spring, they serve seasoned clam and pen shell dishes; in June and July, conger eel sashimi and shabu-shabu; in August and September, gizzard shad sashimi; and from December to May, pen shell dishes. Other menus are available year-round, including live fish sashimi, spicy fish stews, stir-fried dishes, and savory pancakes. The basic table setting overflows with napa cabbage kimchi, white kimchi, seasoned soybean sprouts, sushi, cockles, seafood pancakes, sea squirts, abalone, and sea cucumber.
en.pull_quote: Representative Delicacy: Pen Shell & Clam Sashimi Salad Set · Gaetmaeul Jangheung Samhap / Gaetmaeul Pen Shell Shabu-Shabu Set / Gizzard Shad Course, etc.
paragraphs: Gaetmaeul Hojip is a raw fish specialty restaurant located at Sumun Port in Anyang-myeon, Jangheung-eup, where you can savor seasonal delicacies. In spring, they serve seasoned clam and pen shell dishes; in June and July, conger eel sashimi and shabu-shabu; in August and September, gizzard shad sashimi; and from December to May, pen shell dishes. Other menus are available year-round, including live fish sashimi, spicy fish stews, stir-fried dishes, and savory pancakes.

The basic table setting overflows with napa cabbage kimchi, white kimchi, seasoned soybean sprouts, sushi, cockles, seafood pancakes, sea squirts, abalone, and sea cucumber. Crustaceans produced in the tidal flats of Sumun-ri, such as pen shells, cockles, and clams, have historically been known for their tender and soft texture, earning a spot on the king's dining table. Located close to Sumun Beach, it allows guests to enjoy a scenic meal overlooking the sea. With a large restaurant space, it is also great for family gatherings, group events, and various meetings.

en.title: Kkeunigeokjeong
en.overview: Kkeunigeokjeong is a renowned Jangheung Samhap restaurant located along Jeongnamjin Saturday Market Street. Jangheung Samhap is a dish where Korean beef (hanu), pen shell adductor muscle, and shiitake mushrooms are grilled together. Unlike regular restaurants, the system here involves buying Korean beef at the butcher shop right next door and grilling it together with the pen shell muscles and shiitake mushrooms sold here. The side dishes served with the samhap spread are clean and plentiful.
en.pull_quote: Representative Delicacy: Hanu Stone Plate Bibimbap · Hanu Mushroom Hot Pot / Hanu Yukgaejang / Beef Tartare Bibimbap, etc.
paragraphs: Kkeunigeokjeong is a renowned Jangheung Samhap restaurant located along Jeongnamjin Saturday Market Street. Jangheung Samhap is a dish where Korean beef (hanu), pen shell adductor muscle, and shiitake mushrooms are grilled together. Unlike regular restaurants, the system here involves buying Korean beef at the butcher shop right next door and grilling it together with the pen shell muscles and shiitake mushrooms sold here. The side dishes served with the samhap spread are clean and plentiful.

In addition to samhap, Hanu Stone Plate Bibimbap and Hanu Mushroom Hot Pot are also popular among visitors, and ordering Beef Tartare (Yukhoe) Bibimbap brings out an array of freshly prepared side dishes. Other popular menu items include Cheonggukjang (rich soybean paste stew) packed with shiitake mushrooms, tofu, zucchini, and onions, as well as seaweed (maesaengi) soup and rice cake soup brimming with ocean aromas.

en.pull_quote: Representative Delicacy: Jangheung Samhap · Seasoned Beef Tartare, etc.
paragraphs: As you enter the alleys of Jeongnamjin Jangheung Saturday Market, numerous Jangheung Hanu Samhap restaurants line the streets. Among them, Jeongnamjin Uri Hanu operates alongside a butcher shop, allowing visitors to purchase and enjoy the Korean beef, shiitake mushrooms, and pen shells that make up Jangheung Samhap.

Being a butcher restaurant, it sells fresh Korean beef at affordable prices, allowing you to choose and enjoy various cuts like chuck flap tail, oyster blade, beef tartare, and sirloin to your liking. The beef here is graded 1+A, and the beef tartare is hand-sliced on-site for ultimate freshness. It is a fantastic restaurant where you can buy high-quality Korean beef at a reasonable price and enjoy Jangheung Samhap.

en.title: Nolbeundle Hakwon Farm
en.overview: A rare large-scale farm featuring a vast 150,000-pyeong green field cultivated into a single massive barley field. In spring, visitors can witness the nation's largest barley field, and in autumn, fields of blooming buckwheat. After the farm was authorized as a tourist farm and its scenic beauty became widely known, it established itself as a popular destination visited by numerous tourists and photographers, also gaining attention as a filming location for various dramas, movies, and commercials. Accordingly, Hakwon Farm dedicates itself to landscape agriculture to provide even more beautiful scenery.

After the farm was authorized as a tourist farm and its scenic beauty became widely known, it established itself as a popular destination visited by numerous tourists and photographers, also gaining attention as a filming location for various dramas, movies, and commercials. Accordingly, Hakwon Farm dedicates itself to landscape agriculture to provide even more beautiful scenery. In addition, during the peak blooming seasons of its main crops, barley and buckwheat, it hosts various festivals and events such as the Green Barley Field Festival and Buckwheat Flower Festival. It also operates various auxiliary facilities for visitors, including a restaurant serving dishes made with barley and buckwheat, and a café offering tea, drinks, and desserts.

en.title: Seonunsan Mountain (Jeonbuk West Coast National Geopark)
en.overview: The Nakjodae and Cheonmabong areas of Seonunsan Mountain, known for their stunning sunsets, are composed of rhyolite, a type of volcanic rock. Rhyolite is harder, denser, and more resistant to weathering than the surrounding tuff. Consequently, differential weathering between the rhyolite and tuff creates near-vertical rock cliffs primarily formed of rhyolite, offering magnificent natural scenery. This makes the Seonunsan area an important site for observing stunning natural landscapes while understanding the characteristics of rock weathering.

en.title: Haeseong Jaecheop Sikdang
en.overview: Jaecheop are small, triangular freshwater clams harvested in abundance in the lower reaches of the Seomjingang River, locally called 'gangjorae' in Hadong dialect. Also known as jaechi or dasilgi, their shell color varies depending on their growing environment. In season during May and June, they are rich in taurine, which aids in liver detoxification, making them a popular ingredient for hangover soups. Haeseong Sikdang is a well-known restaurant within the Jaecheop Special Village in Hadong.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialties: Wild Jaecheop Assorted Set · Seomjingang Jaecheop Hoe Dupbap / Seomjingang Jaecheop-guk / Spicy Chinese Mitten Crab Stew, etc.
paragraphs: Jaecheop are small, triangular freshwater clams harvested in abundance in the lower reaches of the Seomjingang River, locally called 'gangjorae' in Hadong dialect. Also known as jaechi or dasilgi, their shell color varies depending on their growing environment. In season during May and June, they are rich in taurine, which aids in liver detoxification, making them a popular ingredient for hangover soups. Haeseong Sikdang is a well-known restaurant within the Jaecheop Special Village in Hadong. Their most popular menu item is the Jaecheop Assorted Set, which comes as a full spread including jaecheop-guk (freshwater clam soup), jaecheop hoe muchim (spicy raw clam salad), and marinated mitten crab.

The jaecheop-guk can be refilled multiple times. The clams are not fishy and retain their unique aroma and rich flavor. The jaecheop hoe muchim features blanched clams generously piled over a mix of assorted vegetables tossed in a spicy sauce; wrapping it in the provided dried seaweed makes the plate disappear in no time. You can also mix the spicy clam salad with rice to enjoy it as bibimbap. The marinated freshwater mitten crab served alongside is savory rather than salty, truly living up to its fame as a 'rice thief' that makes ordering an extra bowl of rice a must.

ja.title: ヘソン・ジェチョプシクダン（海星シジミ食堂）
ja.region_label: 慶尚南道 河동郡 河동邑
ja.addr: 慶尚南道 河동郡 河동邑 蟾津江大路 1877
ja.overview: ジェチョプ（シジミの一種）とは、蟾津江（ソムジンガン）の下流で多く獲れる三角の小さな貝で、河東方言で「カンジョレ」とも呼ばれ、川で獲れる貝を指します。その他にもジェチ、タニシなどとも呼ばれる淡水貝で、育つ環境によって貝の色が変わります。5月～6月が旬で、特に肝臓の解毒作用に良いタウリンが豊富に含まれており、ヘジャングク（酔い覚ましスープ）の食材として愛されています。河東にはシジミ特化村があり、その数ある飲食店の中でも有名な海星食堂です。
ja.pull_quote: 代表的な絶品メニュー：天然シジミ盛り合わせ定食 · 蟾津江シジミ刺身ビビンバ / 蟾津江シジミ汁 / モクズガニの鍋 など
paragraphs: ジェチョプ（シジミの一種）とは、蟾津江の下流で多く獲れる三角の小さな貝で、河東方言で「カンジョレ」とも呼ばれ、川で獲れる貝を指します。その他にもジェチ、タニシなどとも呼ばれる淡水貝で、育つ環境によって貝の色が変わります。5月～6月が旬で、特に肝臓の解毒作用に良いタウリンが豊富に含まれており、ヘジャングク（酔い覚ましスープ）の食材として愛されています。河東にはシジミ特化村があり、その数ある飲食店の中でも有名な海星食堂です。一番の人気メニューはシジミ盛り合わせ定食で、シジミ汁、シジミの和え物、モクズガニの醤油漬けまでセットになった豪華な御膳です。

シジミ汁は何回でもお替りさせてくれます。シジミは臭みがなく、特有の香りと風味が活きています。シジミの和え物は、様々な野菜をピリ辛のタレで和えたものの上に、茹でたシジミの身をたっぷりと載せて提供され、一緒に付いてくる韓国のり包んで食べると一皿がすぐになくなってしまいます。シジミの和え物をご飯に混ぜてビビンバとして食べるのもおすすめです。一緒に提供される淡水に生息するモクズガニを使ったカニの醤油漬けは、塩辛すぎず素朴な味で、「ご飯泥棒」の名にふさわしく、ご飯を追加注文するのが必須です。

zh.title: 海星河蜆食堂
zh.addr: 慶尚南道河동郡河동邑蟾津江大路1877

河蜆湯可以無限量續碗。河蜆沒有腥味，保有獨特的香氣與鮮美滋味。涼拌河蜆生魚片是在拌入香辣醬汁的各式蔬菜上，鋪上滿滿川燙過的河蜆肉，用附上的海苔包著吃，盤子一下子就會見底。也可以將涼拌河蜆生魚片拌入白飯中當作拌飯享用。一同端上的淡水河蟹所製作的醬油醃蟹鹹淡適中，不愧其「白飯神偷」的名號，讓人忍不住想再加點一碗白飯。

en.title: Beodeul Hoetjip
en.overview: Sweetfish (ayu) primarily inhabit clear streams. Born in rivers, the young fish head to coastal waters and return the following spring to the river where they were born to complete their life cycle. It is a premium raw fish dish that is savory, non-fishy, and uniquely fragrant with a subtle scent of cucumber or watermelon. It can be enjoyed grilled, fried, or in spicy fish stews. Because Hadong's Hwagaecheon Stream is a protected area, freshwater fishing requires a permit. The owner of Beodeul Hoetjip holds a fishing license and directly serves fresh raw fish and seafood dishes made with wild freshwater fish, including sweetfish, making it immensely popular.
en.pull_quote: Signature Specialties: Sweetfish Sashimi (Euneo-hoe) · Grilled Sweetfish / Spicy Chinese Mitten Crab Stew / Spicy Catfish Stew, etc.
paragraphs: Sweetfish (ayu) primarily inhabit clear streams. Born in rivers, the young fish head to coastal waters and return the following spring to the river where they were born to complete their life cycle. It is a premium raw fish dish that is savory, non-fishy, and uniquely fragrant with a subtle scent of cucumber or watermelon. It can be enjoyed grilled, fried, or in spicy fish stews. Because Hadong's Hwagaecheon Stream is a protected area, freshwater fishing requires a permit. The owner of Beodeul Hoetjip holds a fishing license and directly serves fresh raw fish and seafood dishes made with wild freshwater fish, including sweetfish, making it immensely popular. The sweetfish sashimi here is sliced with the bones intact and the outer skin left on; while the first impression might not be appealing, tasting it reveals zero fishiness along with a unique aroma and savory flavor.

If fish served with bones sounds intimidating, you can order fried sweetfish. Although the sweetfish is fried whole, it has a remarkably tender texture and is fried without being greasy. After enjoying raw, fried, or grilled fish, it is best to finish your meal with the specialty sweetfish rice. It is cooked in a stone pot like nutritional rice, layering sweetfish over rice along with glutinous rice, pine nuts, and chestnuts. Cooking rice with the fish placed directly on top adds a savory depth.

ja.addr: 慶尚南道 河동郡 花開面 花開路 26
ja.overview: アユはきれいな河川に主に生息します。稚魚は生まれると近海に出て、次の年の春に生まれた河川へ遡って一生を終える魚で、淡白で臭みがなく、ユニークなことにキュウリやスイカのような香りがする高級な刺身のネタです。塩焼きや天ぷら、メウン탕（ピリ辛鍋）などでも食べられます。河東の花開川は保護区のため許可がなければ淡水魚を捕ることができませんが、こちらのボードル刺身店の主人が漁業許可を持っており、自らアユをはじめとする天然の淡水魚を使った刺身や魚料理を提供しているため大人気です。
ja.pull_quote: 代表的な絶品メニュー：アユの刺身 · アユの塩焼き / モクズガニの鍋 / ナマズのメウン탕 など
paragraphs: アユはきれいな河川に主に生息します。稚魚は生まれると近海に出て、次の年の春に生まれた河川へ遡って一生を終える魚で、淡白で臭みがなく、ユニークなことにキュウリやスイカのような香りがする高級な刺身のネタです。塩焼きや天ぷら、メウン탕（ピリ辛鍋）などでも食べられます。河東の花開川は保護区のため許可がなければ淡水魚を捕ることができませんが、こちらのボードル刺身店の主人が漁業許可を持っており、自らアユをはじめとする天然の淡水魚を使った刺身や魚料理を提供しているため大人気です。こちらの鮎の刺身は骨ごと切る骨切りスタイルで皮目も残されているため、第一印象はあまり良くないかもしれませんが、実際に味わってみると臭みが全くなく、独特の香りと淡白な味わいを楽しめます。

如果覺得帶骨生魚片難以接受，也可以點香魚天婦羅。雖然香魚是整隻油炸的，但口感相當軟嫩且不顯油膩。享用完生魚片、天婦羅或烤魚後，建議以特色香魚飯作為完美結尾。店家在石鍋中放入糯米、松子、栗子，並將香魚鋪在米飯上像營養飯一樣炊煮。這種將魚放在飯上一同烹煮的做法...

paragraphs: Spanning the borders of Sannae-myeon in Miryang-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, Sangbuk-myeon in Ulju-gun, Ulsan, and Unmun-myeon in Cheongdo-gun, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Gajisan Provincial Park was designated in November 1979. It encompasses areas around Gajisan Mountain and Yeongchuksan Mountain—collectively known as the 'Yeongnam Alps'—along with Cheongsongsan Mountain. Due to its vast scope, it is divided into Seoknamsa Temple and the adjacent Yangsan-gun district. Peaks such as Gohongsan, Gajisan, Unmunsan, Cheonhwangsan, Ganjolsan, Sinbulsan, and Chwiseosan rise together to form this magnificent mountain cluster known as the Yeongnam Alps. Gajisan and Unmunsan mark the boundary between Gyeongsangnam-do and Gyeongsangbuk-do, with Gajisan being the highest among these peaks.

Gajisan features rocky peaks and silver grass fields blended throughout, forming a mountain ridge that connects to Unmunsan, allowing hikers to traverse the ridgeline. In autumn, the silver grass fields stretching from Seoknam-gogae Pass to the summit present a magnificent spectacle, while bizarre rock formations and Ssalbawi (Rice Rock) catch the eyes of climbers. The area around the summit of Gajisan is dotted with rocky ridges and sparse trees, offering a wide, unobstructed view. Nearby are Baegunsan Mountain, which feels just within reach, and Hobakso Valley, a pond shaped like a traditional Korean pumpkin mortar.

迦智山には至る所に岩峰とススキ野原が調和をなし、雲門山へと続く山筋に沿って稜線縦走ができます。秋になると石南峠から山頂に至るススキ野原が壮観をなし、奇岩怪石やサッバウィ（米岩）が登山客の目を引きます。迦智山の山頂周辺には岩稜が多く、木が少ない代わりに視界が大きく開けています。すぐ目の前にあるかのような白雲山や、カボチャのように見える池のホバクソ（琥珀沼）があります。

en.pull_quote: Located about 32 km from downtown Miryang in Sile Village, Nammyeong-ri, Sannae-myeon, Eoreumgol (Ice Valley) extends from Jaeyaksan Mountain, and about 3 km from there is Hobakso Valley, a branch stream of Gajisan Mountain...
paragraphs: Located about 32 km from downtown Miryang in Sile Village, Nammyeong-ri, Sannae-myeon, Eoreumgol (Ice Valley) extends from Jaeyaksan (Cheonhwangsan) Mountain. About 3 km from there lies Hobakso Valley, a branch stream originating from Gajisan Mountain. Washed by valley waters for hundreds of thousands of years, the jade-like granite bed pours forth white foam, creating stunning natural scenery that earned it a spot among Korea's 100 Best Clear Water Streams. According to the Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam, Hobakso is a deep pool carved out by a waterfall dropping from a height of over 10 meters, named 'Hobakso' because its shape resembles a traditional mill mortar called 'hobak'.

It has a circumference of about 30 meters and is also called Sile Hobakso, Guyeon Waterfall, or Baekryeon Waterfall. It is said that Hobakso historically served as a rain-prayer site during prolonged droughts. Locals of the past reportedly tested its depth by tying a stone to a full spool of silk thread and dropping it, but the thread ran out without ever touching the bottom—testifying to its incredible depth. Composed of a white rock bed, this waterfall valley is a pristine, unpolluted zone surrounded by Baekryeon-sa Temple, Hyeongjeso Pool, and Ocheonpyeong Flat Rock, offering exceptionally scenic views.

paragraphs: 密陽市内から約32km離れた山内面南明里のシレ村には、再薬山（天皇山）から延びる氷谷があり、そこから3kmほど行くと迦智山の一つの水脈であるホバクソ渓谷が現れます。数十万年間、渓谷の水に洗われた白玉のような花崗岩の上を白い泡を立てながら流れ落ちる渓谷の水と周辺の自然景観が美しく、韓国の名水100選にも選ばれています。『東国輿地勝覧』によると、ホバクソは10数メートルの高さから落ちる滝によって深くえぐられた池であり、精米所で使われる臼の一種である「ホバク（カボチャの意）」のように見えることからホバクソと呼ばれるようになったとのことです。

周囲は30mほどで、シレ・ホバクソ、クヨン滝、またはペクニョン滝とも呼ばれます。また、ホバクソは長年干ばつが続いたときに雨乞いを行った場所だとも伝えられています。昔、この地方の人々が水の深さを測るために石を結んだ木綿糸の束をすべて解いて投げ入れたが、底に届かなかったと言われるほど深いそうです。白い岩底からなるこの滝の谷間は、まさに無公害・無汚染のエリアであり、周囲には白蓮寺、ヒョンジェソ（兄弟沼）、五千坪の岩盤などがあり、非常に美しい景色を誇っています。

其周長約30公尺，也被稱為時禮琥珀沼、九淵瀑布或白蓮瀑布。據說在過去長期乾旱時，琥珀沼是舉行祈雨儀式的祈雨所。相傳古時候當地人為了探測水深，將綁著石頭的一整捆絲線全部放下去卻依然觸不到底，可見其水深之深。由白色岩石河床組成的這座瀑布溪谷堪稱無公害、無污染的淨土，周邊有白蓮寺、兄弟沼、五千坪盤石等，景色極為秀麗。

en.title: Miryang Eoreumgol (Ice Valley)
en.overview: Known since ancient times as Sile Binggok (Ice Valley), Eoreumgol is nestled in an open-air valley on the northern mid-slope of Jaeyaksan Mountain. Ice begins to form in early March when the earth's heat starts to rise, typically lasting until mid-July, and the chilling air from the rock crevices gradually subsides after Cheoseo (the end of the heat) following the dog days of summer. In winter, the valley stream rarely freezes; instead, warm vapor with temperatures above freezing rises from the rock crevices, allowing ferns and mosses to maintain their vivid green appearance in this mysterious region.
en.pull_quote: Known since ancient times as Sile Binggok, Eoreumgol is nestled in an open-air valley on the northern mid-slope of Jaeyaksan Mountain. Ice begins to form in early March when the earth's heat starts to rise...
paragraphs: Known since ancient times as Sile Binggok (Ice Valley), Eoreumgol is nestled in an open-air valley on the northern mid-slope of Jaeyaksan Mountain. Ice begins to form in early March when the earth's heat starts to rise, typically lasting until mid-July, and the chilling air from the rock crevices gradually subsides after Cheoseo following the dog days of summer. In winter, the valley stream rarely freezes; instead, warm vapor with temperatures above freezing rises from the rock crevices, allowing ferns and mosses to maintain their vivid green appearance in this mysterious region.

From April onward, the more clear days and intense heat there are, the more ice freezes within the rock crevices and the longer it lasts. Due to recent climate anomalies causing more rainy days, the ice-covered period is not as long as it used to be, but a chilling breeze that gives you goosebumps still blows as soon as you step into the valley entrance. The rock crevices where ice forms maintain an average summer temperature of around 0.2°C, and the stream flowing through the valley averages 4–8°C, making it difficult to keep your feet dipped in the water for more than two minutes. The terrain around Eoreumgol features stunning cliff walls folding like a folding screen around rocky boulder fields and valleys where ice forms.

ja.title: 密陽 氷谷（オレウムゴル）
ja.region_label: 慶尚南道 密陽市 山内面

paragraphs: 遠い昔から「シレ氷谷」と呼ばれてきた氷谷は、再薬山の北側中腹の野外渓谷に位置しています。大地の熱さが次第に増していく3月上旬頃に氷が張り始め、通常は7月中旬まで維持され、三伏の猛暑を過ぎ処暑を迎えると岩の隙間からの冷気が徐々に弱まります。氷谷は冬季には渓谷の水が凍りにくく、むしろ岩の隙間からプラスの気温の温かい湯気が立ち上っており、シダや苔が鮮やかな緑色の姿を保っている神秘的な地域です。

4月からは晴れの日が多いほど、暑さが厳しいほど岩の隙間に多くの氷が張り、長く維持されると言われています。近年は異常気象により雨の日が増え、氷が張っている期間が以前ほど長くはありませんが、渓谷の入口に足を踏み入れると鳥肌が立つほど涼しい風が相変わらず吹き抜けています。氷が張る岩の隙間は夏の平均気温が摂氏0.2℃ほどであり、渓谷を流れる水は平均4～8℃で、渓谷の水に足を浸して2分以上耐えるのは困難です。氷谷周辺の地形は、氷が張る石畑や渓谷を中心に奇岩絶壁が屏風のように立ち並んでいます。

paragraphs: 自古以來被稱為時禮冰谷的冰谷，坐落於再藥山北側半山腰的露天溪谷中。冰谷在大地熱氣逐漸升高的3月上旬左右開始結冰，通常維持到7月中旬，度過三伏酷暑、迎來處暑後，岩石縫隙間的冷氣才會逐漸減弱。冰谷在冬天時溪水不容易結冰，反而岩石縫隙間會冒出攝氏零度以上的熱氣，使蕨類植物與青苔保持翠綠的面貌，是一個相當神祕的地區。
據說從4月開始，晴天越多、天氣越熱，岩石縫隙間結出的冰塊就會越多且維持越久。近年來由於異常氣候導致雨天增加，結冰期間雖不如以往那麼長，但一踏入溪谷入口，那令人起雞皮疙瘩的涼爽清風依然如故地吹拂著。會結冰的岩石縫隙夏季平均氣溫約為攝氏0.2度，流經溪谷的水溫平均為4~8度，雙腳泡在溪谷水中很難撐過2分鐘。冰谷周邊的地形以會結冰的石田與溪谷為中心，奇岩絕壁如屏風般環繞。

en.title: Gumangok Valley (Miryang)
en.overview: Located in Miryang, Gumangok Valley sits at the foot of Gumangsan Mountain and derives its name from the legend that 90,000 citizens sought refuge here to escape the ravages of war during the Japanese invasions of Korea (Imjin War). Flanked by vertical rock walls to the east and west with a narrow gorge opening north and south—a place known as Tongsu-gol—the valley features Gumang Falls, a stunning 40-meter-tall vertical waterfall that creates a breathtaking landscape, complete with a deep pool about 15 meters in diameter forming beneath it.
en.pull_quote: Located in Miryang, Gumangok Valley sits at the foot of Gumangsan Mountain and derives its name from the legend that 90,000 citizens sought refuge here to escape the ravages of war during the Imjin War...
paragraphs: Located in Miryang, Gumangok Valley sits at the foot of Gumangsan Mountain and derives its name from the legend that 90,000 citizens sought refuge here to escape the ravages of war during the Japanese invasions of Korea (Imjin War). Flanked by vertical rock walls to the east and west with a narrow gorge opening north and south—a place known as Tongsu-gol—the valley features Gumang Falls, a stunning 40-meter-tall vertical waterfall that creates a breathtaking landscape, complete with a deep pool about 15 meters in diameter forming beneath it.

Gumangok Valley is dotted with bizarre rock formations and wide bedrock areas such as Byeorakdeumi, Adeulbawi (Son Rock), Sangyeobawi (Bier Rock), and Byeongpungbawi (Folding Screen Rock), along with numerous pools and ponds, drawing comparisons to Cheonbuldong Valley in Seoraksan Mountain. Famous tourist attractions such as Eoreumgol, Seokgolsa Temple, and Unmunsan Mountain are located nearby.
