en.title: Yongduyeon Tourist Resort
en.overview: Located along the Miryanggang River about 1 km upstream from Yeongnamru Pavilion, the representative pavilion of Miryang, this riverside resort is centered around the dragon-head-shaped cliff area of Yongdusan Mountain. From this starting point, the upper reaches of the Miryanggang River extend into wide sandy beaches and pebble beds along the Bukcheon-su and Dongcheon-su streams, while the lower reaches lead to Yeongnamru Pavilion.
en.pull_quote: Located along the Miryanggang River about 1 km upstream from Yeongnamru Pavilion, this riverside resort is centered around the dragon-head-shaped cliff area of Yongdusan Mountain...
paragraphs: Located along the MiryanggangRiver about 1 km upstream from Yeongnamru Pavilion, the representative pavilion of Miryang, this riverside resort is centered around the dragon-head-shaped cliff area of Yongdusan Mountain. From this starting point, the upper reaches of the Miryanggang River extend into wide sandy beaches and pebble beds along the Bukcheon-su and Dongcheon-su streams, while the lower reaches lead to Yeongnamru Pavilion.

In spring, royal azaleas paint Yongdusan Mountain in brilliant red hues; in summer, visitors can enjoy boating and fishing; and in autumn, it is famous for sweetfish fishing amidst colorful foliage. Near the resort is Sammun Songnim, a colony of over 2,000 pine trees aged 100 years or older, alongside an athletic park and a spacious lawn plaza laid out on the riverbank floodplains. Nearby attractions worth visiting include Yeongnamru Pavilion, Bangyijeong Pavilion, Gihoe Songnim, Yerim Seowon Confucian Academy, and Miryang Sculpture Park.

en.title: Pyochungsa Temple (Miryang)
en.overview: Housing numerous cultural heritages, Pyochungsa Temple is a nationally designated temple built to honor the loyal spirit of Master Samyeongdaesa, who made distinguished contributions during the Japanese invasions of Korea (Imjin War). Although reconstructed in 1715 (the 41st year of King Sukjong's reign), all buildings except the Eungjinjeon Hall were destroyed by fire in 1926 and subsequently rebuilt to form the temple complex seen today. Major cultural assets and structures include the National Treasure Bronze Incense Burner with Silver-Inlaid Patterns, the Three-Story Stone Pagoda (a Treasure), as well as provincial cultural heritages such as stone lanterns, Pyochung Seowon Confucian Academy, and Daegwangjeon Hall, along with 25 buildings and around 300 relics of Master Samyeongdaesa.

en.title: Yeonhwasan Provincial Park (연화산도립공원)
en.overview: Located 12 km northwest of Goseong-eup, Yeonhwasan Mountain was named because its mountain contours resemble a blooming lotus flower. Originally called Biseaksan, its name was changed to the current one during the reign of King Injo of the Joseon Dynasty. Consisting of three peaks—Oknyebong, Seondobong, and Mangseonbong—it stands at 524 meters, making it a relatively low mountain, yet it attracts many hikers with its beautiful natural scenery, including lush forests and deep valleys. It was designated as a Gyeongsangnam-do Provincial Park in 1983, and on its northern foothills stands Okcheonsa Temple, founded in 670 (the 10th year of King Munmu of Silla) by the great monk Uisang.

paragraphs: Located 12 km northwest of Goseong-eup, Yeonhwasan Mountain was named because its mountain contours resemble a blooming lotus flower. Originally called Biseaksan, its name was changed to the current one during the reign of King Injo of the Joseon Dynasty. Consisting of three peaks—Oknyebong, Seondobong, and Mangseonbong—it stands at 524 meters, making it a relatively low mountain, yet it attracts many hikers with its beautiful natural scenery, including lush forests and deep valleys. It was designated as a Gyeongsangnam-do Provincial Park in 1983, and on its northern foothills stands Okcheonsa Temple, founded in 670 (the 10th year of King Munmu of Silla) by the great monk Uisang.

The name 'Okcheonsa' originated from a spring behind the temple's main hall (Daeungjeon) that gushes clear water year-round, which is said to be beneficial for stomach and skin diseases. Since 1948, the Okcheongak pavilion has been built and preserved over the spring. Other temples on Yeonhwasan include Baeknyeonam, Cheongnyeonam, and Yeondaeam. Famous local specialties near Yeonhwasan include pine mushrooms and wild berries, and dinosaur footprint fossils from the Mesozoic Cretaceous period can be found in the valleys. en.overview: Located in Hoehwa-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gyeongnam, Danghangpo Tourist Site opened in November 1987. paragraphs: Located in Hoehwa-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gyeongnam, Danghangpo Tourist Site opened in November 1987. It is largely divided into two thematic areas: the Admiral Yi Sun-sin theme and the dinosaur theme. The entire tourist site serves as the main venue for the Gyeongnam Goseong Dinosaur World Expo held every autumn. The Yi Sun-sin theme area commemorates the historic victory of the Battle of Danghangpo and features facilities honoring patriotic spirits, such as Sungchungsa Shrine, Danghangpo Battle Exhibition Hall, Turtle Ship Exhibition Hall, and Chungmugong Diorama Hall. The dinosaur theme area permanently operates various dinosaur contents, such as the Dinosaur Park, Theme Pavilion, and Korean Peninsula Dinosaur Footprint Fossil Hall.

In addition, it features diverse viewing facilities such as the Goseong Natural History Museum, Dinosaur Nara Botanical Garden, and Goseong Suiseki Exhibition Hall, as well as accommodation facilities including camping sites and auto-camping sites. Aside from the Dinosaur Expo, seasonal themed events are operated in spring, summer, and winter to offer year-round attractions. Selected as an 'Excellent Open Tourist Destination' hosted by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, barrier-free walking trails are connected throughout the entire area. Outdoor elevators (escalators) have been installed in sloped sections to improve accessibility, along with disabled-accessible restrooms and tactile guide signs...

paragraphs: Sangjokam County Park offers a panoramic view of the Hallyeo Waterway in the South Sea, where wide rock formations on the sea surface and bizarre cliffs form gorges, representing the pinnacle of splendid natural scenery. Goseong-gun designated this area—boasting the heavenly rock formation Sangjokam and clearly visible dinosaur footprints from the Mesozoic Cretaceous period that hold high preservation value—as a county park by a Goseong-gun notice on November 10, 1983. At the beach in front of the Youth Training Center, smooth pebbles polished by constant tides are laid out, and passing the wide bedrock with dinosaur footprints, the entire mountain facade consists of layered cliffs.

Furthermore, cave-like stone holes piercing deep into the rock wall looping east and west look like a dining table leg, hence it is called 'Ssangjok' (twin legs), or 'Sangjok' / 'Ssangbali' because it resembles multiple legs. Formed by sea erosion, the caves of Sangjokam vary in height, width, and depth, and their uniquely shaped rocks hold many legends. It is traditionally said that in primeval times, fairies descended to set up stone looms and weave royal robes to offer to the Jade Emperor, hence the name 'Ssangjok Gul' (Twin Leg Cave), and the place where the fairies bathed is passed down as 'Seonnyetang' (Fairies' Bath), and...

en.title: Samgye Village (삼계마을)
en.overview: Estimated to have been formed about 500 years ago, Samgye Village was formerly called Gakkye or Gaekgi, but was later named Samgye ('Three Streams') due to its topography where three streams converge. Nestled at the foothills of Nojeokbong Peak in Cheonwangsan Mountain, Samgye Village features lush forests of zelkova, hackberry, and hornbeam trees over 300 years old, making the village panorama even more atmospheric and allowing for forest bathing. Daejujeosuji Reservoir, the largest reservoir in Gyeongnam located right in front of the village, has walking trails built around it, allowing visitors to breathe in plenty of clear rural water and fresh air.

paragraphs: Estimated to have been formed about 500 years ago, Samgye Village was formerly called Gakkye or Gaekgi, but was later named Samgye ('Three Streams') due to its topography where three streams converge. Nestled at the foothills of Nojeokbong Peak in Cheonwangsan Mountain, Samgye Village features lush forests of zelkova, hackberry, and hornbeam trees over 300 years old, making the village panorama even more atmospheric and allowing for forest bathing. Daejujeosuji Reservoir, the largest reservoir in Gyeongnam located right in front of the village, has walking trails built around it, allowing visitors to breathe in plenty of clear rural water and fresh air.

Although Samgye Village is a typical rural village with Cheonwangsan Mountain at its back and Daejujeosuji Reservoir in front, various businesses utilizing the village's natural environment are drawing attention. In particular, the circumferential road offering wonderful views of the reservoir, the parkification of the village forest, Bonghwasan Beacon Mound, and the Chung-hyo Theme Park are more than adequate to showcase a rural village as a comfortable haven for farm-stay families.

en.title: Donghwa Village Fishery Experience Village (동화어촌체험마을)
en.overview: Donghwa Village completed the establishment of experience village infrastructure in March 2005, and all fishermen are joining forces to create an advanced experience village aimed at providing a safe yet special resting space for urbanites looking to enjoy their leisure time. It welcomes visiting tourists with various hands-on programs such as 'Tidal Flat Experience' for digging littleneck clams and 'Torchlight Experience' to catch small octopus and shrimp by the light of torches. In the middle of the village, there is Soleulpiseong Fortress, which served as a supply base for Admiral Yi Sun-sin during the Imjin War, allowing visitors to appreciate the appearance of the old fortress by the sea along with the cozy comfort of 'Donghwa Village' just as its name suggests.

en.title: Namsan Park, Goseong (남산공원(고성))
en.overview: This park offers a panoramic view of the Goseong-eup area and the South Sea. At the park entrance, commemorative monuments detailing the deeds of predecessors are neatly arranged, and climbing 84 steps leads visitors to Bogwangsa Temple, a branch temple of Okcheonsa Temple under the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. To the left of Bogwangsa Temple stand the Memorial Tower built to honor the spirits of patriotic martyrs, a enshrinement hall, and the June 25 Anti-Communist Monument. On the ridge above Bogwangsa Temple, living sports facilities and a magnolia rest area have been established, providing a complete relaxation space combined with physical training utilized by local town residents.

paragraphs: This park offers a panoramic view of the Goseong-eup area and the South Sea. At the park entrance, commemorative monuments detailing the deeds of predecessors are neatly arranged, and climbing 84 steps leads visitors to Bogwangsa Temple, a branch temple of Okcheonsa Temple under the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. To the left of Bogwangsa Temple stand the Memorial Tower built to honor the spirits of patriotic martyrs, a enshrinement hall, and the June 25 Anti-Communist Monument.

On the ridge above Bogwangsa Temple, living sports facilities and a magnolia rest area have been established, providing a complete relaxation space combined with physical training utilized by local town residents. From here, a 3-to-4-meter-wide walking trail is well-paved all the way to Sunam-ri and Sinwol-ri via the mountain summit, taking about an hour to stroll. It is spotlighted as a winter training ground for professional track and athletes, and an octagonal pavilion stands at the peak where the Goseong Bay coast and Goseong-eup can be viewed at a glance, making it a cozy and beautiful place that makes hikers want to linger, offering health promotion and relaxation for the townspeople.

普光寺の上の山腹には生活体育施設とモクレン休憩所が造成され、体力鍛錬とともに休憩所としての完璧な休息空間が造成されており、町民たちが利用している場所である。ここから山の頂上を経て水南里と新ウォルリまで3〜4m幅の散策路がよく整備されており、約1時間で散策できる距離である。専門陸上選手の冬季訓練所として注目を集めている場所であり、頂上には固城湾の海岸と固城邑が一望できる八角亭が建てられており、町民の健康増進や休息はもちろん、山に登る人々に留まりたくなるような温かく美しい場所である。

paragraphs: Located in Georyu-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gyeongnam, Gaokjeong was remodeled by retaining the roof tiles and walls of the building to preserve the memories of an old residential space. The building seamlessly blends the serene tranquility of a Hanok with modern sensibilities, while the seaside scenery unfolding before it—including a lighthouse and Georyu Breakwater—resembles a picturesque painting. From the 1st floor where you can admire waves crashing past large windows, to the 2nd floor with its tasteful interior, and the rooftop overlooking the expansive open sea, photo zones and ocean views can be found throughout the cafe.

Its signature menu is Cream Coffee, featuring Americano or Latte topped with thick, savory cream. It uses Fritz coffee beans, which are also available for separate purchase. A variety of handmade desserts baked fresh in-house are also prepared.

en.title: Neutnamu Hoetjip (Zelkova Raw Fish Restaurant)
en.overview: Located in the Cheongpung Lake Bibimbap Town, Neutnamu Hoetjip boasts a 40-year tradition. Near Cheongpung Lake in Jecheon, there are many restaurants, particularly raw trout specialty houses. The signature dishes here are trout bibimhoe (mixed raw trout) and freshwater spicy fish stew (maeuntang). The trout sashimi is mixed with soybean powder, garlic, sesame oil, carrots, perilla leaves, cabbage, cucumbers, wasabi, andチョジャン (chogochujang), offering a fantastic flavor. Other menu items include charcoal-grilled garlic tteokgalbi, grass carp bibimhoe, mandarin fish maeuntang, tofu hot pot, acorn jelly, and potato pancakes. The bone hangover soup served after the bibimhoe is also exceptional. Although the restaurant shows its age due to its long history, it is kept very clean with tables and chairs for comfortable seating, along with multiple rooms including a main room, making it great for group dining. Takeout orders are available by phone.

ja.title: ヌティナム・フェチプ（欅刺身店）
ja.addr: 忠清北道堤川市清風面裴時論路4
ja.overview: ヌティナム刺身店は清風湖ビビンバタウン内に位置し、40年の伝統を誇るお店である。堤川の清風湖周辺には多くの飲食店があり、特にマスの刺身店が多い。ここのメインメニューはマスのビビンフェ（和え刺身）と川魚の辛口メウンタンである。マスのお刺身をきな粉、ニンニク、ごま油、ニンジン、エゴマの葉、キャベツ、キュウリ、ワサビ、チョジャン（酢コチュジャン）と一緒に和えて食べる味が絶品である。その他にも炭火ニンニク・トッカルビ、ホンオ（タイワンダイ）のビビンフェ、コウライケツギョのメウンタン、豆腐の寄せ鍋、ドングリ묵（ムク）、ジャガイモのチヂミなどを味わうことができる。ビビンフェを食べた後に出てくる骨ヘジャングク（骨付き肉のスープ）の味も絶品である。歴史が古いだけに店舗も年季が入っているが、きれいに整えられており、テーブルと椅子が置かれていて楽に座って食事をすることができる。メインルームをはじめ複数の個室があり、団体での食事にも適している。電話でのテイクアウト注文も可能である。

zh.title: 櫸樹生魚片店（Nutnamu Hoetjip）
zh.addr: 忠清北道堤川市清風面裴時論路4
zh.overview: 櫸樹生魚片店位於清風湖拌飯小鎮內，是一間擁有40年傳統的老字號餐廳。堤川的清風湖周邊有許多餐廳，特別是鱒魚生魚片店林立。這裡的主打招牌菜是鱒魚拌生魚片和淡水辣魚湯。將鱒魚生魚片搭配黃豆粉、大蒜、香油、紅蘿蔔、芝麻葉、高麗菜、小黃瓜、芥末以及醋辣椒醬一起攪拌食用，風味絕佳。除此之外，還能品嚐到炭火大蒜肉餅、草魚拌生魚片、鳜魚辣魚湯、豆腐火鍋、橡子涼粉、馬鈴薯煎餅等。吃完拌生魚片後端上的醒酒排骨湯也是一絕。雖說歷史悠久導致店面也有些歲月痕跡，但內部整理得十分乾淨，並備有桌椅讓顧客能舒適坐着用餐，店內還設有主包廂等多個房間，非常適合團體聚餐。打電話即可預訂外帶。

en.title: Bapsang-wi-ui Boyakhancheop Cheongpung Branch (A Dose of Medicine on the Table)
en.overview: Located 40 minutes away from Jecheon, a clean region with clear water and fresh air, Bapsang-wi-ui Boyakhancheop Cheongpung Branch is a farmhouse-style restaurant that creates unique dishes using deodeok (codonopsis lanceolata), a fragrant and delicious local specialty. The restaurant has two floors: the first floor serves as an experience and education center as well as a processing space, while the second floor features a cozy dining area alongside a display of various processed goods crafted with the owner's neat culinary skills.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delicacies: Bapsang-wi-ui Boyakhancheop Set · Boyakhancheop / Bapsang Special / Spicy Braised Pork Ribs, etc.
paragraphs: Located 40 minutes away from Jecheon, a clean region with clear water and fresh air, Bapsang-wi-ui Boyakhancheop Cheongpung Branch is a farmhouse-style restaurant that creates unique dishes using deodeok (codonopsis lanceolata), a fragrant and delicious local specialty. The restaurant has two floors: the first floor serves as an experience and education center as well as a processing space, while the second floor features a cozy dining area alongside a display of various processed goods crafted with the owner's neat culinary skills.

Main processed products sold here include jangaji (soy sauce pickles), jocheong (rice syrup), cheong (fruit syrups), and fermented soybean pastes made from locally abundant leafy vegetables and deodeok, offering a wonderful view of the surrounding scenery from the second floor. There is also a terrace on the second floor where you can enjoy a breeze and a cup of tea, allowing visitors to fully experience the traditional rural village scenery and sentiment.

en.title: Anmyeondo Natural Recreation Forest
en.overview: Anmyeondo Natural Recreation Forest is the country's only single-species pine forest, where a dense cluster of native Anmyeon pine trees, about 100 years old, thrives across 430ha. Since the Goryeo Dynasty, they were mainly used to build palaces and ships, but as illegal logging worsened, the royal family placed them under special management, and Chungcheongnam-do has managed them since 1965. Currently, the recreation forest is located on a pine forest ridge that appears after passing the wide plains of Bangpo Village past the Anmyeon-eup township.

paragraphs: Anmyeondo Natural Recreation Forest is the country's only single-species pine forest, where a dense cluster of native Anmyeon pine trees, about 100 years old, thrives across 430ha. Since the Goryeo Dynasty, they were mainly used to build palaces and ships, but as illegal logging worsened, the royal family placed them under special management, and Chungcheongnam-do has managed them since 1965. Currently, the recreation forest is located on a pine forest ridge that appears after passing the wide plains of Bangpo Village past the Anmyeon-eup township. The moment you step into the recreation forest, your mind is immediately cleared by the pine scent emanating from the cool, straight-growing pine trees.

Inside the path paved with interlocking blocks, a wonderful building comes into view: the Forest Exhibition Hall, which also serves as the management office. The Forest Exhibition Hall is organized so that visitors can easily understand the timber production process, uses of wood, and utility value of forests. Crossing a small hill along the path to the right of the exhibition hall, you can finally see the forest houses. There are forest houses and forest recreation facilities arranged in a row along the mountain slope, equipped with gas stoves, cooking utensils, and shower facilities.

en.pull_quote: Taean Haean National Park was designated as South Korea's 13th national park in 1978. It spans a total area of 377.019㎢ with 27 beaches spread across a 230km coastline embracing the Taean Peninsula and Anmyeondo Island...
paragraphs: Taean Haean National Park was designated as South Korea's 13th national park in 1978. It spans a total area of 377.019㎢ with 27 beaches spread across a 230km coastline embracing the Taean Peninsula and Anmyeondo Island from north to south. Since ancient times, the region was named Taean (meaning 'Peace and Comfort') because life was not harsh, thanks to the absence of major natural disasters, a mild climate, and abundant food.

The geology of the Taean Haean National Park area mainly consists of Precambrian ancient metamorphic sedimentary rocks and Mesozoic igneous rocks intruding upon them, and the coastal zone mostly comprises alluvial deposits made of medium to fine silt, appearing in the form of sandy beaches and coastal dunes. Topographically, the Taean coast consists of tidal flats, dunes, wetlands, bizarre rock formations, and large and small islands along a ria coastline of approximately 230 km from Hakampho in the north to Yeongmok in the south. Because of this, it is considered one of the representative places showcasing the unique and beautiful scenery of the West Coast. (Source: Taean Haean National Park Website)

paragraphs: 泰安海岸国立公園は1978年に我が国13番目の国立公園に指定された。泰安半島と安眠島を南北に網羅する230kmの海岸線に27のビーチが広がり、総面積は377.019㎢である。昔から大きな自然災害がなく、温暖な気候と豊富な食べ物で生活が困窮しなかったことから、地名を泰安（テアン）と名付けた。

泰安海岸国立公園地域の地質は、先カンブリア時代の古期変成堆積岩類とこれらを貫入した中生代の火成岩類が主をなしており、海岸地帯はほとんど中粒ないし細粒のシルトで構成された沖積層で、砂浜海岸と海岸砂丘の形態で現れる。泰安海岸の地形的に鶴岩浦から南側の永穆に至るまで約230㎞のリアス式海岸線に沿って干潟や砂丘、干潟、湿地、奇岩怪石と大小の島々で構成されている。このため、西海岸特有の美しい景観を代表する場所として挙げられている。（出典：泰安海岸国立公園ホームページ）

paragraphs: 泰安海岸國立公園於1978年被指定為韓國第13座國立公園。南北綿延泰安半島與安眠島長達230公里的海岸線上分佈著27個海灘，總面積達377.019平方公里。自古以來因少有重大自然災害、氣候溫和且食物豐富、生活無虞，故將地名取為「泰安」。
泰安海岸國立公園一帶的地質以前寒武紀古期變質沉積岩類與侵入其中的中生代火成岩類為主，海岸地帶多為中粒至細粒粉砂組成的沖積層，呈現沙灘海岸與海岸沙丘的形態。從地形上看，泰安海岸從北部的鶴岩浦到南側的永穆，沿著約230公里的里亞式海岸線，由泥灘、沙丘、濕地、奇岩怪石以及大大小小的島嶼所組成。因此，被譽為代表西海岸特有美麗風光的首選之地。（資料來源：泰安海岸國立公園官網）

en.title: Euihang Beach
en.overview: Walking past the Sowon-myeon township toward Mallipo Beach, you will find Euihang Beach on the right. Named because its topographical shape resembles an ant's neck, it features a gentle slope and maintains clean seawater even during high tide. The sandy beach, entirely composed of pebbles, sparkles brightly under the sunlight, and the cozy, curved shoreline boasts stunning beauty. Mainly recognized as an undeveloped tourist destination favored for family or educational camping trips, visitors arriving without special preparations can easily use the local homestays (minbak). Like typical West Coast beaches, the shore is gentle and spread with colorful pebbles. Along the Sowon-myeon coast, Baekripo Beach, Cheonripo Beach, Mallipo Beach, Eoeundol Beach, and Padori Beach continue southward from Euihang Beach.

en.title: Mallipo Beach
en.overview: Mallipo Beach is located at the very end of National Route 32 crossing Taean-gun and is designated as part of Taean Haean National Park. As a representative tourist destination of Slow City Taean, it is especially famous for its beautiful scenery. The bow-shaped sandy beach stretches for nearly 1km, featuring a gentle water depth and a wide sandy expanse, making it perfect for swimming.

As a representative tourist destination of Slow City Taean, it is especially famous for its beautiful scenery. The bow-shaped sandy beach stretches for nearly 1km, featuring a gentle water depth and a wide sandy expanse, making it perfect for swimming.

Surrounded by well-equipped accommodation and convenience facilities, it is an ideal retreat for family vacations. Camping is also available in the pine forest spreading widely around the beach, allowing visitors to enjoy both swimming and forest bathing. Additionally, leisure facilities such as marine sports and rocky shore fishing offer plenty of things to do. Savoring fresh seafood such as Mallipo's signature ganggaemi muchim (spicy skate salad), grilled sea eel, and grilled king prawns is another exceptional delight.

en.title: Bangpo Beach
en.overview: Bangpo Beach features excellent sand quality and is great for camping, making it an optimal quiet family getaway. On both sides of the beach stand legendary rock peaks such as Halmi Rock (Grandmother Rock) and Halarbi Rock (Grandfather Rock), and the area is home to a colony of golden rain trees designated as Natural Monument No. 138. Additionally, to the southwest lie Naepasudo and Oepasudo islands, which act as natural breakwaters. Bangpo Port is famous for fresh raw fish caught abundantly, including ray, conger eel, rockfish, and mackerel, and neighbors various beaches like Kkotji and Sambong.

Additionally, to the southwest lie Naepasudo and Oepasudo islands, which act as natural breakwaters. Bangpo Port is famous for fresh raw fish caught abundantly, including ray, conger eel, rockfish, and mackerel, and neighbors various beaches like Kkotji and Sambong. Nearby, attractions such as the Anmyeondo Natural Recreation Forest and an arboretum housing 208 species of natural flora from the central coastal region make it suitable for family relaxation and mental-physical refreshment.

en.title: Mongsanpo Beach
en.overview: Part of Taean Haean National Park, Mongsanpo Beach is surrounded by sandy shores and dense pine forests. With an auto-camping site located within the pine forest spreading widely along the beach, many campers visit to enjoy forest bathing and the fragrance of nature. The beach features a vast tidal flat, drawing frequent crowds looking to catch clams and crabs when the tide goes out. Well-developed sand dunes also make it perfect for tidal flat experiences and natural organism observation with children.
en.pull_quote: Part of Taean Haean National Park, Mongsanpo Beach is surrounded by sandy shores and dense pine forests. With an auto-camping site located within the pine forest spreading widely...
paragraphs: Part of Taean Haean National Park, Mongsanpo Beach is surrounded by sandy shores and dense pine forests. With an auto-camping site located within the pine forest spreading widely along the beach, many campers visit to enjoy forest bathing and the fragrance of nature. The beach features a vast tidal flat, drawing frequent crowds looking to catch clams and crabs when the tide goes out. Well-developed sand dunes also make it perfect for tidal flat experiences and natural organism observation with children.

In particular, if you drive through the tall pine tree tunnel stretching for about 1km to the west, you will find Mongdaepo Port, where you can enjoy various fishing boats and raw restaurants offering fresh wild-caught sashimi at affordable prices. You can enjoy rocky shore fishing at the breakwater or go boat fishing on fishing boats departing from here.

en.title: Chilseon Valley (칠선계곡)
en.overview: Chilseon Valley is hailed as one of Korea's top three valleys, alongside Cheonbuldong Valley in Seoraksan Mountain and Tamna Valley in Hallasan Mountain. Located in Jirisan Mountain, it boasts rugged terrain, stunning scenery, and the mountain's last remaining virgin forest. Stretching from Uitang in Macheon-myeon to Cheonwangbong Peak, the valley's ethereal landscape features 7 waterfalls and 33 pools (so). The hiking trail starts from Chuseong Village in Macheon-myeon and leads to Cheonwangbong Peak; due to the hazards of valley climbing, a significant portion of the trail is set apart from the valley itself.

paragraphs: Chilseon Valley is hailed as one of Korea's top three valleys, alongside Cheonbuldong Valley in Seoraksan Mountain and Tamna Valley in Hallasan Mountain. Located in Jirisan Mountain, it boasts rugged terrain, stunning scenery, and the mountain's last remaining virgin forest. Stretching from Uitang in Macheon-myeon to Cheonwangbong Peak, the valley's ethereal landscape features 7 waterfalls and 33 pools (so). The hiking trail starts from Chuseong Village in Macheon-myeon and leads to Cheonwangbong Peak; due to the hazards of valley climbing, a significant portion of the trail is set apart from the valley itself.

This is due to the rugged terrain, which leaves virtually no safe place to step outside the designated trail. Starting from Chuseong, hikers can witness the true essence of this fairyland as they pass Yongso, Jujiteo, Chuseong Mangbawi Rock, Seonnyetang, Oknyetang, Biseandam, Chilseon Waterfall, Dae륙 Waterfall, Samcheong Waterfall, and Mapokpo Waterfall before finally reaching Cheonwangbong Peak.

這是因為山勢險峻，一旦離開步道便幾乎找不到可以安心落腳的地方。從出發點楸城開始，依序經過龍沼、主地터、楸城望바위、仙女湯、玉女湯、飛仙潭、七仙瀑布、大陸瀑布、三層瀑布、馬瀑布直到天王峰，可以一路飽覽仙境的精華。

en.pull_quote: Located along the Wicheon Stream on the western side of Hamyang-eup, Hamyang Sangnim is a historic forest created by scholar Choe Chi-won during Queen Jinseong's reign in the Unified Silla period to prevent flood damage in Hamyang-eup. Formerly known as Daegwanrim...
paragraphs: Located along the Wicheon Stream on the western side of Hamyang-eup, Hamyang Sangnim is a historic forest created by scholar Choe Chi-won during Queen Jinseong's reign in the Unified Silla period to prevent flood damage in Hamyang-eup. Formerly known as Daegwanrim, the forest was divided into Sangnim (Upper Forest) and Halim (Lower Forest) when its central section was washed away by a flood.

Today, Halim is largely damaged with only traces remaining, while Sangnim preserves its original appearance. Dominated by oak and hornbeam trees, the intertwining wild grapes and kudzu vines evoke the natural vegetation of a deep valley. With around 120 species of trees planted along the embankment, it is also a wonderful natural learning center for children.

en.title: Chilseon Sanjang Sikdang (칠선산장식당)
en.overview: Located in Hamyang-gun, Chilseon Sanjang Restaurant serves traditional local cuisine made with natural wild greens and pristine vegetables from Jirisan Mountain. With a valley nearby, it is frequently visited by people after water play in the summer. Menu items include sanchae bibimbap (wild vegetable bibimbap), dolsot sanchae bibimbap (stone pot wild vegetable bibimbap), spicy native chicken braise, and native lacquer chicken baeksuk. Guests can enjoy a comfortable meal with a valley view, and a cafe is operated right in front, making it ideal for family visits after dining.

en.title: Daeseong Sikdang (대성식당)
en.overview: Daeseong Sikdang is a gukbap (soup with rice) specialty restaurant located in Hamyang-eup, Hamyang-gun, Gyeongsangbuk-do. An old house was remodeled into a restaurant, featuring traditional low-legged tables on the floor inside. Retaining old closets and wallpaper, it gives the cozy feeling of visiting a rural hometown home. There are only two items on the menu: gukbap and suyuk (boiled meat slices). Unlike regular suyuk, the Hanwoo (Korean beef) suyuk is served with thick meat and green onions piled atop a rich, red broth, while the Hanwoo gukbap is generously packed with large chunks of meat, taro stems, and other hearty ingredients.

en.title: Gyeomamjeongsa House, Hahoe Village, Andong (안동 하회마을 겸암정사)
en.overview: Gyeomamjeongsa is a pavilion located near Hahoe Village in Pungcheon-myeon, Andong-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do. It was built by Gyeomam Ryu Un-ryong (1539–1601), a mid-Joseon dynasty scholar and older brother of Seae Ryu Seong-ryong, for studying and fostering younger scholars. Situated on a cliff overlooking the meandering Nakdonggang River, it boasts exceptional natural scenery and is known as a scenic spot offering panoramic views of Hahoe Village and Buyongdae Cliff. The current building was reconstructed by descendants after being destroyed during the Imjin War, and features a sarangchae (men's quarters) and ancestral shrine centered around the main pavilion.

It was built by Gyeomam Ryu Un-ryong (1539–1601), a mid-Joseon dynasty scholar and older brother of Seae Ryu Seong-ryong, for studying and fostering younger scholars. Situated on a cliff overlooking the meandering Nakdonggang River, it boasts exceptional natural scenery and is known as a scenic spot offering panoramic views of Hahoe Village and Buyongdae Cliff.

The current building was reconstructed by descendants after being destroyed during the Imjin War, and features a sarangchae (men's quarters) and ancestral shrine centered around the main pavilion. Gyeomamjeongsa is evaluated as a space offering a glimpse into the scholarship and lifestyle of a Joseon literati, as well as a cultural heritage representing the tradition of Andong's Confucian culture along with Hahoe Village.

en.overview: Jangseung (traditional Korean totem poles) have long been placed at village entrances as guardian deities protecting villagers from evil spirits and diseases, and sometimes as objects of prayer, forming a familiar folk culture among commoners. Around 250 jangseung, carved from discarded trees, gather together. Their expressions vary widely, from rugged, intimidating features with names like Cheonhadaejanggun, Jiyeohajanggun, Jinseodaejanggun, Bukjanggun, and Dangjanggun, to innocent and clumsy ones resembling country children. Dainty jangseung—such as bride-and-groom-shaped ones, a single tree with two distinct faces, or one utilizing a curved trunk to look like a shy maiden peeking out from behind a pillar—spark visitors' curiosity. However, what draws the eye most is the unique Andong-style Hahoe mask-shaped jangseung not found anywhere else.

en.title: Samgwijeong Pavilion (삼귀정)
en.overview: Samgwijeong is a Joseon Dynasty pavilion located in Andong, Gyeongsangbuk-do. It was built in 1496 (the 2nd year of King Yeonsan's reign) by the scholar Kim Yeong-su and his brothers to pray for the health and longevity of their mother, Lady Kwon of Yecheon. Sosan Village, where the pavilion stands, is a clan village for the Andong Kim family. The name 'Samgwijeong' originates from three turtle-shaped rocks to the left of the pavilion. As turtles symbolize longevity, the pavilion embodies deep filial piety toward parents. The current building was reconstructed in 1947.
en.pull_quote: Samgwijeong is a Joseon Dynasty pavilion located in Andong, Gyeongsangbuk-do, built in 1496 by scholar Kim Yeong-su and his brothers to pray for their mother's health and longevity.
paragraphs: Samgwijeong is a Joseon Dynasty pavilion located in Andong, Gyeongsangbuk-do. It was built in 1496 (the 2nd year of King Yeonsan's reign) by the scholar Kim Yeong-su and his brothers to pray for the health and longevity of their mother, Lady Kwon of Yecheon. Sosan Village, where the pavilion stands, is a clan village for the Andong Kim family. The name 'Samgwijeong' originates from three turtle-shaped rocks to the left of the pavilion.

Since turtles symbolize longevity, the pavilion is said to embody deep filial piety toward parents. The current building was reconstructed in 1947. Thanks to its open structure on all four sides, visitors can enjoy panoramic views of the village and surrounding scenery. Inside hangs a signboard reading 'Samgwijeong', written by Lee Jong-jun, a scholar and civil official from Andong.

en.title: Gaemoksa Temple, Andong (개목사)
en.overview: Gaemoksa Temple was originally named Heungguksa Temple and was reportedly founded by Master Uisang during the reign of King Sinmun of Unified Silla (reigned 681–692). According to legend, Master Uisang attained enlightenment through the miracle of a celestial maiden in Cheon-deunggul Cave behind the temple and subsequently established it. The name 'Gaemoksa' was reportedly given during the Joseon Dynasty. Wontongjeon Hall of Gaemoksa, which houses the Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, contains a record discovered during disassembly and repair work in 1969 bearing the phrase 'Cheonsun Wonnyeon', indicating it was built in the 3rd year of King Sejo (1457).
en.pull_quote: Gaemoksa Temple was originally named Heungguksa Temple and was reportedly founded by Master Uisang during the reign of King Sinmun of Unified Silla (681–692).
paragraphs: Gaemoksa Temple was originally named Heungguksa Temple and was reportedly founded by Master Uisang during the reign of King Sinmun of Unified Silla (reigned 681–692). According to legend, Master Uisang attained enlightenment through the miracle of a celestial maiden in Cheon-deunggul Cave behind the temple and subsequently established it. The name 'Gaemoksa' was reportedly given during the Joseon Dynasty.

Wontongjeon Hall of Gaemoksa, which houses the Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, contains a record discovered during disassembly and repair work in 1969 bearing the phrase 'Cheonsun Wonnyeon', suggesting it was built in the 3rd year of King Sejo (1457). It well preserves the architectural style of the early Joseon Dynasty and was designated as a Treasure on January 21, 1963.

en.title: Bongjeongsa Temple [UNESCO World Heritage] (봉정사)
en.overview: Located not far from the city center, Cheondeungsan Bongjeongsa is a serene temple ideal for stepping away from daily life and enjoying peaceful relaxation. It houses Korea's oldest wooden building and allows visitors to take walks and rest amidst clean air and the tranquil atmosphere of a mountain temple. It is also known as a place for spiritual practice, carrying on the traditions of Korean mountain Buddhism. Bongjeongsa was founded in the 12th year of King Munmu of Silla (672) by Neungin, a disciple of Master Uisang.
en.pull_quote: Located not far from the city center, Cheondeungsan Bongjeongsa is a serene temple ideal for stepping away from daily life and enjoying peaceful relaxation.
paragraphs: Located not far from the city center, Cheondeungsan Bongjeongsa is a serene temple ideal for stepping away from daily life and enjoying peaceful relaxation. It houses Korea's oldest wooden building and allows visitors to take walks and rest amidst clean air and the tranquil atmosphere of a mountain temple. It is also known as a place for spiritual practice, carrying on the traditions of Korean mountain Buddhism. Bongjeongsa was founded in the 12th year of King Munmu of Silla (672) by Neungin, a disciple of Master Uisang.

Cheondeungsan Mountain was originally called Daemangsan Mountain. The name 'Cheondeungsan' (Mountain of Heavenly Lantern) originates from a legend where a heavenly fairy lowered a lantern to illuminate the cave while Neungin was practicing asceticism inside a rock cave. Afterward, Neungin folded and released a paper phoenix, which landed and stayed here, leading to the name 'Bongjeongsa' (Temple of the Resting Phoenix). Since its founding, it has been renovated six times and preserves precious cultural heritage including National Treasures and Treasures such as Geungnakjeon Hall, Daeungjeon Hall, and post-Buddha murals, along with a wooden seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, Hwaeom Gangdang, and Gogeumdang. Other notable sites include Deokhwiru Pavilion, Muryang Haehoe, Samseonggak, a three-story stone pagoda, Yeongsanam Hermitage, and Jijoam Hermitage.

ja.title: 鳳停寺 [ユネスコ世界文化遺産]（ポンジョンサ）

ja.overview: 天燈山鳳停寺は都心から遠く離れておらず、少しの間日常を離れて閑静な余裕を楽しむのに良い寺院である。韓国で最も古い木造建築物を有しており、澄んだ空気と趣のある山寺の雰囲気の中で散策と休息を楽しむことができる。また、韓国の山中仏教の伝統を受け継いでおり、修行の場としても知られている。鳳停寺は新羅の文武王12年（672）に義湘大師の弟子である能仁法師が創建した寺院である。

天燈山は元々大望山と呼ばれていたが、能仁法師が岩窟で修行中、天の仙女が灯火を下ろして洞窟の中を明るく照らしてくれたという伝説から「天燈山」という名前の由来となった。その後、能仁法師が紙の鳳凰を折って飛ばしたところ、ここに舞い降りて留まったことから、鳳凰の「鳳」と留まる「停」を取って「鳳停寺」と名付けられた。創建以来、6度にわたって改修され、極楽殿と大殿をはじめとする様々な国宝や宝物、後仏壁画、木造観世音菩薩坐像、華厳講堂、古金堂などの大切な文化遺産を秘蔵している。このほかにも徳輝楼、無量海会、三星閣、三層石塔と霊山庵、知祖庵などがある。

zh.overview: 天燈山鳳停寺距離市區不遠，是暫時遠離日常、享受恬靜悠閒的好去處。這裡保存了韓國最古老的木造建築，遊客可以在清新的空氣與幽靜的山寺氛圍中散步與休憩。此外，它延續了韓國山中佛教的傳統，也是著名的修行場所。鳳停寺由新羅文武王12年（672年）義湘大師的弟子能仁法師所創建。

天燈山原本稱為大望山，相傳能仁法師在岩洞中修行時，天上的仙女降下燈火照亮洞內，因而得名「天燈山」。此後，能仁法師摺了一隻紙鳳凰放飛，鳳凰降落並停留在此處，因此取鳳凰的「鳳」字與停留的「停」字，命名為「鳳停寺」。自創建以來經過六次重修，保存了極樂殿、大雄殿等國寶與寶物、後佛壁畫、木造觀世音菩薩坐像、華嚴講堂、古金堂等珍貴文化遺產。除此之外，還有德輝樓、無量海會、三星閣、三層石塔以及靈山庵、知祖庵等。

en.title: Chuimsae (추임새)
en.overview: Named after 'Chuimsae', the traditional exclamations of encouragement used by masters of Korean traditional music, this is a renowned traditional Andong restaurant. It is well-known as a hotspot where world cultural heritage exploration teams stayed for weeks, visited by celebrities from all walks of life (guestbooks available), and designated as an official restaurant for KEPCO training sessions, university MTs, and forums. Representative dishes include salted mackerel (gan-godeungeo) and soybean paste stew (doenjang-jjigae). Other Korean dishes like Andong jjimdak, Hanwoo sprout bibimbap, Hanwoo gukbap, and baechu-jeon (cabbage pancakes) are also available to suit various tastes.

en.title: Mat 50-nyeon Heotjesabap (맛50년 헛제사밥)
en.overview: As the person who commercialized 'heotjesabap' (fake ancestral ritual food), which is now widely popular in Korea, this restaurant is considered the pioneer of the dish. Passed down to her daughter-in-law, three generations have dedicated themselves to running the restaurant for over 50 years. Heotjesabap is a traditional local food of Andong where various seasoned vegetables are placed over rice and mixed with soy sauce, just like the food prepared for ancestral rites, but without actually holding a ritual. Since Andong has many famous Confucian academies (seowon), Confucian scholars used to gather here to enjoy literature and leisure. They would set up ancestral food, compose sacrificial texts and prayers as if holding a memorial service, and then share the food together. This is how the dish came to be called 'heotjesabap' (false ritual meal).
en.pull_quote: Signature Delicacies: Heotjesabap · Seonbi Table / Grilled Salted Mackerel, etc.

ja.addr: 慶尚北道 安東市 石州路 201（上河洞）
ja.overview: 国内で大流行しているホットジェサバプ（祭祀を行わないのに祭祀膳のように食べるビビンバ）を商品化した人物であり、ホットジェサバプの元祖と言える店。現在、お嫁さんまで代々受け継がれ、3代にわたり50年以上食堂の運営だけに専念している。ホットジェサバプとは、祭祀を行わなくても、まるで祭祀の時のように白ご飯に各種ナムルを載せ、醤油でビビンバにして食べる安東の伝統郷土料理である。安東には有名な書院が多く、昔から儒生たちが集まって風流を楽しんでいた。彼らは祭祀の料理を並べて祝文や祭文を作り、まるで祭祀を行っているかのような真似をした後、その料理を一緒に分け合って食べた。そのため、この料理にホットジェサバプ（嘘の祭祀ご飯）という名前が付けられたのである。

zh.title: 味50年 虛祭祀飯（맛50년 헛제사밥）
zh.addr: 慶尚北道安東市石주路201（上河洞）
zh.overview: 將在韓國大為流行的「虛祭祀飯（Heotjesabap）」商品化，可說是虛祭祀飯的鼻祖。目前由媳婦傳承，三代人超過50年來一直專心經營餐廳。虛祭祀飯是安東的傳統鄉土料理，不實際舉行祭祀，卻如同祭祀飯一般，在白飯上鋪上各種涼拌菜，再用醬油拌著吃。安東有許多著名的書院，過去儒生們經常聚在一起享受風流。他們擺好祭祀料理，寫下祝文與祭文，假裝舉行祭祀後再一起分食這些食物。因此，這道料理便有了「虛祭祀飯（假祭祀飯）」的名稱。

各種涼拌菜，再用醬油拌著吃。安東有許多著名的書院，過去儒生們經常聚在一起享受風流。他們擺好祭祀料理，寫下祝文與祭文，假裝舉行祭祀後再一起分食這些食物。因此，這道料理便有了「虛祭祀飯」的名稱。

en.title: Mokpojin History Park
en.overview: First established in 1439 as Mokpojin, a Joseon naval garrison, this site firmly guarded the maritime routes of the Dadohae archipelago. Also called Manhojin as a 'manho' (naval commander) was stationed here, it was fortified with a castle wall around 1502. As a strategic stronghold for southwestern coastal defense and a meaningful historic site marking the genesis of modern Mokpo, the site was partially restored as a history park in 2014 after being abandoned in 1895. The neatly restored old government office harmonizes with the surrounding lush trees.

As a strategic stronghold for southwestern coastal defense and a meaningful historic site marking the genesis of modern Mokpo, the site was partially restored as a history park in 2014 after being abandoned in 1895.

The neatly restored old government office, Gaksa, harmonizes with the surrounding lush trees, its subtle depth of time naturally causing visitors to pause. Stroll leisurely along the well-organized outdoor walking trails and naturally feel the breath of the Joseon navy and the historical value of the space. Beyond Gaksa, stepping up to the observation deck at the top of the hill reveals a panoramic view of Mokpo-jin port with boats gliding across calm waters. Beyond the colorful old downtown housing, the majestic ridges of Mt. Yudal rise high, making it a great spot to take in both Mokpo's past and present scenery at a glance.

paragraphs: 1439年、朝鮮水軍の陣営である木浦鎮が初めて設置され、多島海の海域を心強く守ってきた場所です。万戸が配置されたことから万戸鎮とも呼ばれ、1502年頃に城を築いて陣城の姿を整えました。西南海岸の国防の要衝地であり、近代木浦の胎動を秘めた意味深い歴史的スポットで、1895年に廃陣となった後に跡地だけ残っていたものを2014年に歴史公園として一部復元しました。

周辺の青々とした樹木と調和し、整然と復元された旧官衙（役所）の建物である客舎（キクサ）は、穏やかな時の深みを伝え、訪れる者の足を自然と立ち止まらせます。きれいに整備された野外散策路に沿ってのんびり歩きながら、朝鮮水軍の息吹と空間が持つ歴史的価値を自然に感じてみましょう。客舎を過ぎて丘の頂上の展望台に立てば、穏やかな波の上に船が行き交う木浦港の風景が爽快に広がります。カラフルな旧市街の住宅の向こうに儒達山（ユダルサン）の稜線が雄大にそびえており、木浦の昔の姿と今日の風景を一望するのにぴったりです。

paragraphs: 這裡於1439年首次設立朝鮮水軍陣營「木浦鎮」，長久以來穩固地守護著多島海的海上門戶。因曾部署萬戶（官職），故也被稱為「萬戶鎮」，並於1502年前後築城，具備了鎮城的規模。作為西南海岸國防的重要據點，以及孕育近代木浦發源地的深厚歷史場所，在1895年廢鎮僅剩遺址後，於2014年部分復原為歷史公園。
與周圍蒼翠樹木相融、整潔復原的舊官衙建築「客舍」，散發著歲月沉澱的深邃氣息，讓造訪者的腳步不禁慢了下來。沿著規劃完善的戶外散步路漫步，自然而然地感受朝鮮水軍的足跡與空間所蘊含的歷史價值。穿過客舍登上山丘頂端的觀景台，平靜水面上船隻來往的木浦港風光便在眼前開闊展開。色彩繽紛的老市區房舍上方，儒達山的山脊雄偉聳立，非常適合將木浦的昔日面貌與今日風光盡收眼底。

en.title: Hwashin Chain Store (Café Hwashin)
en.overview: Carrying on the history of the modern bustling district that flourished as a commercial hub, this cafe is located in the old downtown area near Mokpo Station, offering a special experience where past and present times intersect. Divided into the 1st floor boasting an antique mood and the 2nd floor ideal for relaxed resting, the interior is arranged with soft lighting and warm wooden materials, creating a cozy atmosphere from the moment you step in. The traces of time deeply imbued throughout the building and its neat structure convey the quiet charm of modern architecture, soothing the traveler's excited heart.
en.pull_quote: Signature items: 1990 Hwashin Cream Latte, Black Sesame Cream Latte, Sea Lemonade, Vin Chaud, etc.

It offers a variety of fragrant teas along with signature beverages topped with cream, such as Hwashin Cream Latte, Black Sesame Cream Latte, and Sea Lemonade. Opening at 10:00 AM on weekdays and 9:00 AM on weekends, it is a great place to drop by after an early morning walk. You can enjoy warm tea and sweet snacks while looking out at the modest streets of the old downtown unfolding outside the window, or take a short break after exploring Mokpo Modern History and Culture Street.

ja.title: 華信連鎖店（ファシン・チェンジョム）

ja.overview: 商業の中心地として栄えた近代の繁華街の歴史を受け継ぎ、木浦駅近くの旧市街に位置するカフェです。過去と現在の時間が交差する特別な体験を提供してくれます。古風な趣を誇る1階と、ゆったりとした休息を楽しむのにぴったりの2階に分かれた店内は、間接照明と温かみのある木材で整えられており、足を踏み入れた瞬間から居心地の良い雰囲気を醸し出します。建物のあちこちに深く染み込んだ時代の痕跡と端正な構造が、近代建築特有の趣ある魅力を放ち、旅人の高ぶった心を穏やかに癒やしてくれます。

en.title: Giseungjeondak Hongdae Sangsu Main Branch
en.overview: Giseungjeondak Hongdae Sangsu Main Branch is a chicken feet and poultry specialty restaurant in the Hongdae and Sangsu areas, perfect for everything from a casual meal to a late-night gathering. They serve a variety of chicken dishes such as dakgomtang (chicken soup with rice), dakkalguksu (chicken knife-cut noodles), grilled chicken neck bulgogi, seasoned chicken salad, and old-school whole fried chicken. All chicken and chicken feet used are 100% domestic. Signature dishes include flame-grilled chicken feet with a smoky aroma and broth-style chicken feet simmered in a reduced sauce. The chicken feet seasoning achieves its spice from chili peppers rather than artificial capsaicin.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delights: Flame-Grilled Chicken Feet · Broth Chicken Feet / Dakgomtang / Dakkalguksu, etc.
paragraphs: Giseungjeondak Hongdae Sangsu Main Branch is a chicken feet and poultry specialty restaurant in the Hongdae and Sangsu areas, perfect for everything from a casual meal to a late-night gathering. They serve a variety of chicken dishes such as dakgomtang (chicken soup with rice), dakkalguksu (chicken knife-cut noodles), grilled chicken neck bulgogi, seasoned chicken salad, and old-school whole fried chicken. All chicken and chicken feet used are 100% domestic. Signature dishes include flame-grilled chicken feet with a smoky aroma and broth-style chicken feet simmered in a reduced sauce.

The chicken feet seasoning achieves its spice from chili peppers rather than artificial capsaicin. You can choose between bone-in and boneless options, and order sets served with flying fish roe rice balls and steamed eggs. Side dishes to share, such as shredded potato pancakes and corn cheese, are also available. Enjoy a meal of dakgomtang and dakkalguksu, or pair chicken feet with drinks. It is a great spot for group gatherings with friends or colleagues, as well as wedding-invitation dinner parties.

en.title: Busan Songjeong Matjip Songjeong Codari Main Branch
en.overview: Busan Songjeong Matjip Songjeong Codari Main Branch is a Korean restaurant located in Haeundae-gu, Busan. The signature dishes are spicy braised dried pollack (codari) with radish greens (siraegi) and lotus leaf rice, characterized by cooking the codari and siraegi together. Spice levels can be chosen from mild, normal, and spicy, and you can choose between regular rice and lotus leaf rice. In addition, there are various dishes such as spicy cod head soup and grilled mackerel. The restaurant has a total of 88 seats, accommodating family meals and group visits, and accepts advance reservations along with early breakfast service.

en.title: Chamchi Ssadagu Dongchun Branch
en.overview: Chamchi Ssadagu Dongchun Branch is a tuna specialty restaurant located on the second floor of the Dongchun-dong food alley in Yeonsu-gu, Incheon. Focusing on Bluefin tuna (honmaguro) and Bigeye tuna (big eye), they offer various cuts including medium fatty belly, large fatty belly, and belly button meat. The restaurant features private rooms and group seating, making it ideal for family meals, company dinners, and group gatherings. Along with the signature tuna sashimi, menu items include sushi, corn cheese, fried shrimp, udon, and mini roe rice.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delights: Ssadagu Basic · Premium Tuna / Family Sashimi Set / Salmon Sushi, etc.
paragraphs: Chamchi Ssadagu Dongchun Branch is a tuna specialty restaurant located on the second floor of the Dongchun-dong food alley in Yeonsu-gu, Incheon. Focusing on Bluefin tuna (honmaguro) and Bigeye tuna (big eye), they offer various cuts including medium fatty belly, large fatty belly, and belly button meat. The restaurant features private rooms and group seating, making it ideal for family meals, company dinners, and group gatherings. Along with the signature tuna sashimi, menu items include sushi, corn cheese, fried shrimp, udon, and mini roe rice.

Children's menu items such as egg sushi, salmon sushi, kids' pork cutlet, and snow crab ramen are also available. Preschoolers are free of charge, elementary school students are 50% of the adult rate, and adult rates apply from middle schoolers onward. Parking support for up to 2 hours at a nearby public parking tower is provided when driving. Reservations and takeout are available.

en.title: Cafe Halmi
en.overview: Cafe Halmi is a specialty drip coffee roastery cafe located in Daebunam-dong, Danwon-gu, Ansan-si, Gyeonggi-do. Situated right across from Halmiseom Island on Course 4 of Daebu Haesolgil Trail, it is close to Veradel Equestrian Club and Glass Island Museum. Run by a certified Q Grader, green coffee beans are carefully selected and roasted directly in-house. The signature menu is specialty drip coffee brewed from freshly roasted beans.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delights: 7 Specialty Drip Coffees · Cafe au Lait / Hibiscus Ade / Blueberry Muffin, etc.
paragraphs: Cafe Halmi is a specialty drip coffee roastery cafe located in Daebunam-dong, Danwon-gu, Ansan-si, Gyeonggi-do. Situated right across from Halmiseom Island on Course 4 of Daebu Haesolgil Trail, it is close to Veradel Equestrian Club and Glass Island Museum. Run by a certified Q Grader, green coffee beans are carefully selected and roasted directly in-house. The signature menu is specialty drip coffee brewed from freshly roasted beans.

It offers single-origin coffees highlighting regional characteristics, house blends mixed in-house, and decaf drip coffee. Takeout is available. The red brick exterior building has a multi-level structure with seating on both the 1st and 2nd floors. The 1st-floor window seats offer views of the Daebudo rural village scenery, while the 2nd floor displays vintage manual coffee grinders. It is a great stop while walking Daebu Haesolgil Trail Course 4 or exploring nearby attractions, and the property has parking space for about 15 cars.

en.title: Cafe Meomureu
en.overview: Beautiful garden landscaping and relaxing outdoor seating blend together to offer a tranquil break. Located near Geumeunmorae Riverside Park, Cafe Meomureu is a large cafe with a grand scale and comfortable indoor and outdoor spaces, making it a great spot for family outing visitors. The 1st floor features seating with fresh scenery outside the window and an ordering area, while the 2nd floor has widely spaced seating for a comfortable and uncrowded stay. The signature drink is Yeoju Rice Smoothie made with local Yeoju specialties, topped with crispy nurungji (crispy scorched rice) snacks for a nutty flavor and subtle sweetness.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delights: Yeoju Rice Smoothie · Lemon Salt Bread / Einspänner / Valrhona Chocolate Latte, etc.
paragraphs: Beautiful garden landscaping and relaxing outdoor seating blend together to offer a tranquil break. Located near Geumeunmorae Riverside Park, Cafe Meomureu is a large cafe with a grand scale and comfortable indoor and outdoor spaces, making it a great spot for family outing visitors. The 1st floor features seating with fresh scenery outside the window and an ordering area, while the 2nd floor has widely spaced seating for a comfortable and uncrowded stay.

The signature drink is Yeoju Rice Smoothie made with local Yeoju specialties, topped with crispy nurungji (crispy scorched rice) snacks for a nutty flavor and subtle sweetness. Lemon salt bread, which harmonizes fragrant lemon scent and saltiness within a savory butter flavor, is also a popular menu item. Coffee can be chosen from three bean options including decaf, and you can also enjoy Einspänner, Valrhona Chocolate Latte, and neatly arranged breads and cakes on display. Take a moment to enjoy regional desserts and a cup of aromatic coffee while looking out at the garden.

en.title: Bontodaega
en.overview: Located near Goseong-gun Office in Gyeongsangnam-do, Bontodaega specializes in soy sauce-marinated crab (ganjang gejang). They serve set menus featuring ganjang gejang, soy sauce-marinated scallops, abalone, and shrimp. Aged with low sodium, you can enjoy it without feeling overly salty even when pairing a spoonful of soy sauce with rice. Seafood soybean paste stew, steamed eggs, and stone-pot rice are served alongside; simply mix the freshly cooked rice with the soy sauce and add seaweed flakes, sesame oil, and wasabi to taste.
en.pull_quote: Featured Menu: Ganjang Gejang Set · Marinated Shrimp Set / Marinated Abalone Set / Marinated Scallop Set, etc.
paragraphs: Located near Goseong-gun Office in Gyeongsangnam-do, Bontodaega specializes in soy sauce-marinated crab (ganjang gejang). Aged with low sodium, you can enjoy it without feeling overly salty even when pairing a spoonful of soy sauce with rice.

Seafood soybean paste stew, steamed eggs, and stone-pot rice are served alongside; simply mix the freshly cooked rice with the soy sauce and add seaweed flakes, sesame oil, and wasabi to taste. en.title: Sancheong and Hamyang Incident Memorial Park
en.overview: The Sancheong and Hamyang Incident Memorial Park is a joint graveyard for the victims of the Sancheong-Hamyang civilian massacre. On February 7, 1951, during the Korean War, the 3rd Battalion, 9th Regiment, 11th Division of the South Korean Army massacred 705 innocent civilians in Gahyeon and Banggok villages in Geumseo-myeon, Sancheong-gun, and Jeomchon village in Hyucheon-myeon and Seoju village in Yurim-myeon, Hamyang-gun, while carrying out the Jirisan communist-suppression operation known as 'Gyeonbyeokcheongya'. This park enshrines the spirits of those unjustly sacrificed.
en.pull_quote: The Sancheong and Hamyang Incident Memorial Park is a joint graveyard for the victims of the Sancheong-Hamyang civilian massacre. On February 7, 1951, during the Korean War, the 3rd Battalion...
paragraphs: The Sancheong and Hamyang Incident Memorial Park is a joint graveyard for the victims of the Sancheong-Hamyang civilian massacre. On February 7, 1951, during the Korean War, the 3rd Battalion, 9th Regiment, 11th Division of the South Korean Army massacred 705 innocent civilians in Gahyeon and Banggok villages in Geumseo-myeon, Sancheong-gun, and Jeomchon village in Hyucheon-myeon and Seoju village in Yurim-myeon, Hamyang-gun, while carrying out the Jirisan communist-suppression operation known as 'Gyeonbyeokcheongya'. This park enshrines the spirits of those unjustly sacrificed.

The creation of the joint graveyard and the erection of the memorial tower were realized following the promulgation of the Special Act on Restoring the Reputation of Persons Related to the Incident on January 5, 1996, and the determination of the deceased and bereaved families by the Geochang Incident and Other Related Persons Reputation Restoration Deliberation Committee on February 17, 1998. Following the groundbreaking of the joint graveyard project on December 13, 2001, construction was completed over four years. This graveyard serves as a living educational site where visitors can reaffirm with a solemn heart that under any circumstances, the people are like the sky, history is on the side of justice, and human life has absolute value, while reflecting on the precious values of true peace and human rights left to our descendants by the sacrificed spirits.

ja.title: 山清・咸陽事件追悼公園
ja.region_label: 慶尚南道 山청郡 金西面
ja.addr: 慶尚南道 山청郡 金西面 花渓五峰路 530
ja.overview: 山清・咸陽事件追悼公園は、山清・咸陽事件の犠牲者合同墓地です。朝鮮戦争真っ只中の1951年2月7日、国軍第11師団第9連隊第3大隊が智異山（チリサン）のパルチザン討伐作戦である「堅壁清野」を遂行する過程で、山清郡金西面のガーヒョン、パンゴク村と、咸陽郡休川面のチョムチョン村、楡林面のソジュ村の無辜の民間人705名を虐殺した事件で、この時に理不尽に犠牲となった御霊を祀る墓地です。
ja.pull_quote: 山清・咸陽事件追悼公園は、山清・咸陽事件の犠牲者合同墓地です。朝鮮戦争真っ只中の1951年2月7日、国軍第11師団第9連隊第3大隊が智異山のパルチザン討伐作戦である…
paragraphs: 山清・咸陽事件追悼公園は、山清・咸陽事件の犠牲者合同墓地です。朝鮮戦争真っ只中の1951年2月7日、国軍第11師団第9連隊第3大隊が智異山（チリサン）のパルチザン討伐作戦である「堅壁清野」を遂行する過程で、山清郡金西面のガーヒョン、パンゴク村と、咸陽郡休川面のチョムチョン村、楡林面のソジュ村の無辜の民間人705名を虐殺した事件で、この時に理不尽に犠牲となった御霊を祀る墓地です。

合同墓地の造成と慰霊塔の建立は、1996年1月5日の事件等関連者の名誉回復に関する特別措置法公布と、1998年2月17日の居昌事件等関連者名誉回復審議委員会による死亡者及び遺族の決定によって行われたもので、2001年12月13日の合同墓地造成事業着工以来、4年にわたる工事を経て竣工に至りました。この墓地では、いかなる場合でも国民は天のようであり、歴史は正義の側にあり、人命は絶対的な価値を持つことを厳粛な心で確認しつつ、犠牲となった御霊が私たちの子孫に残してくれた真の平和と人権の貴重な価値を噛みしめる生きた歴史教育の場となるでしょう。

zh.title: 山清·咸陽事件追悼公園

zh.overview: 山清·咸陽事件追悼公園是山清·咸陽事件犧牲者的聯合墓園。韓戰期間的1951年2月7日，南韓陸軍第11師團第9連隊第3大隊在執行智異山游擊隊討伐作戰「堅壁清野」時，在山清郡金西面佳峴村、防谷村與咸陽郡休川面店村、俞林面西柱村屠殺了705名無辜平民，此墓園即是用來安撫當時含冤犧牲的英靈。

聯合墓園的建立與慰靈塔的修建，是根據1996年1月5日公佈的「有關恢復事件相關人員名譽之特別措置法」，以及1998年2月17日居昌事件等相關人員名譽恢復審議委員會對死者及遺屬的認定而推動的。自2001年12月13日聯合墓園造鎮工程動工以來，經過長達4年的施工終於竣工。在這個墓園中，我們將以莊敬的心情再次確認：無論在任何情況下，人民重於蒼天、歷史站在正義的一方、人命具有絕對價值，並藉此省思犧牲英靈留給後代子孫之真理和平與人權的寶貴價值，成為一處活生生的歷史教育場域。

en.title: Hwangmaesan Mountain (Sancheong)
en.overview: Hwangmaesan Mountain, the final major peak of the Taebaek Mountain Range, is known as the place where the Goryeo Dynasty's national guardian monk Muhak practiced asceticism. Together with nearby Hwangmaebong Peak, its southeastern side features bizarre rock cliffs, making it as beautiful as a 'mini Geumgangsan.' Upon reaching the summit, the surrounding scenery resembles fully bloomed plum blossom petals, giving a mystical feeling as if floating alone inside a plum blossom, hence the name Hwangmaesan.

Upon reaching the summit, the surrounding scenery resembles fully bloomed plum blossom petals, giving a mystical feeling as if floating alone inside a plum blossom, hence the name Hwangmaesan.

The 'Hwang' (黃) in Hwangmaesan means wealth, and 'Mae' (梅) means nobility, symbolizing overall abundance. It is also said that if anyone prays with utmost sincerity, one wish will surely come true. In particular, May is famous for the stunning bright red royal azaleas spreading across hundreds of thousands of pyeong of highland.

en.title: Baegundong Valley (Sancheong)
en.overview: Among the foothills of Jirisan Mountain, Baegundong Valley retains the deepest traces of Nammyeong Jo Sik. Inscriptions left by Nammyeong, such as Baegundong (白雲洞), Yongmundongcheon (龍門洞천), Yeongnamjeilcheonseok (嶺南第一泉石), and Nammyeongseonsaengjangjiso (南冥先生杖之所), are carved into the rocks. It is also the actual site where he composed the verse: 'Climbing the green mountain, the whole world is like indigo, yet human greed knows no bounds, covetous of worldly affairs even while viewing the beautiful scenery.'
en.pull_quote: Among the foothills of Jirisan Mountain, Baegundong Valley retains the deepest traces of Nammyeong Jo Sik.
paragraphs: Among the foothills of Jirisan Mountain, Baegundong Valley retains the deepest traces of Nammyeong Jo Sik.

Inscriptions left by Nammyeong, such as Baegundong (白雲洞), Yongmundongcheon (龍門洞天), Yeongnamjeilcheonseok (嶺南第一泉石), and Nammyeongseonsaengjangjiso (南冥先生杖之所), are carved into the rocks. It is also the actual site where he composed the verse: 'Climbing the green mountain, the whole world is like indigo, yet human greed knows no bounds, covetous of worldly affairs even while viewing the beautiful scenery.' Despite the court's calls, he never entered official government service throughout his life, instead living in seclusion in the foothills of Jirisan and teaching many disciples. True to being the great teacher who produced the most righteous army leaders when the Imjin War broke out, he left writings in Baegundong Valley that embody the true character of a scholar living in seclusion (sallim cheosa), who immersed himself in scholarship while gazing at the beauty of nature rather than worldly greed.

en.title: Jirisan National Park (Sancheong)
en.overview: Designated as South Korea's national park on December 29, 1967, Jirisan Mountain spans administrative districts across three provinces and is the largest mountainous national park in the country. Literally translated, Jirisan (智異山) means 'Mountain of Wise Extraordinary Beings.' Perhaps for this reason, more hermits have cultivated and practiced asceticism here than on any other mountain, and the number of hermits deeply hidden in the valleys of Jirisan is said to be uncountable.
en.pull_quote: Designated as South Korea's national park on December 29, 1967, Jirisan Mountain spans administrative districts across three provinces and is the largest mountainous national park in the country...
paragraphs: Designated as South Korea's national park on December 29, 1967, Jirisan Mountain spans administrative districts across three provinces and is the largest mountainous national park in the country. Literally translated, Jirisan (智異山) means 'Mountain of Wise Extraordinary Beings.' Perhaps for this reason, more hermits have cultivated and practiced asceticism here than on any other mountain, and the number of hermits deeply hidden in the valleys of Jirisan is said to be uncountable.

Since ancient times, Jirisan has been revered alongside Geumgangsan and Hallasan as one of the Three Spirit Mountains (Samsin-san), serving as a spiritual sanctuary of national faith. At Cheonwangbong, the main peak of Jirisan, a shrine called Seongmosa was built and a stone statue of the Holy Mother was enshrined, while at Nogo-dan, Namaksa Shrine has worshiped the Seongdo Holy Mother since the Silla Dynasty. Names like Banyabong, Jongsakdae, Yeongshindae, and Nogodan also symbolize this faith. In Gyeongsangnam-do, it extends across Hadong, Hamyang, and Sancheong, and its rich flora and fauna have shaped a diverse yet distinct cultural sphere between the east and west.

paragraphs: 1967年12月29日に韓国の国立公園に指定された智異山（チリサン）は、3つの道の市・郡・面の行政区域にまたがり、国立公園の中で最も広い面積を誇る山岳型国立公園です。「智異山」を文字通り解釈すると「知恵ある異人の山」となります。そのためか、智異山は他のどの山よりも多くの隠者たちが道徳を磨いて修行に励み、智異山の谷間に深く身を隠した隠者の数は推測もつかないほどだったと言われています。

智異山は古くから金剛山、漢拏山とともに三神山の一つとして民族的崇敬を受けてきた民族信仰の霊地です。智異山の霊峰である天王峰（チョンファンボン）には聖母祠という祠が建てられて聖母石像が奉安され、老姑団（ノゴダン）には新羅時代から先導聖母を祀る南岳社がありました。般若峰、鍾石台、霊信台、老姑団といった名前も信仰を象徴しています。慶尚南道では河東、咸陽、山清にまたがっており、智異山の豊かな動植物と同様に、その文化は東西間を異質でありながらも多様な文化圏に作り上げました。

en.title: Tomb of King Guhyeong, Sancheong
en.overview: This stone tomb is known to be the burial site of King Guhyeong, the 10th and final ruler of Geumgwan Gaya. King Guhyeong was the great-grandfather of General Kim Yu-sin. He became king of Garakguk (Gaya) in 521 and reigned for 11 years until surrendering his territory to King Beopheung of Silla in 532. There are two theories regarding this mound: one is that it is a stone pagoda, and the other is that it is a royal tomb. The theory of it being a pagoda is based on similar structures distributed in the Andong and Uiseong regions, while the evidence supporting it as a royal tomb comes from records in the 'Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam' (Augmented Survey of the Geography of Korea).

paragraphs: This stone tomb is known to be the burial site of King Guhyeong, the 10th and final ruler of Geumgwan Gaya. King Guhyeong was the great-grandfather of General Kim Yu-sin. He became king of Garakguk (Gaya) in 521 and reigned for 11 years until surrendering his territory to King Beopheung of Silla in 532. There are two theories regarding this mound: one is that it is a stone pagoda, and the other is that it is a royal tomb. The theory of it being a pagoda is based on similar structures distributed in the Andong and Uiseong regions, while the evidence supporting it as a royal tomb comes from records in the 'Dongguk Yeoji Seungnam', San-eum-hyeon section, which states that there is a nine-dragon stone formation 40 ri deep in the mountains of the district with tiered steps on all four sides, traditionally passed down as a royal tomb.

The record attaching the royal title to this tomb first appears in 'Wansansimneung-gi' by Hong Eui-yeong, a Joseon Dynasty literati, who stated that because there was a temple called Wangsansa to the west of the tomb, it was recorded as King Guhyeong's tomb in the temple's historical records. Unlike ordinary tombs, it consists of terraced stone tiers built in the middle of a sloped hillside.

en.title: Georim Valley
en.overview: Georim Valley is formed by the convergence of several streams: Georimgol as its main current, Dojanggol originating from Yeonhabong and Chotdaebong peaks along the main ridge of Jirisan Mountain, and Jappajingol originating from Hanbeotsaem spring located on the ridge connecting Seseok Plateau to Samsinbong Peak. Georimgol, whose main current alone stretches for some 60 li, draws so many hikers in spring when royal azaleas bloom that the sound of the flowing valley water is drowned out.

Georimgol, whose main current alone stretches for some 60 li, draws so many hikers in spring when royal azaleas bloom that the sound of the flowing valley water is drowned out.

The only drawback is that access is not easy; to reach the valley, you must walk for a while past the Georim Village ticket office, and the path is so hidden that it is not even marked on Jirisan hiking maps, so it is safest to go with an experienced companion. Nearby tourist attractions include a Trick Art Experience Center and the Jirisan Partisan Suppression Exhibition Hall.

その逆もまた良しです。カフェ・ムクシルのユニークなメニューは、手作りの冷出しミルクティーをごま油の瓶に入れて提供する「ムクシルごま油瓶ミルクティー」です。量もたっぷり入っています。その他にも、フラワーティーセットやフルーツティーなど、様々なメニューが用意されています。

paragraphs: Naeri Sikdang is a Korean restaurant located in Naeri, Sancheong-gun, easily accessible just past Naerigyo Bridge along the Sucheol-to-Seongsimwon section of the Jirisan Dulle-gil trail. Side dishes like braised tofu, stir-fried fish cakes, seasoned seaweed, kimchi, pickled cucumbers, stuffed cucumbers, and anchovies are clean and fresh, with their homemade onion kimchi being especially popular. The interior is neat and spacious.

With small private rooms available, group dining is also possible. A dedicated parking lot makes parking very convenient.

en.pull_quote: Among the scenic 'Anui Samdong', Haryimdong Valley preserves the most splendid natural beauty. Traveling about 4 km from Anui...
paragraphs: Among the scenic 'Anui Samdong' (Three Scenic Areas of Anui), Haryimdong Valley preserves the most splendid natural beauty. Traveling about 4 km from Anui along National Route 26 toward Jangsu-gun, Jeollabuk-do, you will find a charming village by the winding waters where Nongwoljeong Pavilion, the pinnacle of Haryimdong Valley, stands. Haryimdong Valley is formed by the Geumcheon River originating from Namdeokyusan Mountain winding its way to create 8 pools and 8 pavilions,

and has long been hailed as a treasure trove of pavilion culture. Four classic pavilions including Nongwoljeong still remain. In particular, Nongwoljeong embodies the romantic scholarly spirit of our ancestors who 'played while teasing the moon,' making it a must-visit spot for poets and literati visiting Hamyang. With tourist amenities fully established since 1993, overnight stays like camping and guesthouses are hassle-free. The campground is built on sandy soil with excellent drainage even in rain, making camping in a tent on a rainy day a uniquely atmospheric experience. Originally destroyed by fire in 2003, Nongwoljeong has been newly restored.

paragraphs: Gibaiksan Yongchu Valley was historically known as 'Anui Samdong' for its three outstanding scenic locations in Anui-hyeon. Yongchu Valley, one of the three, is also called 'Simjindong,' meaning a place where one fell into deep meditative trances due to the beauty of the deep valley. At the entrance of Yongchu Valley stands Simwonjeong Pavilion, the essence of Simjindong, offering a panoramic view of Cheongshindam Pool—said to clear the mind—and layered granite formations. Walking about 3 km past Simwonjeong, the solitary Jogyesun Gate (Iljumun) of Jangusa Temple rises behind a spacious parking lot.

Jangusa Temple, founded by Master Gakyeon during the 9th year of King Soji of Silla, was destroyed during the Korean War, leaving only the Iljumun gate un-restored. Continuing slightly uphill brings you to Yongchusa Temple, in front of which roars Yongchu Waterfall with thunderous water sounds. At the end of Yongchu Valley lies Yongchu Natural Recreation Forest established by Hamyang-gun, featuring cozy mountain cabins, a spacious parking lot, a water play area, and an observatory, along with hiking trails leading up Gibaiksan and Hwangseoksan mountains, ridges of Namdeokyusan Mountain.

en.pull_quote: Deep and wide in the northern part of Mt. Jirisan, Hansin Valley is a stunning valley renowned for its rugged yet magnificent natural scenery...
paragraphs: Deep and wide in the northern part of Mt. Jirisan, Hansin Valley is a stunning valley renowned for its rugged yet magnificent natural scenery stretching from Baekmudong in Macheon-myeon, Hamyang-gun to Seseok Plateau. Hansin Valley holds as many stories as its countless waterfalls.

One origin of its name signifies a deep and wide valley ('Hansin'), while another suggests it is called Hansin because visitors feel a chill in their bodies even in midsummer. The starting point for climbing Hansin Valley is Baekmudong, from where visitors can easily hike past the campsite along a wide path up to Cheotnaduri Waterfall. The 2 km section from Baekmudong to Cheotnaduri Waterfall features a flat footpath flanked by the valley and cliffs, forming a lush forest tunnel that blends with the echoing sound of the valley stream, creating a fantastic hiking course.

en.title: Palgongsan National Park (Eunhaesa District)
en.overview: Palgongsan Mountain was designated as a provincial park on May 13, 1980, and later as a national park on December 31, 2023. Spanning across five cities and counties including Dong-gu and Gunwi-gun in Daegu, as well as Gyeongsan-si, Yeong천-si, and Chilgok-gun in Gyeongsangbuk-do, the national park covers a total area of 126.058 ㎢. Palgongsan is a core high-altitude ecological axis in the Yeongnam region where the Palgongjicheon and Yubongjicheon ridges diverge from the Nakdong Jeongmaek.
en.pull_quote: Palgongsan was designated as a provincial park on May 13, 1980, and as a national park on December 31, 2023. Spanning Daegu, Gunwi-gun, Gyeongsan-si, Yeongcheon-si...
paragraphs: Palgongsan Mountain was designated as a provincial park on May 13, 1980, and later as a national park on December 31, 2023. Spanning across five cities and counties including Dong-gu and Gunwi-gun in Daegu, as well as Gyeongsan-si, Yeongcheon-si, and Chilgok-gun in Gyeongsangbuk-do, the national park covers a total area of 126.058 ㎢. Palgongsan is a core high-altitude ecological axis in the Yeongnam region standing at 1,192.8 meters above sea level, composed of majestic, folding screen-like granite peaks.

Centered around the main peak Birobong (1,192.8m), Dongbong Peak (1,167m) and Seobong Peak (1,153m) stand shoulder to shoulder, enclosing the northern side of the Daegu Basin in the center of the Yeongnam region like a folding screen. Home to dozens of temples and hermitages including the millennium-old Donghwasa Temple, the lush forests and multi-branched valleys feature delicate azaleas in early spring, royal azaleas in late spring, chaste trees in summer, and brilliant autumn foliage, alongside mystical winter snowscapes. The Eunhaesa District is located in Yeongcheon-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and houses Eunhaesa Temple.

en.title: Imgo Seowon Confucian Academy
en.overview: Imgo Seowon is a Confucian academy originally founded in 1553 in Gocheon-dong, Imgo-myeon, by local Confucian scholars to honor the virtue and loyalty of Jeong Mong-ju. It received royal naming [Imgo] in 1554. Destroyed during the Japanese Invasions of Korea, it was relocated to its current site in 1603 and received royal naming again the following year. It played a significant role in enshrining sages and educating local youth by additionally enshrining Jang Hyeon-gwang in 1643 and Hwang Bo-in in 1787, before being dismantled in 1871.
en.pull_quote: Imgo Seowon was founded in 1553 by local scholars to honor the loyalty of Jeong Mong-ju. It received royal naming in 1554, was destroyed during the Imjin War...
paragraphs: Imgo Seowon is a Confucian academy originally founded in 1553 in Gocheon-dong, Imgo-myeon, by local Confucian scholars to honor the virtue and loyalty of Jeong Mong-ju. It received royal naming [Imgo] in 1554. Destroyed during the Japanese Invasions of Korea, it was relocated to its current site in 1603 and received royal naming again the following year. It played a significant role in enshrining sages and educating local youth by additionally enshrining Jang Hyeon-gwang in 1643 and Hwang Bo-in in 1787, before being dismantled in 1871. In 1919, the Junyeonggak Pavilion was built to enshrine Jeong Mong-ju's portrait and hold ancestral rites.

Within the grounds are a shrine, a portrait pavilion (Junyeonggak), a lecture hall, a kitchen, and administrative rooms. The Mutchungsa Shrine houses Jeong Mong-ju's spirit tablet, while Junyeonggak preserves his portrait. The lecture hall consists of a central wooden floor and flanking rooms, used for various academy events, scholar gatherings, and scholarly lectures. Relics preserved in the academy include three sets of Jeong Mong-ju's portraits, 113 woodblocks of the Poeun Collection, 71 woodblocks of Jibong Yuseol, the Poeun Collection, 11 volumes of Eosa Seongri Gunseo, and over 200 other historical books.

paragraphs: 臨皐書院は1553年、地元の儒林の公議により鄭夢周の徳行と忠節をたたえるため臨皐面高川洞に創建された書院である。1554年に「臨皐」と額を賜り、文禄・慶長の役の際に焼失したが、1603年に現在の位置に移転し、翌年に再び額を賜った。1643年に張顕光と1787年に黄ボ・インを追加配香し、先賢の配香と地方教育の一翼を担ってきたが、1871年に毀撤され、1919年に尊英閣を建立して鄭夢周の影政（肖像画）を祀り、祭祀を行ってきた。

境内には祠堂、尊英閣、講堂、厨房、有司室などがあり、祠堂の文忠祠には鄭夢周の位牌が奉安され、尊英閣には影政が所蔵されている。講堂は中央の板の間と両側の脇室からなり、院内の様々な行事や儒林の会合、学問講論の場として使用されている。書院内に所蔵されている遺物には、鄭夢周の影政3幅をはじめ、『圃隠文集』木板113版、『芝峰類説』木板71版、『圃隠集』、『御사성리군서』11巻のほか約200余巻の書籍が収蔵されている。

en.title: Chisan Valley
en.overview: Chisan Valley is a picturesque tourist destination that retains its pristine, untouched natural beauty. Formed by streams flowing north from the ridges of Mount Palgongsan, it is the deepest and widest valley in the mountain range. It is a popular summer water-play spot for Yeongcheon citizens. Next to the stream, flat wooden platforms (pyeongsang) provided free of charge by Yeongcheon City are installed. Additionally, the Chisan Tourist Campground is located nearby, making it very popular among family tourists.

en.title: Yeongcheon Joyanggak Pavilion
en.overview: Standing tall on the northern bank of the Yeongcheon River, Joyanggak Pavilion was built in 1368 (the 17th year of King Gongmin of Goryeo) through the joint efforts of the then-magistrate Lee Yong and local Confucian scholars. Together with Yeongnamnu Pavilion in Miryang and Chokseoknu Pavilion in Jinju, it is called one of the three great pavilions of the Yeongnam region. Also known as Myeongwonru or Seoseru, it originally had several surrounding buildings such as Cheongnyangdang and Ssangcheongdang to its left and right, but all were burned down during the Japanese Invasions of Korea.
en.pull_quote: Joyanggak Pavilion, soaring on the northern bank of the Yeongcheon River, was built in 1368 by magistrate Lee Yong and local scholars. Along with Yeongnamnu and Chokseoknu...
paragraphs: Standing tall on the northern bank of the Yeongcheon River, Joyanggak Pavilion was built in 1368 (the 17th year of King Gongmin of Goryeo) through the joint efforts of the then-magistrate Lee Yong and local Confucian scholars. Together with Yeongnamnu Pavilion in Miryang and Chokseoknu Pavilion in Jinju, it is called one of the three great pavilions of the Yeongnam region.

Also known as Myeongwonru or Seoseru, it originally had several surrounding buildings such as Cheongnyangdang and Ssangcheongdang to its left and right, but all were burned down during the Japanese Invasions of Korea. The 5-bay front and 3-bay side Joyanggak features about 80 hanging boards inscribed with verses by numerous famous sages and romantic poets who passed through this region. The grounds also house monuments such as the Sannam Righteous Army Monument, the Yeongcheon Campaign Victory Monument, Baek Sin-ae's Literary Monument, and the 'Hwaseong Old Ruins' Song Monument.

paragraphs: 永川川の北側の丘の上にそびえ立つ朝陽閣は、高麗の恭民王17年（1368）に当時の府使であった李用と地元の儒林が力を合わせて建てた建物であり、密陽の嶺南楼、晋ジュの触石楼とともに「嶺南の三大楼」の一つに数えられる。
明元楼あるいは西世楼とも呼ばれ、もともとは朝陽閣を中心に左右に清涼堂や双清堂など複数の建物があったが、文禄・慶長の役の際にすべて焼失した。正面5間、側面3間の朝陽閣には、この地方を通り過ぎた数々の名賢や風流客らの詩句が彫られた80余りの扁額が掲げられており、境内には山南義陣碑や永川地区戦勝碑、白信愛文学碑や『皇城昔の地』歌碑などの記念物がある。

en.title: Dolhalmae (Grandma Stone, Yeongcheon)
en.overview: Dolhalmae Park in Bukan-myeon, Yeongcheon features a mineral spring, a Buddha statue, a Dolhalmae (Grandma Stone) statue, the 12 zodiac animal statues, and a stone building housing the actual Grandma Stone. Dolhalmae is a granite stone weighing about 10 kg and measuring 25 cm in diameter used for divination. According to tradition, when you lift the stone with both hands, if it feels light your wish will not come true, but if it refuses to budge, your wish will come true—meaning it gives a yes-or-no answer to your prayers.

paragraphs: Dolhalmae Park in Bukan-myeon, Yeongcheon features a mineral spring, a Buddha statue, a Dolhalmae (Grandma Stone) statue, the 12 zodiac animal statues, and a stone building housing the actual Grandma Stone. Dolhalmae is a granite stone weighing about 10 kg and measuring 25 cm in diameter used for divination. According to tradition, when you lift the stone with both hands, if it feels light your wish will not come true, but if it refuses to budge, your wish will come true—meaning it gives a yes-or-no answer to your prayers. What makes this stone a subject of fascination is not necessarily any mystical prophetic power, but the fact that the stone feels light or heavy depending on the person and their earnest wishes.

The proper way to lift the stone is to first lift it without any specific thoughts, serving as a process to verify that it lifts easily without sincerity. Next, you state your date of birth, address, age, and name, and speak of your wish or trouble, after which whether the stone lifts or not indicates the answer. For about 350 years, local villagers have visited this stone to hold ancestral rites whenever fortunes or misfortunes arose, or when epidemics and tragedies struck the village.

paragraphs: 永川市北安面のトルハルメ公園には、薬水、仏像、トルハルメ銅像、12支の動物像、そしてトルハルメを祀る石造りの建物がある。トルハルメは重さ約10kg、直径25cmの花崗岩で、持ち上げながら自分の運勢を占うものである。両手で石を持ち上げるとき、石を持ち上げられれば自分の願いは叶わず、石が微動だにしなければ願いが叶うという。すなわち、願い事に対して可否の判定を下してくれるというものである。この石が話題を集めているのは、その予言能力の神秘性というよりも、人によって、あるいは願い事によって石が持ち上がったり持ち上がらなかったりするからである。

石を持ち上げるコツは、最初は何も考えずに持ち上げてみることである。真心がないと簡単に持ち上がることを自分で確認する手順である。次に、自分の生年月日、住所、年齢、氏名などを告げ、願い事や悩み事を話すと、石を持ち上げられるかどうかによってその可否を教えてくれるという。この村の住民たちは約350年の間、吉凶禍福があるたびにこの石を訪れて祭祀を行ってきた。また、村に伝染病が流行ったり不幸な出来事が起きた時にも同様にしてきた。
