zh.overview: 永川北安面石奶奶公園內有藥水、佛像、石奶奶銅像、12生肖銅像，以及供奉石奶奶的石造建築。石奶奶是一塊重約10公斤、直徑25公分的花崗岩，人們透過抬起它來占卜自己的運勢。據說用雙手試著將石頭抬起時，如果石頭被輕易抬起代表心願無法實現，若石頭紋絲不動則代表心願會實現，也就是說它會針對心中的祈願給予是否可行的答覆。
zh.pull_quote: 永川北安面石奶奶公園內設有藥水、佛像、石奶奶銅像與生肖像，以及供奉石奶奶的石造建築。石奶奶是一塊重約10公斤的花崗岩...
paragraphs: 永川北安面石奶奶公園內有藥水、佛像、石奶奶銅像、12生肖銅像，以及供奉石奶奶的石造建築。石奶奶是一塊重約10公斤、直徑25公分的花崗岩，人們透過抬起它來占卜自己的運勢。據說用雙手試著將石頭抬起時，如果石頭被輕易抬起代表心願無法實現，若石頭紋絲不動則代表心願會實現，也就是說它會針對心中的祈願給予是否可行的答覆。這塊石頭之所以引起話題，與其說是由於預言能力的神秘與否，不如說是因為根據不同的人或不同的祈願內容，石頭有時提得動、有時提不動。
抬石頭的要領是首先什麼都不想地試著抬抬看，這是用來確認如果沒有誠心就會輕易被抬起來的步驟。接下來報上自己的生辰八字、地址、年齡與姓名等，並說出自己的願望或難題，然後透過石頭是否抬得動來告知結果。大約350年來，當地村民每逢村裡有吉凶禍福時都會來此祭拜，此外若村內爆發傳染病或發生不幸喪事時也會前來祈求。

en.title: Manbulsa Temple (Yeongcheon)
en.overview: Manbulsa Temple in Yeongcheon began when the monk Hakseong established propagation centers in Seoul, Busan, and Daegu in 1987 to fulfill a modern Buddhist vow distinct from the past, culminating in the completion of Manbulsan Mountain temple in 1995. Prior to its establishment, he carried out numerous grand Buddhist projects such as building the Manbulbojeon Hall, transferring the Buddha's true sarira (sacred relics), and enshrinement of an outdoor standing Amitabha Buddha, pouring immense effort into spreading modern Buddhism alongside culture, medical care, and welfare.
en.pull_quote: Manbulsa Temple in Yeongcheon was founded by monk Hakseong, beginning with propagation centers in 1987 and completed in 1995 on Manbulsan Mountain...
paragraphs: Manbulsa Temple in Yeongcheon began when the monk Hakseong established propagation centers in Seoul, Busan, and Daegu in 1987 to fulfill a modern Buddhist vow distinct from the past, culminating in the completion of Manbulsan Mountain temple in 1995. Prior to its establishment, he carried out numerous grand Buddhist projects such as building the Manbulbojeon Hall, transferring the Buddha's true sarira (sacred relics), and enshrinement of an outdoor standing Amitabha Buddha, pouring immense effort into spreading modern Buddhism alongside culture, medical care, and welfare.

Relics preserved here include the Amitabha Buddha, the Samjonbul (Triad Buddha) which is the largest indoor Jeonbul (statue-filled hall) in Korea, 5 grains of the Buddha's true sarira brought from Sri Lanka, and a Bodhi tree. In addition, there are the Yeongcheon Amitabha Great Buddha, stupas, a brass reclining Nirvana statue, the Great Bronze Manbul Peace Bell, the Indung Pagoda, Manbulbojeon Hall, Gwaneumjeon Hall, Daeungjeon Hall, the Beopseongge Dharma Wheel, the Medicine Buddha (Sujeong Yurigwang Yeoraebul), lucky pouches, and ancestral spirit tablets (Yuja Yeongga).

en.title: Pohang Halmaejip
en.addr: Yeongcheon Public Market, 52, Sijang 4-gil, Yeongcheon-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do
en.overview: Located in the Yeongcheon Gomtang Alley in Wansan-dong, Yeongcheon-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Pohang Halmaejip is a traditional gomtang (beef bone soup) restaurant spanning three generations. It has been featured on various broadcast programs including KBS 1TV's 'ometown Report'. Their signature menu is somuk-gomtang (beef head soup), where rice is scalded with hot broth in an earthenware pot (toeryeom). The soup, simmered for a long time with various cuts such as head meat, cheek meat, beef ribs, and honeycomb tripe, is both clear and deeply flavorful.
en.pull_quote: Signature Delicacies: Somuk-gomtang · Doganitang / Yang-gomtang / Hanwoo Somuk-gomtang / Beef Assorted Suyuk, etc.
paragraphs: Located in the Yeongcheon Gomtang Alley in Wansan-dong, Yeongcheon-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do, Pohang Halmaejip is a traditional gomtang (beef bone soup) restaurant spanning three generations. It has been featured on various broadcast programs including KBS 1TV's 'ometown Report'.

Their signature menu is somuk-gomtang (beef head soup), where rice is scalded with hot broth in an earthenware pot (toeryeom). The soup, simmered for a long time with various cuts such as head meat, cheek meat, beef ribs, and honeycomb tripe, is both clear and deeply flavorful. You can also enjoy various other menu items such as pork gomtang, offal soup (naejangtang), and tripe gomtang. With great accessibility close to East Yeongcheon IC, the nearby Yeongcheon Public Market Food Market makes it a wonderful place to explore together.

It is also famous for its 'blind date bulletin board' that connected many young couples. en.pull_quote: Signature Delicacy: Legendary Tteokbokki, Seafood Tteokbokki, Budae Tteokbokki, Omerice, etc.
paragraphs: Opened in 1971, Sora in Gongneung-dong is a historic eatery filled with memories for Korea Military Academy cadets, Seoul Women's University students, and national athletes from the Taereung National Training Center. Starting out as the three sisters' 'Sora Hyugesail (Sora Rest Area),' it is now run by the 3rd generation and has been designated a Seoul Future Heritage for its long-standing tradition.

It is also famous for its 'blind date bulletin board' that connected many young couples. Its signature dish, soup tteokbokki, uses malt-barley flour and chili powder instead of gochujang, creating a clear and refreshing broth. Along with the Sora Set—consisting of kimchi fried rice, rabokki, jilpeoni (mushy tteokbokki), and rice balls—it offers student-tailored menus like the Yuksa Set and Barom Set.

en.title: DMZ Market
en.overview: Every Saturday and Sunday, the DMZ Market is held in the Milky Way Bridge parking lot, focusing on local foods produced directly by Cheorwon residents. The variety is truly diverse, including native yam grown in Cheorwon, as well as agricultural products like aralia and balloon flower roots, mulberry ice cream, buckwheat rice cakes, wooden cutting boards, and straw crafts. All these products, sold by about 30 farms, are local specialties that have not undergone long-distance transportation, helping to reduce carbon emissions in one stone.

ja.title: DMZ市場
ja.region_label: 江原道チョルウォン郡東城邑
ja.overview: 毎週土曜日と日曜日には、ミルキーウェイブリッジの駐車場でDMZマーケットが開催され、チェルウォン住民が直接生産した地元食材が中心となっています。品類は本当に多様で、チェルウォン産のヤムイモのほか、アラリアやバルーンフラワーの根、桑の木製アイスクリーム、そばの餅、木製のまな板、わら工芸品などがあります。これらすべては約30の農場で販売されており、長距離輸送を経ていない地元の特産品であり、一気に炭素排出削減に貢献しています。

en.title: Ganseong Traditional Market
en.overview: Goseong Ganseong Traditional Market is a commercial building-style market established in 1965, with market days on the 2nd and 7th of every month. There are four market entrances and exits for easy access. Additionally, thanks to the modern arcade and neatly maintained floors, shopping is pleasant and tidy in a more pleasant and tidy atmosphere. Goseong Ganseong Traditional Market has created a street called the Food Shopping Street. The main foods in the food stall are savory and delicious dishes like ongsimi, buckwheat pancakes, and dorumuk stew.

en.overview: Opened for the first time on May 1, 1994, Farmers' Dawn Market provides consumers with fresh and safe seasonal produce grown directly by farmers, and through a producer real-name system, it provides satisfaction and trust not only to local consumers who wish to purchase products but also to consumers from other regions. It operates annually along the Wonjucheon riverside from April to December, from 04:00~09:00. Next to the shelves stacking crops, the producer's name and contact information are displayed.

en.title: Daejin Port Fish Market
en.overview: Daejin Port is located at the northernmost tip of the East Sea in Daejin-ri, Hyeonnae-myeon, Goseong-gun, Gangwon-do, and is one of the larger fishing ports in the East Sea. Along the coast, there is also a market selling fish caught by the fishermen. Passing through the Daejin Port market and warehouse, there is a fish market selling fresh sashimi. In front of the building, dried seafood is sold, and inside, about ten sashimi restaurants are clustered. You can also scoop sashimi fresh and eat it directly from the second floor. en.title: Yuklim Pass
en.overview: This place was reborn from an alley that once walked a path of decline into a famous spot in Chuncheon. Yuknim Pass was a major commercial district in Chuncheon until the 1980s~1990s, connecting the now-closed 'Yukrim Theater' and Chuncheon Central Market. However, due to new downtown development and relocation of commercial districts, foot traffic stopped and vacant shops increased. In response, Chuncheon City began revitalizing Yuklim Pass in 2015 through the Makgeolli Village specialized street creation project and the Youth Mall project.

en.overview: Located in Gangneung City, Gangwon Province, Jumunjin Fish Market is a traditional market established in 1936 along Jumunjin Port, famous for squid catching. This market is connected with various types of businesses including a general market, dried seafood market, and sashimi center, making it a traditional market popular with domestic and international tourists as well as a East Sea fish market. It handles fresh seafood such as freshly caught squid, mackerel, pollock, saury mackerel, saury crab, and various dried seafood in the East Sea, and is lower than the regular market.

en.title: Sagang Market
en.overview: Sagang Market gets its name ('Sagang', meaning sandy river) from the days when sea tides reached the front of the village, leaving white sandy deposits like a river. It has long served as a crucial transportation hub and distribution center connecting southern regions like Songsan, Daebudo, Yeongheungdo, Suwon, and Ansan. Opened in 1915 with a history of periodic markets held even earlier, it expanded significantly in the 1980s. It is also a historically meaningful site tied to the March 1st Independence Movement in 1919.

en.title: Seorak Nunmegol Market
en.overview: Seorak Nunmegol Market opened as a 5-day periodic market in May 1942, with market days held on the 1st and 6th of every month. In August 2020, the commercial district in the center of Seorak-myeon was registered as a traditional market, making it a place where the past and future coexist. Exciting performances, hands-on experiences, and flea markets are held in the Seorak Nunmegol Market plaza. The main offerings are centered around restaurants, along with butcher shops, hardware stores, and vegetable vendors. Selected as a digital traditional market, it also supports online purchasing, pickup, and package delivery services.

en.overview: Seongnam General Market is located in Sinhung-dong, Sujeong-gu. It is a 5-story above-ground building with a total floor area of 3,233㎡. en.title: Seongnam Central Public Market
en.overview: Seongnam Central Market is a traditional market that naturally developed around 1970 before the official launch of Seongnam City. Originally formed by two adjacent traditional markets, it suffered two fires before being reborn as a modern 7-story building (1 basement floor) spanning 3,519.4㎡ through a traditional market modernization project. It is equipped with multi-functional facilities including stores, refrigerated/frozen storage, parking lots, and various conveniences. Notably, parking spaces from the 3rd to 8th floors keep the area congestion-free.

en.title: Seongho Market
en.overview: Located in Seongnam-dong, Jungwon-gu, Seongnam-si, Seongho Market is known as one of Seongnam's top 3 markets alongside Central Market and Moran Market. Consisting of a single ground floor, Seongho Market operates as a lifestyle-oriented retail market selling jokbal (braised pig trotters), side dishes, fruits, and vegetables. It naturally formed in 1968 by residents who migrated to the Seongnam area before its elevation to a city. Spanning approximately 39,250㎡, it once boasted around 1,000 stores, though the number has now halved.

en.title: Sosa General Market
en.overview: Sosa General Market is a traditional market established around the Sosa-dong area in 1980. Rice stores and barbershops began appearing in the marketplace around 1978, followed by street vendors, centered around which the market took shape. Because it was located in an alley, it was called an alley market or a goblin market. Since the market was situated along a major road, local residents had to pass through it to head to Bucheon Station or catch a bus. With such high foot traffic, it boasts a relatively large commercial district.

en.title: Hwacheon Market
en.overview: Hwacheon Market is a traditional open-air market located in the northernmost part of South Korea. It was established in 1953 after the Korean War by displaced people who could not return to their hometowns in the North. Housed in a steel-framed polycarbonate sheet building, the market features around 100 neatly organized shops. They sell local specialties and agricultural and marine products direct from the clean region of Hwacheon, alongside clothing, miscellaneous goods, and everyday necessities.

ja.overview: 江原道横城郡横城邑一帯で開かれる横城民俗市場は、長い歴史を持つ伝統市場で、かつて「東大門の外で一番の市場」と呼ばれたほど全国的に知られた場所です。1919年4月1日の市場の日には江原地域初の万歳運動が繰り広げられた歴史的な場所でもあり、日本統治時代には地元の商人や住民団結して日本人商人の商圏形成を防いだという意味深い空間として伝えられています。現在も1日と6日に市場が立ちます。

zh.region_label: 江原特別自治道橫城郡橫城邑
zh.overview: 橫城民俗市場在江原道橫城郡橫城邑一帶舉行，是一座歷史悠久的傳統市場，過去曾被稱為「東大門外第一大集市」，在全國享有盛名。這裡也是1919年4月1日集市日當天，江原地區首次爆發萬歲運動的歷史現場；據說在日治時期，當地商人和居民團結一致，阻止了日本商人形成商業區。現在每逢1號和6號仍會舉辦集市。

en.title: Garaebi Market (Ganap Market)
en.overview: Garaebi Market is a traditional 5-day periodic market held on days ending in 4 and 9, retaining the savory and lively atmosphere of a traditional countryside folk market in Yangju, close to Seoul. Also known as Ganap Market because it is located in Ganap-ri, Gwangjeok-myeon, it is a great place for family outings as it operates a large, free public parking lot inside. The market is divided into sections by items such as fish, miscellaneous goods, and vegetables, and also sells various street foods.

en.title: Gapyeong Jatgoeul Traditional Market
en.overview: Gapyeong Jatgoeul Traditional Market opened on July 28, 1923, when merchants gathered along the stream in front of Bonapsan Mountain, making it the oldest traditional market in northern Gyeonggi Province. Registered as a traditional market in 2015, it strives to revitalize the market by running a merchant college, joint marketing projects including flea markets, and a weekend night market. In 2020, it launched the electric vehicle 'Jatgoeul Heungbus' connecting Jarasum Island, Gapyeong Rail Bike, and Gapyeong Jatgoeul Market.

en.overview: Gapyeong Hyeonri 5-Day Market is a traditional periodic market located in Jojong-myeon, Gapyeong-gun, opening every 4th and 9th of the month. en.title: Gyeonggi Anseong Market
en.overview: During the Joseon Dynasty, Anseong Market was large enough to be counted among the top three markets along with Daegu and Jeonju as a gateway to Seoul. It was a bustling place filled with various crafts and merchant lodgings, to the extent that people said two or three more items could be found here than in Seoul. Today, however, it has been modernized to the point where it is hard to find its old appearance. The messy old market has been reorganized into a clean and neat look with high roofs so visitors can comfortably shop regardless of season or weather.

en.title: Maesan Market
en.overview: Maesan Market is a traditional market located right in front of Suwon Station. Registered in 2011, it is the latest market to be formed in Suwon. 'Maesan' is a place name given because there were many plum blossom trees, and street vendors gathered one by one along a covered stream to form today's market. Through a landscape improvement project, display stands and signs were upgraded, and LED and line lighting were installed to modernize the facilities. It sells agricultural, marine, and livestock products as well as manufactured goods.

en.title: Moran Folk 5-Day Market
en.overview: Moran Folk 5-Day Market is a comprehensive traditional market located in Seongnam-si, Gyeonggi-do. Held every five days on dates ending in 4 and 9, it is the largest folk 5-day market in the country. It is right outside Exit 5 of Moran Station on the Suin-Bundang Line or Subway Line 8. Looking down from a building rooftop across the main road, the sight of the Moran Folk 5-Day Market covered in colorful parasols can be seen at a glance. Word of mouth has spread about its uniqueness as a traditional market in the middle of the city.

en.title: Munsan Freedom Market
en.overview: Representing traditional markets in northern Paju-si, Munsan Freedom Market originated from Munsan Port near the Imjin River during the Joseon Dynasty and is a 5-minute walk from Munsan Station on the Gyeongui Line. Serving as a collection hub for goods supplied to Hanyang as well as Pocheon, Gaeseong, and Cheorwon via the Imjin River, Munsan Freedom Market survived both the Japanese colonial period and the Korean War. After continuing its legacy as a 5- and 10-day market, it was revived as a 4- and 9-day market in 1989. You can buy diverse and fresh products at affordable prices alongside great street food.

en.title: Gunpo Yeokjeon Market (Gunpo Station Market)
en.overview: Located near Exit 1 of Gunpo Station, Gunpo Yeokjeon Market is a representative traditional market in Gunpo with a long history and tradition. Originating in 1929, it flourished when the market relocated to the front of the current Gunpo Station, drawing merchants even from Anyang and Suwon. In the 1950s, it was officially registered under its current name, Gunpo Yeokjeon Market. By the 1980s, it was a bustling, prominent market in Gyeonggi Province, overflowing with people from nearby industrial complexes, earning it the nickname 'Dokbaebitreo' (Goblin Site) due to its incredible crowds.

en.title: Gwonseon Jonghap Market (Gwonseon General Market)
en.overview: Established in 1987 with a shopping area of 27,236㎡, Gwonseon Market is a traditional market well-known for its wide array of sundae (blood sausage) and jokbal (pigs' trotters) shops, often referred to as a jokbal market. Rain or shine, visitors can enjoy comfortable shopping regardless of the weather, making it a beloved spot for local residents.

en.overview: Held at the Bukbyeon-dong public parking lot, Gimpo's largest traditional periodic market opens on every 2nd and 7th of the month. en.overview: Yangsu-ri Traditional Market is one of the three major traditional markets in Yangpyeong, Gyeonggi-do, located at the confluence of the Bukhan River (originating from Mt. Geumgang) and the Namhan River (originating from Geomryongso Spring in Gangwon-do). Its origin lies in the Yangsu-ri ferry port. It flourished greatly due to its strategic location connecting Jeongseon and Danyang in Gangwon-do along the upper Namhan River water route with Ttukseom and Mapo Ferry, the endpoints of the waterway. Yangsu-ri Traditional Market is about 40 minutes away from Seoul.

en.overview: Cheongpyeong is a place full of memories from the Riverside Song Festivals of the 1980s and 1990s. Starting as a cattle market in 1923, Cheongpyeong Yeoul Market was officially recognized as a traditional market in May 2021. Selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups' 'First Step Market' project in 2023, it continues to grow as a market connected with its customers. In particular, it offers a wide variety of food, making it fun to pick and choose. To leap forward as a nationwide market, it has hosted the Cheongpyeong Healing Challenge, featuring bicycle tours around Cheongpyeong and plogging activities for environmental protection.

en.title: Paldalmun Gate Market
en.overview: Paldalmun Market, along with Yeongdong Market, is known as a 'market created by a king.' King Jeongjo, the 22nd monarch of the Joseon Dynasty, summoned descendants of Gosan Yun Seon-do—who had settled in Haenam, Jeollanam-do and were engaged in the trading business—to Suwon. The market is said to have formed as merchants from all over the country began to eye Suwon. Initiated alongside the history of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, Paldalmun Market has centered around Paldalmun Gate until today, following King Jeongjo's vision to establish Suwon as a center of commerce and economy.

Established in its current location since 1936, Janghowon Market was once a market of considerable scale due to its location at a transportation hub, straddling the Cheongmicheon Stream between Janghowon-eup, Icheon-si, Gyeonggi-do and Gamgok-myeon, Eumseong-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do. Therefore, people in this area call it Icheon Janghowon or Eumseong Janghowon, forming the same living zone with only different administrative districts.

en.overview: Located right across from Jeonggok Port, this comprehensive fish market offers a variety of seafood for purchase or to be prepared at on-site restaurants. The 1st floor features live sliced raw fish (hwedjip) and dried seafood shops, alongside dining areas. Parking is available in front of the building or across the street at the Jeonggok Port floating dock parking lot. With Jeonggok Port within walking distance, visitors can enjoy fresh raw fish while taking in views of the harbor.

en.title: Joam Market (조암시장)
en.overview: Joam Market in Hwaseong-si, Gyeonggi-do, was also known as Samgoe Marketplace. Because Joam was close to the sea and had a well-developed agriculture industry, seafood trading such as oysters and blue crabs, as well as agricultural crops, flourished here. In the 1980s, the cattle market disappeared, and with the construction of the Hwaseong Embankment, seafood trade decreased, gradually reducing the size of the market. However, on market days, it bustles with visitors coming to experience the warm hospitality and affection of Joam Market.

en.title: Samcheonpo Yonggung Fisheries Market
en.overview: Located in Samcheonpo, known for its clean waters and strong tidal currents second only to Jindo Uldolmok, Samcheonpo Yonggung Fisheries Market is always stocked with an abundance of fresh seafood. Inspired by nearby Bito Island—the setting of the traditional folktale 'Byeoljubujeon' (The Rabbit and the Tortoise)—the harbor's old and small fish market was reborn as a 'dragon palace' themed experiential market. Visitors can find friendly murals and sculptures related to the folktale throughout the market.

en.title: Jayu Market (Jinju)
en.overview: Jinju Jayu Market is a traditional market located right next to Jinju City Hall. Opened in August 1979, it is a medium-sized commercial building-style market. It features many shops primarily selling fresh ingredients such as vegetables, fruits, meat, and fish. It won the grand prize at the 2019 National Traditional Market Country-of-Origin Management Evaluation. Visitors can find abundant Jinju specialty products and fresh agricultural and marine products. Steeped in the history and charm of Jinju, this traditional market offers a variety of sights, foods, and experiences.

en.title: Jirisan Hamyang Market
en.overview: Jirisan Hamyang Market is a traditional market located in downtown Hamyang-eup. In August 2015, it changed its name from the former Hamyang Jungang Permanent Market to Jirisan Hamyang Market. Operating as a permanent traditional market since 1983, a 5-day periodic market is held on dates ending in 2 and 7. It primarily sells agricultural and specialty products grown and produced within Hamyang-gun, near Mt. Jirisan. In particular, Hamyang apples and onions are major specialties produced in highland areas superior in quality to those from other regions.

en.title: Jinyeong Traditional Market
en.overview: Located in Jinyeong-ri, Jinyeong-eup, Gimhae-si, Gyeongsangnam-do, Jinyeong Traditional Market is a historic traditional market dating back to 1935, with markets opening every 4th and 9th of the month. Famous for Jinyeong sweet persimmons, the market sells groceries such as agricultural and marine products, as well as various foods like gukbap (rice soup), tteokbokki, jokbal (trotters), and puffed rice. Because it directly sells crops produced in nearby rural areas, you can purchase them at affordable prices. Although it is an old traditional market, the stores are neatly arranged, making it easy to navigate for first-time visitors.

en.title: Hadong Hwagaejangteo Market
en.overview: A traditional market formed at the meeting point of the Seomjin_gang River and Hwagaecheon Stream, where people from the Yeongnam and Honam regions once traded goods and interacted. It is widely known as the backdrop of Kim Dong-ri's novel 'Yeokma (The Fate)' and the popular song 'Hwagaejangteo'. In the past, marine products and salt from the southern coast, grains from Honam, and wild greens and woodenware from Jirisan Mountain gathered here, distributed to various regions via Seomjin_gang river transport. Although it declined for a time due to changes in transportation and distribution environments, it has been revitalized with traditional merchant houses and green tea specialty shops.

A market naturally formed as people from Gyeongsang-do and Jeolla-do exchanged goods based on the Seomjin_gang River. The downtown market, which also served as a motif for the novel 'Toji (The Land)', has been passed down through generations to become the Hadong Public Market, officially established in 1977. Since the 2000s, it experienced a slump due to large supermarkets and department stores.

en.overview: Gaeun Ajagae Market formed as a market since the Joseon Dynasty and officially received market establishment permission in 1981. en.overview: A traditional market where Jinju's western Jungang Market and northern Cheonggwa Market meet. Opened in 1962, it boasts over 60 years of history as one of Jinju's time-honored traditional markets. Originally named Jangdae Market, it was renamed Nongae Market to revitalize the stagnant traditional market. Nongae Market hosts 'Olppam Night Market,' the region's only permanent night market. Combining the words 'olppami' (owl) and 'bam' (night), it runs every Saturday starting at 6 PM.

en.title: Deoksan 5-Day Market
en.overview: Since the mid-Joseon Dynasty, the area encompassing Samjang-myeon and Sacheon-myeon was called Deoksanam, with Deoksan Market being the most famous. Held every 5 days (on the 4th and 9th), Deoksan Market served as a vital commercial hub near Cheonwangbong Peak, the main peak of Jirisan Mountain, where local residents bought and sold daily necessities and food to sustain their livelihoods. It offers various herbs, wild greens, and vegetables from Jirisan, and dried persimmons are famous in winter, though traded goods have evolved over time.

en.title: Gyeongju Jungang Market
en.overview: Gyeongju Jungang Market has a long history, dating back to the early 1900s when farmers and peddlers formed a marketplace that operated as a general market for over 70 years. It grew into a mid-to-large-scale shopping complex market in 1983, and locals also refer to it as the 'Lower Market'. The market is a relatively large traditional market with about 600 stores and 100 street vendors across 11 buildings, where local residents sell fresh local specialties they grew themselves.

en.overview: Passing through Hyeongsan Bridge at the Pohang Hyeongsan Rotary and going straight past Donghae-myeon for about 8 km leads to the entrance of Guryongpo-eup along with a Guryongpo tourist information map. en.title: Gumi Haepyeong Market
en.overview: Haepyeong-myeon in Gumi was a vital transportation hub where people frequently traveled, even housing a national inn called 'Sigawon' and the Haepyeong Guest House during the reign of King Seonjo in the Joseon Dynasty. Although both inns disappeared during the Japanese invasions of Korea, the village naturally developed around commerce, marking the beginning of Gumi Haepyeong Market. Regular markets were fully established in the early 1920s and flourished in the 1960s and 70s. In particular, the cattle market was large enough to trade 200 to 300 cows a day in Gumi.

en.title: Gumi Agricultural and Fishery Products Wholesale Market
en.overview: Located on Seonsan-daero, Goa-eup, Gumi-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do. It is the center of agricultural product distribution in the southwestern region of Gyeongsangbuk-do and ranked 2nd nationwide in customer satisfaction in 2020 as a developed-nation-style wholesale market for producers and consumers. Electronic auctions are conducted for all types of fruits and vegetables, and special policies are implemented such as an illegal activity reporting center, shipper loss compensation, market price verification systems, and shipper registration systems. en.title: Geumho Traditional Market
en.overview: Geumho Market originally opened as a periodic market around 1942 and was officially established as a traditional market on December 1, 1955. Depending on the season, visitors can find fresh local agricultural goods and daily necessities such as chili peppers, sesame seeds, watermelons, and grains. It is a wonderful market where you can enjoy a modern, pleasant shopping environment alongside the warm, heartfelt hospitality of a traditional Korean market.

en.title: Seongju Traditional Market
en.overview: Seongju Traditional Market is a local market centered around regional specialties and agricultural products. From early morning, merchants display their goods to welcome customers, filling the market with seasonal wild greens like aralia shoots (dureup) and chwinamul, alongside a wide array of fresh local produce. en.title: Shinyeongju Beongae Market
en.overview: Shinyeongju Beongae Market is a traditional market established in 1986 that operates both as a permanent market and a periodic 5-day market. Following the relocation of Yeongju Station to its current location in Hyucheon-dong, Yeongju-si in 1973, a morning 'flash' (beongae) market sprang up near the station, opening and closing in a flash. To revitalize the local economy, these scattered flash markets were later consolidated into a permanent market, which began growing in earnest. Since 1982, a traditional 5-day market has also been held on the 5th and 10th of every month.

en.overview: Angang Market is located in Yangwol-ri, Angang-eup, Gyeongju-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do. en.overview: Originating from the guest house operations during the Cheongdo Dohobu period of the Joseon Dynasty, the Cheongsong 5-day market developed into a regular market in the 1920s. The market stretches from the intercity bus terminal along the roadside in front of Korea Telecom in Cheongsong-eup.

en.title: Hamchang Traditional Market
en.overview: Hamchang Traditional Market originally opened as a periodic market held in Hamchang-hyeon every 1st and 6th day during the late Joseon Dynasty. It flourished when Hamchang Station was included on the Gyeongbuk Line opened in 1931, and its name was changed to Hamchang Market in Hamchang-gun. It registered as a regular periodic market in 1951, and was reorganized into a public market in February 1965 in accordance with market publicization policies. Operating as both a permanent market and a 5-day periodic market, it offers a wide variety of goods including agricultural products, seafood, fruits, daily necessities, and clothing.

en.overview: Also known as Jain-jang or Jain Jeontong, this market originated naturally from street stalls dating back to the Silla Dynasty. en.title: Jukdo Market
en.overview: Pohang Jukdo Market was formed 50 years ago when street vendors began settling in the swampy reed fields of Pohang's inner harbor. Jukdo Market Merchant Association was officially established in October 1969, and it stands as the largest traditional market on the east coast of Gyeongsangbuk-do. Located 500m east of Oggeori, the center of Pohang, Jukdo Fish Market is the largest permanent market on the east coast. With about 200 raw fish restaurants clustered inside the marine products auction house, visitors can enjoy fresh seafood from the East Coast at affordable prices all year round.

en.title: 1913 Songjeong Station Market
en.overview: Sharing its history with Songjeong Station since 1913, Songjeong Station Daily Market is a time-honored traditional market with a 100-year history. Once bustling with customers looking for daily ingredients and goods, this place has gradually declined like any other traditional market after being pushed aside by large supermarkets that sprouted up everywhere since the 1990s. In response, Songjeong Station Market chose not to 'confront' large supermarkets but rather to acknowledge its 'difference' and strengthen the unique characteristics of a traditional market.

en.title: Gwangju Yangdong Market
en.overview: Yangdong Market is a traditional market located in Seo-gu, Gwangju, and is the largest in the city. Its origins are known to date back to the 1910s when a market was held on the sandy beach under Gwangju Bridge on the 2nd and 7th of every month. Yangdong Market is packed with a diverse array of goods and abundant food options, earning it the reputation as a 'symbol of generous hospitality.' It remains a vital hub for holiday preparations, and locals still say that if you want to buy hongeo (fermented skate), you must go to Yangdong Market.

en.overview: Gunwi Market is a traditional 5-day rural market where a wide variety of goods are traded, ranging from seasonal agricultural produce, seafood, and livestock to clothing, food, and daily necessities at low prices. The market primarily features local agricultural products such as garlic, cucumbers, hot peppers, and Chinese cabbage produced in Gunwi, alongside produce gathered from neighboring areas sold at bargain or retail prices. It also hosts a cattle market, earthenware vendors, and a traditional blacksmith shop.

Nammun Market features raw fish restaurants and eateries, but it is especially famous for its three renowned rice cake shops: Seoul Tteokjip, Gyeongnam Tteokjip, and Nakwon Tteokjip.

en.overview: Gyodong Market is a traditional market situated between Daegu Station and Dongseongro. Following liberation and especially right after the Korean War, refugees gathered from all over, naturally forming the market. Unlike other large traditional markets in Daegu, narrow alleys remain, allowing visitors to feel a sense of nostalgia. For those who have visited the same pathways over many years, it is a market filled with memories and familiarity. Entering the alleys by following the cute goblin guide sign at the entrance, you will find friendly neighbors.

Its name, 'Beongae' (meaning 'lightning' or 'flash'), originates from the 1970s when itinerant merchants from rural areas near Daegu gathered spontaneously using early morning trains to sell vegetables and fruits from 3:00 AM to 11:00 AM. Formally established in 1988, its main traded items are agricultural and marine products, alongside clothing, fish, and general goods. The National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (Nonghyup) wholesale market is located right next door.

en.title: Malbau Market (2nd, 4th, 7th, 9th)
en.overview: Malbau Market, a representative traditional market in Buk-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City, is named after a rock shaped like a horse's footprint (Malbau). Boasting a tradition of over 50 years, legend has it that during the mid-Joseon dynasty, Righteous Army General Kim Deok-ryeong shot an arrow here, rode his horse faster than the arrow, and left a hoofprint on the rock. Although the original rock is gone and buildings now stand in its place, the market thrives along the alleys between these buildings.

en.overview: Along with Seomun Market, this is one of the largest traditional markets in Daegu. en.title: Bongdeok Market, Daegu
en.overview: Bongdeok Market is one of the representative traditional markets in Nam-gu, Daegu. Following the Korean War, the market overflowed with goods from nearby US military bases. Everything from C-rations, blankets, sewing machines, and frying pans to various second-hand goods and military supplies filled the market. Born naturally amidst such an unfortunate history, Bongdeok Market enjoyed its peak prosperity in the 1970s and 1980s, growing into one of Daegu's top four markets before the advent of large supermarkets.

ja.overview: 鳳德市場は大邱広域市南区を代表する市場の一つである。朝鮮戦争を経て、市場には周辺の米軍部隊から流れ出た物資があふれた。Cレーションをはじめ、毛布、ミシン、フライパンに至るまで、あらゆる旧放出品や軍需物資が市場内を埋め尽くした。そうした不幸な歴史の中で自然発生的に生まれた大邱南区の鳳德市場は、70年代と80年代に最高の繁栄期を迎え、大邱の4大市場へと成長したが、大型マートの登場以前の話である。

en.title: Anjirang Market, Daegu
en.overview: Located midway along the path from Anjirang Five-way Intersection to Apsan Anjiranggol, Anjirang Market has moved past its glamorous past and gained new vitality with the recent influx of seasoned gopchang (beef/pork tripe) restaurants. en.title: Pyeonghwa Market, Daegu
en.overview: A traditional market located in Sinam-dong, Dong-gu, Daegu. Having continued for some 50 years since its emergence in the 1970s, Daegu Pyeonghwa Market is a small-scale market consisting of about 80 stores in a commercial-residential complex format. When it first opened in the 1970s, Pyeonghwa Market was not large. In the late 1970s, as surrounding hills and fields turned into residential areas, it began to take the shape of a market, and flourished starting in the 1980s.

en.overview: Located on Dongseong-ro in Jung-gu, the Daegu Herbal Medicine Wholesale Market is a global herbal medicine distribution hub with a 360-year tradition. en.title: Bangcheon Market
en.overview: Bangcheon Market is a traditional market located next to Suseonggyo Bridge, one of the 12 bridges crossing Sincheon Stream which passes north-to-south through downtown Daegu. After the liberation in 1945, war refugees returning from Japan and Manchuria started selling goods here to make a living, and it came to be called Bangcheon Market because it was established along the Sincheon embankment. At the time, it stretched about 500 meters south from Suseonggyo Bridge along the stream bank.

en.title: Bullo Traditional Market
en.overview: Bullo Market is a traditional market with a long history dating back to the 1930s, located on the route past Daegu International Airport toward Palgongsan Mountain and Pagyesa Temple. It operates as both a permanent market and a periodic 5-day market, and until the early 1980s, its commercial area was so vibrant that it ranked among the top 5 periodic markets in Gyeongsangbuk-do. About 130 permanent shops run from the north to the south of the market, making it great for shopping even on non-market days.

Notable dishes at Saegil Market include duruchigi (spicy stir-fried pork) and bulgogi, with the duruchigi being especially famous for its great taste. en.title: Seongdang Market
en.overview: A great market to drop by while touring downtown Daegu. It is a historic market that has stood in the southern part of Daegu for over 50 years. Stores inside the market sell local Daegu delicacies. A variety of eateries specializing in pork cutlets, noodles, sliced raw fish, rice cakes, and traditional Korean confectioneries (hangwa) are lined up here. The Cudrania tricuspidata (gujeokppong) noodles are particularly famous. Nearby attractions include E-World, Duryu Mural Village, Duryu Park, and Daemyeong Culture Street.

en.title: Sintanjin Market
en.overview: Sintanjin Market is a traditional 5-day periodic market located west of Sintanjin Station in northern Daedeok-gu, Daejeon. First appearing in records from the late Joseon Dynasty, it boasts a history of about 300 years. It grew rapidly after the opening of Sintanjin Station on the Gyeongbu Line in 1905. The bustling market scene truly begins as you pass under the railway underpass or overpass from Sintanjin Station, bustling with about 1,000 street vendors and shoppers. Traditional market sights like puffed rice vendors and candy sellers add to the charm.

en.title: Chimsan Golmok Market (Chimsan Alley Market)
en.overview: Located in Chimsan-dong, Buk-gu, Daegu, Chimsan Golmok Market is a small alley market with an unclear history of when it was formed or when it began to decline. At first glance, it doesn't look like a traditional market since there is no separation between the roadway and sidewalk, but it once enjoyed a golden age when shops were packed tightly together. Today, with many factories built in the surrounding area, local foot traffic has dropped, leaving only about 10 stores maintaining its legacy along a roughly 100-meter stretch.

en.overview: Hyeonpung Baeknyeon Dokkaebi Market is a traditional market located in Hyeonpung-eup, Dalseong-gun, Daegu. Having opened in March 1918, it has surpassed a century of history to become the market it is today. It consists of a traditional market where visitors can experience cross-generational culture, a traditional 5-day periodic market held on dates ending in 5 and 10, and a youth mall that injects fresh vitality into the traditional market across eras and generations. Visitors can find fresh local specialties grown directly by local residents, native products, and more.

en.title: Geoje Market
en.overview: Geoje Market is the largest conventional market in Yeonje-gu with a tradition of over 50 years. You can purchase a variety of items ranging from fresh seafood, raw fish, and various foods to clothing and general goods. There are many famous restaurants inside Geoje Market, with hand-cut noodles (son-kalguksu) being especially renowned. Specialized hand-cut noodle shops line the market alley, and with many other famous foods available, local residents and tourists constantly visit. If you want to leave special memories when visiting Busan, this is a must-visit spot.

ja.title: 巨済市場（コジェシジャン）
ja.overview: 巨済市場は50余年の伝統を誇る蓮堤区最大規模の常設市場です。新鮮な海鮮や刺身、各種グルメから衣類、雑貨に至るまで、多様な品目を購入することができます。巨済市場内には美味しい店が多く、特に有名なのは手打ちカルグクスです。市場の路地に沿って手打ちカルグクス専門店が軒を連ねており、この他にも有名なグルメが多く、地域住民や観光客の足が途絶えません。釜山訪問時に特別な思い出を残したい方におすすめです。

en.title: Guseo Osige Market
en.overview: Located in Geumjeong-gu, Busan, Guseo Osige Market is a shopping district-style market near Exit 1 of Guseo Station. Once a bustling place visited by many customers with around 400 stores, it has declined as other commercial districts in Busan developed. However, it remains popular as a daily grocery shopping spot where you can purchase various foods and daily necessities in one place. Even nowadays, fresh agricultural products such as vegetables, wild greens, hand-made tofu, and acorn jelly grown and made directly by elderly women are sold.

Inside the building, you will find stores selling dried seafood, supermarkets, and raw fish restaurants, while the surrounding area features shops selling vegetables, fruits, and everyday goods.

en.title: Busan International Seafood Wholesale Market

Gijang Market feels more like a traditional lively street market ('jeojatgeori') than a modern commercial market. Its main characteristic is that seasonal specialties define the market throughout the year: seaweed and anchovies in spring, and brown seaweed in fall.

en.title: Busan Jungang Market
en.overview: Jungang Market is a traditional market located in the Beomcheon-dong area, well-known as a specialized flower market. Reconstructed in 2012, flower shops operate inside a mixed-use building equipped with a spacious parking lot. The building consists of 4 underground floors and 30 floors above ground, with shopping areas spanning from the 1st basement floor to the 3rd floor above ground. The basement features a food court, while the upper floors house general retail stores including jewelry shops and a wholesale flower market.

en.title: Busan Pyeonghwa Wholesale Market
en.overview: Busan Pyeonghwa Wholesale Market was established in June 1969 at its current location, initially starting as a hardware market following a new construction project. Later, following the trends of the times in the early 1970s, it transformed into a specialized clothing market, attracting about 40 wholesale merchants and over 100 clothing vendors. It converted the 3rd floor into a factory space for on-site production, securing competitiveness against similar traditional markets and laying the foundation for growth. Today, it serves as a major commercial district covering Busan as well as the Yeongnam and Honam regions.

en.title: Daebyeon Market
en.overview: Located at Daebyeon Port, the representative hub for anchovies accounting for 60% of the country's driftnet anchovy catches, Gijang Daebyeon Market comes alive during the spring and autumn anchovy seasons. Stalls line the market, bustling with people buying fresh anchovies, salted anchovies, and various seafood. Along with anchovies, it also offers Gijang specialties such as seaweed, kelp, and dried fish. Visitors right by the sea can even watch fishermen shaking anchovies out of their nets.

en.title: Deokpo Market
en.overview: Located in Sasang-gu, Busan, Deokpo Market derives its name from 'Deok' (meaning hill) and 'Po' (meaning port), originally signifying a market located on a hill. The name was given because a large port once stood here, and a natural market naturally formed as crowds gathered around it. However, when Deokpo Market was registered as an official traditional market in 2007, its meaning was changed from 'market on a hill' to 'market full of blessings.' It offers abundant food and sights.

en.title: Dongnae Market
en.overview: Dongnae Market carries on the legacy of Dongnae Jangteo, the largest 5-day periodic market in the Busan region during the Joseon Dynasty, maintaining its large scale today. Many shops within the market have preserved their deep-rooted traditions for a long time. Surrounding the exterior of the building are herbal medicine stores, a restaurant alley with prices that rarely increase, and fashion accessories where gentle haggling is welcomed—with most businesses boasting at least 40 to 50 years of history. Rich in history and stories, it is a great place to visit with children and family.

en.title: Myeongji Market
en.overview: Myeongji Market is a representative traditional market in the Gangseo area of Busan with a 50-year history. Having evolved from a 5-day periodic market and a dawn market, it has been famous as a live fish market for the past 30 years. Thanks to its geographical advantage where the Nakdonggang River converges, it boasts abundant catches and short distribution distances from the production areas, keeping the live fish fresh across its 120-plus stores. In late summer every year, the market hosts its proud 'Gizzard Shad Festival,' establishing itself proudly alongside Jagalchi Market, Gukje Market, and Kkangtong Market as one of Busan's premier markets.

zh.overview: 鳴旨市場是擁有50年歷史的釜山江西地區代表性傳統市場，歷經五日市與早市後，自30年前起以活魚市場聞名。受惠於洛東江交匯處的地理優勢，漁獲量豐富且距離產地流通距離短，非常便於維持活魚的新鮮度，目前有約120家店舖營業中。每年夏末，鳴旨市場引以為傲的「斑鰶節」在此舉辦，與札嘎其市場、國際市場、罐頭市場並列，是名副其實的釜山代表性市場。

Opened in 2006, it currently consists of about 100 shops stretching out in a row. Mainly focusing on fresh foods such as agricultural, marine, and livestock products, as well as various daily necessities, it is closely tied to the daily lives of nearby residents. Currently home to around 210 thriving stores, it was officially registered as a traditional market in 2006. Spanning 14,000㎡ with approximately 500 workers, the market handles all kinds of livestock products including Korean beef (Hanwoo), beef cattle, dairy cattle, imported meat, pork, by-products, and boiled pork slices (pyeonyuk), supplying and delivering them nationwide to maximize the efficiency and economic scale of meat distribution.

en.overview: Gupo Market is a large-scale traditional market that is hard to find in modern city centers. Historically developed around the Gupo-naru ferry on the Nakdonggang River, it has long been a vibrant commercial hub with active trade connecting neighboring regions like Gimhae and Yangsan. Operating as a hybrid of a permanent daily market and a periodic traditional 5-day market, it still buzzes with people buying and selling freshly delivered fruits, vegetables, seafood, and everyday goods on market days, offering the lively atmosphere of a nostalgic rural marketplace.

en.overview: Gukje Market Youth Street is a vibrant alley filled with large and small clothing stores. It is a unique specialty district packed with shops and sports stores targeting younger generations. Browsing through the numerous wholesale clothing boutiques makes it easy to find rare apparel and accessories. Affordable dress shops and men's suit stores, compared to other regions, are another point of pride for this street. Located inside Gukje Market, visitors can enjoy shopping alongside a wide variety of sights and street foods.

en.title: Namhang Market (남항시장)
en.overview: Namhang Market formed in the 1960s when people began gathering to live in Yeongdo, Busan, following the Korean War. Boasting the third-largest scale in Busan with a tradition of over 60 years, Namhang Market blends the charm of a traditional market with modern, comfortable facilities for convenient shopping. It primarily handles agricultural, marine, and livestock products either directly sourced from local farms or homegrown. Alongside side-dish shops selling fish cakes (eomuk) and kimchi, you can also find daily necessities and clothing.

A commercial-residential complex market, Suyoung Paldo Market offers everything from agricultural and marine products to clothing, general goods, jewelry, pharmacies, and local eateries. With a vaulted arcade roof installed, visitors can enjoy shopping comfortably regardless of the weather.

en.title: Sindonga Seafood Market
en.overview: Completed in 1987, Sindonga Seafood Complex Market (Sindonga Raw Fish Center) houses 186 live fish restaurants. The basement features a food center where visitors can taste regional delicacies like seasoned beef intestines (yang gopchang) and hagfish (gomjangeo) combined with Jagalchi Market's fresh ingredients and Busan's signature spicy seasoning. The first floor hosts live fish and abalone shops, while the second floor features dried seafood stores with a refreshing ocean breeze. The third floor is densely packed with raw fish centers.

en.title: Ynongdong Market
en.overview: Unlike naturally formed traditional markets, Yeondong Market was established when a real estate developer built the market structure and sold individual retail spaces. en.title: Bujeon Market Town (부전마켓타운)
en.overview: Bujeon Market Town originally started as 'Gijang Alley Market'. Its origins trace back to after the Korean War, when peddlers carrying agricultural and marine products produced in nearby regions such as Gijang, Seosaeng, Ilgwang, and Wolnae unloaded their loads at Bujeon Station on the Donghae Nambu Line and began selling them. The Gijang Alley Market became Bujeon Market, which has now evolved into Bujeon Market Town. It brings together six markets including Bujeon Sangga, Bujeon Market, Seomyeon General Market, Bujeon Ginseng Market, Bujeon General Shopping Center, and Busan Electronics General Shopping Center.

en.overview: Bupyeong Kkangtong Market in Busan was formed after the Korean War as US military surplus goods and various imported items were distributed here. It is said to have earned the nickname 'Kkangtong (Can) Market' because many canned goods, such as fruits and fish, were imported. At the time, it supplied imported goods to major markets nationwide, earning it the name 'Dotegi Market' (a bustling flea market). It was large enough that you could find almost anything, including foreign goods, and has established itself as one of Busan's representative markets leading to today's International Market.

en.overview: Haeundae Market is adjacent to Haeundae Beach, one of Busan's largest tourist destinations, making it a popular traditional market for tourists looking to enjoy food and shopping during the summer vacation season. en.title: Gyeongdong Market
en.overview: Opened in June 1960, Gyeongdong Market is a specialized agricultural market. Offering specialty products foraged from mountains and fields alongside various agricultural goods at reasonable prices, it has established itself as a representative traditional market in downtown Seoul. Following the completion of the Gyeongdong Building in 1985, the nation's largest ginseng market and herbal medicine specialty shops were established here, developing the market's expertise and scale in medicinal herbs and ginseng. Today, Gyeongdong Market continues to thrive as a hub for agricultural goods, medicinal herbs, and ginseng.

ja.title: 京東市場
ja.overview: 京東市場は1960年6月にオープンした農産物専門市場です。山や野原で採取した特産物をはじめ、様々な農産物をリーズナブルな価格で販売しており、ソウル都心の代表的な伝統市場として定着しました。1985年に京東ビルが竣工した後は、国内最大規模の人参市場と漢方薬専門商街が形成されました。これを基盤に、薬材と人参の分野で専門性と規模を備えた市場へと発展しました。今日、京東市場は農産物や薬材、人参などを扱う市場として賑わっています。

zh.title: 京東市場

en.title: Gyeongchang Market
en.overview: A traditional market situated in Sinwol-dong, Yangcheon-gu, Seoul, where you can purchase various ingredients and daily necessities at reasonable prices. It is well-stocked with fresh vegetables, fruits, fish, and meat, and features alleys lined with street foods and unique shops. Convenient for local residents doing their grocery shopping, the market also boasts excellent convenience facilities, including a restroom inside the customer support center. It offers a neat, tidy appearance with affordable prices and a friendly atmosphere where you can expect a little extra bonus (deom).

Spanning a total area of about 2,200㎡ with around 70 stores, it is a small-to-medium market where Zero Pay is widely accepted. With an arched arcade roof for convenient shopping regardless of the weather, the market hosts various events like flea markets and elderly support programs to engage the local community.

en.overview: Originating from street vendors who gathered near Hwarangdae Station following the opening of the Gyeongchun Railway on July 25, 1939, Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi (Goblin) Market started as a traditional goblin market where vendors would vanish instantly like goblins when crackdowns occurred, only to reassemble snugly along the railroad tracks once the crackdown ended. Known for selling high-quality goods at affordable prices and boasting that it has everything you need as if conjured by a goblin's magic club, it is Nowon-gu's representative neighborhood living market.

en.title: Gwanak Sinsa Market
en.overview: Located in Sillim-dong, Gwanak-gu, Seoul, Gwanak Sinsa Market is an alley-style market surrounded by residential villa and multi-family housing areas. Developed into a market after installing a 300-meter-long arcade in 2006 as part of a traditional market revitalization project, it is neatly organized in a modern style and offers great accessibility just 3 to 4 minutes away from Sindaebang Station. In 2019, it was featured on a TV program showcasing mini haeshintang (seafood stew), nostalgic bread, Chinese twisted doughnuts (kwabaegi), honey rice cakes (kkultteok), and kaljjajang (knife-cut noodles with black bean sauce).

en.title: Bangsan General Market
en.overview: Bangsan General Market is a traditional industrial materials market located in Bangsan-dong, Jung-gu, Seoul. It is a one-stop shop for a wide variety of items ranging from hardware, packaging, bookbinding, and craft materials to stationery and fancy goods. With small shops clustered together, it is easy to compare prices and make custom purchases, making it a beloved practical material supplier for small business owners, designers, and creators. It is a traditional market that continues to gain steady popularity for its reasonable prices and diverse product selection.

en.title: Bongil Market
en.overview: A traditional two-building market located in Euncheon-dong, Gwanak-gu, Seoul. First opened in 1971 and operating to this day, it is a small market consisting of about 36 stores including supermarkets, clothing shops, tailoring shops, restaurants, butcher shops, and bakeries. Ddukdo Youth Market was once one of Seoul's top three markets alongside Namdaemun Market and Dongdaemun Market, located on the route bringing goods from Gangwon-do since the Joseon Dynasty. Its current appearance was established in 1962. en.title: Moraenae Market Food Alley
en.overview: Located in Namgajwa-dong, Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, this food alley is a traditional market formed in 1966. Its name originates from 'Moraenae,' the historical local name for the Namgajwa-dong area. In the past, it served as a lifestyle hub for local residents as a traditional market, but its function as a market has now ceased. However, the food alley that developed alongside the market is still operating. It offers a variety of foods, including traditional Chinese restaurants, galbi (ribs) houses, snack bars, and chicken offal soup eateries.

ja.title: モレネ市場グルメ通り
ja.overview: ソウル市西大門区南加佐洞に位置するグルメ通りは、1966年に形成された伝統市場で、南加佐洞一帯を呼んでいた「モレネ」という地域名から市場の名前が由来しました。かつては在来市場として地域住民の生活の中心地としての役割を果たしていましたが、現在は市場としての機能は停止した状態です。しかし、市場とともに形成されたグルメ通りは今も営業を続けています。中華料理店、カルビ店、粉食店、鶏の内臓鍋店など、伝統を守り続ける様々なグルメを提供しています。

zh.title: 沙乃래（摩麗內）市場美食街
zh.overview: 位於首爾市西대門區南加佐洞的美食街是1966年形成的傳統市場，市場名稱源自過去稱呼南加佐洞一帶的地區名「沙乃래（Moraenae，意為沙川）」。過去它曾作為傳統市場擔任當地居民的生活中心，目前市場功能已停擺。不過，與市場一同發展起來的美食街至今仍在營業。這裡提供各種傳統美食，包括中餐館、烤排骨店、小吃店、辣炒雞雜店等充滿歷史韻味的店家。

en.title: Mokdong Kkaebi Market
en.overview: A traditional market located in Mok 3-dong, Yangcheon-gu, Seoul. At the market entrance, there is a cute goblin ('kkaebi') character photo zone, and goblin-shaped lighting hangs above each store, making it a joy to explore. It is packed with fresh agricultural, marine, and livestock ingredients, as well as delicious street food. With great accessibility near Deungchon Station on Subway Line 9 and convenient parking facilities, it is easy to visit by car. It is rich with things to see, eat, and buy.

en.overview: Bamnamugol Market is a semi-subterranean alley market formed underneath the pedestrian walkway along Opaesan-ro. Although not very large, it boasts a history of over 50 years. Formed across low-ceilinged, narrow alleyways, many stores continue to operate here today. It sells a variety of items including agricultural products, marine products, street food, clothing, and daily necessities, making it fun to explore. Right next to the market, newly redeveloped apartment complexes and modern commercial buildings create a striking contrast.

en.title: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
en.overview: Originating next to Seoul Station on Eiju-ro in 1927, Noryangjin Fisheries Market boasts a long history of over 90 years and is Korea's largest inland wholesale market specializing in seafood. A new wholesale market was built in Noryangjin in 1971, and in 2002, the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (Suhyup) acquired the market to promote fishermen's income and the development of the fishery industry. Through modernization projects, it has been reborn as Korea's representative seafood wholesale market where distribution and culture coexist, handling 5% of the capital area's transaction volume.

en.overview: Opened in the 1970s, this is the oldest traditional market in Gwangjin-gu, organized neatly as an alley-style market. Walking a bit further toward the northern end of Yeongdonggyo Bridge connects directly to Yeongdonggyo Alley Market, allowing visitors to explore both simultaneously. Packed with delicious street food, it is frequently visited by people of all ages, and the stores located along the alleyways welcome visitors.

en.overview: Semaul Traditional Market is a traditional market located in Jamsil. en.title: Suhyup Gangseo Fish Market
en.overview: As the largest fishery market in the southwestern area of Seoul, it stably supplies marine products collected daily at dawn from production areas across the country through auctions. It sells a variety of fresh seafood, including live sliced fish (hwaluhwe), fish, shellfish, crustaceans, dried seafood, and salted fish (jeotgal). Consumers can have their newly purchased seafood cooked immediately at the specialized restaurants on the 2nd floor. The restaurant area offers a wide variety of seafood dishes and a broad menu selection, making it great for family gatherings or get-togethers.

en.title: Sungin Market
en.overview: A traditional market located near Miasageori Station. It sells various foods and daily necessities at affordable prices and is closely connected to the daily lives of local residents. Retaining its long history and cozy atmosphere, it leaves a warm impression on visitors. While delicious street foods like bunsik (snacks), twigim (fried dishes), and jokbal (pigs' trotters) are popular, it is especially famous as a market known for delicious tteokbokki.

en.title: Jeongok Market
en.overview: Jeongok Market is a traditional market located in Jangan-dong, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, which opened in 1975. It is a single-building, multi-story commercial complex spanning a basement level and two above-ground floors, with a total area of 1,358㎡. It has maintained its traditional market form without major changes since its opening. Inside the market, there are various eateries well-known as local culinary hotspots, serving kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), makguksu (buckwheat noodles), and hotteok (sweet pancakes). Nearby attractions include Jangan Neighborhood Park and Baebongsan Mountain.

en.title: Nanchang Onggijonggi Market
en.overview: Situated in Onyang-myeon, Ulju-gun, Ulsan Metropolitan City, Nanchang Onggijonggi Market is a historic traditional market held every Saturday and on the 3rd, 8th, 13th, 18th, 23rd, and 28th of every month. It was named 'Nanchang' because a warehouse storing grain during the Joseon Dynasty was located in the southern part of Ulsan. It came to be called 'Onggijonggi Market' as onggi (traditional earthenware) produced in the nearby Oegosan Onggi Village during the 1970s and 80s was distributed nationwide. It offers regional specialties such as Ulsan's Seosaeng pears, along with fruits, meat, and seafood.

en.overview: Established in 1974, Hakseong Saebyeok Market is Ulsan's premier wholesale and retail food market, recording over 60 billion won in annual sales and more than 5,000 daily visitors. It is renowned for offering fresh ingredients directly from production areas at affordable prices. Operating mainly at dawn, it primarily handles bulk wholesale transactions. The market features two specially designed alleys and an LED digital billboard at the entrance to actively promote the market.

zh.title: 鶴城黎明市場（Hakseong Saebyeok Market）

Firmly established as a traditional market, Hogae Public Market serves as the commercial hub of the Hogae area. It originated when people gathered around the now-closed Hogae Station, built in the 1920s. Located near the Hogae Community Center and Hogae Station, it was famously known as the go-to place for soybeans until the early 1970s.

Divided into Building A and Building B, the market consists of about 110 stores (including 26 street vendors). en.title: Bupyeong General Market
en.overview: Bupyeong General Market is a traditional market with a long history. Its origins trace back to street vendor alleys that formed as the area around Bupyeong Station was developed and the population grew during the Japanese colonial period. It took on the true appearance of a market after the Korean War. As military supplies leaked from nearby U.S. military bases were traded here, it was called the 'Goblin Market' or 'Yankee Market,' and its scale gradually expanded. Later, with the establishment of a fruit and vegetable wholesale market in the 1970s, it grew into a major hub serving Incheon as well as Gimpo and Yeongdeungpo.

en.title: Seondu 5-ri Fish Market
en.overview: Seondu 5-ri Fish Market is a seafood direct-sales dining area on Ganghwado Island, Incheon, where boat owners run their own restaurants directly, allowing visitors to enjoy fresh seafood. Located right by the sea, it offers fresh raw fish (sashimi) such as mullet, rockfish, flounder, sea bass, and sea bream, along with spicy fish stew and steamed shellfish while watching the sunset. Takeout is also available. Seasonal menu prices and availability may vary depending on seafood supply conditions. Tents and brazier spots are located around the fish market.

en.title: Soraepogu General Fish Market
en.overview: Soraepogu General Fish Market is a seafood market located in Incheon Metropolitan City. Many customers visit to buy fresh live fish of great quality and quantity at competitive prices depending on the season. In spring, visitors can enjoy freshly caught blue crabs on the day boats arrive at Soraepogu, and during the Kimjang (kimchi-making) season, the market is filled with flavorful salted seafood (jeotgal). Unlike the old, crowded, and messy port, it is a neatly zoned modern fish market equipped with a seawater purification system to enhance customer satisfaction, featuring air conditioning and heating.

zh.overview: 蘇來浦口綜合魚市場是位於仁川廣域市的魚市場。這裡因隨季節供應價格實惠且份量十足的新鮮活魚而吸引大量遊客造訪。春天時，遊客可以在蘇來浦口漁船入港當天品嚐現撈的花蟹；到了泡菜季（Kimjang），市場裡則擺滿了風味絕佳的各式醃漬海鮮（Jeotgal）。與以往雜亂髒亂的舊港口不同，這是一個規劃整齊、採用海水淨化系統的現代化魚市場，大幅提升了顧客滿意度，並設有冷暖氣設備。

en.overview: A traditional market located in Gajwa-dong, Incheon Metropolitan City, structured in a straight line across a wide road. In the 1960s, a store called 'Geobuk Sanghoe' gained fame, leading to the formation of a commercial district centered around it. The market was established along the village name, Geobuk-gol (Turtle Valley). Over 30 years, merchants gathered one by one to form and operate the market. Located near the Seoknam-dong Administrative Welfare Center, it is widely used by busy office workers and local residents.

en.overview: A cultural tourism-type market frequently visited by both domestic and foreign tourists, Singi Market attracts crowds daily with its charming alleys and abundant shopping and food options. True to its name ('Singi' meaning fascinating/novel), there are many fascinating things here. One of them is 'Singi Tongbo,' which can only be used here. Shaped like ancient brass coins, Singi Tongbo is Singi Market's own currency system used instead of real money. Each Singi Tongbo is exchangeable for a value of 500 won, perfect for enjoying snacks in the food alley.

Early in the port opening period, it was called Sinpo Market, meaning 'new port.' It was renamed Sinpo International Market in 2010. zh.overview: 自1996年市場開市以來，玉蓮市場被周邊的公寓社區環繞，長期以來與延壽區居民一同成長。為了從服務當地居民的生活型市場，蛻變為連結松島國際都市與松島KTX的觀光型傳統市場，該市場正持續努力中。這裡備有豐富且新鮮的美食，不僅吸引鄰近居民，也吸引了其他地區的遊客造訪。

en.overview: Yonghyeon Market naturally emerged in the 1960s as people gathered around Mt. Subongsan. Commercial activity gradually developed as shops opened around the former Han-il Theater, and it flourished from its early formation with over 1,000 stores in operation. During the operation of the past Suin Line railway, it enjoyed a boom that attracted metropolitan residents from as far away as Ansan, Gyeonggi-do.

zh.title: 仁川龍峴市場
zh.overview: 龍峴市場是在1960年代人們聚集在水봉山一帶時自然形成的。當時韓日劇場周邊開始出現商店，商業圈逐漸發展起來，自市場形成初期起便有上千家店鋪營業，盛況空前。過去在水仁線鐵路運行時期，甚至吸引了遠至京畿道安山等首都圈地區的人們前來，生意十分興隆。

en.title: Incheon Jeil Market
en.overview: Jeil Market is a traditional market located in Yonghyeon-dong, Incheon, selling various ingredients such as vegetables and meat, daily necessities, and street food. Situated at the intersection of the Gyeongin National Highway and the road toward Inha University, it is a neighborhood market that local residents have used for a long time. Various restaurants are located inside the market, and the 'Gopchang Alley', clustered with pork tripe specialty restaurants, is particularly famous.
en.practical_header: Check Before You Go · Market Days · Items Sold · Parking · Amenities

ja.title: 仁川第一市場（インチョン・チェイルシジャン）
ja.overview: 第一市場は仁川龍ヒョン洞に位置する伝統市場で、野菜や肉類をはじめとする各種食材や生活用品、グルメなどを販売しています。京仁国道と仁하大学方面の道路が交わる地点に位置し、地域住民が長年利用してきた生活市場です。市場内部には様々な飲食店があり、特に豚ホルモン専門店が集まるホルモン横丁が有名です。

zh.title: 仁川第一市場
zh.overview: 第一市場是位於仁川龍峴洞的傳統市場，販售包含蔬菜、肉類在內的各種食材、生活用品以及美食等。它位於京仁國道與仁하大學方向道路的交會點，是當地居民長期使用的生活市場。市場內部設有各式餐廳，其中特別以聚集了許多豬大腸專賣店的「大腸街」聞名。

en.title: Incheon General Fish Market
en.overview: The history of Incheon General Fish Market dates back to Incheon's opening port era. It is known that a fishery market naturally formed in the late 1880s as Japanese residents living in Incheon consumed a large amount of fish. It developed gradually along with Incheon's port opening, and became today's Incheon General Fish Market in 1975 when an urban renewal project reclaimed the coastal pier area. It offers fresh fish and seafood caught directly from nearby coastal waters as well as same-day deliveries from across the country.

ja.title: 仁川総合魚市場
ja.overview: 仁川総合魚市場の歴史は、仁川の開化期にまでさかのぼります。1880年代末、仁川に居住する日本人が魚を多く消費するようになり、自然に水産市場ができたと言われています。その後、仁川の開港とともに発展し続け、1975年に沿岸埠頭一帯を埋め立てる都市整備事業が進められ、今日の仁川総合魚市場となりました。近海で直接獲れた新鮮な魚や海産物、全国から当日配送される商品が揃っています。

zh.title: 仁川綜合魚市場
zh.overview: 仁川綜合魚市場的歷史可以追溯到仁川的開化期。據說在1880年代末，居住在仁川的日本人消耗大量魚類，因而自然形成了水產市場。隨後隨著仁川開港而不斷發展，1975年因進行填平沿岸碼頭一帶的都市整頓事業，成為今日的仁川綜合魚市場。這裡販售直接從附近海域捕獲的新鮮魚類、海鮮，以及從全韓國當日配送的商品。

en.title: Incheon Jungang Market
en.overview: Located in Geumgok-dong, Incheon, Jungang Market is a traditional market frequently visited by both locals and tourists, serving as a space to experience the local economy and culture together. It is convenient for shopping with shops selling a variety of items such as fresh agricultural and marine products, food, daily necessities, and clothing, allowing visitors to purchase high-quality goods at reasonable prices. Various eateries, snack bars, and side-dish shops are located throughout the market.
en.practical_header: Check Before You Go · Market Days · Items Sold · Parking · Amenities

ja.title: 仁川中央市場（インチョン・チュンアンシジャン）
ja.overview: 仁川広域市金谷洞に位置する中央市場は、地域住民はもちろん観光客も多く訪れる伝統市場で、地域の経済と文化を同時に感じられる空間です。新鮮な農水産物やグルメ、生活用品、衣類など様々な品目を販売する商店が集まっており、お買い物に便利で、リーズナブルな価格で良質な商品を購入できます。市場の所々に多様なグルメや軽食、おかず店が並んでいます。
ja.practical_header: お出かけ前の確認・市の日・販売品目・駐車場・便利施設

zh.title: 仁川中央市場
zh.overview: 位於仁川廣域市金谷洞的中央市場，是當地居民以及許多遊客造訪的傳統市場，也是一個能同時感受當地經濟與文化的空間。這裡聚集了販售新鮮農水產品、美食、生活用品、服飾等多樣商品的店舖，購物相當便利，能以合理的價格買到高品質的商品。市場各處設有各種小吃、分食餐館和小菜店，吸引源源不絕的訪客。
zh.practical_header: 購物前確認 · 集市日 · 販售品項 · 停車 · 便利設施

en.title: Incheon Hyundai Market
en.overview: Hyundai Market is a representative traditional market located in Songnim-dong, Incheon. Formed between 1960 and 1979, it is a medium-sized market gathering about 250 stores. Having completed facility modernization early on, it features a pleasant and clean shopping environment. With arcades installed over the market streets, it is easy to get around even in bad weather, and parking facilities are well-equipped for shopping convenience.

zh.title: 仁川現代市場

en.title: Ilsin General Market
en.overview: Ilsin General Market is a market street formed by roadside stalls and shops centered around Buil General Market near Bugae Station on Incheon Line 1. Initially remaining just as a commercial area surrounding Buil General Market, it was officially registered as Ilsin General Market in 2020 after integrating with Buil General Market. By registering as a formal traditional market, it receives business support to vitalize traditional markets, such as building a new parking lot and installing market roof arcades for merchants and residents.

en.overview: Located between Sipjeong-dong and Ganseok-dong near the Juan National Industrial Complex in Incheon, Yeoumul Traditional Market is a small, shopping-building-style traditional market featuring around 70 stores. Thanks to a market modernization project, it features arched roofing and neat organization, offering a clean and convenient shopping experience. There is a well-known galbitang (beef rib soup) restaurant here that has been featured on TV programs. Nearby, you will find several other markets, including Incheon Livestock Market, Ganseok General Market, Sinsing Dongam Fish Market, and Gongdan General Market.

en.title: Yeongjong Tourist Fish Market (영종관광어시장)
en.overview: Situated at Gubup Baeteo, which was once the only ferry pier connecting Yeongjongdo Island to the mainland, Yeongjong Tourist Fish Market is a two-story, building-style market housing numerous raw fish restaurants under one roof. Visitors can purchase fresh sliced raw fish (hoe), king crab, and shellfish on the first floor and enjoy them on the second floor by paying a separate table setting fee. It is a popular spot in the metropolitan area for enjoying fresh seafood while looking out at the sea. With several hotels located nearby, it is frequently visited by tourists looking to taste fresh seafood in a cozy atmosphere.

ja.overview: 永宗島と陸地を結ぶ唯一の船着き場だった九邑船着場（クウプベッテオ）に位置する永宗観光魚市場は、刺身店が一つの建物に集まっている2階建てのビル型市場です。1階で新鮮な刺身、キングクラブ、貝類を買い、2階で別途のセッティング料を払って食べられる仕組みになっています。首都圏で海を見ながら刺身が食べられる場所として、市場周辺にホテルが多数あり、観光客が刺身を味わうために訪れるアットホームな規模の市場です。

zh.overview: 坐落於過去連接永宗島與陸地的唯一渡口「九邑渡口（구읍뱃터）」，永宗觀光魚市場是一棟集結了許多生魚片店的兩層樓建築型市場。遊客可以在1樓購買新鮮的生魚片、帝王蟹與貝類，然後到2樓支付額外的人頭費（代客料理費）享用美食。這裡是首都圈內能夠邊看海邊品嚐生魚片的好去處，市場周邊有許多飯店，吸引許多觀光客前來品嚐海鮮，規模小巧溫馨。

en.overview: Oepohang Salted Seafood & Fisheries Direct Market is a specialized seafood market offering everything from fresh shrimp, octopus, squid, and clams to various salted seafood (jeotgal) like pollack roe and salted squid. Formerly operated as open-air stalls, the market is now equipped with modern arched roofing, providing a pleasant shopping environment. Every October, the Ganghwa Island Saeujeot (salted shrimp) Festival is held at Oepohang Port, drawing crowds of people purchasing salted seafood for kimchi-making season. The market also features raw fish restaurants where you can dine after shopping.

Through remodeling projects to revitalize the traditional market, arched roofing has been installed, and signage and pavement have been neatly arranged, allowing visitors to shop in a pleasant environment.

en.title: Jinheung General Market
en.overview: Jinheung General Market is a commercial building-style market established in 1979, and is currently Bupyeong's largest wholesale market. In 2019, it won the Ministry of SMEs and Startups Minister Award at the National Excellent Market Fair. The market consists of four buildings: Ga, Na, Da, and Ra, among which dried seafood is the most famous. In addition, it sells various items such as seafood, meat, diverse street foods, kitchenware, and daily necessities. In the past, it operated mainly as a wholesale market opening at dawn.

en.title: Tojigeumgo Market
en.overview: Tojigeumgo Market got its name after Tojigeumgo, the predecessor of the Korea Land Corporation, reclaimed salt pans and tidal flats in the 1970s to build a model housing complex, leading to the creation of a market in the area. Surrounded by apartment complexes, it is frequently visited by homemakers and operates about 130 stores. With well-organized roof arcades, walkways, and a home-delivery service, it is a very convenient market. It offers easy-to-go packed items.

en.title: Hagik Market
en.overview: Located in Hagik-dong, Michuhol-gu, Incheon, this traditional market was formed when factories moved into Hagik-dong in the 1960s, creating residential areas and merchants settling around them. Opened in 1962, it currently operates 65 stores. Although modernized and renovated, there are still many street vendors selling fish, vegetables, and fruits. It features small eateries such as dumpling shops, noodle houses, and gukbap (soup with rice) restaurants, alongside hardware stores and cosmetics shops typical of traditional markets.

en.title: Gangjin Ogamtong Market
en.overview: Gangjin Ogamtong Market is a premier cultural tourism-type market linked with tourism, infused with the traditional culture of Gangjin Bay under the vision of a wellbeing culture representing happiness, health, and life satisfaction. It connects Gangjin's 9 major tourist attractions—such as the poetry literature of Youngrang (famous for 'Until the Peonies Blossom'), Dasan Chodang, and the Goryeo Celadon Museum—with 5 major festivals including the Youngrang Literature Festival, Celadon Festival, and Maryang Port Festival. Discovering specialties and linked with the Ogamnuri Town, it is a wellbeing cultural tourism market full of happiness and life satisfaction.

en.title: Goheung Traditional Market
en.overview: Located in the center of Goheung-eup, Goheung Traditional Market bustles with merchants and residents on market days. Operating from early morning until afternoon, it mainly distributes food and clothing. The cattle market, which once had a narrow space, has been expanded and relocated to the outskirts. The market is rich in local specialties like reclaimed land rice, garlic, yuzu, pomegranates, and fresh seasonal seafood from clean waters. Among the various foods, charcoal-grilled fish is particularly famous, drawing many visitors.

en.overview: Opened shortly after 1945, this market is held every 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd, and 27th of the month. en.title: Neungju Traditional Market
en.overview: Neungju Traditional Market is a small, building-style market established in 1923, held every 5th and 10th of the month. The market mainly features agricultural products from Hwasun, offering plenty of sights to see during peach season. Due to various locally produced specialties, it is frequently visited by residents from nearby Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City. Although not large, it sells diverse items including fruits, vegetables, clothing, and side dishes. Enjoy the friendly and vibrant market atmosphere!

en.title: Damyang Market
en.overview: Damyang, home to world-famous bamboo groves, has been famous for bamboo since the Joseon Dynasty and is a primary production region for bamboo handicrafts. While Damyang has a long history of bamboo product manufacturing, the market itself was formed during the Japanese colonial period. The bamboo market is a specialized market unique to Damyang-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City, held along the dikeside walkway in Damju-ri, Damyang-eup. en.title: Daechi Market
en.overview: Located in Daechi-ri, Daejeon-myeon, Damyang-gun, Daechi Market is a traditional market primarily selling various agricultural goods and daily necessities. Main agricultural products of Daechi-ri include rice, barley, beans, and sesame, while specialties include cordyceps and cherry tomatoes. Although it once flourished, it now maintains its legacy on a 2,237㎡ site housing 25 stores. Daechi Market opens on days ending in 3 and 8.

en.title: Deogyang Market
en.overview: Located in Deogyang-ri, Sora-myeon, Yeosu-si, Deogyang Market was established in 1932. On market days, a small number of merchants conduct business, and restaurants selling beef gopchang (tripe) and beef cattle are particularly famous, drawing steady streams of visitors. Deogyang Market underwent an environmental improvement project in 2008 to upgrade restrooms and market building facilities, and is now well-known for its spacious parking lot, neat signboards, and delicious gopchang.

en.title: Dokcheonjang Market
en.overview: Opened on October 1, 1964, Dokcheon 5-Day Market is held every 4th and 9th day of the month (specifically on the 4th, 9th, 14th, 19th, 24th, and 29th). Spanning an area of 4,670㎡ with 934 stores, it thrives alongside some 200 nearby shops. Agricultural, marine, and livestock products are actively traded at this traditional market, which meets every five days. In the past, its cattle market was so bustling that 100 to 200 head of cattle were traded in a single day.

en.title: Maryang Noltto Fisheries Market
en.overview: Known as the Naples of Korea, Maryang Beautiful Port is a vital maritime transport hub connecting the mainland and Jeju Island. It is celebrated for its pristine living ocean, the evergreen forest of Maryang Gukam Island (a natural monument), and the scenic Maryang Gogeum Bridge. Held every Saturday, the Maryang Noltto Fisheries Market offers seafood of the 'highest freshness,' 'highest quality,' and 'lowest price.' It is a vibrant destination combining local Gangjin agricultural, livestock, and marine foods with cultural events like concerts.
