en.title: Mokpo Dried Seafood Street
en.overview: Located near Mokpo Port, Dried Seafood Street is where you can find an abundance of marine products from the Jeolla region all in one place. Lined with various dried seafood items such as brown croaker (mineo), fermented skate (hongeo), anchovies, and kelp, it is a popular shopping spot for locals and tourists alike. Many shops offer free samples, allowing visitors to taste various seafood before making a purchase.

en.title: Mokpo Dongbu Market
en.overview: Mokpo Dongbu Market is the largest market in Mokpo, boasting a 60-year history that began when street vendors started gathering one by one in 1956. Following construction work between 2006 and 2008 to install an arcade roof, it overcame the drawbacks of traditional markets to enhance convenience. It continually evolves by diversifying its customer base through the issuance of nationwide Onnuri gift certificates. It also features great facilities including a spacious parking lot and restrooms.

ja.title: 木浦東部市場
ja.overview: 木浦の東部市場は木浦で最も大きな市場で、1956年から露天商たちが一つ二つと集まって市場を形成し、現在の規模を備えた60年の歴史を誇る市場である。2006年から2008年にかけての工事を経てアーケードを設置し、在来市場の欠点を補うことで利便性を高め、全国共通の「オンヌリ商品券」を発行して顧客層の多様化を図るなど、絶えず変化している市場である。施設面でも広い駐車場やトイレが整備されている。

zh.overview: 木浦東部市場是木浦最大規模的市場，源自1956年路邊攤販陸續聚集而形成的具有60年歷史的傳統市場。經過2006年至2008年的整修加裝拱廊頂棚，改善了傳統市場的缺點並提升便利性；同時發行全國通用的「溫麗商品券」以吸引多元客群，是一個不斷求新求變的市場。在設施方面，也擁有寬敞的停車場與洗手間。

en.title: Mokpo Sinjungang Market
en.overview: Established in 1999, Mokpo Sinjungang Market is a small, commercial-building-style market. About 10 years after opening as a temporary market, it was registered as a traditional market (certified market) under the Special Act on the Promotion of Traditional Markets and Shopping Districts, entering the legal system and paving the way for revitalization. Since then, like other traditional markets, it has expanded its food and specialty offerings, and is particularly known as a clothing-centric market. Inside, you will find restaurants and clothing stores such as raw fish restaurants, pocha snack bars, sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup) eateries, hanbok shops, and shoe stores.

ja.title: 木浦新中央市場
ja.overview: 木浦新中央市場は1999年に開設された店舗ビル型の小型市場である。臨時市場としてオープンしてから約10年を経て、「伝統市場及び商店街育成のための特別法」に基づく伝統市場（認定市場）として登録され、制度圏に進入することで市場活性化への道が開かれた。その後、他の伝統市場と同様にグルメや特産品を充実させ、衣類が中心の市場として知られている。市場内には刺身店、屋台、スンデクッパ、韓服店、靴店などの飲食店や衣料品店が入っている。

zh.overview: 木浦新中央市場是1999年開辦的商場建築型小型市場。作為臨時市場開業約10年後，依據「傳統市場及商店街振興特別法」被註冊為傳統市場（認定市場），正式進入體制內，開啟了市場活化的契機。此後，如同其他傳統市場一樣，不斷補足美食與特產，目前以販售服飾為主而聞名。市場內設有生魚片店、布帳馬車小吃攤、血腸湯飯、韓服店、鞋店等餐飲與服飾店鋪。

en.title: Mokpo Jayu Market
en.overview: Mokpo Jayu Market is a merchant-run market established through an installment savings campaign initiated by the vendors themselves. Famous for its delicious food and high-quality products, it attracts customers not only from Mokpo but also from neighboring regions, boasting high sales. To impress customers, merchants wear name tags bearing store names alongside the phrase 'We will serve you with kindness,' and they have introduced a 100% exchange and refund policy to boost customer satisfaction. Furthermore, strong bonds among the merchants allow for autonomous operation.

ja.overview: 木浦自由市場は、商使たちが自ら積立運動を行って作り上げた商人のための市場である。美味しいグルメと質の高い商品のおかげで、木浦だけでなく近隣地域の顧客も訪れ、売上が高い市場としても有名である。「親切にお迎えいたします」という言葉とともに店舗名が書かれた名札を着用して顧客感動のために努力しており、100%交換・払戻制度を導入して顧客満足度を高めている。また、商人たちの団結力が強く、自主的な運営が行われている。

The market primarily deals in grains, cotton fabrics, bamboo crafts, chestnuts, bowls, daily sundries, and local specialties such as native honey and Dolsilmapo (traditional ramie fabric) from Seokgok-myeon.

en.title: Gongsan Market
en.overview: Gongsan-myeon is located about 12 km southwest of Naju City Hall, bordering Wanggok-myeon and Bannam-myeon to the east, Yeongam-gun to the south, Donggang-myeon to the west, and Hampyeong-gun to the north, with Mt. Gusubong and Mt. Gomunsan rising within the area. With the Yeongsan River flowing to the north and the Sampo River to the south, it is an agriculturally prosperous region blessed with convenient irrigation. Although smaller than in the past, a 5-day market still operates here on the 1st and 6th of every month, featuring grains and more.

You can purchase fresher seafood—ranging from fresh catches by small fishing boats and tidal flat marine life to sliced raw fish—than what is typically brought in from outside regions.

It is a great place to purchase various food items and goods, including Gwangyang's famous grilled chicken and fresh agricultural and marine products. With bakeries and restaurants available as well, a visit is highly recommended to enjoy a hearty meal and dessert.

en.title: Gurye 5-Day Market
en.overview: Along with Hwagae Market, the Gurye 5-Day Market has long been one of the representative countryside markets in the Yeonghonam region. Considerably larger than 5-day markets in other areas, it bustles with lively crowds gathering from Hadong, Gokseong, Namwon, Suncheon, Gwangyang, and beyond. It is especially famous for wild mountain herbs and medicinal ingredients, offering various wild greens harvested from Mt. Jirisan and Mt. Baegunsan—such as pine mushrooms, bracken, deodeok, aster greens, and Jakseolcha tea—as well as aster scaber greens, herbal medicines, and Gurye's specialty, cornus fruits (sansuyu).

en.title: Gurim Market
en.overview: Opened on May 19, 1966, the Gurim 5-Day Market is held every 2nd and 7th day of the cycle (the 2nd, 7th, 12th, 17th, 22nd, and 27th of every month). Spanning a site area of 6,606㎡ with 66 store buildings, the market buildings were renovated in 1998 to serve as a gathering place for local residents and a specialty sales point near tourist attractions. Depending on the season, it offers fresh, clean local agricultural products such as garlic, chili peppers, persimmons, bracken, deodeok, aralia shoots, chamnamul (ormer greens), and bellflower roots.

en.title: Naju Moksa Goeul Market
en.overview: Naju Moksa Goeul Market is a traditional market that carries on Naju's long-standing market culture, where you can experience the region's rich local produce and heritage. As part of an urban restoration project, Seongbuk Market and Geumgye Daily Market in downtown Naju were integrated to create the current market in 2012, and it was selected as a Culture and Tourism-type Market in 2013. Operating various cultural programs such as the Saturday Cultural Market and Saturday Night Market, it has established itself as a vibrant space enjoyed by both locals and tourists alike.

en.title: Namri Market
en.overview: Market days are the 3rd, 8th, 13th, 23rd, and 28th of every month. Most merchants reside in Haenam-eup, with some from Hwangsan-myeon, totaling around 100 vendors. en.title: Mokpo Chungho Market
en.overview: Mokpo Chungho Market is famous for its octopus, boasting the largest number of octopus vendors in the country. It is a vibrant market rich with a wide variety of seafood, including skate. Around 6 stalls specialize in skate, while most other seafood stalls focus primarily on octopus. Recognized as the top market among some 1,500 traditional markets nationwide for transparent country-of-origin labeling on seafood, it's a place where you can make purchases with confidence.

Muan is also famous for sweet potatoes, with over 60% of its farmland dedicated to them. Notably, the coastal areas feature reddish loamy soil, perfect for growing produce.

zh.title: 筏교場（筏橋五日市）
zh.overview: 1920年前後由日本人設立筏교水產株式會社，並以此為中心每日開設魚市場等開始發展。到了1930年代，為了將鄰近高興半島生產的農水產品運送至日本而開通鐵路，隨著筏교成長為據點商業城市，定期市場也自然蓬勃發展起來。光復後於1947年遷移至現今筏교邑筏교里2番地一帶的細網市場。

en.title: Seosijang Market
en.overview: A traditional market primarily dealing in seafood and clothing. Notably, Seosijang is located close to the Yeosu Coastal Ferry Terminal and the Yeosu Fisheries Cooperatives Cooperative Market, facilitating the trade of fresh and diverse seafood. The Pungmul Street inside Seosijang is frequently visited by out-of-town tourists looking for fresh fish and sliced raw fish (hoe). You can also expect warm hospitality in the food alley selling Deokyang gopchang hotpot, boiled pork head meat, and jokbal (trotters).

ja.title: 西市場（ソシジャン）
ja.overview: 水産物と衣類を主な取り扱う伝統市場です。特に西市場は麗水沿岸旅客ターミナルや麗水水産業協同組合公판場などに近い距離にあり、新鮮で多様な水産物が取引されています。西市場内にある風物通りは、新鮮な魚や刺身を探す遠方からの観光客が多く訪れます。徳陽（トクヤン）ホルモン鍋や豚の頭肉、豚足などを売るグルメ通りの温かい人情も期待できます。

zh.title: 西市場
zh.overview: 主要販售水產物與服飾的傳統市場。特別是西市場鄰近麗水沿岸客運碼頭與麗水水產業協同組合公判場等，因此有許多新鮮多樣的水產物在此交易。西市場內的風物街吸引了許多尋找新鮮魚類和生魚片的外地遊客前來造訪。在販售德陽烤腸火鍋、豬頭肉、豬腳等美食街裡，也能感受到滿滿的人情味。

en.title: Seokgok Traditional Market
en.overview: Established to increase national income through the smooth distribution of local agricultural products and to enhance the convenience of local residents. It is operated on a site spanning 5,371 square meters with wooden-tin buildings covering a total floor area of 952 square meters across 50 blocks, and is particularly famous for its cattle market. In the past, it was also called Dolsiljang or Dosiljang because there were many pebbles nearby.

en.title: Suncheon Araetjang Market
en.overview: Araetjang is located in Pungdeok-dong (along the Dongcheon stream) in Suncheon. As the largest traditional market in the Honam region, Suncheon Araetjang is the biggest among all 5-day markets nationwide. It has gained popularity as a food tourism destination where visitors can affordably purchase various agricultural and marine products produced around Suncheon, Yeosu, and Beolgyo. With a night market opening on Friday and Saturday nights, it has emerged as a hot spot favored by young people and tourists.

en.title: Suncheon Jungang Market
en.overview: Opened in 1981, Jungang Market is located in the heart of Suncheon's old downtown area, offering excellent accessibility. Surrounded by a trendy fashion street favored by the youth, the historic Gopchang (tripe) Alley, and the Okcheon waterfront cultural space, it blends shopping, local cuisine, and culture. Inside the market, you can find a variety of shops selling clothes, soft tofu (sundubu), mills, seafood, vegetables, fruits, rice cakes, bakeries, traditional sweets (yugwa), glutinous rice donuts, and dumplings.

ja.overview: 1981年にオープンした中央市場は、順天の旧都心の中心地に位置しており、アクセスの良さが抜群です。市場の周辺には、若い世代に人気のファッション通り、歴史と伝統を誇るホルモン（コプチャン）通り、玉川（オクチョン）の水辺文化空間などが隣接しており、ショッピング、グルメ、文化が調和した空間となっています。市場内には、洋服店、スンドゥブ店、精米所、海鮮店、野菜店、果物店、餅店、ベーカリー、ユガ（伝統菓子）、찹쌀도넛（찹쌀ドーナツ）、マンドゥなどを販売する多様な店舗が軒を連ねています。

en.overview: Sinbuk Market is located along National Route 13 in Sinbuk-myeon toward the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City area, opening every 3rd, 8th, 13th, 18th, 23rd, and 28th of the month. Nevertheless, it maintains its heritage and continues to hold a 5-day periodic market. Traded goods include locally produced grains and regional agricultural products.

en.title: Yeosu Gyodong Market
en.overview: Yeosu Gyodong Market is packed with fresh seafood caught from the clean waters of the front sea of Yeosu. Originally a small spot where fishermen spread out mats to sell their freshly caught fish, it has now grown into a substantial permanent market stretching about 1 kilometer long. With more open-air stall vendors than fixed shops, it offers a warm, cozy atmosphere reminiscent of a rural 5-day market rather than an urban market. As a dawn market, visiting early in the morning allows you to experience the bustling market energy and authentic local daily life.

ja.overview: 麗水矯洞市場は、きれいな麗水の沖合で獲れた新鮮な海産物がぎっしりと並ぶ場所です。もともとは魚介類を持ち寄って露店で販売していた小さな場所でしたが、現在は全長が1キロメートルに達するほどの相当な規模の常設市場へと発展しました。店舗というより露店が多く、都市の市場とは違って地方の5日市のような温かい雰囲気が感じられます。ここは朝市であるため、朝早く訪れることで、市場の活気や人々のリアルな暮らしぶりを見物することができます。

zh.overview: 麗水橋洞市場擺滿瞭從乾淨的麗水前海捕獲的新鮮海產。這裡原本是漁民帶回剛捕獲的魚貨後擺地攤販售的小地方，如今已發展成全長達1公里、相當規模的常設市場。由於露天攤販比一般店面更多，因此比起都市市場，更能感受到地方五日市般溫馨人情味。這裡屬於早市，需趁清晨前往，才能欣賞到市場忙碌的熱鬧氛圍與濃厚的人情生活面貌。

en.title: Yeosu Seafood Specialty Market
en.overview: Yeosu Seafood Specialty Market is one of Yeosu's specialized markets featuring raw fish restaurants where export-strategic marine species freshly caught from the Yeosu sea—such as fish, sea cucumbers, small octopus, sea squirts, and blue crabs—are kept in aquariums and prepared on the spot. About 100 merchants operate here. Seawater pumped from near Dolsan Bridge is purified and sterilized to supply the aquariums at each stall, maintaining the freshness of the live fish. An online seafood shopping mall is also operated.

In particular, Yeosu Seafood Market offers affordable prices and rare species not easily found in metropolitan seafood markets, such as monkfish, rockfish, and mackerel pike for raw slicing.

en.title: Yeokjeon Market (Suncheon)
en.overview: Opened in 1979, Yeokjeon Market is a mid-sized shopping center-style traditional market rich in diverse sights. Traditional markets in downtown Suncheon include Ujang and Arajang, alongside permanent markets like Yeokjeon Market and Jungang Market. While Ujang and Arajang are widely known to tourists as cultural tourism-themed markets, Yeokjeon Market is a daily life-oriented traditional market frequently visited by Suncheon citizens. Moreover, restaurants from neighboring areas such as Yeosu and Gwangyang come here starting early in the dawn to purchase fresh ingredients.

en.title: Yeonggwang Chili Pepper Specialty Market
en.overview: Yeonggwang Chili Pepper Specialty Market originated from a chili trading section within the 5-day market formed at Hantjeon Intersection in Yeonggwang-eup, Yeonggwang-gun, Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated City, and was officially designated as a specialty market in April 1995. 'Yeonggwang Taeyangcho' (sun-dried chili) grown in Yeonggwang's fertile red clay nurtured by sea breezes and dried in sunlight and wind features a vibrant red color and thick flesh.

In the past, transactions of Yedang rice exceeded 500 bags, and most were directly shipped to major cities such as Busan and Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Metropolitan City by professional wholesale merchants. The market has shifted from a focus on polished rice and grain trade to a small-scale trade of miscellaneous grains.

en.title: Wando Traditional Market
en.overview: The fishery industry has thrived here since ancient times, and the fishing style is currently transitioning from capture fisheries to aquaculture. Surrounded by the sea on all sides, the area is blessed with abundant tourism resources and rich fishery resources everywhere. In particular, the freshness of sea bream, flounder, abalone, and sea bass produced in the clean waters is renowned as the best in the country, and seaweed, brown seaweed, and kelp are great for preventing adult diseases and women's skin care. Wando Market opens every 5 days based on dates ending in 5, maintaining a traditional market atmosphere.

en.overview: Jeongnamjin Jangheung Saturday Market is a bustling traditional market where you can find both fresh agricultural and marine products. The regular market offers a rich variety of fish and shellfish caught along the southern coast, as well as fertile agricultural produce grown near the Tamjingang River basin.

en.title: Joseong Market (조성시장)
en.overview: Joseong 5-Day Market dates back to the late Joseon Dynasty, originally established as 'Joseongwon Market' in front of the current health center near Joseong Station. Because residents from Daeseo-myeon and Donggang-myeon in Goheung-gun also used it, it formed a relatively large trading hub with a lively atmosphere. With the opening of the railway in the 1930s improving transportation, the grain market flourished so much that rice was traded from early morning until late afternoon.

en.overview: Located behind the Gwangyang Intercity Bus Terminal, Jungma Market resembles a large outlet building rather than a traditional market from the outside. The inside is much the same. Visitors and locals alike flock here to buy fresh, wild raw fish at about 70% of the price charged by nearby raw fish restaurants. In addition, it offers fresh vegetables, manufactured goods, dried seafood, side dishes, street food, pottery, and jewelry.

en.overview: Changpyeong Traditional Market holds its 5-day market on dates ending in 5 and 10. The market offers local specialties such as traditional Korean confectioneries (hangwa), bamboo salt, and rice taffy (ssalyeot), alongside agricultural products and daily necessities. In particular, the Changpyeong Gukbap (gukbap/soup with rice) Street is right next door, making it a great place to enjoy a hearty bowl of gukbap followed by rice taffy or hangwa for dessert.

en.title: Sunchang Market
en.overview: Located in Namgye-ri, Sunchang-eup, Sunchang-gun, Jeollabuk-do, Sunchang Market was established with the construction of traditional market buildings in 1923 and is held every 1st and 6th of the month. It is famous for agricultural products like chili peppers, rice, and beans, as well as its 'Sundae Alley' selling Sunchang's specialty traditional blood sausage. In the 1960s and 70s, it thrived as one of the top 7 cattle markets in the country, attracting about 5,000 visitors a day, with embroidery merchants flocking from all over for its famous embroidery products.

en.title: Shinyoung Market (Gunsan)
en.overview: Located in Jungang-dong, Shinyoung Market is a compact market formed in the 1980s when street vendors from the public market parking area were relocated to the current site on Korea Railroad Authority land and the covered stream area. Currently consisting of about 120 stores, it features rain-shielding facilities so visitors can conveniently shop even on rainy days. Products sold include Pacific saury, salted seafood, vegetables, yellow corvina, blue crabs, mackerel, tongue sole, and various shellfish.

en.title: Yeosan Market
en.overview: The exact origin of Yeosan Market is not precisely recorded, but since ancient times, it has served as a treasure trove of daily necessities. Historically, a wood market was held here alongside fish, dried seafood, fabrics, and general daily goods flowing in from Ganggyeong, as well as firewood for fuel. Today, the market primarily deals in vegetables, clothing, household goods, and miscellaneous items, with garlic and chili peppers as seasonal staples.

en.title: Wonpyeong Public Market
en.overview: Located in Geumsan-myeon, Gimje-si, Wonpyeong Public Market is a traditional market with a long history dating back to the reign of King Seonjo in the Joseon Dynasty. It is known as a historic site where the Donghak Peasant Revolution was actively centered around the Wonpyeong marketplace. Furthermore, it was a site of the March 1st Independence Movement during the Japanese colonial period, imbuing the market with the spirit of national autonomy and independence. Today, periodic 5-day markets are held here.

It sells a variety of items including vegetables, fruits, meat, fish, dried seafood, clothing, and sundries, and is characterized by the steady supply of fresh agricultural products produced in neighboring areas such as Wanju. All around the market, visitors can taste Jeonju's various foods and experience the vibrant merchants and friendly atmosphere.

en.title: Jeongeup Shintaein Market
en.overview: During the Japanese colonial period, Shintaein was renowned as the city with the highest grain trade volume in the Honam region. Operating as a traditional 5-day periodic market since the 1910s, Shintaein Market was newly reopened on December 30, 2008, following a market modernization project. A key feature of the market is its generally affordable seafood prices. It is also located in a major chili pepper production hub, allowing visitors to purchase top-quality chili peppers and fine chili powder produced at the Shintaein Agricultural Cooperative processing plant.

Originally called 'Jeongeup 2nd Market,' it was renamed 'Jeongeup Yeonji Market' in July 2011 to better reflect the local identity and characteristics. en.title: Julpo Market
en.overview: In the past, Julpo served as a major collection and distribution hub for agricultural and marine products in the southern part of Buan-gun. Alongside Beopseongpo in Jeollanam-do and Seocheon in Chungcheongnam-do, it was one of the three major ports on the southern west coast. During the yellow croaker fishing season, numerous brokers gathered from the Chilsan and Wido fishing grounds for active trade and distribution of croakers and salted seafood. Although the reclamation of Gomso Bay changed its landscape, the market continues its long tradition since the late Joseon Dynasty, actively trading grains, fish, and salted seafood.

zh.title: 茁浦市場
zh.region_label: 全羅北道扶安郡茁浦面
zh.overview: 過去的茁浦是扶安郡南部農水產品交易的重要物資集散地。與全羅南道的法聖浦、忠清南道的舒川並列為南部西海岸的三大港口。在大黃魚漁汛期，七山漁場與衛島近海漁場會聚集許多客商，大黃魚與鹹魚類的集散與買賣非常熱絡。雖然隨著곰소（格浦/熊梭）灣的填海造陸，往日的輝煌已不復見，但作為自朝鮮時代末期起便因客商活動而影響深遠的市場，至今仍活躍於穀物、魚類及鹹魚類的交易。

en.title: Jinan Plateau Market
en.overview: Jinan, along with Muju and Jangsu, is part of the representative highland region commonly referred to as 'Mujinjang.' Being a region surrounded by mountains, exchange among residents and logistics distribution were historically difficult, which naturally led to the development of 5-day periodic markets. Jinan Plateau Market was reorganized into a building-style market in February 2010 and operates as a permanent market, while still hosting a traditional 5-day market every 4th and 9th day. On market days, over a hundred stalls fill the area, creating a vibrant and lively atmosphere.

ja.overview: 鎮安（チナン）は茂朱、長寿とともにいわゆる「無珍長」とも呼ばれる代表的な高原地帯である。山に囲まれた地域であるだけに、住民間の交流や物資の流通が容易ではなかったため、5日市が発達した。鎮安高原市場は2010年2月に建物型市場として施設を整備し常設市場として運営されているが、現在も4日と9日ごとに5日市が一緒に開かれる。5日市が立つ日には百余りの店舗が立ち並び、市場活気に満ち溢れる。

zh.region_label: 全羅北道鎮安郡鎮安邑
zh.overview: 鎮安與茂朱、長수（長壽）並稱為「無珍長」的代表性高原地區。由於是群山環繞的地區，居民之間的交流與物資流通並不容易，因而促使五日集市蓬勃發展。鎮安高原市場於2010年2月整頓為建築型市場並作為常設市場營運，但至今仍會在每逢4號與9號時舉行五日集市。到了集市日，上百個攤位熱鬧進駐，整個市場充滿了蓬勃朝氣。

en.title: Chaeseokgang Seafood Market
en.overview: Located at the entrance of Chaeseokgang, Chaeseokgang Seafood Market is a commercial seafood market where visitors can buy and taste the freshest live fish and seafood in Buan. Styled like a raw fish restaurant complex on the first floor, it sells wild-caught live fish (as well as farmed varieties) such as flathead mullet, rockfish, red seabream, and greenling, alongside various seafood including tiger prawns, webfoot octopus, hard-shelled clams, abalone, turban shells, pen shells, and scallops.

en.title: Chunhyanggol Public Market
en.overview: Situated in the heart of Namwon, Chunhyanggol Public Market is the city's representative central market and the largest traditional market in Namwon. While operating as a permanent market, a traditional 5-day market also opens on the 4th and 9th of the month. Offering a diverse range of items including food, clothing, general goods, herbal medicines, and local eateries, its long history makes it a warm marketplace brimming with nostalgic charm. Visitors can enjoy vitalized local commerce and purchase fresh agricultural and specialty products grown in Namwon.

en.title: Hamyeol Market
en.overview: Hamyeol Market originated in Geumseong-myeon during the late Joseon Dynasty and later developed at its current location during the Japanese colonial period after briefly operating near Hamyeol Station. From the 1950s to the 1970s, it flourished as a distribution hub for goods coming from Ganggyeong and Ungpo. However, with the introduction of city buses around 1975, commercial activity shifted heavily toward nearby Iksan, causing the market to shrink. Today, it operates as a 5-day periodic market offering vegetables, clothing, miscellaneous goods, fish, and fruits.

en.title: Hwangdeung Market
en.overview: Hwangdeung Market is a traditional market formed during the Joseon Dynasty. Fueled by goods such as fish, salted seafood (jeotgal), and salt flowing in from Napo and Gomgae (now Ungpo), it was quite large for a rural market. During the 1940s to 1960s, its cattle market and horsehair headband (manggeon) market thrived together. Today, a permanent market has formed due to local industries like stone processing, but the 5-day periodic market still operates. Seasonal agricultural trading is particularly active, with spring sweet potato shoots enjoying great popularity.

en.title: Goseong 5-Day Market
en.overview: Goseong Market is located in Goseong-ri, the village housing the Seongsan-eup Office near Seongsan Ilchulbong Peak, a major tourist attraction in eastern Jeju Island, right along National Route 12. After relocating to its current site in 1984, it has grown into a relatively large 5-day market utilized not only by Seongsan-eup residents but also by those from nearby Udo-myeon and Gujwa-eup. You can experience a distinct rural market atmosphere quite different from urban 5-day markets. It offers fruits and vegetables, marine products, meat, daily necessities, clothing, farming tools, and general goods.

zh.overview: 大靜五日市場於韓戰時期開業，是濟州島西部地區規模最大的五日集市。由於位於摹瑟浦，因此也被稱為摹瑟浦五日場。據說當時大靜邑設有飛機場與陸軍訓練所，隨著所需的生活用品與物資來往頻繁，市場規模逐漸擴大，自然而然地形成了市場。在大靜邑內幾經搬遷後，現落腳於大靜邑下摹里。正如其龐大的規模，常吸引許多船員與當地居民造訪。

en.title: Dongmun Public Market
en.overview: Jeju Dongmun Public Market is connected to Dongmun Traditional Market, one of Jeju's oldest traditional markets, making it a popular spot to experience a traditional Jeju atmosphere. Here, you can enjoy various regional traditional foods like black pork, meat noodles (gogi-guksu), and omegi rice cakes, alongside Jeju specialties such as tangerines, tilefish (okdom), and hairtail (galchi). It is very convenient for picking up gifts or souvenirs on the way to the airport, prompting many travelers to visit at the end of their itinerary.

en.title: Dongmun Seafood Market
en.overview: Opened in 1970, Jeju Dongmun Seafood Market is a specialized seafood market in Jeju that sells fresh marine products caught on the same day. It primarily sells Jeju silver hairtail, tilefish, and mackerel sashimi. In addition to fresh seafood like abalone and damselfish (jari), it also offers salted seafood and dried fish. With affordable prices, you can enjoy fresh, high-quality raw fish at a reasonable cost. A customized service allows customers to purchase items of their choice directly at the market and enjoy them freshly prepared at a nearby restaurant.

en.title: Dongmun Traditional Market
en.overview: Dongmun Traditional Market is a long-standing traditional market and one of the most representative markets in Jeju Island. Together with the Dongmun Seafood Market, it forms the most important and largest permanent traditional market in Jeju. It first formed right after liberation in August 1945, serving as Jeju's only permanent market at the time and acting as the base for all commercial activity on the island. After a massive fire in March 1954 reduced the entire market to ashes, it was rebuilt the same year.

Situated in a coastal town, it features a variety of shops selling fresh seafood and daily necessities, alongside local treats like mung beanjeon and sea urchin gimbap.

en.title: Boseong Market
en.overview: Located within the old downtown of Jeju, Boseong Market is a traditional market that has maintained its place for over 50 years since its opening in 1972. It offers a glimpse into the lives of Jeju-si merchants through its uniquely nostalgic atmosphere. The market features a wide variety of shops, including restaurants, butcher shops, seafood vendors, dried fish stores, bakeries, rice cake shops, and tailoring services. Abundant market foods are a must-try, with Jeju-style traditional sundae (blood sausage) being the top specialty in the densely packed restaurant area.

en.overview: Bullanji Night Market is located at the entrance of Jungmun 5-Day Market. 'Bullanji' is the Jeju dialect for firefly, and the market lights up as darkness falls over Jungmun. From fresh sliced raw fish to pajeon (scallion pancakes), toast, duruchigi (stir-fried pork and vegetables), and meat noodles, visitors can enjoy choosing food to suit their budget and palate. The night market consists of about 8 food stalls, with the outdoor seating area being particularly popular over the indoor space. Grab an outdoor table of your choice and enjoy your favorite food.

zh.title: 西歸浦每日 올레（Olleh）市場
zh.overview: 西歸浦每日Olleh市場是位於西歸浦市中心的傳統市場，也是西歸浦市內規模最大、歷史最悠久的常設市場。365天總是擠滿了濟州居民與遊客，對活化地方經濟扮演著重要角色。過去這裡和一般市場一樣販售農水產品、工業製品與衣物等，但近年來主要以西歸浦特產橘子、漢拏峰柑橘、鮮魚及黑豬肉為主。吸引了眾多觀光客前來尋寶。

en.title: Seogwipo Hyangto 5-Day Market
en.overview: Seogwipo Hyangto 5-Day Market is a representative 5-day periodic market in Seogwipo-si, opened in 1995 and held every 4th and 9th day of the month. Maintaining its long-standing tradition alongside its large scale, the market is neatly organized into clear sections, making it pleasant to explore. Offering a variety of goods ranging from seasonal fruits, fresh seafood, and vegetables to cute miscellaneous goods and clothing, it is a popular destination for both locals and tourists alike. It established the nation's first customer service charter and features various amenities.

ja.title: 西帰浦郷土五日市場
ja.overview: 西帰浦郷土五日市場は、西帰浦市を代表する五日市場（5日ごとに開かれる市場）で、1995年に開設され毎月4日と9日に開催されます。大きな規模とともに長い伝統を誇り、区画がすっきりと整理されていて見て回るのに最適です。旬の果物や新鮮な水産物、野菜などの食べ物をはじめ、可愛らしい雑貨や衣類まで多様な商品を販売しており、道民と観光客の双方が訪れる市場です。全国初の顧客サービス憲章を制定し、様々な便宜施設を備えています。

zh.overview: 西歸浦鄉土五日市場是代表西歸浦市的五日集市，於1995年開市，每逢國曆4日、9日營業。除了規模龐大、歷史悠久外，區域規劃整齊清爽，非常適合漫步參觀。這裡販售當季水果、新鮮水產、蔬菜等美食，以及精美雜貨與衣物等多樣化商品，是當地居民與遊客都會造訪的市場。這裡制定了全國首例的顧客服務憲章，並備有多樣化的便利設施。

en.title: Seomun Public Market
en.overview: Seomun Public Market is a traditional 60-year-old market located in the western center of Jeju-si. Comprising about 80 stores, it has been designated as a specialized market for meat consumption, particularly livestock and butcher products, recording the most active meat consumption in Jeju Island. The market houses three butcher marts. After purchasing your desired cuts of meat at affordable prices, you can head to the restaurant building where butcher-style dining rooms are located, pay a table setting fee, and grill and enjoy your meat on the spot.

ja.title: 西門公設市場
ja.overview: 西門公設市場は、済州市の西部中心部に位置する60年の歴史を持つ伝統的な常設市場です。約80の店舗を備えており、畜産や精肉など肉類消費の特化市場に選定され、済州道内で最も活発に肉類が消費されている場所です。市場内には3つの精肉マートがあります。希望する部位の肉を安く購入した後、精肉食堂が入った商店街の建物に向かうと、セッティング代（上膳料）を支払ってその場で買った肉を焼いて食べることができます。

zh.overview: 西門公設市場位於濟州市西部中心，是一座擁有60年歷史的傳統市集。擁有約80間店舖，被選定為肉品消費特化市場（特別是畜產與肉舖），是濟州道內肉品消費最熱絡的地方。市場內設有3間精肉超市。以實惠的價格購買想要的肉品部位後，前往設有精肉餐廳的商街大樓，支付代客料理費（桌費）就可以當場享用剛買的肉。

en.title: Seobudu Seafood Market
en.overview: Located a 15-minute drive from Jeju International Airport, Seobudu Seafood Market is a National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (Suhyup) distribution center where you can find fresh seasonal fish at affordable prices. Every early morning, freshly caught fish arrive at the pier and go up for auction. Once the auction ends, visitors can browse seasonal fish and various foods, but you need to go early in the morning to experience it. It sells a variety of live seafood, including Jeju's specialty silver cutlassfish, filefish, tilefish, and bigfin reef squid.
en.practical_header: Check Before You Go · Market Days · Items Sold · Parking · Amenities

ja.title: 西埠頭（ソブドゥ）水産市場
ja.overview: 済州国際空港から車で15分の距離にある西埠頭水産市場は、新鮮な旬の魚をリーズナブルな価格で購入できる水協（水産業協同組合）の公品場です。毎早朝、獲れたての魚が埠頭を通って搬入され、競りにかけられます。競りが終わると旬の魚や各種グルメを見学できますが、早朝に行かなければ見ることができません。済州の特産品であるタチウオからカワハギ、アマダイ、アオリイカなど、様々な活魚を販売しています。
ja.practical_header: お出かけ前の確認 · 開催日 · 販売品目 · 駐車場 · 施設

zh.title: 西埠頭水產市場
zh.overview: 西埠頭水產市場距離濟州國際空港車程約15分鐘，是水協（水產業協同組合）公營批發市場，能以實惠的價格買到新鮮的當季漁獲。每天清晨，剛捕獲的鮮魚會透過碼頭運送並進行拍賣。拍賣結束後可以參觀當季鮮魚與各種美食，但必須一大早去才看得到。這裡販售濟州特產白帶魚、剝皮魚、馬頭魚、萊氏擬魷魚等各種活海鮮。

en.title: Seehwa Folk 5-Day Market
en.overview: Seehwa Folk 5-Day Market is conveniently located near the four-way intersection in downtown Seehwa, offering great accessibility. It is a traditional Jeju market where residents and merchants mingle to buy and sell goods, allowing visitors to catch a glimpse of the genuine lives of Jeju people. Like most traditional markets in Korea, it is a 5-day periodic market, featuring a wide variety of goods at affordable prices.

en.overview: Despite its designated location, Jeju City Folk 5-Day Market is a popular public marketplace for locals and visitors alike, thanks to its affordable prices and favorable conditions. Held once every five days, the market is loved by people of all ages, from children to the elderly.

zh.overview: 儘管位於指定地點，濟州市民俗五日市場憑藉物美價廉等優勢，不僅吸引濟州市區居民，連外地遊客也經常造訪，是濟州當地民眾喜愛的國民商圈。因此，市場具備綜合商圈的特點，涵蓋餐飲業、服飾業以及日常生活所需的各種必需品。這是個每5天營業一次的傳統市場，深受從長者到小孩等各年齡層的喜愛。

en.title: Jungmun Local 5-Day Market
en.overview: Located in the heart of the Jungmun Tourist Complex, Jungmun Local 5-Day Market originated in the 1950s with war refugees and officially opened in 1965, carrying a long history to this day. This traditional 5-day market is where local Jeju residents shop for homegrown agricultural produce and seafood caught along the coast. While smaller than Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market or Jeju Folk 5-Day Market, it offers plenty of local sights and charm.

en.title: Pyoseon 5-Day Market
en.overview: Pyoseon 5-Day Market is a small, charming market located in downtown Pyoseon where you can experience the warm hospitality of southern Jeju. Held on every 2nd and 7th of the month, the market is divided into three buildings: the main building selling daily necessities and agricultural goods, a fish market offering fresh seasonal seafood, and a small dining area serving sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup) and gogi guksu (pork noodle soup). The fish market, adjacent to Pyoseon Port, is especially great for getting top-quality seafood at reasonable prices.

en.title: Hallim Maeil Market
en.overview: In Hallim, Jeju, there are two types of markets: the Hallim 5-Day Market, held every five days, and Hallim Maeil Market, a permanent daily market. Although smaller than other daily markets, Hallim Maeil Market is well-stocked with agricultural, livestock, and marine products, as well as clothing, interior shops, and side-dish stores. Rather than being a tourist-oriented market, it is primarily frequented by local residents, offering an authentic and unpretentious local vibe. Deep inside the market, you'll find a famous spot known for sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup).

en.title: Ganggyeong Daeheung Market
en.overview: Ganggyeong-eup in Nonsan-si, Chungcheongnam-do is famous for Ganggyeong Port and Ganggyeong salted seafood (jeotgal). The history of Ganggyeong Market dates back to the late 17th century around the Ganggyeongcheon Stream. By the late 19th century, it emerged as a major market, famously ranked alongside the markets of Daegu and Pyongyang as one of the 'Joseon Top 3 Markets' (1st Pyongyang, 2nd Ganggyeong, 3rd Daegu), boasting deep tradition and history. Ganggyeong Daeheung Market was established in October 1955 to carry on Ganggyeong's legacy as a commercial city, originating from the first 5-day traditional market.

en.title: Kanggyeong Jeotgal Market (Fermented Seafood Market)
en.overview: Kanggyeong Jeotgal Market is a specialty market naturally formed within the town of Ganggyeong-eup, Nonsan. Reaching its peak in the 1930s, its geographic location on the lower Geumgang River and intersection with the Honam Railway made it a major transportation hub connecting both the West Sea and the inland. Consequently, it thrived as a bustling trading center for various seafood, centering around jeotgal (salted fermented seafood). Even after river transport on the Geumgang declined, this tradition continued, and today it has grown into the nation's largest jeotgal market, where visitors can purchase a wide variety of salted seafood at very affordable prices.

en.overview: Opened in 1937, Gongju Sanseong Market is a traditional market with deep historical and cultural roots, located right below the fortress walls of Gongsanseong Fortress, the royal palace site of the Baekje Kingdom. Notably, 'SoriMaru', a radio station run by the market merchants, plays a major role in revitalizing the market.

en.title: Geumsan Geumbit Market
en.overview: Also known as Geumsan Jang, Geumsan Geumbit Market is a traditional market located in the downtown area of Geumsan-gun. en.overview: First opened in 1971, Nonsan Hwaji Central Market is located in Daegyo-dong, Nonsan-si, Chungcheongnam-do. Hwaji Central Market is packed with fresh food and offers a wide variety of ingredients at affordable prices.

en.title: Daecheon Port Seafood Market
en.overview: Daecheon Port Seafood Market is situated at the entrance of Daecheon Port. It is a permanent market where you can purchase various freshly caught seafood brought in by Boryeong fishermen. en.overview: Namwon Yongnam Market was a representative market of Namwon until the early 1970s and was once famous for its water dropwort (minari) cultivation fields. Located close to Chunhyanggol Market and Gwanghalluwan Garden, it is in a prime spot to explore alongside nearby attractions. en.title: Namwon Inwol Market (남원인월시장)
en.overview: Inwol Market is a traditional market utilized by residents of Jeolla-do and Gyeongsang-do since the late Joseon Dynasty. Opening every 5 days, it started with the sale of local agricultural specialties and the barter of daily necessities. Later, the current Inwol Traditional Market was established, serving residents of Inwol-myeon, Ayong-myeon, Sannae-myeon, Macheon-myeon, Unbong-myeon, Hamyang-myeon, and Beonam-myeon. Serving as a major transportation hub connecting Jeolla-do and Gyeongsang-do, it acts as a marketplace of harmony for residents of both regions. The market is located at the entrance of Jirisan Mountain.

en.overview: Namwon Public Market is Namwon's representative permanent traditional market, established in 1970 near Gwanghalluwan Garden by relocating the outer-castle market that used to open across the Yocheon Stream after the Japanese Invasions of Korea (Imjin War). It is fully stocked with all daily necessities including clothing, general merchandise, bowls, dried fish, fresh fish, fruits, and ancestral ritual items, while also selling local specialties such as Jirisan medicinal herbs, Namwon knives, and woodenware. Popular local foods include traditional sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup) unique to Namwon Market, sweetfish (uneo) sashimi, chueotang (loach soup), and wild vegetable set meals.

en.title: Biin Market
en.overview: Biin Market is a major market in northern Seocheon-gun, historically famous in the winter for trading seafood, especially laver (gim). Today, trade centers mainly around agricultural grains, seafood, sundries, and daily necessities. Along with the Ganchi Market in Moryeong-gun to the north, it is a large gathering place for merchants and locals alike. Biin-myeon, where the market is held, is located in the mountainous terrain at the tail end of the Charyeong Mountain Range, with Wolmyeongsan Mountain rising in the center.

en.title: Seocheon Special Market
en.overview: Seocheon Special Market is a historic market in downtown Seocheon where a 5-day periodic market has been held since the Joseon Dynasty. However, the market was previously located elsewhere. As the population and number of merchants grew, the commercial district expanded, leading to the relocation to the current site. Consequently, the old market site is called 'Gu-jangteo' (old market), and the current one is called 'Sae-jangteo' (new market). Entering the 21st century, it was rebuilt as a modern 2-story specialized market featuring a seafood market on the 1st floor and restaurants on the 2nd floor.

en.title: Yeokjeon Market (Yesan)
en.overview: Yesan Yeokjeon Market is a medium-sized commercial building-style traditional market located in Yesan-gun, Chungnam, first opened in 1955. A regular market is held on the 3rd and 8th of every month, serving as part of the 5-day market network around Oga-myeon, Yesan. Its main items include homegrown agricultural products such as chili peppers, sesame seeds, and Yesan apples. Notably, due to the increased distribution of fresh vegetables including Yesan apples and its convenient transportation right in front of Yesan Station, it is a place easily accessible to many visitors.

en.title: Chupungnyeong Market (추풍령장)
en.overview: Yeongdong-gun in Chungcheongbuk-do has six traditional markets, including Yeongdong, Yongsan, Hwanggan, Chupungnyeong, Sangchon, and Haksan markets. Among them, Chupungnyeong Market is a 5-day periodic market held on dates ending in 3 and 8 (the 3rd, 8th, 13th, 18th, 23rd, and 28th of every month). The main crops cultivated in Chupungnyeong-myeon include rice, grapes, apples, and chili peppers. Historically, Chupungnyeong rice has been nationally recognized for its clear and transparent grains and exceptional taste, and the rice is milled directly on-site.

en.overview: A regular traditional market held every 5 days around Chungui-dong, Chungju-si, Chungcheongbuk-do. en.overview: A traditional market located in the heart of Chungju-si, established on December 30, 1964, as part of the government's market policy for small merchants. en.title: Yeonsan Market
en.overview: Yeonsan Market is located in Yeonsan-ri, Yeonsan-myeon, Nonsan-si, Chungcheongnam-do. Opened in 1911, it is a small, combined commercial and residential building-style market held every 5th and 10th day of the month. In the 1950s and 60s, it was a bustling market that even drew shoppers from neighboring areas, but its scale gradually shrank as the rural population declined from the 1980s onward. It offers a nostalgic glimpse into a traditional countryside market, making it a great stop during your travels. Located close to Yangchon (Hipass) IC.

en.overview: Cheonan Yeokjeon Market was formed around Cheonan Station in 1951 right after the Korean War as refugees gathered in the area. Connected to the Seoul Metropolitan Subway Line 1 via Cheonan Station, it is easily accessible by public transport and blends traditional charm with modern elements. zh.region_label: 忠清南道天安市東南區
zh.overview: 天安站前市場於1951年韓戰結束後不久，隨著難民湧入天安站周邊而逐漸形成。於1955年正式被認定為天安公設市場並沿用至今。由於透過天安站與首都圈地鐵1號線相連，遊客可搭乘大眾交通工具輕鬆抵達，是一個完美融合傳統與現代的景點。結合青年創業與都市再生計畫，市場內進駐了青年創業店舖、烘焙坊、咖啡廳、多元文化餐飲店、流行服飾及其他零售商店。

en.title: Cheongyang Market
en.overview: Cheongyang Market originated from a rural market set up along the streams of Cheongyang-eup and settled in its current location in 1971. Today, it operates simultaneously as a permanent market and a 5-day periodic market held on days ending in 2 and 7. Cheongyang-gun is a mountainous, remote area with limited farmland, featuring the rugged and deep Chilgaksan Mountain, the highest in the county. Gogi-ja (goji berries) harvested from the foothills of Chilgaksan Mountain are Cheongyang Market's signature specialty. Goji berries are known to purify the blood, help clear acne or boils, and prevent adult diseases.

en.title: Taean Seobu Market (Taean West Market)
en.overview: In Taean-eup, which travelers bound for the sea often rush past, lies Seobu Market, filled with warm laughter and generous hospitality. Along with fresh seafood from the Taean sea, grandmothers neatly display hand-picked spring greens such as shepherd's purse, mugwort, and water dropwort, waiting for customers. Long-established local eateries are hidden away in every corner. Grab a shopping basket and fill it with the vibrant spring of Taean at a traditional market where they say they have 'everything except what doesn't exist.'

en.overview: Located in Taean, Taean Dongbu Market was established in 1918. In the mid-1980s, the old market buildings were demolished and rebuilt into modern concrete shopping buildings, establishing it as the representative permanent market of the Taean region. Currently, about 100 stores operate in Taean Dongbu Market, offering a wide variety of goods including local agricultural and marine products, clothing, general merchandise, and manufactured goods. Taean Dongbu Market is famous for its dried seafood specialty stores, raw fish centers, and various street foods.

en.title: Pangyo Market
en.overview: Pangyo Market was originally located in the center of Pangyo-ri, but moved to its current location in Hyeonam-ri following liberation. In the past, it was famous as a base camp where peddlers (bubusang) gathered to trade goods. The cattle market here was also widely known, and it is said that up to 100 cattle were traded in a single day at one time. Traded items include agricultural products, clothing, and general merchandise. Although it was a large traditional market when it first opened, it faced a decline in the 1980s with the opening of distribution industries and a sharp decrease in the rural population.

en.title: Hansan 5-Day Market
en.overview: The Hansan 5-Day Market is held on the 1st, 6th, 11th, 16th, 21st, and 26th of every month between the Hansan Terminal and Hansan Elementary School. There are also alley shops that stay open every day even when the market is not officially operating. Although registered as a regular market in 1956, it is said to have been established before the Joseon Dynasty. At the vegetable street near the market entrance, you can find a rich variety of vegetables and mixed grains such as spinach, radishes, carrots, shepherd's purse, and mugwort. At the fish stall, you can see Seocheon's specialty, dabde (half-beak/flatfish).

en.overview: Hapdeok Market, also known as Bergeunae Market, was nationally famous, and in the past, many merchants from nearby Cheonan and Asan would visit. Located in a plain region, its main traded items include a large volume of agricultural products. Because it is not far from the sea, a wide variety of seafood can also be found alongside plenty of manufactured goods necessary for daily life. The market developed significantly when the township (myeon) was promoted to a town (eup) in 1973. It has currently been rebuilt and reopened with modernized facilities.

Separated from Chungju Public Market by the Chungjucheon Stream, Muhak Market naturally formed alongside the expansion of the Chungju Free Market and Chungju Public Market.

en.title: Boeun Traditional Market
en.overview: The origin of the Boeun Market dates back to the late 18th century. Historical records in regional gazetteers state that Dusan-si Market opened in the northern area during the late 18th century on the 3rd and 8th days of the month. In the 1860s, markets were held in Hoein (4th and 9th), Dusan (3rd and 8th), Boeun town (5th and 10th), Wonam (2nd and 7th), Gwan-gi (1st and 6th), and Maro (4th and 9th).

en.title: Gwan-gi Traditional Market
en.overview: Gwanteo Market (Gwan-gi Traditional Market), located in Gwan-gi-ri, Maro-myeon, Boeun-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, is a naturally formed 5-day periodic market. In its early days, it operated as a barter market for grains alongside a cattle market, thriving until the 1970s. However, with the opening of distribution industries and a sharp decline in the rural population, it gradually declined in the 1980s. Continuing its traditional heritage, it still operates as a 5-day market today, while administrative agencies and the market promotion association work to revitalize the traditional marketplace.

ja.overview: 永同地域は小白山脈と蘆령山脈の険しい山勢が調和をなし、3道の境界の中に錦江の水流が山すそに沿って美しい景観を作り出している中、商品の需要と供給の関係によって価格が形成される5日ごとに開かれる田舎の市場の性格を帯びている。干し柿、シイタケ、ブドウ、リンゴなどの地域特産品が多く生産されているだけでなく、2,000本の街路樹の柿の木が植えられており、柿の本場であることを実感させてくれる場所だ。

zh.title: 永同市場
zh.region_label: 忠清北道永同郡永同邑
zh.overview: 永同地區擁有小白山脈與蘆령山脈險峻的山勢交織，三道交界處伴隨著錦江水流沿著山麓形成優美景色。這裡保留了每五天舉辦一次的鄉村傳統市集特色，價格隨商品的供需關係而定。除了盛產柿餅、香菇、葡萄、蘋果等許多地方特產外，當地還種植了兩千棵行道柿子樹，讓人深刻感受到這裡是柿子之鄉。

en.title: Yeongchun Jaerae Market
en.overview: Yeongchun Jaerae Market is a traditional market in Danyang-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, held every 3rd and 8th day of the month. It is a typical rural township marketplace where visitors can experience a nostalgic atmosphere. The market features wild edible greens, medicinal herbs, and jujubes personally gathered by rural women living at the foot of Sobaeksan Mountain, as well as local specialties like Yeongchun soapstone inkstones, straw shoes, and woven string bags made by neighborhood elders.

en.title: Ochang Traditional Market
en.overview: Located in Ochang-eup, Cheongju—a place where cutting-edge high-tech industries coexist with agriculture, the foundation of all things—this market sits in a major transportation hub. It once thrived with grain markets, fish markets, general goods markets, and a cattle market. However, due to the development of transportation and the closure of the cattle market, it now operates on a smaller scale. The market is held on every 3rd and 8th day of the month.

en.title: Okcheon-jang Market
en.overview: Okcheon-jang is a 5-day periodic market held around Geumgucheon Stream in Geumgu-ri, Okcheon-eup, every 5th and 10th day of the month. Originally held in the old town area (Sanggye-ri, Hagye-ri), the regular market moved to its current location along the Geumgu-ri embankment in 1937 due to transportation developments. It thrives with about 200 general stores and 350 mobile vendors. In the past, residents from nearby areas like Dongi, Annam, Annae, Gunseo, and Gunbuk would gather on market days to trade various agricultural goods.

en.title: Yongsan-jang Market
en.overview: Yongsan-myeon, the first gateway to Yeongdong-gun on the Gyeongbu Expressway (Seoul→Busan), features a mild climate and abundant water resources with the Chogangcheon and Beophwacheon streams crossing through, offering stunning scenery. Grapes, tobacco, ginseng, and chili peppers make up the bulk of Yongsan-myeon's production. Recently, the number of cattle breeding farms has been steadily increasing, ranking first in Yeongdong-gun with 461 households raising 1,859 cattle. Along with this, it satisfies the palates of many travelers.

en.title: Wonmaru Market
en.overview: Wonmaru Market is located in Bunpyeong-dong, Seowon-gu, Cheongju-si. It is a relatively well-organized traditional market featuring arcades forming a crossroad layout with very few street vendors. It was naturally established following the development of large Jugong apartment complexes nearby. The market mainly deals in vegetables, fruits, meat, fresh chicken, seafood, children's clothing, general goods, and rice cakes. It is a vibrant traditional market that coexists with local residents by hosting various festivals every year.

en.title: Eumseong-jang Market
en.overview: Eumseong-jang is a traditional market located in Eubnae 2-ri, Eumseong-eup, Eumseong-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do. The Cultural Village area where Eumseong-jang is held is called 'Jangteo' (marketplace), and the marketplace near Eumseonggyo Bridge is called 'Chaeseojeon' (vegetable market). As Eumseong-eup is the administrative and transportation hub of the Eumseong region, Eumseong-jang has historically functioned as the most influential distribution base in Eumseong-gun. Since Gamwon-yeok station was located in Eubnae-ri, Eumseong-eup during the Joseon Dynasty, Eumseong-jang naturally adapted to these regional conditions.
